## <span class="secno">1. </span><span class="content">Introduction</span><a href="#introduction" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is informative.*

This standard defines an interface definition language, Web IDL, that
can be used to describe interfaces that are intended to be implemented
in web browsers. Web IDL is an IDL variant with a number of features
that allow the behavior of common script objects in the web platform to
be specified more readily. How interfaces described with Web IDL
correspond to constructs within JavaScript execution environments is
also detailed here.

Concretely, Web IDL provides a syntax for specifying the surface APIs of
web platform objects, as well as JavaScript bindings that detail how
those APIs manifest as JavaScript constructs. This ensures common tasks,
such as installing global properties, processing numeric inputs, or
exposing iteration behavior, remain uniform across web platform
specifications: such specifications describe their interfaces using Web
IDL, and then use prose to specify API-specific details.

The term "JavaScript" is used to refer to ECMA-262, rather than the
official term ECMAScript, since the term JavaScript is more widely
known.

## <span class="secno">2. </span><span class="content">Interface definition language</span><a href="#idl" class="self-link"></a>

This section describes a language, *Web IDL*, which can be used to
define interfaces for APIs in the Web platform. A specification that
defines Web APIs can include one or more <span id="dfn-idl-fragment"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="IDL fragment">IDL
fragments</span> that describe the interfaces (the state and behavior
that objects can exhibit) for the APIs defined by that specification. An
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> is a sequence of definitions that
matches the [Definitions](#prod-Definitions) grammar symbol. The set of
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a> that an implementation supports
is not ordered. See [IDL grammar](#idl-grammar) for the complete grammar
and an explanation of the notation used.

The different kinds of <span id="dfn-definition" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">definitions</span> that can appear in an
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> are:
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface definitions</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a>,
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin"
data-link-type="dfn">partial mixin definitions</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function"
data-link-type="dfn">callback functions</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interfaces</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace"
data-link-type="dfn">namespaces</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace"
data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace definitions</a>,
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionaries</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-dictionary"
data-link-type="dfn">partial dictionary definitions</a>,
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef"
data-link-type="dfn">typedefs</a> and
<a href="#includes-statement" id="ref-for-includes-statement"
data-link-type="dfn">includes statements</a>. These are all defined in
the following sections.

Each <a href="#dfn-definition" id="ref-for-dfn-definition"
data-link-type="dfn">definition</a> (matching
[Definition](#prod-Definition)) can be preceded by a list of
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> (matching
[ExtendedAttributeList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeList)), which can control
how the definition will be handled in language bindings. The extended
attributes defined by this specification that are language binding
agnostic are discussed in [§ 2.14 Extended
attributes](#idl-extended-attributes), while those specific to the
JavaScript language binding are discussed in [§ 3.3 Extended
attributes](#js-extended-attributes).

``` highlight
[extended_attributes]
interface identifier {
  /* interface_members... */
};
```

``` grammar
Definitions ::
    ExtendedAttributeList Definition Definitions
    ε
```

``` grammar
Definition ::
    CallbackOrInterfaceOrMixin
    Namespace
    Partial
    Dictionary
    Enum
    Typedef
    IncludesStatement
```

<div id="example-25f60a7c" class="example">

<a href="#example-25f60a7c" class="self-link"></a>

The following is an example of an
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a>.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Paint { };

[Exposed=Window]
interface SolidColor : Paint {
  attribute double red;
  attribute double green;
  attribute double blue;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Pattern : Paint {
  attribute DOMString imageURL;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface GraphicalWindow {
  constructor();
  readonly attribute unsigned long width;
  readonly attribute unsigned long height;

  attribute Paint currentPaint;

  undefined drawRectangle(double x, double y, double width, double height);

  undefined drawText(double x, double y, DOMString text);
};
```

Here, four <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> are being defined. The
`GraphicalWindow` interface has two
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>, one writable attribute, and two
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> defined on it. Objects that
implement the `GraphicalWindow` interface will expose these attributes
and operations in a manner appropriate to the particular language being
used.

In JavaScript, the attributes on the IDL interfaces will be exposed as
accessor properties and the operations as data properties whose value is
a <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-built-in-function-objects" data-link-type="dfn">built-in
function object</a> on a prototype object for all `GraphicalWindow`
objects; each JavaScript object that implements `GraphicalWindow` will
have that prototype object in its prototype chain.

The <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> that appears on
`GraphicalWindow` causes a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#constructor"
id="ref-for-constructor" data-link-type="dfn">constructor</a> to exist
in JavaScript implementations, so that calling `new GraphicalWindow()`
would return a new object that implemented the interface.

All <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> have the
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>, which ensures the
interfaces are only available in <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm" data-link-type="dfn">realms</a> whose <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-global"
id="ref-for-concept-realm-global" data-link-type="dfn">global object</a>
is a <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window"
id="ref-for-window" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Window</code></a> object.

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.1. </span><span class="content">Names</span><a href="#idl-names" class="self-link"></a>

Every <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface definition</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace①"
data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace definition</a>,
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary①"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-dictionary①"
data-link-type="dfn">partial dictionary definition</a>,
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> and
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef①"
data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a> (together called
<span id="dfn-named-definition" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="" lt="named definition">named definitions</span>) and every
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a>,
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a>, and
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a> has an
<span id="dfn-identifier" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">identifier</span>, as do some
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a>. The identifier is determined by an
[identifier](#prod-identifier) token somewhere in the declaration:

- For <a href="#dfn-named-definition" id="ref-for-dfn-named-definition"
  data-link-type="dfn">named definitions</a>, the
  [identifier](#prod-identifier) token that appears directly after the
  interface, namespace, dictionary, enum or callback keyword determines
  the identifier of that definition.

  ``` highlight
  interface interface_identifier { /* interface_members... */ };
  partial interface interface_identifier { /* interface_members... */ };
  namespace namespace_identifier { /* namespace_members... */ };
  partial namespace namespace_identifier { /* namespace_members... */ };
  dictionary dictionary_identifier { /* dictionary_members... */ };
  partial dictionary dictionary_identifier { /* dictionary_members... */ };
  enum enumeration_identifier { "enum", "values" /* , ... */ };
  callback callback_identifier = return_type (/* arguments... */);
  callback interface callback_interface_identifier { /* interface_members... */ };
  ```

- For <a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②"
  data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
  <a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef②"
  data-link-type="dfn">typedefs</a> and
  <a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①"
  data-link-type="dfn">dictionary members</a>, the final
  [identifier](#prod-identifier) token before the semicolon at the end
  of the declaration determines the identifier.

  ``` highlight
  [extended_attributes]
  interface identifier {
    attribute type attribute_identifier;
  };

  typedef type typedef_identifier;

  dictionary identifier {
    type dictionary_member_identifier;
  };
  ```

- For <a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①"
  data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, the [identifier](#prod-identifier)
  token before the equals sign determines the identifier.

  ``` highlight
  const type constant_identifier = 42;
  ```

- For <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②"
  data-link-type="dfn">operations</a>, the
  [identifier](#prod-identifier) token that appears after the return
  type but before the opening parenthesis (that is, one that is matched
  as part of the [OptionalOperationName](#prod-OptionalOperationName)
  grammar symbol in an [OperationRest](#prod-OperationRest)) determines
  the identifier of the operation. If there is no such
  [identifier](#prod-identifier) token, then the operation does not have
  an identifier.

  ``` highlight
  interface interface_identifier {
    return_type operation_identifier(/* arguments... */);
  };
  ```

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Operations can have no identifier when
they are being used to declare a
<a href="#dfn-special-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-special-operation"
data-link-type="dfn">special kind of operation</a>, such as a getter or
setter.

For all of these constructs, the
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> is the value of the
[identifier](#prod-identifier) token with any leading U+005F (\_)
removed.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> A leading U+005F (\_) is used to
escape an identifier from looking like a reserved word so that, for
example, an interface named "`interface`" can be defined. The leading
U+005F (\_) is dropped to unescape the identifier.

Operation arguments can take a slightly wider set of identifiers. In an
operation declaration, the identifier of an argument is specified
immediately after its type and is given by either an
[identifier](#prod-identifier) token or by one of the keywords that
match the [ArgumentNameKeyword](#prod-ArgumentNameKeyword) symbol. If
one of these keywords is used, it need not be escaped with a leading
underscore.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  return_type operation_identifier(argument_type argument_identifier /* , ... */);
};
```

``` grammar
ArgumentNameKeyword ::
    attribute
    callback
    const
    constructor
    deleter
    dictionary
    enum
    getter
    includes
    inherit
    interface
    iterable
    maplike
    mixin
    namespace
    partial
    readonly
    required
    setlike
    setter
    static
    stringifier
    typedef
    unrestricted
```

If an [identifier](#prod-identifier) token is used, then the
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of the operation argument is the
value of that token with any leading U+005F (\_) removed. If instead one
of the [ArgumentNameKeyword](#prod-ArgumentNameKeyword) keyword token is
used, then the <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of the operation argument is simply
that token.

The <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of any of the abovementioned IDL
constructs (except operation arguments) must not be "`constructor`",
"`toString`", or begin with a U+005F (\_). These are known as
<span id="dfn-reserved-identifier" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">reserved identifiers</span>.

Although the "`toJSON`"
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> is not a
<a href="#dfn-reserved-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-reserved-identifier"
data-link-type="dfn">reserved identifier</a>, it must only be used for
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> that convert objects to
<a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types"
data-link-type="dfn">JSON types</a>, as described in [§ 2.5.3.1
toJSON](#idl-tojson-operation).

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Further restrictions on identifier
names for particular constructs can be made in later sections.

Within the set of
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment④"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a> that a given implementation
supports, the <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of every
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>,
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary②"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary</a>,
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration①"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function②"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> and
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef③"
data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a> must not be the same as the identifier
of any other <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace③"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>,
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary③"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary</a>,
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration②"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function③"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface③"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef④"
data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a>.

Within an <a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a>, a reference to a
<a href="#dfn-definition" id="ref-for-dfn-definition①"
data-link-type="dfn">definition</a> need not appear after the
declaration of the referenced definition. References can also be made
across <a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a>.

<div id="example-679e8e2c" class="example">

<a href="#example-679e8e2c" class="self-link"></a>

Therefore, the following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> is valid:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface B : A {
  undefined f(SequenceOfLongs x);
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface A {
};

typedef sequence<long> SequenceOfLongs;
```

</div>

<div id="example-1192ff1f" class="example">

<a href="#example-1192ff1f" class="self-link"></a>

The following <a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> demonstrates how
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">identifiers</a> are given to definitions and
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member"
data-link-type="dfn">interface members</a>.

``` highlight
// Typedef identifier: "number"
typedef double number;

// Interface identifier: "System"
[Exposed=Window]
interface System {

  // Operation identifier:          "createObject"
  // Operation argument identifier: "interface"
  object createObject(DOMString _interface);

  // Operation argument identifier: "interface"
  sequence<object> getObjects(DOMString interface);

  // Operation has no identifier; it declares a getter.
  getter DOMString (DOMString keyName);
};

// Interface identifier: "TextField"
[Exposed=Window]
interface TextField {

  // Attribute identifier: "const"
  attribute boolean _const;

  // Attribute identifier: "value"
  attribute DOMString? _value;
};
```

Note that while the second
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> on the `TextField`
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> need not have been escaped with an
underscore (because "`value`" is not a keyword in the IDL grammar), it
is still unescaped to obtain the attribute’s
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>.

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.2. </span><span class="content">Interfaces</span><a href="#idl-interfaces" class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a> are used to describe object
oriented systems. In such systems, objects are entities that have
identity and which are encapsulations of state and behavior. An
<span id="dfn-interface" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">interface</span> is a definition (matching interface
[InterfaceRest](#prod-InterfaceRest)) that declares some state and
behavior that an object implementing that interface will expose.

``` highlight
[extended_attributes]
interface identifier {
  /* interface_members... */
};
```

An interface is a specification of a set of
<span id="dfn-interface-member" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="" lt="interface member">interface members</span> (matching
[InterfaceMembers](#prod-InterfaceMembers)). These are the
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> that appear between the braces in the
interface declaration.

Interfaces in Web IDL describe how objects that implement the interface
behave. In bindings for object oriented languages, it is expected that
an object that implements a particular IDL interface provides ways to
inspect and modify the object’s state and to invoke the behavior
described by the interface.

An interface can be defined to <span id="dfn-inherit"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="interface" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">inherit</span> from another interface. If the identifier of
the interface is followed by a U+003A (:) and an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>, then that identifier identifies the
inherited interface. An object that implements an interface that
inherits from another also implements that inherited interface. The
object therefore will also have members that correspond to the interface
members from the inherited interface.

``` highlight
interface identifier : identifier_of_inherited_interface {
  /* interface_members... */
};
```

The order that members appear in has significance for property
enumeration in the [JavaScript binding](#js-interfaces).

Interfaces may specify an interface member that has the same name as one
from an inherited interface. Objects that implement the derived
interface will expose the member on the derived interface. It is
language binding specific whether the overridden member can be accessed
on the object.

<div id="example-367b9481" class="example">

<a href="#example-367b9481" class="self-link"></a>

Consider the following two interfaces.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface A {
  undefined f();
  undefined g();
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface B : A {
  undefined f();
  undefined g(DOMString x);
};
```

In the JavaScript language binding, an instance of `B` will have a
prototype chain that looks like the following:

    [Object.prototype: the Object prototype object]
         ↑
    [A.prototype: interface prototype object for A]
         ↑
    [B.prototype: interface prototype object for B]
         ↑
    [instanceOfB]

Calling `instanceOfB.f()` in JavaScript will invoke the f defined on
`B`. However, the f from `A` can still be invoked on an object that
implements `B` by calling `A.prototype.f.call(instanceOfB)`.

</div>

The <span id="dfn-inherited-interfaces" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">inherited interfaces</span> of a given
interface `A` is the set of all interfaces that `A` inherits from,
directly or indirectly. If `A` does not
<a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit"
data-link-type="dfn">inherit</a> from another interface, then the set is
empty. Otherwise, the set includes the interface `B` that `A`
<a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit①"
data-link-type="dfn">inherits</a> from and all of `B`’s
<a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a>.

An interface must not be declared such that its inheritance hierarchy
has a cycle. That is, an interface `A` cannot inherit from itself, nor
can it inherit from another interface `B` that inherits from `A`, and so
on.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="inclusive inherited interfaces"
algorithm-for="interface">

The <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list"
data-link-type="dfn">list</a> of
<span id="interface-inclusive-inherited-interfaces"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="interface" dfn-type="dfn"
noexport="">inclusive inherited interfaces</span> of an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> `I` is defined as follows:

1.  Let `result` be « ».

2.  Let `interface` be `I`.

3.  While `interface` is not null:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="ref-for-list-append" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
        `interface` to `result`.

    2.  Set `interface` to the
        <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧"
        data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that `I`
        <a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit②"
        data-link-type="dfn">inherits</a> from, if any, and null
        otherwise.

4.  Return `result`.

</div>

Note that general multiple inheritance of interfaces is not supported,
and objects also cannot implement arbitrary sets of interfaces. Objects
can be defined to implement a single given interface `A`, which means
that it also implements all of `A`’s <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces①" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a>. In addition, an
<a href="#includes-statement" id="ref-for-includes-statement①"
data-link-type="dfn">includes statement</a> can be used to define that
objects implementing an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> `A` will always also include the
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> of the
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a> `A`
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include"
data-link-type="dfn">includes</a>.

Each interface member can be preceded by a list of
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> (matching
[ExtendedAttributeList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeList)), which can control
how the interface member will be handled in language bindings.

``` highlight
[extended_attributes]
interface identifier {

  [extended_attributes]
  const type constant_identifier = 42;

  [extended_attributes]
  attribute type identifier;

  [extended_attributes]
  return_type identifier(/* arguments... */);
};
```

The IDL for interfaces can be split into multiple parts by using
<span id="dfn-partial-interface" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">partial interface</span> definitions (matching partial
interface [PartialInterfaceRest](#prod-PartialInterfaceRest)). The
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of a partial interface definition
must be the same as the identifier of an interface definition. All of
the members that appear on each of the partial interfaces are considered
to be members of the interface itself.

``` highlight
interface SomeInterface {
  /* interface_members... */
};

partial interface SomeInterface {
  /* interface_members... */
};
```

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Partial interface definitions are
intended for use as a specification editorial aide, allowing the
definition of an interface to be separated over more than one section of
the document, and sometimes multiple documents.

The order of appearance of an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> definition and any of its
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface②"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a> definitions does not matter.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> A partial interface definition cannot
specify that the interface
<a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit③"
data-link-type="dfn">inherits</a> from another interface. Inheritance is
to be specified on the original
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> definition.

The relevant language binding determines how interfaces correspond to
constructs in the language.

The following extended attributes are applicable to interfaces:
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject" id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNoInterfaceObject</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#LegacyOverrideBuiltIns" id="ref-for-LegacyOverrideBuiltIns"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyOverrideBuiltIns</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\],
and \[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\].

The following extended attributes are applicable to
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface③"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interfaces</a>:
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#LegacyOverrideBuiltIns" id="ref-for-LegacyOverrideBuiltIns①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyOverrideBuiltIns</code></a>\],
and \[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\].

<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②"
data-link-type="dfn">Interfaces</a> must be annotated with an
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute③"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="qualified name">

The <span id="qualified-name" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
noexport="">qualified name</span> of an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> `interface` is defined as follows:

1.  Let `identifier` be the
    <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of `interface`.

2.  If `interface` has a
    \[<a href="#LegacyNamespace" id="ref-for-LegacyNamespace"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyNamespace</code></a>\]
    <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute④"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>, then:

    1.  Let `namespace` be the identifier argument of the
        \[<a href="#LegacyNamespace" id="ref-for-LegacyNamespace①"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyNamespace</code></a>\]
        <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑤"
        data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>.

    2.  Return the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-concatenate"
        id="ref-for-string-concatenate" data-link-type="dfn">concatenation</a>
        of « `namespace`, `identifier` » with separator U+002E (.).

3.  Return `identifier`.

</div>

``` grammar
CallbackOrInterfaceOrMixin ::
    callback CallbackRestOrInterface
    interface InterfaceOrMixin
```

``` grammar
InterfaceOrMixin ::
    InterfaceRest
    MixinRest
```

``` grammar
InterfaceRest ::
    identifier Inheritance { InterfaceMembers } ;
```

``` grammar
Partial ::
    partial PartialDefinition
```

``` grammar
PartialDefinition ::
    interface PartialInterfaceOrPartialMixin
    PartialDictionary
    Namespace
```

``` grammar
PartialInterfaceOrPartialMixin ::
    PartialInterfaceRest
    MixinRest
```

``` grammar
PartialInterfaceRest ::
    identifier { PartialInterfaceMembers } ;
```

``` grammar
InterfaceMembers ::
    ExtendedAttributeList InterfaceMember InterfaceMembers
    ε
```

``` grammar
InterfaceMember ::
    PartialInterfaceMember
    Constructor
```

``` grammar
PartialInterfaceMembers ::
    ExtendedAttributeList PartialInterfaceMember PartialInterfaceMembers
    ε
```

``` grammar
PartialInterfaceMember ::
    Const
    Operation
    Stringifier
    StaticMember
    Iterable
    AsyncIterable
    ReadOnlyMember
    ReadWriteAttribute
    ReadWriteMaplike
    ReadWriteSetlike
    InheritAttribute
```

``` grammar
Inheritance ::
    : identifier
    ε
```

<div id="example-0f0ea08a" class="example">

<a href="#example-0f0ea08a" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> demonstrates the definition of two
mutually referential
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a>. Both `Human` and `Dog` inherit from
`Animal`. Objects that implement either of those two interfaces will
thus have a `name` attribute.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Animal {
  attribute DOMString name;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Human : Animal {
  attribute Dog? pet;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Dog : Animal {
  attribute Human? owner;
};
```

</div>

<div id="example-25ab6a82" class="example">

<a href="#example-25ab6a82" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①①"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines simplified versions of a
DOM <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> and a
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface④"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Node {
  readonly attribute DOMString nodeName;
  readonly attribute Node? parentNode;
  Node appendChild(Node newChild);
  undefined addEventListener(DOMString type, EventListener listener);
};

callback interface EventListener {
  undefined handleEvent(Event event);
};
```

Plain objects can implement a
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> like `EventListener`:

``` highlight
var node = getNode();                                // Obtain an instance of Node.

var listener = {
  handleEvent: function(event) {
    // ...
  }
};
node.addEventListener("click", listener);            // This works.

node.addEventListener("click", function() { ... });  // As does this.
```

It is not possible for such an object to implement an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> like `Node`, however:

``` highlight
var node = getNode();  // Obtain an instance of Node.

var newNode = {
  nodeName: "span",
  parentNode: null,
  appendChild: function(newchild) {
    // ...
  },
  addEventListener: function(type, listener) {
    // ...
  }
};
node.appendChild(newNode);  // This will throw a TypeError exception.
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.3. </span><span class="content">Interface mixins</span><a href="#idl-interface-mixins" class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="interface-mixin" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">interface mixin</span> is a definition (matching interface
[MixinRest](#prod-MixinRest)) that declares state and behavior that can
be <a href="#include" id="ref-for-include①"
data-link-type="dfn">included</a> by one or more
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a>, and that are exposed by objects
that implement an <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include②"
data-link-type="dfn">includes</a> the
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>.

``` highlight
interface mixin identifier {
  /* mixin_members... */
};
```

<span class="marker">Note:</span>
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③"
data-link-type="dfn">Interface mixins</a>, much like
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface④"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interfaces</a>, are intended for use as a
specification editorial aide, allowing a coherent set of functionalities
to be grouped together, and included in multiple interfaces, possibly
across documents. They are not meant to be exposed through language
bindings. Guidance on when to choose
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interfaces</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a>, or
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface mixins</a> can be found in
[§ 2.3.1 Using mixins and partials](#using-mixins-and-partials).

An <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> is a specification of a set of
<span id="interface-mixin-member" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="" lt="interface mixin member">interface mixin members</span>
(matching [MixinMembers](#prod-MixinMembers)), which are the
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>,
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a>,
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attributes</a>, and
<a href="#dfn-stringifier" id="ref-for-dfn-stringifier"
data-link-type="dfn">stringifiers</a> that appear between the braces in
the <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> declaration.

These <a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant③"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>,
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a>,
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute①"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attributes</a>, and
<a href="#dfn-stringifier" id="ref-for-dfn-stringifier①"
data-link-type="dfn">stringifiers</a> describe the behaviors that can be
implemented by an object, as if they were specified on the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include③"
data-link-type="dfn">includes</a> them.

<a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute"
data-link-type="dfn">Static attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation"
data-link-type="dfn">static operations</a>,
<a href="#dfn-special-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-special-operation①"
data-link-type="dfn">special operations</a>, and
<a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration" data-link-type="dfn">iterable</a>,
<a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable</a>,
<a href="#dfn-maplike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-maplike-declaration"
data-link-type="dfn">maplike</a>, and
<a href="#dfn-setlike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-setlike-declaration"
data-link-type="dfn">setlike declarations</a> cannot appear in
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> declarations.

As with interfaces, the IDL for
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a> can be split into multiple
parts by using <span id="partial-interface-mixin"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">partial interface
mixin</span> definitions (matching partial interface
[MixinRest](#prod-MixinRest)). The
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①①"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of a
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin②"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface mixin</a>
<a href="#dfn-definition" id="ref-for-dfn-definition②"
data-link-type="dfn">definition</a> must be the same as the
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①②"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of an
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>
<a href="#dfn-definition" id="ref-for-dfn-definition③"
data-link-type="dfn">definition</a>. All of the
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> that appear on each of the
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin③"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface mixin</a>
<a href="#dfn-definition" id="ref-for-dfn-definition④"
data-link-type="dfn">definitions</a> are considered to be
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> of the
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> itself, and—by extension—of the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> that
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include④"
data-link-type="dfn">include</a> the
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>.

``` highlight
interface mixin SomeMixin {
  /* mixin_members... */
};

partial interface mixin SomeMixin {
  /* mixin_members... */
};
```

The order that members appear in has significance for property
enumeration in the [JavaScript binding](#js-interfaces).

Note that unlike <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②①"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> or
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary④"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionaries</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a> do not create types.

Of the extended attributes defined in this specification, only the
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\], and
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
extended attributes are applicable to
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a>.

An <span id="includes-statement" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
noexport="">includes statement</span> is a definition (matching
[IncludesStatement](#prod-IncludesStatement)) used to declare that all
objects implementing an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> `I` (identified by the first
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①③"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>) must additionally include the
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member②"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> of
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> `M` (identified by the second
identifier). <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②③"
data-link-type="dfn">Interface</a> `I` is said to <span id="include"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="interface" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">include</span>
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> `M`.

``` highlight
interface_identifier includes mixin_identifier;
```

The first <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①④"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> must reference a
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> `I`. The second identifier must
reference an <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> `M`.

Each
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member③"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> of `M` is considered to be a
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member②"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> of each
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> `I`, `J`, `K`, … that
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">includes</a> `M`, as if a copy of each
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member④"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> had been made. So for a given member `m`
of `M`, interface `I` is considered to have a
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member③"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> `m`<sub>`I`</sub>, interface `J` is
considered to have a <a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member④"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> `m`<sub>`J`</sub>, interface `K` is
considered to have a <a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> `m`<sub>`K`</sub>, and so on. The
<span id="host-interfaces" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
noexport="">host interfaces</span> of `m`<sub>`I`</sub>,
`m`<sub>`J`</sub>, and `m`<sub>`K`</sub>, are `I`, `J`, and `K`
respectively.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> In JavaScript, this implies that each
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation③"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a> declared as a
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> of
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> `M`, and exposed as a data
property with a
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-built-in-function-objects①"
data-link-type="dfn">built-in function object</a> value, is a distinct
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-built-in-function-objects②"
data-link-type="dfn">built-in function object</a> in each
<a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object"
data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype object</a> whose associated
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">includes</a> `M`. Similarly, for
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute④"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>, each copy of the accessor property
has distinct
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-built-in-function-objects③"
data-link-type="dfn">built-in function objects</a> for its getters and
setters.

The order of appearance of
<a href="#includes-statement" id="ref-for-includes-statement②"
data-link-type="dfn">includes statements</a> affects the order in which
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> are
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">included</a> by their
<a href="#host-interfaces" id="ref-for-host-interfaces"
data-link-type="dfn">host interface</a>.

<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">Member</a> order isn’t clearly specified, in
particular when
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a> are defined in separate
documents. It is discussed in [issue
\#432](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/432).

No
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> defined in this
specification are applicable to
<a href="#includes-statement" id="ref-for-includes-statement③"
data-link-type="dfn">includes statements</a>.

<div id="example-mixin" class="example">

<a href="#example-mixin" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①②"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, `Entry`, and an
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>, `Observable`. The
<a href="#includes-statement" id="ref-for-includes-statement④"
data-link-type="dfn">includes statement</a> specifies that
`Observable`’s
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> are always included on objects
implementing `Entry`.

``` highlight
interface Entry {
  readonly attribute unsigned short entryType;
  // ...
};

interface mixin Observable {
  undefined addEventListener(DOMString type,
                        EventListener listener,
                        boolean useCapture);
  // ...
};

Entry includes Observable;
```

A JavaScript implementation would thus have an `addEventListener`
property in the prototype chain of every `Entry`:

``` highlight
var e = getEntry();          // Obtain an instance of Entry.
typeof e.addEventListener;   // Evaluates to "function".
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
CallbackOrInterfaceOrMixin ::
    callback CallbackRestOrInterface
    interface InterfaceOrMixin
```

</div>

</div>

``` grammar
    InterfaceRest
    MixinRest
```


``` grammar
    PartialDictionary
    Namespace
```

``` grammar
MixinRest ::
    mixin identifier { MixinMembers } ;
```

``` grammar

    ExtendedAttributeList MixinMember MixinMembers
    ε
```

``` grammar
MixinMember ::
    Const
    RegularOperation
    Stringifier
    OptionalReadOnly AttributeRest
```

``` grammar
IncludesStatement ::
    identifier includes identifier ;
```

#### <span class="secno">2.3.1. </span><span class="content">Using mixins and partials</span><a href="#using-mixins-and-partials" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is informative.*

<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②①"
data-link-type="dfn">Interface mixins</a> allow the sharing of
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant④"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, and
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation③"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> across *multiple*
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a>. If you’re only planning to extend a
single interface, you might consider using a
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a> instead.

For example, instead of:

``` highlight
interface mixin WindowSessionStorage {
  readonly attribute Storage sessionStorage;
};
Window includes WindowSessionStorage;
```

do:

``` highlight
partial interface Window {
  readonly attribute Storage sessionStorage;
};
```

Additionally, you can rely on extending
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a> exposed by other
specifications to target common use cases, such as
<a href="#dfn-exposed" id="ref-for-dfn-exposed"
data-link-type="dfn">exposing</a> a set of
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation④"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> across both window and worker
contexts.

For example, instead of the common but verbose:

``` highlight
interface mixin GlobalCrypto {
  readonly attribute Crypto crypto;
};

Window includes GlobalCrypto;
WorkerGlobalScope includes GlobalCrypto;
```

you can extend the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#windoworworkerglobalscope"
id="ref-for-windoworworkerglobalscope" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope</code></a>
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> using a
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin④"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface mixin</a>:

``` highlight
partial interface mixin WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope {
  readonly attribute Crypto crypto;
};
```

### <span class="secno">2.4. </span><span class="content">Callback interfaces</span><a href="#idl-callback-interfaces" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-callback-interface" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">callback interface</span> is a
<a href="#dfn-definition" id="ref-for-dfn-definition⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">definition</a> matching callback interface
[identifier](#prod-identifier) {
[CallbackInterfaceMembers](#prod-CallbackInterfaceMembers) } ;. It can
be implemented by any object, as described in [§ 2.12 Objects
implementing interfaces](#idl-objects).

<span class="marker">Note:</span> A
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> is not an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>. The name and syntax are left over
from earlier versions of this standard, where these concepts had more in
common.

A <a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> is a specification of a set
of <span id="callback-interface-member" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="callback interface member">callback
interface members</span> (matching
[CallbackInterfaceMembers](#prod-CallbackInterfaceMembers)). These are
the <a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> that appear between the braces in the
interface declaration.

``` highlight
callback interface identifier {
  /* interface_members... */
};
```

<span class="marker">Note:</span> See also the similarly named
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function④"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> definition.

<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">Callback interfaces</a> must define exactly one
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation④"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a>.

<div class="warning">

Specification authors should not define
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interfaces</a> unless required to describe
the requirements of existing APIs. Instead, a
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> should be used.

The definition of
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#callbackdef-eventlistener"
id="ref-for-callbackdef-eventlistener" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">EventListener</code></a> as a
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> is an example of an existing
API that needs to allow objects with a given property (in this case
`handleEvent`) to be considered to implement the interface. For new
APIs, and those for which there are no compatibility concerns, using a
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> will allow only a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object" data-link-type="dfn">function object</a>
(in the JavaScript language binding).

</div>

<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①①"
data-link-type="dfn">Callback interfaces</a> which declare
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> must be annotated with an
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>.

``` grammar
CallbackRestOrInterface ::
    CallbackRest
    interface identifier { CallbackInterfaceMembers } ;
```

``` grammar
CallbackInterfaceMembers ::
    ExtendedAttributeList CallbackInterfaceMember CallbackInterfaceMembers
    ε
```

``` grammar
CallbackInterfaceMember ::
    Const
    RegularOperation
```

### <span class="secno">2.5. </span><span class="content">Members</span><a href="#idl-members" class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">Interfaces</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a>, and
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace④"
data-link-type="dfn">namespaces</a> are specifications of a set of
<span id="dfn-member" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">members</span> (respectively matching
[InterfaceMembers](#prod-InterfaceMembers),
[MixinMembers](#prod-MixinMembers), and
[NamespaceMembers](#prod-NamespaceMembers)), which are the
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>,
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a>, and other declarations that appear
between the braces of their declarations.
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">Attributes</a> describe the state that an object
implementing the <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> will expose, and
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> describe the behaviors that can be
invoked on the object.
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">Constants</a> declare named constant values that
are exposed as a convenience to users of objects in the system.

<div class="note" role="note">

When an <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">includes</a> an
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>, each
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> of the interface mixin is also
considered a member of the interface. In contrast,
<a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit④"
data-link-type="dfn">inherited</a> interface members are not considered
members of the interface.

</div>

The <a href="#constructor-steps" id="ref-for-constructor-steps"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor steps</a>,
<a href="#getter-steps" id="ref-for-getter-steps"
data-link-type="dfn">getter steps</a>,
<a href="#setter-steps" id="ref-for-setter-steps"
data-link-type="dfn">setter steps</a>, and
<a href="#method-steps" id="ref-for-method-steps"
data-link-type="dfn">method steps</a> for the various
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> defined on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> or
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> have access to a
<span id="this" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">this</span> value, which is an IDL value of the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> type that the member is declared on
or that <a href="#include" id="ref-for-include⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">includes</a> the
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> the member is declared on.

<a href="#setter-steps" id="ref-for-setter-steps①"
data-link-type="dfn">Setter steps</a> also have access to
<span id="the-given-value" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">the given value</span>, which is an IDL value of the type the
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> is declared as.

<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">Interfaces</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixins</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①②"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interfaces</a> and
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">namespaces</a> each support a different set of
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a>, which are specified in [§ 2.2
Interfaces](#idl-interfaces), [§ 2.3 Interface
mixins](#idl-interface-mixins), [§ 2.4 Callback
interfaces](#idl-callback-interfaces), and [§ 2.6
Namespaces](#idl-namespaces), and summarized in the following
informative table:

|  | <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">Interfaces</a> | <a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①③"
data-link-type="dfn">Callback interfaces</a> | <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">Interface mixins</a> | <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">Namespaces</a> |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| <a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">Constants</a> | ● | ● | ● |  |
| <a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute②"
data-link-type="dfn">Regular attributes</a> | ● |  | ● | Only <a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a> attributes |
| <a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute①"
data-link-type="dfn">Static attributes</a> | ● |  |  |  |
| <a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">Regular Operations</a> | ● | ● | ● | ● |
| <a href="#dfn-stringifier" id="ref-for-dfn-stringifier②"
data-link-type="dfn">Stringifiers</a> | ● |  | ● |  |
| <a href="#dfn-special-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-special-operation②"
data-link-type="dfn">Special Operations</a> | ● |  |  |  |
| <a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation①"
data-link-type="dfn">Static Operations</a> | ● |  |  |  |
| <a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration①" data-link-type="dfn">Iterable
declarations</a> | ● |  |  |  |
| <a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration①"
data-link-type="dfn">Asynchronously iterable declarations</a> | ● |  |  |  |
| <a href="#dfn-maplike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-maplike-declaration①"
data-link-type="dfn">Maplike declarations</a> | ● |  |  |  |
| <a href="#dfn-setlike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-setlike-declaration①"
data-link-type="dfn">Setlike declarations</a> | ● |  |  |  |

#### <span class="secno">2.5.1. </span><span class="content">Constants</span><a href="#idl-constants" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-constant" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">constant</span> is a declaration (matching
[Const](#prod-Const)) used to bind a constant value to a name. Constants
can appear on <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> and
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①④"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interfaces</a>.

Constants have in the past primarily been used to define named integer
codes in the style of an enumeration. The Web platform is moving away
from this design pattern in favor of the use of strings. Editors who
wish to use this feature are strongly advised to discuss this by [filing
an
issue](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/new?title=Intent%20to%20use%20Constants)
before proceeding.

``` highlight
const type constant_identifier = 42;
```

The <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of a
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a> must not be the same as the identifier
of another
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a> or
<a href="#callback-interface-member"
id="ref-for-callback-interface-member" data-link-type="dfn">callback
interface member</a> defined on the same
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>. The identifier also must
not be "`length`", "`name`" or "`prototype`".

<span class="marker">Note:</span> These three names are the names of
properties that are defined on the
<a href="#dfn-interface-object" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-object"
data-link-type="dfn">interface object</a> in the JavaScript language
binding.

The type of a constant (matching [ConstType](#prod-ConstType)) must not
be any type other than a
<a href="#dfn-primitive-type" id="ref-for-dfn-primitive-type"
data-link-type="dfn">primitive type</a>. If an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> is used, it must reference a
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a> whose type is a primitive type.

The [ConstValue](#prod-ConstValue) part of a constant declaration gives
the value of the constant, which can be one of the two boolean literal
tokens (true and false), an [integer](#prod-integer) token, a
[decimal](#prod-decimal) token, or one of the three special floating
point constant values (-Infinity, Infinity and NaN).

<span class="marker">Note:</span> These values – in addition to strings
and the empty sequence – can also be used to specify the
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
data-link-type="dfn">default value of a dictionary member</a> or
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value" class="allow-2119"
data-link-type="dfn">of an optional argument</a>. Note that strings, the
empty sequence \[\], and the default dictionary {} cannot be used as the
value of a <a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①①"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a>.

The value of the boolean literal tokens true and false are the IDL
<a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a> values `true`
and `false`.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="value of integer tokens">

The value of an [integer](#prod-integer) token is an integer whose value
is determined as follows:

1.  Let `S` be the sequence of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
    id="ref-for-scalar-value" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>
    matched by the [integer](#prod-integer) token.

2.  Let `sign` be −1 if `S` begins with U+002D (-), and 1 otherwise.

3.  Let `base` be the base of the number based on the
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
    id="ref-for-scalar-value①" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>
    that follow the optional leading U+002D (-):

    U+0030 (0), U+0058 (X)  
    U+0030 (0), U+0078 (x)  
    The base is 16.

    U+0030 (0)  
    The base is 8.

    Otherwise  
    The base is 10.

4.  Let `number` be the result of interpreting all remaining
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
    id="ref-for-scalar-value②" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>
    following the optional leading U+002D (-) character and any
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
    id="ref-for-scalar-value③" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>
    indicating the base as an integer specified in base `base`.

5.  Return `sign` × `number`.

</div>

The type of an [integer](#prod-integer) token is the same as the type of
the constant, dictionary member or optional argument it is being used as
the value of. The value of the [integer](#prod-integer) token must not
lie outside the valid range of values for its type, as given in [§ 2.13
Types](#idl-types).

<div id="decimal-token-value" class="algorithm"
algorithm="value of decimal tokens">

The value of a [decimal](#prod-decimal) token is either an IEEE 754
single-precision floating point number or an IEEE 754 double-precision
floating point number, depending on the type of the constant, dictionary
member or optional argument it is being used as the value for,
determined as follows:

1.  Let `S` be the sequence of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
    id="ref-for-scalar-value④" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>
    matched by the [decimal](#prod-decimal) token.

2.  Let `result` be the Mathematical Value that would be obtained if `S`
    were parsed as a JavaScript
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-literals-numeric-literals"
    id="ref-for-sec-literals-numeric-literals"
    data-link-type="dfn">NumericLiteral</a>.

3.  If the [decimal](#prod-decimal) token is being used as the value for
    a
    <a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float" data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">float</code></a> or
    <a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>,
    then the value of the [decimal](#prod-decimal) token is the IEEE 754
    single-precision floating point number closest to `result`.

4.  Otherwise, the [decimal](#prod-decimal) token is being used as the
    value for a
    <a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double" data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">double</code></a> or
    <a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>,
    and the value of the [decimal](#prod-decimal) token is the IEEE 754
    double-precision floating point number closest to `result`.
    <a href="#biblio-ieee-754" data-link-type="biblio"
    title="IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic">[IEEE-754]</a>

</div>

The value of a constant value specified as Infinity, -Infinity, or NaN
is either an IEEE 754 single-precision floating point number or an IEEE
754 double-precision floating point number, depending on the type of the
constant, dictionary member, or optional argument it is being used as
the value for:

Type <a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>, constant value Infinity  
The value is the IEEE 754 single-precision positive infinity value.

Type <a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>, constant value Infinity  
The value is the IEEE 754 double-precision positive infinity value.

Type <a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>, constant value -Infinity  
The value is the IEEE 754 single-precision negative infinity value.

Type <a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>, constant value -Infinity  
The value is the IEEE 754 double-precision negative infinity value.

Type <a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>, constant value NaN  
The value is the IEEE 754 single-precision NaN value with the bit
pattern 0x7fc00000.

Type <a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>, constant value NaN  
The value is the IEEE 754 double-precision NaN value with the bit
pattern 0x7ff8000000000000.

The type of a [decimal](#prod-decimal) token is the same as the type of
the constant, dictionary member or optional argument it is being used as
the value of. The value of the [decimal](#prod-decimal) token must not
lie outside the valid range of values for its type, as given in [§ 2.13
Types](#idl-types). Also, Infinity, -Infinity and NaN must not be used
as the value of a
<a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">float</code></a> or
<a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a>.

The value of the null token is the special null value that is a member
of the <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable types</a>. The type of the null token is
the same as the type of the constant, dictionary member or optional
argument it is being used as the value of.

If `VT` is the type of the value assigned to a constant, and `DT` is the
type of the constant, dictionary member or optional argument itself,
then these types must be compatible, which is the case if `DT` and `VT`
are identical, or `DT` is a
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a> whose
<a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type"
data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> is `VT`.

<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①②"
data-link-type="dfn">Constants</a> are not associated with particular
instances of the <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface③⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> on which they appear. It is
language binding specific whether
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①③"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> are exposed on instances.

<div class="note" role="note">

The JavaScript language binding does however allow
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①④"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> to be accessed through objects
implementing the IDL
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> on which the
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> are declared. For example, with the
following IDL:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface A {
  const short rambaldi = 47;
};
```

the constant value can be accessed in JavaScript either as `A.rambaldi`
or `instanceOfA.rambaldi`.

</div>

The following extended attributes are applicable to constants:
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\], and
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\].

``` grammar
Const ::
    const ConstType identifier = ConstValue ;
```

``` grammar
ConstValue ::
    BooleanLiteral
    FloatLiteral
    integer
```

``` grammar
BooleanLiteral ::
    true
    false
```

``` grammar
FloatLiteral ::
    decimal
    -Infinity
    Infinity
    NaN
```

``` grammar
ConstType ::
    PrimitiveType
    identifier
```

<div id="example-221dba30" class="example">

<a href="#example-221dba30" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①③"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> demonstrates how
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> of the above types can be defined.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Util {
  const boolean DEBUG = false;
  const octet LF = 10;
  const unsigned long BIT_MASK = 0x0000fc00;
  const double AVOGADRO = 6.022e23;
};
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.2. </span><span class="content">Attributes</span><a href="#idl-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="dfn-attribute" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">attribute</span> is an
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a> or
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a> (matching inherit
[AttributeRest](#prod-AttributeRest), static
[OptionalReadOnly](#prod-OptionalReadOnly)
[AttributeRest](#prod-AttributeRest), stringifier
[OptionalReadOnly](#prod-OptionalReadOnly)
[AttributeRest](#prod-AttributeRest),
[OptionalReadOnly](#prod-OptionalReadOnly)
[AttributeRest](#prod-AttributeRest), or
[AttributeRest](#prod-AttributeRest)) that is used to declare data
fields with a given type and
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> whose value can be retrieved and (in
some cases) changed. There are two kinds of attributes:

1.  <a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute③"
    data-link-type="dfn">regular attributes</a>, which are those used to
    declare that objects implementing the
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④①"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> will have a data field member
    with the given
    <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>

    ``` highlight
    interface interface_identifier {
      attribute type identifier;
    };
    ```

2.  <a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute②"
    data-link-type="dfn">static attributes</a>, which are used to
    declare attributes that are not associated with a particular object
    implementing the interface

    ``` highlight
    interface interface_identifier {
      static attribute type identifier;
    };
    ```

If an attribute has no static keyword, then it declares a
<span id="dfn-regular-attribute" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">regular attribute</span>. Otherwise, it declares a
<a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute③"
data-link-type="dfn">static attribute</a>. Note that in addition to
being <a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface members</a>,
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only②"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute④"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attributes</a> can be
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member①"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace members</a> as well.

The <span id="getter-steps" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">getter steps</span> of an attribute `attr` should be
introduced using text of the form “The `attr` getter steps are:”
followed by a list, or “The `attr` getter steps are to” followed by an
inline description.

The <span id="setter-steps" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">setter steps</span> of an attribute `attr` should be
introduced using text of the form “The `attr` setter steps are:”
followed by a list, or “The `attr` setter steps are to” followed by an
inline description.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> When defining
<a href="#getter-steps" id="ref-for-getter-steps①"
data-link-type="dfn">getter steps</a>, you implicitly have access to
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>. When
defining <a href="#setter-steps" id="ref-for-setter-steps②"
data-link-type="dfn">setter steps</a>, you implicitly have access to
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①" data-link-type="dfn">this</a> and
<a href="#the-given-value" id="ref-for-the-given-value"
data-link-type="dfn">the given value</a>.
