The <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> must not be the same as the
identifier of another
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a> defined on the same
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>. The identifier of a static attribute
must not be "`prototype`".

The type of the attribute is given by the type (matching
[Type](#prod-Type)) that appears after the attribute keyword. If the
[Type](#prod-Type) is an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> or an identifier followed by ?, then
the identifier must identify an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration③"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a>.

The type of the attribute, after resolving typedefs, must not be a
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type②"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a> or non-nullable version of any of the
following types:

- a <a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type"
  data-link-type="dfn">sequence type</a>

- an <a href="#async-sequence-type" id="ref-for-async-sequence-type"
  data-link-type="dfn">async sequence type</a>

- a <a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary"
  data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a>

- a <a href="#record-type" id="ref-for-record-type"
  data-link-type="dfn">record type</a>

- a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type"
  data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> that has a nullable or
  non-nullable sequence type, dictionary, or record as one of its
  <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
  id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
  data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>

The attribute is <span id="dfn-read-only" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">read only</span> if the readonly keyword is
used before the attribute keyword. An object that implements the
interface on which a read only attribute is defined will not allow
assignment to that attribute. It is language binding specific whether
assignment is simply disallowed by the language, ignored or an exception
is thrown.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  readonly attribute type identifier;
};
```

Attributes whose type is a
<a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type"
data-link-type="dfn">promise type</a> must be
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only③"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>. Additionally, they cannot have any
of the
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a>
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\], or
\[<a href="#SameObject" id="ref-for-SameObject" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">SameObject</code></a>\].

A <a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a> that is not
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only④"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a> can be declared to
<span id="dfn-inherit-getter" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">inherit its getter</span> from an ancestor interface. This can
be used to make a read only attribute in an ancestor interface be
writable on a derived interface. An attribute
<a href="#dfn-inherit-getter" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit-getter"
data-link-type="dfn">inherits its getter</a> if its declaration includes
inherit in the declaration. The read only attribute from which the
attribute inherits its getter is the attribute with the same identifier
on the closest ancestor interface of the one on which the inheriting
attribute is defined. The attribute whose getter is being inherited must
be of the same type as the inheriting attribute.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> The grammar ensures that inherit does
not appear on a <a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a> attribute or a
<a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute④"
data-link-type="dfn">static attribute</a>.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Ancestor {
  readonly attribute TheType theIdentifier;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Derived : Ancestor {
  inherit attribute TheType theIdentifier;
};
```

When the stringifier keyword is used in a
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a> declaration, it indicates
that objects implementing the interface will be stringified to the value
of the attribute. See [§ 2.5.5 Stringifiers](#idl-stringifiers) for
details.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  stringifier attribute DOMString identifier;
};
```

The following
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> are applicable to regular
and static attributes:
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#SameObject" id="ref-for-SameObject①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SameObject</code></a>\], and
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\].

The following
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> are applicable only to
regular attributes:
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientThis" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientThis"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientThis</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyUnforgeable</code></a>\].

``` grammar
ReadOnlyMember ::
    readonly ReadOnlyMemberRest
```

``` grammar
ReadOnlyMemberRest ::
    AttributeRest
    MaplikeRest
    SetlikeRest
```

``` grammar
ReadWriteAttribute ::
    AttributeRest
```

``` grammar
InheritAttribute ::
    inherit AttributeRest
```

``` grammar
AttributeRest ::
    attribute TypeWithExtendedAttributes AttributeName ;
```

``` grammar
AttributeName ::
    AttributeNameKeyword
    identifier
```

``` grammar
AttributeNameKeyword ::
    required
```

``` grammar
OptionalReadOnly ::
    readonly
    ε
```

<div id="example-ca172334" class="example">

<a href="#example-ca172334" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①④"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> demonstrates how
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①①"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a> can be declared on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Animal {

  // A simple attribute that can be set to any string value.
  readonly attribute DOMString name;

  // An attribute whose value can be assigned to.
  attribute unsigned short age;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Person : Animal {

  // An attribute whose getter behavior is inherited from Animal, and need not be
  // specified in the description of Person.
  inherit attribute DOMString name;
};
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.3. </span><span class="content">Operations</span><a href="#idl-operations" class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="dfn-operation" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">operation</span> is an
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
<a href="#callback-interface-member"
id="ref-for-callback-interface-member①" data-link-type="dfn">callback
interface member</a> or
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member②"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a> (matching static
[RegularOperation](#prod-RegularOperation), stringifier,
[RegularOperation](#prod-RegularOperation) or
[SpecialOperation](#prod-SpecialOperation)) that defines a behavior that
can be invoked on objects implementing the interface. There are three
kinds of operation:

1.  <a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a>, which are those used to
    declare that objects implementing the
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> will have a method with the given
    <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②①"
    data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>

    ``` highlight
    interface interface_identifier {
      return_type identifier(/* arguments... */);
    };
    ```

2.  <a href="#dfn-special-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-special-operation③"
    data-link-type="dfn">special operations</a>, which are used to
    declare special behavior on objects implementing the interface, such
    as object indexing and stringification

    ``` highlight
    interface interface_identifier {
      /* special_keyword */ return_type identifier(/* arguments... */);
      /* special_keyword */ return_type (/* arguments... */);
    };
    ```

3.  <a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation②"
    data-link-type="dfn">static operations</a>, which are used to
    declare operations that are not associated with a particular object
    implementing the interface

    ``` highlight
    interface interface_identifier {
      static return_type identifier(/* arguments... */);
    };
    ```

If an operation has an identifier but no static keyword, then it
declares a <span id="dfn-regular-operation" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">regular operation</span>. If the operation has
a <a href="#dfn-special-keyword" id="ref-for-dfn-special-keyword"
data-link-type="dfn">special keyword</a> used in its declaration (that
is, any keyword matching [Special](#prod-Special), or the stringifier
keyword), then it declares a special operation. A single operation can
declare both a regular operation and a special operation; see [§ 2.5.6
Special operations](#idl-special-operations) for details on special
operations. Note that in addition to being
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface members</a>, regular operations can also
be <a href="#callback-interface-member"
id="ref-for-callback-interface-member②" data-link-type="dfn">callback
interface members</a> and
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member③"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace members</a>.

If an operation has no identifier, then it must be declared to be a
special operation using one of the special keywords.

The identifier of a
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a> or
<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation③"
data-link-type="dfn">static operation</a> must not be the same as the
identifier of a <a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a> or
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①②"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> defined on the same
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>. The identifier of a static operation
must not be "`prototype`".

<span class="marker">Note:</span> The identifier can be the same as that
of another operation on the interface, however. This is how operation
overloading is specified.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> The
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②②"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of a
<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation④"
data-link-type="dfn">static operation</a> can be the same as the
identifier of a
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a> defined on the same
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>.

The <span id="dfn-return-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">return type</span> of the operation is given by the type
(matching [Type](#prod-Type)) that appears before the operation’s
optional <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②③"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>. If the return type is an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②④"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> followed by ?, then the identifier
must identify an <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary</a>,
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration④"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a>.

An operation’s arguments (matching [ArgumentList](#prod-ArgumentList))
are given between the parentheses in the declaration. Each individual
argument is specified as a type (matching [Type](#prod-Type)) followed
by an <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> (matching
[ArgumentName](#prod-ArgumentName)).

<span class="marker">Note:</span> For expressiveness, the identifier of
an operation argument can also be specified as one of the keywords
matching the [ArgumentNameKeyword](#prod-ArgumentNameKeyword) symbol
without needing to escape it.

If the [Type](#prod-Type) of an operation argument is an identifier
followed by ?, then the identifier must identify an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface④⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a>. If the operation argument type is an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> not followed by ?, then the
identifier must identify any one of those definitions or a
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary</a>.

If the operation argument type, after resolving typedefs, is a
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type③"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a>, its
<a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type①"
data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> must not be a
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary①"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a>.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  return_type identifier(type identifier, type identifier /* , ... */);
};
```

The identifier of each argument must not be the same as the identifier
of another argument in the same operation declaration.

Each argument can be preceded by a list of
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> (matching
[ExtendedAttributeList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeList)), which can control
how a value passed as the argument will be handled in language bindings.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  return_type identifier([extended_attributes] type identifier, [extended_attributes] type identifier /* , ... */);
};
```

<div id="example-891877a9" class="example">

<a href="#example-891877a9" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> demonstrates how
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> can be declared on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Dimensions {
  attribute unsigned long width;
  attribute unsigned long height;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Button {

  // An operation that takes no arguments and returns a boolean.
  boolean isMouseOver();

  // Overloaded operations.
  undefined setDimensions(Dimensions size);
  undefined setDimensions(unsigned long width, unsigned long height);
};
```

</div>

An operation or
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> is considered to be
<span id="dfn-variadic" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">variadic</span> if the final argument uses the ... token just
after the argument type. Declaring an operation to be variadic indicates
that the operation can be invoked with any number of arguments after
that final argument. Those extra implied formal arguments are of the
same type as the final explicit argument in the operation declaration.
The final argument can also be omitted when invoking the operation. An
argument must not be declared with the ... token unless it is the final
argument in the operation’s argument list.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  return_type identifier(type... identifier);
  return_type identifier(type identifier, type... identifier);
};
```

<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①②"
data-link-type="dfn">Extended attributes</a> that
<a href="#dfn-xattr-argument-list" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-argument-list"
data-link-type="dfn">take an argument list</a>
(\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\],
of those defined in this specification) and
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">callback functions</a> are also considered to be
<a href="#dfn-variadic" id="ref-for-dfn-variadic"
data-link-type="dfn">variadic</a> when the ... token is used in their
argument lists.

<div id="example-c79ed320" class="example">

<a href="#example-c79ed320" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface that has two
variadic operations:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface IntegerSet {
  readonly attribute unsigned long cardinality;

  undefined union(long... ints);
  undefined intersection(long... ints);
};
```

In the JavaScript binding, variadic operations are implemented by
functions that can accept the subsequent arguments:

``` highlight
var s = getIntegerSet();  // Obtain an instance of IntegerSet.

s.union();                // Passing no arguments corresponding to 'ints'.
s.union(1, 4, 7);         // Passing three arguments corresponding to 'ints'.
```

A binding for a language that does not support variadic functions might
specify that an explicit array or list of integers be passed to such an
operation.

</div>

An argument is considered to be an <span id="dfn-optional-argument"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">optional
argument</span> if it is declared with the optional keyword. The final
argument of a <a href="#dfn-variadic" id="ref-for-dfn-variadic①"
data-link-type="dfn">variadic</a> operation is also considered to be an
optional argument. Declaring an argument to be optional indicates that
the argument value can be omitted when the operation is invoked. The
final argument in an operation must not explicitly be declared to be
optional if the operation is
<a href="#dfn-variadic" id="ref-for-dfn-variadic②"
data-link-type="dfn">variadic</a>.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  return_type identifier(type identifier, optional type identifier);
};
```

Optional arguments can also have a
<span id="dfn-optional-argument-default-value" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="optional argument" dfn-type="dfn" export="">default
value</span> specified. If the argument’s identifier is followed by a
U+003D (=) and a value (matching [DefaultValue](#prod-DefaultValue)),
then that gives the optional argument its
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value①"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a>. The implicitly optional final
argument of a <a href="#dfn-variadic" id="ref-for-dfn-variadic③"
data-link-type="dfn">variadic</a> operation must not have a default
value specified. The default value is the value to be assumed when the
operation is called with the corresponding argument omitted.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  return_type identifier(type identifier, optional type identifier = "value");
};
```

It is strongly suggested not to use a
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value②"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a> of true for
<a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a>-typed
arguments, as this can be confusing for authors who might otherwise
expect the default conversion of undefined to be used (i.e., false).
<a href="#biblio-api-design-principles" data-link-type="biblio"
title="Web Platform Design Principles">[API-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES]</a>

If the type of an argument is a
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary②"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a> or a
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> that has a
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary③"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a> as one of its
<a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types①"
data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>, and that dictionary
type and its ancestors have no <a href="#required-dictionary-member"
id="ref-for-required-dictionary-member"
data-link-type="dfn">required</a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member②"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a>, and the argument is either the final
argument or is followed only by
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a>, then the argument must be
specified as optional and have a default value provided.

<div class="note" role="note">

This is to encourage API designs that do not require authors to pass an
empty dictionary value when they wish only to use the dictionary’s
default values.

Usually the default value provided will be {}, but in the case of a
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> that has a dictionary type as one of
its <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types②"
data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a> a default value could be
provided that initializes some other member of the union.

</div>

When a boolean literal token (true or false), the null token, an
[integer](#prod-integer) token, a [decimal](#prod-decimal) token or one
of the three special floating point literal values (Infinity, -Infinity
or NaN) is used as the <a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value③"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a>, it is interpreted in the same
way as for a <a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a>.

When the undefined token is used as the
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value④"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a>, the value is the IDL
<a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a> value.

<div id="string-literal" class="algorithm"
algorithm="value of string literal tokens">

Optional argument default values can also be specified using a
[string](#prod-string) token, whose
<span id="value-of-string-literal-tokens" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" lt="value of string literal tokens"
noexport="">value</span> is a
<a href="#dfn-string-type" id="ref-for-dfn-string-type"
data-link-type="dfn">string type</a> determined as follows:

1.  Let `S` be the sequence of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
    id="ref-for-scalar-value⑤" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>
    matched by the [string](#prod-string) token with its leading and
    trailing U+0022 (")
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
    id="ref-for-scalar-value⑥" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>
    removed.

2.  Depending on the type of the argument:

    <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>  
    <a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a>  
    an <a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a> type  
    The value of the [string](#prod-string) token is `S`.

    <a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a>  
    Assert: `S` doesn’t contain any
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
    id="ref-for-code-point" data-link-type="dfn">code points</a> higher
    than U+00FF.

    The value of the [string](#prod-string) token is the
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#isomorphic-encode"
    id="ref-for-isomorphic-encode" data-link-type="dfn">isomorphic
    encoding</a> of `S`.

</div>

If the type of the
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①"
data-link-type="dfn">optional argument</a> is an
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>, then its
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a> if specified must be one of the
<a href="#dfn-enumeration-value" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration-value"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration’s values</a>.

Optional argument default values can also be specified using the two
token value \[\], which represents an empty sequence value. The type of
this value is the same as the type of the optional argument it is being
used as the default value of. That type must be a
<a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type①"
data-link-type="dfn">sequence type</a>, a
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type④"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a> whose
<a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type②"
data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> is a
<a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type②"
data-link-type="dfn">sequence type</a> or a
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type③"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> or
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a> union type that has a
<a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type③"
data-link-type="dfn">sequence type</a> in its
<a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types③"
data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>.

Optional argument default values can also be specified using the two
token value {}, which represents a default-initialized (as if from ES
null or an object with no properties) dictionary value. The type of this
value is the same as the type of the optional argument it is being used
as the default value of. That type must be a
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary④"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a>, or a
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type④"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> that has a
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a> in its
<a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types④"
data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>.

<div id="example-6c1a4d6e" class="example">

<a href="#example-6c1a4d6e" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with a single
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> that can be invoked with two
different argument list lengths:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface ColorCreator {
  object createColor(double v1, double v2, double v3, optional double alpha);
};
```

It is equivalent to an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that has two
<a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded"
data-link-type="dfn">overloaded</a>
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a>:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface ColorCreator {
  object createColor(double v1, double v2, double v3);
  object createColor(double v1, double v2, double v3, double alpha);
};
```

</div>

<div id="example-6acab27b" class="example">

<a href="#example-6acab27b" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with an operation that takes a
dictionary argument:

``` highlight
dictionary LookupOptions {
  boolean caseSensitive = false;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface AddressBook {
  boolean hasAddressForName(USVString name, optional LookupOptions options = {});
};
```

If `hasAddressForName` is called with only one argument, the second
argument will be a default-initialized `LookupOptions` dictionary, which
will cause `caseSensitive` to be set to false.

</div>

The following extended attributes are applicable to operations:
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Default" id="ref-for-Default" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Default</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyUnforgeable</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#NewObject" id="ref-for-NewObject" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">NewObject</code></a>\], and
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\].

The <span id="method-steps" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">method steps</span> of an operation `operation` should be
introduced using text of the form “The
`operation``(``arg1``, ``arg2``, ...)` method steps are:” followed by a
list, or “The `operation``(``arg1``, ``arg2``, ...)` method steps are
to” followed by an inline description.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> When defining
<a href="#method-steps" id="ref-for-method-steps①"
data-link-type="dfn">method steps</a>, you implicitly have access to
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this②" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>.

``` grammar
DefaultValue ::
    ConstValue
    string
    [ ]
    { }
    null
    undefined
```

``` grammar
Operation ::
    RegularOperation
    SpecialOperation
```

``` grammar
RegularOperation ::
    Type OperationRest
```

``` grammar
SpecialOperation ::
    Special RegularOperation
```

``` grammar
Special ::
    getter
    setter
    deleter
```

``` grammar
OperationRest ::
    OptionalOperationName ( ArgumentList ) ;
```

``` grammar
OptionalOperationName ::
    OperationName
    ε
```

``` grammar
OperationName ::
    OperationNameKeyword
    identifier
```

``` grammar
OperationNameKeyword ::
    includes
```

``` grammar
ArgumentList ::
    Argument Arguments
    ε
```

``` grammar
Arguments ::
    , Argument Arguments
    ε
```

``` grammar
Argument ::
    ExtendedAttributeList ArgumentRest
```

``` grammar
ArgumentRest ::
    optional TypeWithExtendedAttributes ArgumentName Default
    Type Ellipsis ArgumentName
```

``` grammar
ArgumentName ::
    ArgumentNameKeyword
    identifier
```

``` grammar
Ellipsis ::
    ...
    ε
```

<div>

``` grammar
ArgumentNameKeyword ::
    attribute
    callback
    const
    constructor
    deleter
    dictionary
    enum
    getter
    includes
    inherit
    interface
    iterable
    maplike
    mixin
    namespace
    partial
    readonly
    required
    setlike
    setter
    static
    stringifier
    typedef
    unrestricted
```

</div>

##### <span class="secno">2.5.3.1. </span><span class="content">toJSON</span><a href="#idl-tojson-operation" class="self-link"></a>

By declaring a `toJSON`
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a>, an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> specifies how to convert the objects
that implement it to
<a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types①"
data-link-type="dfn">JSON types</a>.

The `toJSON`
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①①"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a> is reserved for this usage.
It must take zero arguments and return a
<a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types②"
data-link-type="dfn">JSON type</a>.

The <span id="dfn-json-types" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="" lt="JSON type">JSON types</span> are:

- <a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type"
  data-link-type="dfn">numeric types</a>,

- <a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean②"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a>,

- <a href="#dfn-string-type" id="ref-for-dfn-string-type①"
  data-link-type="dfn">string types</a>,

- <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">nullable types</a> whose
  <a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type③"
  data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> is a
  <a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types③"
  data-link-type="dfn">JSON type</a>,

- <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types"
  data-link-type="dfn">annotated types</a> whose
  <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
  id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type" data-link-type="dfn">inner
  type</a> is a <a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types④"
  data-link-type="dfn">JSON type</a>,

- <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">union types</a> whose
  <a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type"
  data-link-type="dfn">member types</a> are
  <a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">JSON types</a>,

- <a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">typedefs</a> whose
  <a href="#type-being-given-a-new-name"
  id="ref-for-type-being-given-a-new-name" data-link-type="dfn">type being
  given a new name</a> is a
  <a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">JSON type</a>,

- <a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type④"
  data-link-type="dfn">sequence types</a> whose parameterized type is a
  <a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types⑦"
  data-link-type="dfn">JSON type</a>,

- <a href="#dfn-frozen-array-type" id="ref-for-dfn-frozen-array-type"
  data-link-type="dfn">frozen array types</a> whose parameterized type
  is a <a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">JSON type</a>,

- <a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">dictionary types</a> where the types of all
  <a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member③"
  data-link-type="dfn">members</a> declared on the dictionary and all
  its <a href="#dfn-inherited-dictionaries"
  id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-dictionaries" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
  dictionaries</a> are
  <a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">JSON types</a>,

- <a href="#idl-record" id="ref-for-idl-record"
  data-link-type="dfn">records</a> where all of their
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-getting-the-values"
  id="ref-for-map-getting-the-values" data-link-type="dfn">values</a>
  are <a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types①⓪"
  data-link-type="dfn">JSON types</a>,

- <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object" data-link-type="idl"><code
  class="idl">object</code></a>,

- <a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface types</a> that have a `toJSON`
  operation declared on themselves or one of their
  <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
  id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces②" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
  interfaces</a>.

How the `toJSON`
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①②"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a> is made available on an
object in a language binding, and how exactly the
<a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types①①"
data-link-type="dfn">JSON types</a> are converted into a JSON string, is
language binding specific.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> In the JavaScript language binding,
this is done by exposing a `toJSON` method which returns the
<a href="#dfn-json-types" id="ref-for-dfn-json-types①②"
data-link-type="dfn">JSON type</a> converted into a JavaScript value
that can be turned into a JSON string by the
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-json.stringify"
id="ref-for-sec-json.stringify" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">JSON.stringify()</code></a> function. Additionally, in the
JavaScript language binding, the `toJSON` operation can take a
\[<a href="#Default" id="ref-for-Default①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Default</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①③"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>, in which case the
<a href="#default-tojson-steps" id="ref-for-default-tojson-steps"
data-link-type="dfn">default toJSON steps</a> are exposed instead.

<div id="tojson-example" class="example">

<a href="#tojson-example" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface `Transaction`
that has a `toJSON` method defined in prose:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Transaction {
  readonly attribute DOMString from;
  readonly attribute DOMString to;
  readonly attribute double amount;
  readonly attribute DOMString description;
  readonly attribute unsigned long number;
  TransactionJSON toJSON();
};

dictionary TransactionJSON {
  Account from;
  Account to;
  double amount;
  DOMString description;
};
```

The `toJSON`
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①③"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a> of `Transaction`
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> could be defined as follows:

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="example tojson">

The `toJSON()` method steps are:

1.  Let `json` be a new
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="ref-for-ordered-map" data-link-type="dfn">map</a>.

2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="ref-for-list-iterate" data-link-type="dfn">For each</a>
    attribute <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> `attr` in « "from", "to",
    "amount", "description" »:

    1.  Let `value` be the result of running the
        <a href="#getter-steps" id="ref-for-getter-steps②"
        data-link-type="dfn">getter steps</a> of `attr` on
        <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this③" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>.

    2.  Set `json`\[`attr`\] to `value`.

3.  Return `json`.

</div>

In the JavaScript language binding, there would exist a `toJSON()`
method on `Transaction` objects:

``` highlight
// Get an instance of Transaction.
var txn = getTransaction();

// Evaluates to an object like this:
// {
//   from: "Bob",
//   to: "Alice",
//   amount: 50,
//   description: "books"
// }
txn.toJSON();

// Evaluates to a string like this:
// '{"from":"Bob","to":"Alice","amount":50,"description":"books"}'
JSON.stringify(txn);
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.4. </span><span id="Constructor" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Constructor operations</span><a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors②⑤"
class="self-link"></a>

If an <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> has a
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors②"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> member (matching
[Constructor](#prod-Constructor)), it indicates that it is possible to
create objects that <a href="#implements" id="ref-for-implements"
data-link-type="dfn">implement</a> the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> using a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#constructor"
id="ref-for-constructor①" data-link-type="dfn">constructor</a>.

Multiple <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors③"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operations</a> may appear on a given
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>. For each
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors④"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> on the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑤⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, there will be a way to attempt to
construct an instance by passing the specified arguments.

The <span id="constructor-steps" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">constructor steps</span> of a
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> that is a member of an
interface named `interface` should be introduced using text of the form
“The `new ``interface``(``arg1``, ``arg2``, ...)` constructor steps
are:” followed by a list, or “The
`new ``interface``(``arg1``, ``arg2``, ...)` constructor steps are to”
followed by an inline description.

The <a href="#constructor-steps" id="ref-for-constructor-steps①"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor steps</a> must do nothing, initialize
the value passed as
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this④" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>, or
throw an exception.

<a href="#example-constructor-steps" class="self-link"></a>If the
constructor does not initialize
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this⑤" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>, one
can write “The `new Example(``init``)` constructor steps are to do
nothing.”

See [§ 3.7.1 Interface object](#interface-object) for details on how a
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> is to be implemented.

<div id="example-94745458" class="example">

<a href="#example-94745458" class="self-link"></a>

The following IDL defines two interfaces. The second has
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operations</a>, while the first does
not.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface NodeList {
  Node item(unsigned long index);
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Circle {
  constructor();
  constructor(double radius);
  attribute double r;
  attribute double cx;
  attribute double cy;
  readonly attribute double circumference;
};
```

A JavaScript implementation supporting these interfaces would implement
a \[\[Construct\]\] internal method on the `Circle` interface object
which would return a new object that
<a href="#implements" id="ref-for-implements①"
data-link-type="dfn">implements</a> the interface. It would take either
zero or one argument.

It is unclear whether the `NodeList` interface object would implement a
\[\[Construct\]\] internal method. In any case, trying to use it as a
constructor will cause a
<a href="#exceptiondef-typeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-typeerror"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a> to be
thrown. [\[whatwg/webidl Issue
\#698\]](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/698)

``` highlight
var x = new Circle();      // This uses the zero-argument constructor to create a
                           // reference to a platform object that implements the
                           // Circle interface.

var y = new Circle(1.25);  // This also creates a Circle object, this time using
                           // the one-argument constructor.

var z = new NodeList();    // This would throw a TypeError, since no
                           // constructor is declared.
```

</div>

``` grammar
Constructor ::
    constructor ( ArgumentList ) ;
```

<div>

``` grammar
ArgumentList ::
    Argument Arguments
    ε
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
Arguments ::
    , Argument Arguments
    ε
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
Argument ::
    ExtendedAttributeList ArgumentRest
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
ArgumentRest ::
    optional TypeWithExtendedAttributes ArgumentName Default
    Type Ellipsis ArgumentName
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
ArgumentName ::
    ArgumentNameKeyword
    identifier
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
Ellipsis ::
    ...
    ε
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
ArgumentNameKeyword ::
    attribute
    callback
    const
    constructor
    deleter
    dictionary
    enum
    getter
    includes
    inherit
    interface
    iterable
    maplike
    mixin
    namespace
    partial
    readonly
    required
    setlike
    setter
    static
    stringifier
    typedef
    unrestricted
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.5. </span><span class="content">Stringifiers</span><a href="#idl-stringifiers" class="self-link"></a>

When an <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> has a <span id="dfn-stringifier"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">stringifier</span>,
it indicates that objects that implement the interface have a
non-default conversion to a string. Stringifiers can be specified using
a stringifier keyword, which creates a stringifier operation when used
alone.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  stringifier;
};
```

Prose accompanying the interface must define the
<span id="dfn-stringification-behavior" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">stringification behavior</span> of the
interface.

The stringifier keyword can also be placed on an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①③"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a>. In this case, the string to convert
the object to is the value of the attribute. The stringifier keyword
must not be placed on an attribute unless it is declared to be of type
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> or
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a>. It also
must not be placed on a
<a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">static attribute</a>.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  stringifier attribute DOMString identifier;
};
```

On a given <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, there must exist at most one
stringifier.

``` grammar
Stringifier ::
    stringifier StringifierRest
```

``` grammar
StringifierRest ::
    OptionalReadOnly AttributeRest
    ;
```

<div id="example-f23c7f2e" class="example">

<a href="#example-f23c7f2e" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface that will
stringify to the value of its `name` attribute:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Student {
  constructor();
  attribute unsigned long id;
  stringifier attribute DOMString name;
};
```

In the JavaScript binding, using a `Student` object in a context where a
string is expected will result in the value of the object’s `name`
property being used:

``` highlight
var s = new Student();
s.id = 12345678;
s.name = '周杰倫';

var greeting = 'Hello, ' + s + '!';  // Now greeting == 'Hello, 周杰倫!'.
```

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②①"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface that has
custom stringification behavior that is not specified in the IDL itself.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Student {
  constructor();
  attribute unsigned long id;
  attribute DOMString? familyName;
  attribute DOMString givenName;

  stringifier;
};
```

Thus, there needs to be prose to explain the stringification behavior.
We assume that the `familyName` and `givenName` attributes are backed by
family name and given name concepts, respectively.

> The <a href="#dfn-stringification-behavior"
> id="ref-for-dfn-stringification-behavior"
> data-link-type="dfn">stringification behavior</a> steps are:
>
> 1.  If
>     <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this⑥" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
>     family name is null, then return
>     <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this⑦" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
>     given name.
>
> 2.  Return the concatenation of
>     <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this⑧" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
>     given name, followed by U+0020 SPACE, followed by
>     <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this⑨" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
>     family name.

A JavaScript implementation of the IDL would behave as follows:

``` highlight
var s = new Student();
s.id = 12345679;
s.familyName = 'Smithee';
s.givenName = 'Alan';

var greeting = 'Hi ' + s;  // Now greeting == 'Hi Alan Smithee'.
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.6. </span><span class="content">Special operations</span><a href="#idl-special-operations" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-special-operation" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">special operation</span> is a declaration of a
certain kind of special behavior on objects implementing the interface
on which the special operation declarations appear. Special operations
are declared by using a <span id="dfn-special-keyword"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">special keyword</span>
in an operation declaration.

There are three kinds of special operations. The table below indicates
for a given kind of special operation what special keyword is used to
declare it and what the purpose of the special operation is:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
| Special operation | Keyword | Purpose |
| <span id="dfn-getter" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="getter">Getters</span> | getter | Defines behavior for when an object is indexed for property retrieval. |
| <span id="dfn-setter" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="setter">Setters</span> | setter | Defines behavior for when an object is indexed for property assignment or creation. |
| <span id="dfn-deleter" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="deleter">Deleters</span> | deleter | Defines behavior for when an object is indexed for property deletion. |

Not all language bindings support all of the four kinds of special
object behavior. When special operations are declared using operations
with no identifier, then in language bindings that do not support the
particular kind of special operations there simply will not be such
functionality.

<div id="example-a42afb64" class="example">

<a href="#example-a42afb64" class="self-link"></a>

The following IDL fragment defines an interface with a getter and a
setter:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Dictionary {
  readonly attribute unsigned long propertyCount;

  getter double (DOMString propertyName);
  setter undefined (DOMString propertyName, double propertyValue);
};
```

In language bindings that do not support property getters and setters,
objects implementing
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">Dictionary</a> will not have that special behavior.

</div>

Defining a special operation with an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> is equivalent to separating the
special operation out into its own declaration without an identifier.
This approach is allowed to simplify
<a href="#method-steps" id="ref-for-method-steps②"
data-link-type="dfn">method steps</a> of an interface’s operations.

<div id="example-50d7ab88" class="example">

<a href="#example-50d7ab88" class="self-link"></a>

The following two interfaces are equivalent:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Dictionary {
  readonly attribute unsigned long propertyCount;

  getter double getProperty(DOMString propertyName);
  setter undefined setProperty(DOMString propertyName, double propertyValue);
};
```

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Dictionary {
  readonly attribute unsigned long propertyCount;

  double getProperty(DOMString propertyName);
  undefined setProperty(DOMString propertyName, double propertyValue);

  getter double (DOMString propertyName);
  setter undefined (DOMString propertyName, double propertyValue);
};
```

</div>

A given <a href="#dfn-special-keyword" id="ref-for-dfn-special-keyword①"
data-link-type="dfn">special keyword</a> must not appear twice on an
operation.

Getters and setters come in two varieties: ones that take a
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> as a
property name, known as <span id="dfn-named-property-getter"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export=""
lt="named property getter">named property getters</span> and
<span id="dfn-named-property-setter" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="named property setter">named property
setters</span>, and ones that take an
<a href="#idl-unsigned-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long</code></a> as a
property index, known as <span id="dfn-indexed-property-getter"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export=""
lt="indexed property getter">indexed property getters</span> and
<span id="dfn-indexed-property-setter" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="indexed property setter">indexed property
setters</span>. There is only one variety of deleter:
<span id="dfn-named-property-deleter" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="named property deleter">named property
deleters</span>. See <a href="#idl-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-idl-indexed-properties">§ 2.5.6.1 Indexed properties</a> and
<a href="#idl-named-properties"
id="ref-for-idl-named-properties">§ 2.5.6.2 Named properties</a> for
details.

On a given <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, there must exist at most one
<a href="#dfn-named-property-deleter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-deleter" data-link-type="dfn">named
property deleter</a>, and at most one of each variety of getter and
setter.

If an interface has a setter of a given variety, then it must also have
a getter of that variety. If it has a
<a href="#dfn-named-property-deleter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-deleter①" data-link-type="dfn">named
property deleter</a>, then it must also have a
<a href="#dfn-named-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-getter" data-link-type="dfn">named
property getter</a>.

Special operations declared using operations must not be
<a href="#dfn-variadic" id="ref-for-dfn-variadic④"
data-link-type="dfn">variadic</a> nor have any
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument②"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a>.

If an object implements more than one
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that defines a given special
operation, then it is undefined which (if any) special operation is
invoked for that operation.

##### <span class="secno">2.5.6.1. </span><span class="content">Indexed properties</span><a href="#idl-indexed-properties" id="ref-for-idl-indexed-properties②"
class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that defines an
<a href="#dfn-indexed-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-getter" data-link-type="dfn">indexed
property getter</a> is said to <span id="dfn-support-indexed-properties"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">support indexed
properties</span>. By extension, a
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> is said to
<a href="#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-indexed-properties" data-link-type="dfn">support
indexed properties</a> if it implements an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that itself does.

If an interface <a href="#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-indexed-properties①"
data-link-type="dfn">supports indexed properties</a>, then the interface
definition must be accompanied by a description of what indices the
object can be indexed with at any given time. These indices are called
the <span id="dfn-supported-property-indices" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">supported property indices</span>.

Interfaces that <a href="#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-indexed-properties②"
data-link-type="dfn">support indexed properties</a> must define an
<a href="#dfn-integer-type" id="ref-for-dfn-integer-type"
data-link-type="dfn">integer-typed</a>
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①④"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> named "`length`".

Indexed property getters must be declared to take a single
<a href="#idl-unsigned-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long</code></a>
argument. Indexed property setters must be declared to take two
arguments, where the first is an
<a href="#idl-unsigned-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long</code></a>.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  getter type identifier(unsigned long identifier);
  setter type identifier(unsigned long identifier, type identifier);

  getter type (unsigned long identifier);
  setter type (unsigned long identifier, type identifier);
};
```

The following requirements apply to the definitions of indexed property
getters and setters:

- If an <a href="#dfn-indexed-property-getter"
  id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-getter①" data-link-type="dfn">indexed
  property getter</a> was specified using an
  <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> with an
  <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier②⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>, then the value returned when
  indexing the object with a given
  <a href="#dfn-supported-property-indices"
  id="ref-for-dfn-supported-property-indices"
  data-link-type="dfn">supported property index</a> is the value that
  would be returned by invoking the operation, passing the index as its
  only argument. If the operation used to declare the indexed property
  getter did not have an identifier, then the interface definition must
  be accompanied by a description of how to
  <span id="dfn-determine-the-value-of-an-indexed-property"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">determine the value
  of an indexed property</span> for a given index.

- If an <a href="#dfn-indexed-property-setter"
  id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-setter" data-link-type="dfn">indexed
  property setter</a> was specified using an operation with an
  identifier, then the behavior that occurs when indexing the object for
  property assignment with a given supported property index and value is
  the same as if the operation is invoked, passing the index as the
  first argument and the value as the second argument. If the operation
  used to declare the indexed property setter did not have an
  identifier, then the interface definition must be accompanied by a
  description of how to
  <span id="dfn-set-the-value-of-an-existing-indexed-property"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">set the value of an
  existing indexed property</span> and how to
  <span id="dfn-set-the-value-of-a-new-indexed-property"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">set the value of a
  new indexed property</span> for a given property index and value.

<div class="note" role="note">

Note that if an <a href="#dfn-indexed-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-getter②" data-link-type="dfn">indexed
property getter</a> or <a href="#dfn-indexed-property-setter"
id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-setter①"
data-link-type="dfn">setter</a> is specified using an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> with an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>, then indexing an object with an
integer that is not a <a href="#dfn-supported-property-indices"
id="ref-for-dfn-supported-property-indices①"
data-link-type="dfn">supported property index</a> does not necessarily
elicit the same behavior as invoking the operation with that index. The
actual behavior in this case is language binding specific.

In the JavaScript language binding, a regular property lookup is done.
For example, take the following IDL:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface A {
  getter DOMString toWord(unsigned long index);
};
```

Assume that an object implementing `A` has
<a href="#dfn-supported-property-indices"
id="ref-for-dfn-supported-property-indices②"
data-link-type="dfn">supported property indices</a> in the range 0 ≤
`index` \< 2. Also assume that toWord is defined to return its argument
converted into an English word. The behavior when invoking the
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①①"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> with an out of range index is
different from indexing the object directly:

``` highlight
var a = getA();

a.toWord(0);  // Evalautes to "zero".
a[0];         // Also evaluates to "zero".

a.toWord(5);  // Evaluates to "five".
a[5];         // Evaluates to undefined, since there is no property "5".
```

</div>

<div id="example-5c76d88c" class="example">

<a href="#example-5c76d88c" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②②"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface `OrderedMap`
which allows retrieving and setting values by name or by index number:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface OrderedMap {
  readonly attribute unsigned long size;

  getter any getByIndex(unsigned long index);
  setter undefined setByIndex(unsigned long index, any value);

  getter any get(DOMString name);
  setter undefined set(DOMString name, any value);
};
```

Since all of the special operations are declared using operations with
identifiers, the only additional prose that is necessary is that which
describes what keys those sets have. Assuming that the `get()` operation
is defined to return null if an attempt is made to look up a
non-existing entry in the `OrderedMap`, then the following two sentences
would suffice:

> An object `map` implementing `OrderedMap` supports indexed properties
> with indices in the range 0 ≤ `index` \< `map.size`.
>
> Such objects also support a named property for every name that, if
> passed to `get()`, would return a non-null value.

As described in [§ 3.9 Legacy platform
objects](#js-legacy-platform-objects), a JavaScript implementation would
create properties on a <a href="#dfn-legacy-platform-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-legacy-platform-object" data-link-type="dfn">legacy
platform object</a> implementing `OrderedMap` that correspond to entries
in both the named and indexed property sets. These properties can then
be used to interact with the object in the same way as invoking the
object’s methods, as demonstrated below:

``` highlight
// Assume map is a legacy platform object implementing the OrderedMap interface.
var map = getOrderedMap();
var x, y;

x = map[0];       // If map.length > 0, then this is equivalent to:
                  //
                  //   x = map.getByIndex(0)
                  //
                  // since a property named "0" will have been placed on map.
                  // Otherwise, x will be set to undefined, since there will be
                  // no property named "0" on map.

map[1] = false;   // This will do the equivalent of:
                  //
                  //   map.setByIndex(1, false)

y = map.apple;    // If there exists a named property named "apple", then this
                  // will be equivalent to:
                  //
                  //   y = map.get('apple')
                  //
                  // since a property named "apple" will have been placed on
                  // map.  Otherwise, y will be set to undefined, since there
                  // will be no property named "apple" on map.

map.berry = 123;  // This will do the equivalent of:
                  //
                  //   map.set('berry', 123)

delete map.cake;  // If a named property named "cake" exists, then the "cake"
                  // property will be deleted, and then the equivalent to the
                  // following will be performed:
                  //
                  //   map.remove("cake")
```

</div>

##### <span class="secno">2.5.6.2. </span><span class="content">Named properties</span><a href="#idl-named-properties" id="ref-for-idl-named-properties③"
class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that defines a
<a href="#dfn-named-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-getter①" data-link-type="dfn">named
property getter</a> is said to <span id="dfn-support-named-properties"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">support named
properties</span>. By extension, a
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object①"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> is said to
<a href="#dfn-support-named-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-named-properties" data-link-type="dfn">support
named properties</a> if it implements an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that itself does.

If an interface <a href="#dfn-support-named-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-named-properties①" data-link-type="dfn">supports
named properties</a>, then the interface definition must be accompanied
by a description of the ordered set of names that can be used to index
the object at any given time. These names are called the
<span id="dfn-supported-property-names" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">supported property names</span>.

Named property getters and deleters must be declared to take a single
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> argument.
Named property setters must be declared to take two arguments, where the
first is a <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  getter type identifier(DOMString identifier);
  setter type identifier(DOMString identifier, type identifier);
  deleter type identifier(DOMString identifier);

  getter type (DOMString identifier);
  setter type (DOMString identifier, type identifier);
  deleter type (DOMString identifier);
};
```

The following requirements apply to the definitions of named property
getters, setters and deleters:

- If a <a href="#dfn-named-property-getter"
  id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-getter②" data-link-type="dfn">named
  property getter</a> was specified using an
  <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①②"
  data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> with an
  <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③①"
  data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>, then the value returned when
  indexing the object with a given
  <a href="#dfn-supported-property-names"
  id="ref-for-dfn-supported-property-names" data-link-type="dfn">supported
  property name</a> is the value that would be returned by invoking the
  operation, passing the name as its only argument. If the operation
  used to declare the named property getter did not have an identifier,
  then the interface definition must be accompanied by a description of
  how to <span id="dfn-determine-the-value-of-a-named-property"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">determine the value
  of a named property</span> for a given property name.

- If a <a href="#dfn-named-property-setter"
  id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-setter" data-link-type="dfn">named
  property setter</a> was specified using an operation with an
  identifier, then the behavior that occurs when indexing the object for
  property assignment with a given supported property name and value is
  the same as if the operation is invoked, passing the name as the first
  argument and the value as the second argument. If the operation used
  to declare the named property setter did not have an identifier, then
  the interface definition must be accompanied by a description of how
  to <span id="dfn-set-the-value-of-an-existing-named-property"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">set the value of an
  existing named property</span> and how to
  <span id="dfn-set-the-value-of-a-new-named-property"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">set the value of a
  new named property</span> for a given property name and value.

- If a <a href="#dfn-named-property-deleter"
  id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-deleter②" data-link-type="dfn">named
  property deleter</a> was specified using an operation with an
  identifier, then the behavior that occurs when indexing the object for
  property deletion with a given supported property name is the same as
  if the operation is invoked, passing the name as the only argument. If
  the operation used to declare the named property deleter did not have
  an identifier, then the interface definition must be accompanied by a
  description of how to <span id="dfn-delete-an-existing-named-property"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">delete an existing
  named property</span> for a given property name.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> As with
<a href="#idl-indexed-properties" id="ref-for-idl-indexed-properties③"
data-link-type="dfn">indexed properties</a>, if an
<a href="#dfn-named-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-getter③" data-link-type="dfn">named
property getter</a>, <a href="#dfn-named-property-setter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-setter①" data-link-type="dfn">setter</a>
or <a href="#dfn-named-property-deleter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-deleter③"
data-link-type="dfn">deleter</a> is specified using an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①③"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> with an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③②"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>, then indexing an object with a name
that is not a <a href="#dfn-supported-property-names"
id="ref-for-dfn-supported-property-names①"
data-link-type="dfn">supported property name</a> does not necessarily
elicit the same behavior as invoking the operation with that name; the
behavior is language binding specific.

#### <span class="secno">2.5.7. </span><span class="content">Static attributes and operations</span><a href="#idl-static-attributes-and-operations" class="self-link"></a>

<span id="dfn-static-attribute" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">Static attributes</span> and <span id="dfn-static-operation"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">static
operations</span> are ones that are not associated with a particular
instance of the <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> on which it is declared, and is
instead associated with the interface itself. Static attributes and
operations are declared by using the static keyword in their
declarations.

It is language binding specific whether it is possible to invoke a
static operation or get or set a static attribute through a reference to
an instance of the interface.

``` grammar
StaticMember ::
    static StaticMemberRest
```

``` grammar
StaticMemberRest ::
    OptionalReadOnly AttributeRest
    RegularOperation
```

<div id="example-639bc49b" class="example">

<a href="#example-639bc49b" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②③"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface `Circle` that
has a static operation declared on it:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Point { /* ... */ };

[Exposed=Window]
interface Circle {
  attribute double cx;
  attribute double cy;
  attribute double radius;

  static readonly attribute long triangulationCount;
  static Point triangulate(Circle c1, Circle c2, Circle c3);
};
```

In the JavaScript language binding, the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object①" data-link-type="dfn">function object</a>
for `triangulate` and the accessor property for `triangulationCount`
will exist on the
<a href="#dfn-interface-object" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-object①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface object</a> for `Circle`:

``` highlight
var circles = getCircles();           // an Array of Circle objects

typeof Circle.triangulate;            // Evaluates to "function"
typeof Circle.triangulationCount;     // Evaluates to "number"
Circle.prototype.triangulate;         // Evaluates to undefined
Circle.prototype.triangulationCount;  // Also evaluates to undefined
circles[0].triangulate;               // As does this
circles[0].triangulationCount;        // And this

// Call the static operation
var triangulationPoint = Circle.triangulate(circles[0], circles[1], circles[2]);

// Find out how many triangulations we have done
window.alert(Circle.triangulationCount);
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.8. </span><span class="content">Overloading</span><a href="#idl-overloading" class="self-link"></a>

If a
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①④"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a> or
<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">static operation</a> defined on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑥⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> has an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③③"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> that is the same as the identifier
of another operation on that interface of the same kind (regular or
static), then the operation is said to be <span id="dfn-overloaded"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">overloaded</span>. When
the identifier of an overloaded operation is used to invoke one of the
operations on an object that implements the interface, the number and
types of the arguments passed to the operation determine which of the
overloaded operations is actually invoked.
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">Constructor operations</a> can be overloaded too.
There are some restrictions on the arguments that overloaded operations
and constructors can be specified to take, and in order to describe
these restrictions, the notion of an *effective overload set* is used.

A set of overloaded
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①④"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> must either:

- contain no <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> whose
  <a href="#dfn-return-type" id="ref-for-dfn-return-type"
  data-link-type="dfn">return type</a> is a
  <a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type①"
  data-link-type="dfn">promise type</a>;

- only contain <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> whose
  <a href="#dfn-return-type" id="ref-for-dfn-return-type①"
  data-link-type="dfn">return type</a> is a
  <a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type②"
  data-link-type="dfn">promise type</a>.

<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">Operations</a> must not be overloaded across
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>, and
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface mixin</a> definitions.

<div class="note" role="note">

For example, the overloads for both `f` and `g` are disallowed:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface A {
  undefined f();
};

partial interface A {
  undefined f(double x);
  undefined g();
};

partial interface A {
  undefined g(DOMString x);
};
```

Note that <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operations</a> and
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①④"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> are disallowed from
appearing on
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a> definitions, so there is no
need to also disallow overloading for constructors.

</div>

An <span id="dfn-effective-overload-set" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">effective overload set</span> represents the
allowable invocations for a particular
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>, constructor (specified with a
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> or
