\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]),
or <a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>. The algorithm to
<a href="#compute-the-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-compute-the-effective-overload-set"
data-link-type="dfn">compute the effective overload set</a> operates on
one of the following four types of IDL constructs, and listed with them
below are the inputs to the algorithm needed to compute the set.

For regular operations  
For static operations  
- the <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦①"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> on which the
  <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation①⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> are to be found

- the <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③④"
  data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of the operations

- the number of arguments to be passed

For constructors  
- the <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦②"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> on which the
  <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①①"
  data-link-type="dfn">constructor operations</a> are to be found

- the number of arguments to be passed

For legacy factory functions  
- the <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦③"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> on which the
  \[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction④"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
  <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> are to be found

- the <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of the legacy factory function

- the number of arguments to be passed

An <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a> is used, among other things, to determine whether there
are ambiguities in the overloaded operations and constructors specified
on an interface.

The <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-item"
id="ref-for-list-item" data-link-type="dfn">items</a> of an
<a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set①" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a> are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple" id="ref-for-tuple"
data-link-type="dfn">tuples</a> of the form
(<a href="#effective-overload-set-tuple-callable"
id="ref-for-effective-overload-set-tuple-callable"
data-link-type="dfn">callable</a>,
<a href="#type-list" id="ref-for-type-list" data-link-type="dfn">type
list</a>, <a href="#optionality-list" id="ref-for-optionality-list"
data-link-type="dfn">optionality list</a>) whose
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="ref-for-struct-item" data-link-type="dfn">items</a> are described
below:

- A <span id="effective-overload-set-tuple-callable"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="effective overload set tuple"
  dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">callable</span> is an
  <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②⓪"
  data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> if the
  <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
  id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set②" data-link-type="dfn">effective
  overload set</a> is for
  <a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a>,
  <a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">static operations</a>, or
  <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①②"
  data-link-type="dfn">constructor operations</a>; and it is an
  <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> if the
  <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
  id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set③" data-link-type="dfn">effective
  overload set</a> is for <a href="#dfn-legacy-factory-function"
  id="ref-for-dfn-legacy-factory-function" data-link-type="dfn">legacy
  factory functions</a>.

- A <span id="type-list" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
  noexport="">type list</span> is a
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list①"
  data-link-type="dfn">list</a> of IDL types.

- An <span id="optionality-list" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
  noexport="">optionality list</span> is a
  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list②"
  data-link-type="dfn">list</a> of three possible
  <span id="dfn-optionality-value" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
  dfn-type="dfn" export="">optionality values</span> – "required",
  "optional" or "variadic" – indicating whether the argument at a given
  index was declared as being
  <a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument③"
  data-link-type="dfn">optional</a> or corresponds to a
  <a href="#dfn-variadic" id="ref-for-dfn-variadic⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">variadic</a> argument.

Each <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple" id="ref-for-tuple①"
data-link-type="dfn">tuple</a> represents an allowable invocation of the
operation, constructor, or callback function with an argument value list
of the given types. Due to the use of
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument④"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a> and
<a href="#dfn-variadic" id="ref-for-dfn-variadic⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">variadic</a> operations and constructors, there may
be multiple items in an <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set④" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a> identifying the same operation or constructor.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="compute the effective overload set">

The algorithm below describes how to
<span id="compute-the-effective-overload-set" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">compute the effective overload set</span>.
The following input variables are used, if they are required:

- the identifier of the operation or legacy factory function is `A`

- the argument count is `N`

- the interface is `I`

Whenever an argument of an extended attribute is mentioned, it is
referring to an argument of the extended attribute’s
<a href="#dfn-xattr-named-argument-list"
id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-named-argument-list" data-link-type="dfn">named
argument list</a>.

1.  Let `S` be an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
    id="ref-for-ordered-set" data-link-type="dfn">ordered set</a>.

2.  Let `F` be an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
    id="ref-for-ordered-set①" data-link-type="dfn">ordered set</a> with
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-item"
    id="ref-for-list-item①" data-link-type="dfn">items</a> as follows,
    according to the kind of <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
    id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set⑤" data-link-type="dfn">effective
    overload set</a>:

    For regular operations  
    The elements of `F` are the
    <a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> with identifier `A`
    defined on interface `I`.

    For static operations  
    The elements of `F` are the
    <a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">static operations</a> with identifier `A`
    defined on interface `I`.

    For constructors  
    The elements of `F` are the
    <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①③"
    data-link-type="dfn">constructor operations</a> on interface `I`.

    For legacy factory functions  
    The elements of `F` are the
    \[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction⑤"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
    <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> on interface `I` whose
    <a href="#dfn-xattr-named-argument-list"
    id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-named-argument-list①" data-link-type="dfn">named
    argument lists'</a> identifiers are `A`.

3.  Let `maxarg` be the maximum number of arguments the operations,
    legacy factory functions, or callback functions in `F` are declared
    to take. For <a href="#dfn-variadic" id="ref-for-dfn-variadic⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">variadic</a> operations and legacy factory
    functions, the argument on which the ellipsis appears counts as a
    single argument.

    <span class="marker">Note:</span> So
    `undefined f(long x, long... y);` is considered to be declared to
    take two arguments.

4.  Let `max` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#eqn-max" id="ref-for-eqn-max"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">max</a>(`maxarg`, `N`).

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
    id="ref-for-list-iterate①" data-link-type="dfn">For each</a>
    operation or extended attribute `X` in `F`:

    1.  Let `arguments` be the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list③"
        data-link-type="dfn">list</a> of arguments `X` is declared to
        take.

    2.  Let `n` be the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
        id="ref-for-list-size" data-link-type="dfn">size</a> of
        `arguments`.

    3.  Let `types` be a
        <a href="#type-list" id="ref-for-type-list①" data-link-type="dfn">type
        list</a>.

    4.  Let `optionalityValues` be an
        <a href="#optionality-list" id="ref-for-optionality-list①"
        data-link-type="dfn">optionality list</a>.

    5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
        id="ref-for-list-iterate②" data-link-type="dfn">For each</a>
        `argument` in `arguments`:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
            id="ref-for-list-append①" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
            the type of `argument` to `types`.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
            id="ref-for-list-append②" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
            "variadic" to `optionalityValues` if `argument` is a final,
            variadic argument, "optional" if `argument` is
            <a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument⑤"
            data-link-type="dfn">optional</a>, and "required" otherwise.

    6.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
        id="ref-for-set-append" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a> the
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple" id="ref-for-tuple②"
        data-link-type="dfn">tuple</a> (`X`, `types`,
        `optionalityValues`) to `S`.

    7.  If `X` is declared to be
        <a href="#dfn-variadic" id="ref-for-dfn-variadic⑧"
        data-link-type="dfn">variadic</a>, then:

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
            id="ref-for-list-iterate③" data-link-type="dfn">For each</a>
            `i` in <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#the-range"
            id="ref-for-the-range" data-link-type="dfn">the range</a>
            `n` to `max` − 1, inclusive:

            1.  Let `t` be a
                <a href="#type-list" id="ref-for-type-list②" data-link-type="dfn">type
                list</a>.

            2.  Let `o` be an
                <a href="#optionality-list" id="ref-for-optionality-list②"
                data-link-type="dfn">optionality list</a>.

            3.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
                id="ref-for-list-iterate④" data-link-type="dfn">For each</a>
                `j` in
                <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#the-range"
                id="ref-for-the-range①" data-link-type="dfn">the range</a>
                0 to `n` − 1, inclusive:

                1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                    id="ref-for-list-append③" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
                    `types`\[`j`\] to `t`.

                2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                    id="ref-for-list-append④" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
                    `optionalityValues`\[`j`\] to `o`.

            4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
                id="ref-for-list-iterate⑤" data-link-type="dfn">For each</a>
                `j` in
                <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#the-range"
                id="ref-for-the-range②" data-link-type="dfn">the range</a>
                `n` to `i`, inclusive:

                1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                    id="ref-for-list-append⑤" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
                    `types`\[`n` − 1\] to `t`.

                2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                    id="ref-for-list-append⑥" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
                    "variadic" to `o`.

            5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
                id="ref-for-set-append①" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
                the
                <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple" id="ref-for-tuple③"
                data-link-type="dfn">tuple</a> (`X`, `t`, `o`) to `S`.

    8.  Let `i` be `n` − 1.

    9.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-while"
        id="ref-for-iteration-while" data-link-type="dfn">While</a> `i`
        ≥ 0:

        1.  If `arguments`\[`i`\] is not
            <a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument⑥"
            data-link-type="dfn">optional</a> (i.e., it is not marked as
            "optional" and is not a final, variadic argument), then
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-break"
            id="ref-for-iteration-break" data-link-type="dfn">break</a>.

        2.  Let `t` be a
            <a href="#type-list" id="ref-for-type-list③" data-link-type="dfn">type
            list</a>.

        3.  Let `o` be an
            <a href="#optionality-list" id="ref-for-optionality-list③"
            data-link-type="dfn">optionality list</a>.

        4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate"
            id="ref-for-list-iterate⑥" data-link-type="dfn">For each</a>
            `j` in <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#the-range"
            id="ref-for-the-range③" data-link-type="dfn">the range</a> 0
            to `i` − 1, inclusive:

            1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                id="ref-for-list-append⑦" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
                `types`\[`j`\] to `t`.

            2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
                id="ref-for-list-append⑧" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
                `optionalityValues`\[`j`\] to `o`.

        5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
            id="ref-for-set-append②" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a> the
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple" id="ref-for-tuple④"
            data-link-type="dfn">tuple</a> (`X`, `t`, `o`) to `S`.

            <span class="marker">Note:</span> if `i` is 0, this means to
            add to `S` the tuple (`X`, « », « »); (where "« »"
            represents an
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-is-empty"
            id="ref-for-list-is-empty" data-link-type="dfn">empty list</a>).

        6.  Set `i` to `i` − 1.

6.  Return `S`.

</div>

<div id="example-95a1dcae" class="example">

<a href="#example-95a1dcae" class="self-link"></a>

For the following interface:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface A {
  /* f1 */ undefined f(DOMString a);
  /* f2 */ undefined f(Node a, DOMString b, double... c);
  /* f3 */ undefined f();
  /* f4 */ undefined f(Event a, DOMString b, optional DOMString c, double... d);
};
```

assuming `Node` and `Event` are two other interfaces of which no object
can implement both, the <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set⑥" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a> for
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> with identifier `f` and
argument count 4 is:

``` set
«
  (f1, « DOMString »,                           « required »),
  (f2, « Node, DOMString »,                     « required, required »),
  (f2, « Node, DOMString, double »,             « required, required, variadic »),
  (f2, « Node, DOMString, double, double »,     « required, required, variadic, variadic »),
  (f3, « »,                                     « »),
  (f4, « Event, DOMString »,                    « required, required »),
  (f4, « Event, DOMString, DOMString »,         « required, required, optional »),
  (f4, « Event, DOMString, DOMString, double », « required, required, optional, variadic »)
»
```

</div>

Two types are <span id="dfn-distinguishable" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">distinguishable</span> if the following
algorithm returns *true*.

1.  If one type <a href="#dfn-includes-a-nullable-type"
    id="ref-for-dfn-includes-a-nullable-type" data-link-type="dfn">includes
    a nullable type</a> and the other type either
    <a href="#dfn-includes-a-nullable-type"
    id="ref-for-dfn-includes-a-nullable-type①" data-link-type="dfn">includes
    a nullable type</a>, is a
    <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> with
    <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
    id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a> including a
    <a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a>, or is a
    <a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a>, return *false*.

    <div id="example-distinguishability-nullable" class="example">

    <a href="#example-distinguishability-nullable" class="self-link"></a>
    None of the following pairs are distinguishable:
    - <a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double②"
      data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a>`?` and
      `Dictionary1`
    - `(Interface1 or `<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long" data-link-type="idl"><code
      class="idl">long</code></a>`)?` and
      `(Interface2 or `<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString⑤"
      data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>`)?`
    - `(Interface1 or `<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long①" data-link-type="idl"><code
      class="idl">long</code></a>`?)` and
      `(Interface2 or `<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString⑥"
      data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>`)?`
    - `(Interface1 or `<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long②" data-link-type="idl"><code
      class="idl">long</code></a>`?)` and
      `(Interface2 or `<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString⑦"
      data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>`?)`
    - `(Dictionary1 or `<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long③" data-link-type="idl"><code
      class="idl">long</code></a>`)` and
      `(Interface2 or `<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString⑧"
      data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>`)?`
    - `(Dictionary1 or `<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long④" data-link-type="idl"><code
      class="idl">long</code></a>`)` and
      `(Interface2 or `<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString⑨"
      data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>`?)`

    </div>

2.  If both types are either a
    <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> or
    <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a>
    <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>, return *true* if each member
    type of the one is distinguishable with each member type of the
    other, or *false* otherwise.

3.  If one type is a
    <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> or nullable union type, return
    *true* if each
    <a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type①"
    data-link-type="dfn">member type</a> of the union type is
    distinguishable with the non-union type, or *false* otherwise.

4.  Consider the two "innermost" types derived by taking each type’s
    <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
    id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type①" data-link-type="dfn">inner
    type</a> if it is an
    <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types①"
    data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a>, and then taking its
    <a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type④"
    data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> inner type if the result is a
    <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a>. If these two innermost types
    appear or are in categories appearing in the following table and
    there is a “●” mark in the corresponding entry or there is a letter
    in the corresponding entry and the designated additional requirement
    below the table is satisfied, then return *true*. Otherwise return
    *false*.

    Categories:

    interface-like  
    - <a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface①"
      data-link-type="dfn">interface types</a>

    - <a href="#dfn-buffer-source-type" id="ref-for-dfn-buffer-source-type"
      data-link-type="dfn">buffer source types</a>

    dictionary-like  
    - <a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary⑨"
      data-link-type="dfn">dictionary types</a>

    - <a href="#record-type" id="ref-for-record-type①"
      data-link-type="dfn">record types</a>

    - <a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface"
      data-link-type="dfn">callback interface types</a>

    sequence-like  
    - <a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type⑤"
      data-link-type="dfn">sequence types</a>

    - <a href="#dfn-frozen-array-type" id="ref-for-dfn-frozen-array-type①"
      data-link-type="dfn">frozen array types</a>

    <table id="distinguishable-table" class="complex data matrix"
    style="width:100%;">
    <colgroup>
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    <col style="width: 7%" />
    </colgroup>
    <thead>
    <tr>
    <th class="corner"></th>
    <th><div>
    <span>undefined</span>
    </div></th>
    <th><div>
    <span>boolean</span>
    </div></th>
    <th><div>
    <span>numeric types</span>
    </div></th>
    <th><div>
    <span>bigint</span>
    </div></th>
    <th><div>
    <span>string types</span>
    </div></th>
    <th><div>
    <span>object</span>
    </div></th>

    1.  The two identified interface-like types are not the same, and no
        single
        <a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object②"
        data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> implements both
        interface-like types.

    2.  The types are distinguishable, but there is [a separate
        restriction on their use in
        overloading](#limit-bigint-numeric-overloading) below. Please
        also note [the advice about using unions of these
        types](#limit-bigint-numeric-unions).

    3.  A
        <a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①②"
        data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> that does not have
        \[<a href="#LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull"
        id="ref-for-LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull</code></a>\] extended
        attribute is distinguishable from a type in the dictionary-like
        category.

        <div class="note" role="note">

        For example, when converting an ECMAScript value to
        <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①⓪"
        data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> which includes a
        <a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①③"
        data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> and a dictionary-like
        type, if the value is
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-iscallable"
        id="ref-for-sec-iscallable" data-link-type="dfn">callable</a>,
        then it is converted to a
        <a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①④"
        data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>. Otherwise, it is
        converted to a dictionary-like type.

        </div>

    4.  The types are distinguishable, but when converting from an
        ECMAScript value, a
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-string-objects"
        id="ref-for-sec-string-objects" data-link-type="dfn">string object</a>
        is never converted to an
        <a href="#async-sequence-type" id="ref-for-async-sequence-type①"
        data-link-type="dfn">async sequence type</a> (even if it has a
        <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
        id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">%Symbol.iterator%</code></a> method), if a
        <a href="#dfn-string-type" id="ref-for-dfn-string-type②"
        data-link-type="dfn">string type</a> is also in the overload set
        or union.

    <div id="example-distinguishability-diff-types" class="example">

    <a href="#example-distinguishability-diff-types" class="self-link"></a>
    <a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double③"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> and
    <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①⓪"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> are
    distinguishable because there is a ● at the intersection of
    <a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type①"
    data-link-type="dfn">numeric types</a> with
    <a href="#dfn-string-type" id="ref-for-dfn-string-type③"
    data-link-type="dfn">string types</a>.

    </div>

    <div id="example-distinguishability-same-category" class="example">

    <a href="#example-distinguishability-same-category"
    class="self-link"></a>
    <a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double④"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> and
    <a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">long</code></a> are not distinguishable because they are
    both <a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type②"
    data-link-type="dfn">numeric types</a>, and there is no ● or letter
    at the intersection of
    <a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type③"
    data-link-type="dfn">numeric types</a> with
    <a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type④"
    data-link-type="dfn">numeric types</a>.

    </div>

    <div id="example-distinguishability-callback-interfaces"
    class="example">

    <a href="#example-distinguishability-callback-interfaces"
    class="self-link"></a> Given:
    ``` highlight
    callback interface CBIface {
        undefined handle();
    };

    [Exposed=Window]
    interface Iface {
        attribute DOMString attr2;
    };

    dictionary Dict {
        DOMString field1;
    };
    ```

    `CBIface` is distinguishable from `Iface` because there’s a ● at the
    intersection of dictionary-like and interface-like, but it is not
    distinguishable from `Dict` because there’s no ● at the intersection
    of dictionary-like and itself.

    </div>

    <div id="example-distinguishability-promises" class="example">

    <a href="#example-distinguishability-promises" class="self-link"></a>
    <a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type③"
    data-link-type="dfn">Promise types</a> do not appear in the above
    table, and as a consequence are not distinguishable with any other
    type.

    </div>

If there is more than one
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-item"
id="ref-for-list-item②" data-link-type="dfn">item</a> in an
<a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set⑦" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a> that has a given
<a href="#type-list" id="ref-for-type-list④" data-link-type="dfn">type
list</a> <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
id="ref-for-list-size①" data-link-type="dfn">size</a>, then for those
items there must be an index `i` such that for each pair of items the
types at index `i` are
<a href="#dfn-distinguishable" id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishable"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishable</a>. The lowest such index is
termed the <span id="dfn-distinguishing-argument-index"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">distinguishing argument
index</span> for the items of the <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set⑧" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a> with the given type list size.

An <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set⑨" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a> must not contain more than one
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-item"
id="ref-for-list-item③" data-link-type="dfn">item</a> with the same
<a href="#type-list" id="ref-for-type-list⑤" data-link-type="dfn">type
list</a> <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
id="ref-for-list-size②" data-link-type="dfn">size</a>, where one
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-item"
id="ref-for-list-item④" data-link-type="dfn">item</a> has a
<a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">bigint</code></a> argument at the
<a href="#dfn-distinguishing-argument-index"
id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishing-argument-index"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishing argument index</a> and another has a
<a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">numeric type</a> argument at the
<a href="#dfn-distinguishing-argument-index"
id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishing-argument-index①"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishing argument index</a>.

<div id="example-cfba37ec" class="example">

<a href="#example-cfba37ec" class="self-link"></a>

Consider the <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set①⓪" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a> shown in the previous example. There are multiple items
in the set with type lists 2, 3 and 4. For each of these type list size,
the <a href="#dfn-distinguishing-argument-index"
id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishing-argument-index②"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishing argument index</a> is 0, since
`Node` and `Event` are
<a href="#dfn-distinguishable" id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishable①"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishable</a>.

The following use of overloading however is invalid:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface B {
  undefined f(DOMString x);
  undefined f(USVString x);
};
```

since <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> and
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a> are not
distinguishable.

</div>

In addition, for each index `j`, where `j` is less than the
<a href="#dfn-distinguishing-argument-index"
id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishing-argument-index③"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishing argument index</a> for a given type
list size, the types at index `j` in all of the items' type lists must
be the same, and the
<a href="#dfn-optionality-value" id="ref-for-dfn-optionality-value"
data-link-type="dfn">optionality values</a> at index `j` in all of the
items' optionality lists must be the same.

<div id="example-dab6ca0a" class="example">

<a href="#example-dab6ca0a" class="self-link"></a>

The following is invalid:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface B {
  /* f1 */ undefined f(DOMString w);
  /* f2 */ undefined f(long w, double x, Node y, Node z);
  /* f3 */ undefined f(double w, double x, DOMString y, Node z);
};
```

For argument count 4, the <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set①①" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a> is:

``` set
«
  (f1, « DOMString »,                       « required »),
  (f2, « long, double, Node, Node »,        « required, required, required, required »),
  (f3, « double, double, DOMString, Node », « required, required, required, required »)
»
```

Looking at items with type list size 4, the
<a href="#dfn-distinguishing-argument-index"
id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishing-argument-index④"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishing argument index</a> is 2, since
`Node` and <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> are
<a href="#dfn-distinguishable" id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishable②"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishable</a>. However, since the arguments
in these two overloads at index 0 are different, the overloading is
invalid.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">2.5.8.1. </span><span class="content">Overloading vs. union types</span><a href="#idl-overloading-vs-union" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is informative.*

<div class="non-normative">

For specifications defining IDL
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②①"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a>, it might seem that
<a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded①"
data-link-type="dfn">overloads</a> and a combination of
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①①"
data-link-type="dfn">union types</a> and
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a> have some feature overlap.

It is first important to note that
<a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded②"
data-link-type="dfn">overloads</a> have different behaviors than
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①②"
data-link-type="dfn">union types</a> or
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a>, and one *cannot* be fully
defined using the other (unless, of course, additional prose is
provided, which can defeat the purpose of the Web IDL type system). For
example, consider the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-stroke"
id="ref-for-dom-context-2d-stroke" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">stroke()</code></a> operations defined on the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasdrawpath"
id="ref-for-canvasdrawpath" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">CanvasDrawPath</code></a> interface
<a href="#biblio-html" data-link-type="biblio"
title="HTML Standard">[HTML]</a>:

``` highlight
interface CanvasDrawPathExcerpt {
  undefined stroke();
  undefined stroke(Path2D path);
};
```

Per the JavaScript language binding, calling `stroke(undefined)` on an
object implementing `CanvasDrawPathExcerpt` would attempt to call the
second overload, yielding a
<a href="#exceptiondef-typeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-typeerror①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a> since
undefined cannot be [converted](#js-to-interface) to a
<a href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#path2d"
id="ref-for-path2d" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Path2D</code></a>. However, if the operations were instead
defined with
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a> and merged into one,

``` highlight
interface CanvasDrawPathExcerptOptional {
  undefined stroke(optional Path2D path);
};
```

the <a href="#dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm"
id="ref-for-dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm"
data-link-type="dfn">overload resolution algorithm</a> would treat the
`path` argument as missing given the same call `stroke(undefined)`, and
not throw any exceptions.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> For this particular example, the
latter behavior is actually what Web developers would generally expect.
If <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#canvasdrawpath"
id="ref-for-canvasdrawpath①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">CanvasDrawPath</code></a> were to be designed today,
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a> would be used for
`stroke()`.

Additionally, there are semantic differences as well.
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①③"
data-link-type="dfn">Union types</a> are usually used in the sense that
"any of the types would work in about the same way". In contrast,
<a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded③"
data-link-type="dfn">overloaded</a> operations are designed to map well
to language features such as C++ overloading, and are usually a better
fit for operations with more substantial differences in what they do
given arguments of different types. However, in most cases, operations
with such substantial differences are best off with different names to
avoid confusion for Web developers, since the JavaScript language does
not provide language-level overloading. As such, overloads are rarely
appropriate for new APIs, instead often appearing in legacy APIs or in
specialized circumstances.

That being said, we offer the following recommendations and examples in
case of difficulties to determine what Web IDL language feature to use:

- In the unusual case where the operation needs to return values of
  different types for different argument types,
  <a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded④"
  data-link-type="dfn">overloading</a> will result in more expressive
  IDL fragments. <span class="note">This is almost never appropriate API
  design, and separate operations with distinct names usually are a
  better choice for such cases.</span>

  Suppose there is an operation `calculate()` that accepts a
  <a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
  class="idl">long</code></a>,
  <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①③"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>, or
  `CalculatableInterface` (an
  <a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface②"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a>) as its only argument, and
  returns a value of the same type as its argument. It would be clearer
  to write the IDL fragment using
  <a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">overloaded</a> operations as

  ``` highlight
  interface A {
    long calculate(long input);
    DOMString calculate(DOMString input);
    CalculatableInterface calculate(CalculatableInterface input);
  };
  ```

  than using a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①④"
  data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> with a
  <a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef①⓪"
  data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a> as

  ``` highlight
  typedef (long or DOMString or CalculatableInterface) Calculatable;
  interface A {
    Calculatable calculate(Calculatable input);
  };
  ```

  which does not convey the fact that the return value is always of the
  same type as `input`.

  If the specified `calculate()` is a new API and does not have any
  compatibility concerns, it is suggested to use different names for the
  overloaded operations, perhaps as

  ``` highlight
  interface A {
    long calculateNumber(long input);
    DOMString calculateString(DOMString input);
    CalculatableInterface calculateCalculatableInterface(CalculatableInterface input);
  };
  ```

  which allows Web developers to write explicit and unambiguous code.

- When the operation has significantly different semantics for different
  argument types or lengths,
  <a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">overloading</a> is preferred. Again, in such
  scenarios, it is usually better to create separate operations with
  distinct names, but legacy APIs sometimes follow this pattern.

  As an example, the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-conditional-3/#dom-css-supports"
  id="ref-for-dom-css-supports" data-link-type="idl"><code
  class="idl">supports(property, value)</code></a> and <a
  href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-conditional-3/#dom-css-supports-conditiontext"
  id="ref-for-dom-css-supports-conditiontext" data-link-type="idl"><code
  class="idl">supports(conditionText)</code></a> operations of the
  <a href="https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-1/#namespacedef-css"
  id="ref-for-namespacedef-css" data-link-type="idl"><code
  class="idl">CSS</code></a> interface are defined as the following IDL
  fragment <a href="#biblio-css3-conditional" data-link-type="biblio"
  title="CSS Conditional Rules Module Level 3">[CSS3-CONDITIONAL]</a>
  <a href="#biblio-cssom" data-link-type="biblio"
  title="CSS Object Model (CSSOM)">[CSSOM]</a>.

  ``` highlight
  partial interface CSS {
    static boolean supports(CSSOMString property, CSSOMString value);
    static boolean supports(CSSOMString conditionText);
  };
  ```

  Using
  <a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①①"
  data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a> one can rewrite the IDL
  fragment as follows:

  ``` highlight
  partial interface CSSExcerptOptional {
    static boolean supports(CSSOMString propertyOrConditionText, optional CSSOMString value);
  };
  ```

  Even though the IDL is shorter in the second version, two
  distinctively different concepts are conflated in the first argument.
  Without <a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded⑦"
  data-link-type="dfn">overloads</a>, the question "is `property` or
  `conditionText` paired with `value`?" is much more difficult to answer
  without reading the <a href="#method-steps" id="ref-for-method-steps③"
  data-link-type="dfn">method steps</a> of the operation. This makes the
  second version remarkably less readable than the first.

  Another consideration is that the
  <a href="#method-steps" id="ref-for-method-steps④"
  data-link-type="dfn">method steps</a> for
  <a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">overloaded</a> operations can be specified in
  separate blocks, which can aid in both reading and writing
  specifications. This is not the case for
  <a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①②"
  data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a>. This means that in the
  first case the specification author can write the
  <a href="#method-steps" id="ref-for-method-steps⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">method steps</a> of the operations as:

  <div class="algorithm" algorithm="execute supports() with overloads">

  The `supports(``property``, ``value``)` method steps are:

  1.  …

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The `supports(``conditionText``)` method steps are:

  1.  …

  </div>

  Yet using `value` as an
  <a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①③"
  data-link-type="dfn">optional argument</a>, the specification author
  has to use more boilerplate-style text to effectively replicate the
  <a href="#dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm"
  id="ref-for-dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm①"
  data-link-type="dfn">overload resolution algorithm</a>.

  <div class="algorithm"
  algorithm="execute supports() with optional argument">

  The `supports(``propertyOrConditionText``, ``value``)` method steps
  are:

  1.  If `value` is given, then:

      1.  Let `property` be `propertyOrConditionText`.

      2.  …

  2.  Otherwise:

      1.  Let `conditionText` be `propertyOrConditionText`.

      2.  …

  </div>

  If the two overloads have little to no shared parts, it is better to
  leave overload resolution to the IDL mechanism.

- If the operation accepts multiple types for multiple arguments with no
  coupling between types of different arguments,
  <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">union types</a> can sometimes be the only viable
  solution.

  ``` highlight
  typedef (long long or DOMString or CalculatableInterface) SupportedArgument;
  interface A {
    undefined add(SupportedArgument operand1, SupportedArgument operand2);
  };
  ```

  For the `add()` operation above, to specify it using
  <a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">overloads</a> would require

  ``` highlight
  interface A {
    undefined add(long long operand1, long long operand2);
    undefined add(long long operand1, DOMString operand2);
    undefined add(long long operand1, CalculatableInterface operand2);
    undefined add(DOMString operand1, long long operand2);
    undefined add(DOMString operand1, DOMString operand2);
    undefined add(DOMString operand1, CalculatableInterface operand2);
    undefined add(CalculatableInterface operand1, long long operand2);
    undefined add(CalculatableInterface operand1, DOMString operand2);
    undefined add(CalculatableInterface operand1, CalculatableInterface operand2);
  };
  ```

  and nine times the corresponding prose!

- Specification authors are encouraged to treat missing argument and
  undefined argument the same way in the JavaScript language binding.

  Given the following IDL fragment:

  ``` highlight
  interface A {
    undefined foo();
    undefined foo(Node? arg);
  };
  ```

  Using the JavaScript language binding, calling `foo(undefined)` and
  `foo(null)` would both run the steps corresponding to the
  `foo(``arg``)` operation, with `arg` set to null, while `foo()` alone
  would go to the first overload. This can be a surprising behavior for
  many API users. Instead, specification authors are encouraged to use
  an
  <a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①④"
  data-link-type="dfn">optional argument</a>, which would categorize
  both `foo()` and `foo(undefined)` as "`arg` is missing".

  ``` highlight
  interface A {
    undefined foo(optional Node? arg);
  };
  ```

  In general, optionality is best expressed using the optional keyword,
  and not using overloads.

When the case fits none of the categories above, it is up to the
specification author to choose the style, since it is most likely that
either style would sufficiently and conveniently describe the intended
behavior. However, the definition and [conversion
algorithms](#js-to-union) of
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">union types</a> and
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a> are simpler to implement and
reason about than <a href="#dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm"
id="ref-for-dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm②"
data-link-type="dfn">those</a> of
<a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">overloads</a>, and usually result in more idiomatic
APIs in the JavaScript language binding. Thus, unless any other
considerations apply,
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">union types</a>,
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a>, or both are the default
choice.

Specifications are also free to mix and match union types and overloads,
if the author finds it appropriate and convenient.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.5.9. </span><span class="content">Iterable declarations</span><a href="#idl-iterable" class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> can be declared to be
<span id="dfn-iterable" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">iterable</span> by using an
<span id="dfn-iterable-declaration" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">iterable declaration</span> (matching
[Iterable](#prod-Iterable)) in the body of the interface.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  iterable<value_type>;
  iterable<key_type, value_type>;
};
```

Objects implementing an interface that is declared to be iterable
support being iterated over to obtain a sequence of values.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> In the JavaScript language binding, an
interface that is iterable will have `entries`, `forEach`, `keys`,
`values`, and <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.iterator%</code></a> properties on its
<a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype object</a>.

If a single type parameter is given, then the interface has a
<span id="dfn-value-iterator" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">value iterator</span> and provides values of the specified
type. If two type parameters are given, then the interface has a
<span id="dfn-pair-iterator" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">pair iterator</span> and provides
<a href="#value-pair" id="ref-for-value-pair" data-link-type="dfn">value
pairs</a> with the given types.

A <span id="value-pair" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
noexport="">value pair</span>, given a key type and a value type, is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct" id="ref-for-struct"
data-link-type="dfn">struct</a> with two
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
id="ref-for-struct-item①" data-link-type="dfn">items</a>:

1.  an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
    id="ref-for-struct-item②" data-link-type="dfn">item</a> whose
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-name"
    id="ref-for-struct-name" data-link-type="dfn">name</a> is "key",
    which is referred to as the
    <a href="#value-pair" id="ref-for-value-pair①"
    data-link-type="dfn">value pair</a>’s <span id="value-pair-key"
    class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="value pair" dfn-type="dfn"
    noexport="">key</span>, and whose value is an IDL value of the key
    type;

2.  an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-item"
    id="ref-for-struct-item③" data-link-type="dfn">item</a> whose
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#struct-name"
    id="ref-for-struct-name①" data-link-type="dfn">name</a> is "value",
    which is referred to as the
    <a href="#value-pair" id="ref-for-value-pair②"
    data-link-type="dfn">value pair</a>’s <span id="value-pair-value"
    class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="value pair" dfn-type="dfn"
    noexport="">value</span>, and whose value is an IDL value of the
    value type.

A <a href="#dfn-value-iterator" id="ref-for-dfn-value-iterator"
data-link-type="dfn">value iterator</a> must only be declared on an
interface that <a href="#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-indexed-properties③"
data-link-type="dfn">supports indexed properties</a>. The value-type of
the <a href="#dfn-value-iterator" id="ref-for-dfn-value-iterator①"
data-link-type="dfn">value iterator</a> must be the same as the type
returned by the <a href="#dfn-indexed-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-getter③" data-link-type="dfn">indexed
property getter</a>. A
<a href="#dfn-value-iterator" id="ref-for-dfn-value-iterator②"
data-link-type="dfn">value iterator</a> is implicitly defined to iterate
over the object’s indexed properties.

A <a href="#dfn-pair-iterator" id="ref-for-dfn-pair-iterator"
data-link-type="dfn">pair iterator</a> must not be declared on an
interface that <a href="#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-indexed-properties④"
data-link-type="dfn">supports indexed properties</a>.

Prose accompanying an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with a
<a href="#dfn-pair-iterator" id="ref-for-dfn-pair-iterator①"
data-link-type="dfn">pair iterator</a> must define a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list④"
data-link-type="dfn">list</a> of
<a href="#value-pair" id="ref-for-value-pair③"
data-link-type="dfn">value pairs</a> for each instance of the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, which is the list of
<span id="dfn-value-pairs-to-iterate-over" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">value pairs to iterate over</span>.

<div class="note" role="note">

The JavaScript forEach method that is generated for a
<a href="#dfn-value-iterator" id="ref-for-dfn-value-iterator③"
data-link-type="dfn">value iterator</a> invokes its callback like
Array.prototype.forEach does, and the forEach method for a
<a href="#dfn-pair-iterator" id="ref-for-dfn-pair-iterator②"
data-link-type="dfn">pair iterator</a> invokes its callback like
Map.prototype.forEach does.

Since <a href="#dfn-value-iterator" id="ref-for-dfn-value-iterator④"
data-link-type="dfn">value iterators</a> are currently allowed only on
interfaces that <a href="#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-indexed-properties⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">support indexed properties</a>, it makes sense to
use an Array-like forEach method. There could be a need for
<a href="#dfn-value-iterator" id="ref-for-dfn-value-iterator⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">value iterators</a> (a) on interfaces that do not
<a href="#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-indexed-properties⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">support indexed properties</a>, or (b) with a
forEach method that instead invokes its callback like
Set.prototype.forEach (where the key is the same as the value). If
you’re creating an API that needs such a forEach method, please [file an
issue](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/new?title=Enhancement%20request%20for%20Iterables).

</div>

<span class="marker">Note:</span> This is how
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-array-iterator-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-array-iterator-objects" data-link-type="dfn">array
iterator objects</a> work. For interfaces that
<a href="#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-indexed-properties⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">support indexed properties</a>, the iterator
objects returned by `entries`, `keys`, `values`, and <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.iterator%</code></a> are actual
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-array-iterator-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-array-iterator-objects①" data-link-type="dfn">array
iterator objects</a>.

<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">Interfaces</a> with an
<a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration②" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declaration</a> must not have any
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> named "`entries`",
"`forEach`", "`keys`", or "`values`", or have any
<a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces③" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> that have
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> with these names.

<div id="example-d2254660" class="example">

<a href="#example-d2254660" class="self-link"></a>

Consider the following interface `SessionManager`, which allows access
to a number of `Session` objects keyed by username:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface SessionManager {
  Session getSessionForUser(DOMString username);

  iterable<DOMString, Session>;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Session {
  readonly attribute DOMString username;
  // ...
};
```

The behavior of the iterator could be defined like so:

> The <a href="#dfn-value-pairs-to-iterate-over"
> id="ref-for-dfn-value-pairs-to-iterate-over" data-link-type="dfn">value
> pairs to iterate over</a> are the list of
> <a href="#value-pair" id="ref-for-value-pair④"
> data-link-type="dfn">value pairs</a> with the
> <a href="#value-pair-key" id="ref-for-value-pair-key"
> data-link-type="dfn">key</a> being the username and the
> <a href="#value-pair-value" id="ref-for-value-pair-value"
> data-link-type="dfn">value</a> being the open `Session` object on the
> `SessionManager` object corresponding to that username, sorted by
> username.

In the JavaScript language binding, the
<a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype object</a> for the
`SessionManager` <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> has a `values` method that is a
function, which, when invoked, returns an iterator object that itself
has a `next` method that returns the next value to be iterated over. It
has `keys` and `entries` methods that iterate over the usernames of
session objects and username/`Session` object pairs, respectively. It
also has a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.iterator%</code></a> method that allows a
`SessionManager` to be used in a `for..of` loop that has the same value
as the `entries` method:

``` highlight
// Get an instance of SessionManager.
// Assume that it has sessions for two users, "anna" and "brian".
var sm = getSessionManager();

typeof SessionManager.prototype.values;            // Evaluates to "function"
var it = sm.values();                              // values() returns an iterator object
String(it);                                        // Evaluates to "[object SessionManager Iterator]"
typeof it.next;                                    // Evaluates to "function"

// This loop will log "anna" and then "brian".
for (;;) {
  let result = it.next();
  if (result.done) {
    break;
  }
  let session = result.value;
  console.log(session.username);
}

// This loop will also log "anna" and then "brian".
for (let username of sm.keys()) {
  console.log(username);
}

// Yet another way of accomplishing the same.
for (let [username, session] of sm) {
  console.log(username);
}
```

</div>

An interface must not have more than one
<a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration③" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declaration</a>. The <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces④" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> of an interface with an
<a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration④" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declaration</a> must not also have an
<a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration⑤" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declaration</a>. An interface with an
<a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration⑥" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declaration</a> and its <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces⑤" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> must not have a
<a href="#dfn-maplike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-maplike-declaration②"
data-link-type="dfn">maplike declaration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-setlike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-setlike-declaration②"
data-link-type="dfn">setlike declaration</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration②"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a>.

The following extended attributes are applicable to
<a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration⑦" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declarations</a>:
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\], and
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\].

``` grammar
Iterable ::
    iterable < TypeWithExtendedAttributes OptionalType > ;
```

``` grammar
OptionalType ::
    , TypeWithExtendedAttributes
    ε
```

#### <span class="secno">2.5.10. </span><span id="idl-async-iterable" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Asynchronously iterable declarations</span><a href="#idl-async-iterable-declaration" class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑦⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> can be declared to be asynchronously
iterable by using an <span id="dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export=""
lt="asynchronously iterable declaration|async_iterable">asynchronously
iterable declaration</span> (matching
[AsyncIterable](#prod-AsyncIterable)) in the body of the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  async_iterable<value_type>;
  async_iterable<value_type>(/* arguments... */);
  async_iterable<key_type, value_type>;
  async_iterable<key_type, value_type>(/* arguments... */);
};
```

Objects that <a href="#implements" id="ref-for-implements②"
data-link-type="dfn">implement</a> an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that is declared to be asynchronously
iterable support being iterated over asynchronously to obtain a sequence
of values.

If a single type parameter is given, then the interface has a
<span id="value-asynchronously-iterable-declaration"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">value asynchronously
iterable declaration</span> and asynchronously provides values of the
specified type. If two type parameters are given, then the interface has
a <span id="pair-asynchronously-iterable-declaration"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">pair asynchronously
iterable declaration</span> and asynchronously provides
<a href="#value-pair" id="ref-for-value-pair⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">value pairs</a> with the given types.

If given, an <a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration③"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a>’s arguments
(matching [ArgumentList](#prod-ArgumentList)) must all be
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">optional arguments</a>.

<div class="note" role="note">

In the JavaScript language binding, an interface that is asynchronously
iterable will have <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.asyncIterator%</code></a> and `values` properties on
its <a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype object</a>. If the interface
has a <a href="#pair-asynchronously-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-pair-asynchronously-iterable-declaration"
data-link-type="dfn">pair asynchronously iterable declaration</a>, it
will additionally have `entries` and `keys` properties. All of these
methods can be passed optional arguments, which correspond to the
argument list in the <a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration④"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a>, and are
processed by the <a href="#asynchronous-iterator-initialization-steps"
id="ref-for-asynchronous-iterator-initialization-steps"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronous iterator initialization steps</a>, if
any exist.

With this in mind, the requirement that all arguments be optional
ensures that, in the JavaScript binding, `for`-`await`-`of` can work
directly on instances of the interface, since `for`-`await`-`of` calls
the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.asyncIterator%</code></a> method with no arguments.

</div>

Prose accompanying an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with an
<a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a> must define
a <span id="dfn-get-the-next-iteration-result" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">get the next iteration result</span> algorithm.
This algorithm receives the instance of the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that is being iterated, as well as
the async iterator itself (which can be useful for storing state). It
must return a <a href="#idl-promise" id="ref-for-idl-promise"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Promise</code></a> that either
rejects, resolves with a special <span id="end-of-iteration"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export=""
lt="end of iteration">end of iteration</span> value to signal the end of
the iteration, or resolves with one of the following:

for <a href="#value-asynchronously-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-value-asynchronously-iterable-declaration"
data-link-type="dfn">value asynchronously iterable declarations</a>:  
a value of the type given in the declaration;

for <a href="#pair-asynchronously-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-pair-asynchronously-iterable-declaration①"
data-link-type="dfn">pair asynchronously iterable declarations</a>:  
a <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tuple" id="ref-for-tuple⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">tuple</a> containing a value of the first type
given in the declaration, and a value of the second type given in the
declaration.

The prose may also define an <span id="asynchronous-iterator-return"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">asynchronous iterator
return</span> algorithm. This algorithm receives the instance of the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that is being iterated, the async
iterator itself, and a single argument value of type
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a>. This algorithm is invoked in the case of
premature termination of the async iterator. It must return a
<a href="#idl-promise" id="ref-for-idl-promise①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Promise</code></a>; if that
promise fulfills, its fulfillment value will be ignored, but if it
rejects, that failure will be passed on to users of the async iterator
API.

In the JavaScript binding, this algorithm allows customizing the
behavior when the async iterator’s `return()` method is invoked. This
most commonly occurs when a `break` or `return` statement causes an exit
from a `for`-`await`-`of` loop.

We could add a similar hook for `throw()`. So far there has been no
need, but if you are creating an API that needs such capabilities,
please [file an
issue](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/new?title=Enhancement%20request%20for%20Async%20Iterables).

The prose may also define
<span id="asynchronous-iterator-initialization-steps"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">asynchronous iterator
initialization steps</span>. These receive the instance of the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> being iterated, the newly-created
iterator object, and a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">list</a> of IDL values representing the arguments
passed, if any.

<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">Interfaces</a> with an
<a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a> must not
have any <a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②①"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> named "`entries`", "`keys`",
or "`values`", or have any <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces⑥" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> that have
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②②"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②①"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> with these names.

<div id="example-69bd6dcd" class="example">

<a href="#example-69bd6dcd" class="self-link"></a>

Consider the following interface `SessionManager`, which allows access
to a number of `Session` objects keyed by username:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface SessionManager {
  Session getSessionForUser(DOMString username);

  async_iterable<DOMString, Session>;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Session {
  readonly attribute DOMString username;
  // ...
};
```

The behavior of the iterator could be defined like so:

> The <a href="#asynchronous-iterator-initialization-steps"
> id="ref-for-asynchronous-iterator-initialization-steps①"
> data-link-type="dfn">asynchronous iterator initialization steps</a>
> for a `SessionManager` async iterator `iterator` are:
>
> 1.  Set `iterator`’s
>     <span id="sessionmanager-async-iterator-current-state"
>     class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="SessionManager async iterator"
>     dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">current state</span> to "not yet
>     started".
>
> To <a href="#dfn-get-the-next-iteration-result"
> id="ref-for-dfn-get-the-next-iteration-result" data-link-type="dfn">get
> the next iteration result</a> for a `SessionManager` `manager` and its
> async iterator `iterator`:
>
> 1.  Let `promise` be a new promise.
>
> 2.  Let `key` be the following value, if it exists, or null otherwise:
>
>     If `iterator`’s <a href="#sessionmanager-async-iterator-current-state"
>     id="ref-for-sessionmanager-async-iterator-current-state"
>     data-link-type="dfn">current state</a> is "not yet started"  
>     the smallest username in `manager`’s open sessions, in
>     lexicographical order
>
>     Otherwise  
>     the smallest username in `manager`’s open sessions that is greater
>     than `iterator`’s current state, in lexicographical order
>
>     <span class="marker">Note:</span> `iterator`’s
>     <a href="#sessionmanager-async-iterator-current-state"
>     id="ref-for-sessionmanager-async-iterator-current-state①"
>     data-link-type="dfn">current state</a> might no longer be present
>     in the open sessions.
>
> 3.  If `key` is null, then:
>
>     1.  Resolve `promise` with
>         <a href="#end-of-iteration" id="ref-for-end-of-iteration"
>         data-link-type="dfn">end of iteration</a>.
>
> 4.  Otherwise:
>
>     1.  Let `session` be the `Session` object corresponding to `key`.
>
>     2.  Resolve `promise` with (`username`, `session`).
>
>     3.  Set `iterator`’s
>         <a href="#sessionmanager-async-iterator-current-state"
>         id="ref-for-sessionmanager-async-iterator-current-state②"
>         data-link-type="dfn">current state</a> to `username`.
>
> 5.  Return `promise`.

In the JavaScript language binding, the
<a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype object</a> for the
`SessionManager` <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> has a `values` method that is a
function, which, when invoked, returns an asynchronous iterator object
that itself has a `next` method that returns the next value to be
iterated over. It has `keys` and `entries` methods that iterate over the
usernames of session objects and (username, `Session`) object pairs,
respectively. It also has a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.asyncIterator%</code></a> method that allows a
`SessionManager` to be used in a `for await..of` loop that has the same
value as the `entries` method:

``` highlight
// Get an instance of SessionManager.
// Assume that it has sessions for two users, "anna" and "brian".
var sm = getSessionManager();

typeof SessionManager.prototype.values;            // Evaluates to "function"
var it = sm.values();                              // values() returns an iterator object
typeof it.next;                                    // Evaluates to "function"

// This loop will log "anna" and then "brian".
for await (let username of sm.keys()) {
  console.log(username);
}

// Yet another way of accomplishing the same.
for await (let [username, session] of sm) {
  console.log(username);
}
```

</div>

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> must not have more than one
<a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a>. The
<a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces⑦" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> of an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑧⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with an
<a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a> must not
also have an <a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a>. An
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with an
<a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a> and its
<a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces⑧" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> must not have a
<a href="#dfn-maplike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-maplike-declaration③"
data-link-type="dfn">maplike declaration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-setlike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-setlike-declaration③"
data-link-type="dfn">setlike declaration</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration⑧" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declaration</a>.

The following extended attributes are applicable to
<a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration①①"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declarations</a>:
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\], and
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\].

these
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> are not currently taken
into account. When they are, the effect will be as you would expect.

``` grammar
AsyncIterable ::
    async_iterable < TypeWithExtendedAttributes OptionalType > OptionalArgumentList ;
```

``` grammar
OptionalArgumentList ::
    ( ArgumentList )
    ε
```

#### <span class="secno">2.5.11. </span><span class="content">Maplike declarations</span><a href="#idl-maplike" class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> can be declared to be
<span id="dfn-maplike" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">maplike</span> by using a <span id="dfn-maplike-declaration"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">maplike
declaration</span> (matching [ReadWriteMaplike](#prod-ReadWriteMaplike)
or readonly [MaplikeRest](#prod-MaplikeRest)) in the body of the
interface.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  readonly maplike<key_type, value_type>;
  maplike<key_type, value_type>;
};
```

Objects implementing an interface that is declared to be maplike
represent an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="ref-for-ordered-map①" data-link-type="dfn">ordered map</a> of
key–value pairs, initially empty, known as that object’s
<span id="dfn-map-entries" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">map entries</span>. The types used for the keys and values are
given in the angle brackets of the maplike declaration. Keys are
required to be unique.

Specification authors can modify the contents of the
<a href="#dfn-map-entries" id="ref-for-dfn-map-entries"
data-link-type="dfn">map entries</a>, which will automatically be
reflected in the contents of the object as observed by JavaScript code.

Maplike interfaces support an API for querying the map entries
appropriate for the language binding. If the readonly keyword is not
used, then it also supports an API for modifying the map entries.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> In the JavaScript language binding,
the API for interacting with the map entries is similar to that
available on JavaScript <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/keyed-collections.html#sec-map-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-map-objects" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Map</code></a> objects. If the readonly keyword is used,
this includes `entries`, `forEach`, `get`, `has`, `keys`, `values`, <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.iterator%</code></a> methods, and a `size` getter.
For read–write maplikes, it also includes `clear`, `delete`, and `set`
methods.

Maplike interfaces must not have any
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②③"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②②"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> named "`entries`",
"`forEach`", "`get`", "`has`", "`keys`", "`size`", or "`values`", or
have any <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces⑨" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> that have
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②④"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②③"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> with these names.

Read–write maplike interfaces must not have any
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②①"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a> or
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> named "`clear`", "`delete`", or
"`set`", or have any <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces①⓪" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> that have
