<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②②"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a> or
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> with these names.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Read-write maplike interfaces *can*
have *regular operations* named "`clear`", "`delete`", or "`set`", which
will override the default implementation of those methods (defined in
[§ 3.7.11 Maplike declarations](#js-maplike)). If such regular
operations are defined, they must match the input and output
expectations of each method, defined in their default implementation
sections.

An interface must not have more than one
<a href="#dfn-maplike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-maplike-declaration④"
data-link-type="dfn">maplike declaration</a>. The
<a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces①①" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> of a maplike interface must not also have a
<a href="#dfn-maplike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-maplike-declaration⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">maplike declaration</a>. A maplike interface and
its <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces①②" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> must not have an <a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration⑨" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declaration</a>, an <a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration①②"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a>, a
<a href="#dfn-setlike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-setlike-declaration④"
data-link-type="dfn">setlike declaration</a>, or an
<a href="#dfn-indexed-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-getter④" data-link-type="dfn">indexed
property getter</a>.

<div>

``` grammar
ReadOnlyMember ::
    readonly ReadOnlyMemberRest
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
ReadOnlyMemberRest ::
    AttributeRest
    MaplikeRest
    SetlikeRest
```

</div>

``` grammar
ReadWriteMaplike ::
    MaplikeRest
```

``` grammar
MaplikeRest ::
    maplike < TypeWithExtendedAttributes , TypeWithExtendedAttributes > ;
```

No
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> defined in this
specification are applicable to
<a href="#dfn-maplike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-maplike-declaration⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">maplike declarations</a>.

Add example.

#### <span class="secno">2.5.12. </span><span class="content">Setlike declarations</span><a href="#idl-setlike" class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> can be declared to be
<span id="dfn-setlike" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">setlike</span> by using a <span id="dfn-setlike-declaration"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">setlike
declaration</span> (matching [ReadWriteSetlike](#prod-ReadWriteSetlike)
or readonly [SetlikeRest](#prod-SetlikeRest)) in the body of the
interface.

``` highlight
interface interface_identifier {
  readonly setlike<type>;
  setlike<type>;
};
```

Objects implementing an interface that is declared to be setlike
represent an <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="ref-for-ordered-set②" data-link-type="dfn">ordered set</a> of
values, initially empty, known as that object’s
<span id="dfn-set-entries" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">set entries</span>. The type of the values is given in the
angle brackets of the setlike declaration. Values are required to be
unique.

Specification authors can modify the contents of the
<a href="#dfn-set-entries" id="ref-for-dfn-set-entries"
data-link-type="dfn">set entries</a>, which will automatically be
reflected in the contents of the object as observed by JavaScript code.

Setlike interfaces support an API for querying the set entries
appropriate for the language binding. If the readonly keyword is not
used, then it also supports an API for modifying the set entries.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> In the JavaScript language binding,
the API for interacting with the set entries is similar to that
available on JavaScript <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/keyed-collections.html#sec-set-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-set-objects" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Set</code></a> objects. If the readonly keyword is used,
this includes `entries`, `forEach`, `has`, `keys`, `values`, <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.iterator%</code></a> methods, and a `size` getter.
For read–write setlikes, it also includes `add`, `clear`, and `delete`
methods.

Setlike interfaces must not have any
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②③"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②④"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> named "`entries`",
"`forEach`", "`has`", "`keys`", "`size`", or "`values`", or have any
<a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces①③" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> that have
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②④"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>,
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a> with these names.

Read–write setlike interfaces must not have any
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a> or
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> named "`add`", "`clear`", or
"`delete`", or have any <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces①④" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> that have
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a> or
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> with these names.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Read-write setlike interfaces *can*
have *regular operations* named "`add`", "`clear`", or "`delete`", which
will override the default implementation of those methods (defined in
[§ 3.7.12 Setlike declarations](#js-setlike)). If such regular
operations are defined, they must match the input and output
expectations of each method, defined in their default implementation
sections.

An interface must not have more than one
<a href="#dfn-setlike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-setlike-declaration⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">setlike declaration</a>. The
<a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces①⑤" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> of a setlike interface must not also have a
<a href="#dfn-setlike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-setlike-declaration⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">setlike declaration</a>. A setlike interface and
its <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces①⑥" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> must not have an <a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration①⓪" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declaration</a>, an <a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration①③"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a>, a
<a href="#dfn-maplike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-maplike-declaration⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">maplike declaration</a>, or an
<a href="#dfn-indexed-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-getter⑤" data-link-type="dfn">indexed
property getter</a>.

<div>

``` grammar
ReadOnlyMember ::
    readonly ReadOnlyMemberRest
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
ReadOnlyMemberRest ::
    AttributeRest
    MaplikeRest
    SetlikeRest
```

</div>

``` grammar
ReadWriteSetlike ::
    SetlikeRest
```

``` grammar
SetlikeRest ::
    setlike < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > ;
```

No
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> defined in this
specification are applicable to
<a href="#dfn-setlike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-setlike-declaration⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">setlike declarations</a>.

Add example.

### <span class="secno">2.6. </span><span class="content">Namespaces</span><a href="#idl-namespaces" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-namespace" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">namespace</span> is a definition (matching
[Namespace](#prod-Namespace)) that declares a global singleton with
associated behaviors.

``` highlight
namespace identifier {
  /* namespace_members... */
};
```

A namespace is a specification of a set of
<span id="dfn-namespace-member" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="" lt="namespace member">namespace members</span> (matching
[NamespaceMembers](#prod-NamespaceMembers)), which are the
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a>,
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attributes</a>, and
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant③①"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> that appear between the braces in the
namespace declaration. These operations and attributes describe the
behaviors packaged into the namespace.

As with interfaces, the IDL for namespaces can be split into multiple
parts by using <span id="dfn-partial-namespace" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">partial namespace</span> definitions (matching
partial [Namespace](#prod-Namespace)). The
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of a partial namespace definition
must be the same as the identifier of a namespace definition. All of the
members that appear on each of the partial namespace definitions are
considered to be members of the namespace itself.

``` highlight
namespace SomeNamespace {
  /* namespace_members... */
};

partial namespace SomeNamespace {
  /* namespace_members... */
};
```

<span class="marker">Note:</span> As with partial interface definitions,
partial namespace definitions are intended for use as a specification
editorial aide, allowing the definition of a namespace to be separated
over more than one section of the document, and sometimes multiple
documents.

The order that members appear in has significance for property
enumeration in the [JavaScript binding](#js-namespaces).

Note that unlike interfaces or dictionaries, namespaces do not create
types.

Of the extended attributes defined in this specification, only the
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\], and
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
extended attributes are applicable to namespaces.

<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">Namespaces</a> must be annotated with the
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②①"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>.

<div>

``` grammar
Partial ::
    partial PartialDefinition
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
PartialDefinition ::
    interface PartialInterfaceOrPartialMixin
    PartialDictionary
    Namespace
```

</div>

``` grammar
Namespace ::
    namespace identifier { NamespaceMembers } ;
```

``` grammar
NamespaceMembers ::
    ExtendedAttributeList NamespaceMember NamespaceMembers
    ε
```

``` grammar
NamespaceMember ::
    RegularOperation
    readonly AttributeRest
    Const
```

<div id="example-namespace" class="example">

<a href="#example-namespace" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②④"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines a
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

``` highlight
namespace VectorUtils {
  readonly attribute Vector unit;
  double dotProduct(Vector x, Vector y);
  Vector crossProduct(Vector x, Vector y);
};
```

A JavaScript implementation would then expose a global `VectorUtils`
data property which was a simple object (with prototype <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">%Object.prototype%</code></a>)
with enumerable data properties for each declared operation, and
enumerable get-only accessors for each declared attribute:

``` highlight
Object.getPrototypeOf(VectorUtils);                         // Evaluates to Object.prototype.
Object.keys(VectorUtils);                                   // Evaluates to ["dotProduct", "crossProduct"].
Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(VectorUtils, "dotProduct"); // Evaluates to { value: <a function>, enumerable: true, configurable: true, writable: true }.
Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(VectorUtils, "unit");       // Evaluates to { get: <a function>, enumerable: true, configurable: true }.
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.7. </span><span class="content">Dictionaries</span><a href="#idl-dictionaries" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-dictionary" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">dictionary</span> is a definition (matching
[Dictionary](#prod-Dictionary)) used to define an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="ref-for-ordered-map②" data-link-type="dfn">ordered map</a> data type
with a fixed, ordered set of
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="ref-for-map-entry" data-link-type="dfn">entries</a>, termed
<span id="dfn-dictionary-member" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">dictionary members</span>, where
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-getting-the-keys"
id="ref-for-map-getting-the-keys" data-link-type="dfn">keys</a> are
strings and
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-getting-the-values"
id="ref-for-map-getting-the-values①" data-link-type="dfn">values</a> are
of a particular type specified in the definition.

``` highlight
dictionary identifier {
  /* dictionary_members... */
};
```

Dictionary instances do not retain a reference to their
language-specific representations (e.g., the corresponding JavaScript
object). So for example, returning a dictionary from an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②②"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> will result in a new JavaScript
object being created from the current values of the dictionary. And, an
operation that accepts a dictionary as an argument will perform a
one-time conversion from the given JavaScript value into the dictionary,
based on the current properties of the JavaScript object. Modifications
to the dictionary will not be reflected in the corresponding JavaScript
object, and vice-versa.

Dictionaries must not be used as the type of an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> or
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant③②"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a>.

A dictionary can be defined to <span id="dfn-inherit-dictionary"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="dictionary" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">inherit</span> from another dictionary. If the identifier of
the dictionary is followed by a colon and a
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>, then that identifier identifies the
inherited dictionary. The identifier must identify a dictionary.

A dictionary must not be declared such that its inheritance hierarchy
has a cycle. That is, a dictionary `A` cannot inherit from itself, nor
can it inherit from another dictionary `B` that inherits from `A`, and
so on.

``` highlight
dictionary Base {
  /* dictionary_members... */
};

dictionary Derived : Base {
  /* dictionary_members... */
};
```

The <span id="dfn-inherited-dictionaries" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">inherited dictionaries</span> of a given
dictionary `D` is the set of all dictionaries that `D` inherits from,
directly or indirectly. If `D` does not
<a href="#dfn-inherit-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit-dictionary"
data-link-type="dfn">inherit</a> from another dictionary, then the set
is empty. Otherwise, the set includes the dictionary `E` that `D`
<a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">inherits</a> from and all of `E`’s
<a href="#dfn-inherited-dictionaries"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-dictionaries①" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
dictionaries</a>.

<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member④"
data-link-type="dfn">Dictionary members</a> can be specified as
<span id="required-dictionary-member" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="dictionary member" dfn-type="dfn" export="">required</span>,
meaning that converting a language-specific value to a dictionary
requires providing a value for that member. Any dictionary member that
is not <a href="#required-dictionary-member"
id="ref-for-required-dictionary-member①"
data-link-type="dfn">required</a> is
<span id="dictionary-member-optional" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="dictionary member" dfn-type="dfn" export="">optional</span>.

Note that specifying
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary members</a> as
<a href="#required-dictionary-member"
id="ref-for-required-dictionary-member②"
data-link-type="dfn">required</a> only has an observable effect when
converting other representations of dictionaries (like a JavaScript
value supplied as an argument to an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②③"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>) to an IDL dictionary. Specification
authors should leave the members <a href="#dictionary-member-optional"
id="ref-for-dictionary-member-optional"
data-link-type="dfn">optional</a> in all other cases, including when a
dictionary type is used solely as the
<a href="#dfn-return-type" id="ref-for-dfn-return-type②"
data-link-type="dfn">return type</a> of
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②④"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a>.

A given dictionary value of type `D` can have
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="ref-for-map-entry①" data-link-type="dfn">entries</a> for each of the
dictionary members defined on `D` and on any of `D`’s
<a href="#dfn-inherited-dictionaries"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-dictionaries②" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
dictionaries</a>. Dictionary members that are specified as
<a href="#required-dictionary-member"
id="ref-for-required-dictionary-member③"
data-link-type="dfn">required</a>, or that are specified as having a
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value①"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a>, will always have such
corresponding <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="ref-for-map-entry②" data-link-type="dfn">entries</a>. Other members'
entries might or might not
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
id="ref-for-map-exists" data-link-type="dfn">exist</a> in the dictionary
value.

In the JavaScript binding, a value of undefined for the property
corresponding to a
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a> is treated the same as
omitting that property. Thus, it will cause an error if the member is
<a href="#required-dictionary-member"
id="ref-for-required-dictionary-member④"
data-link-type="dfn">required</a>, or will trigger the
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value②"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a> if one is present, or will result
in no <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="ref-for-map-entry③" data-link-type="dfn">entry</a> existing in the
dictionary value otherwise.

As with <a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">operation argument default values</a>, it is
strongly encouraged not to use true as the
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value③"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a> for
<a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a>-typed
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary members</a>, as this can be confusing
for authors who might otherwise expect the default conversion of
undefined to be used (i.e., false).
<a href="#biblio-api-design-principles" data-link-type="biblio"
title="Web Platform Design Principles">[API-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES]</a>

An <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="ref-for-ordered-map③" data-link-type="dfn">ordered map</a> with
string <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-getting-the-keys"
id="ref-for-map-getting-the-keys①" data-link-type="dfn">keys</a> can be
implicitly treated as a dictionary value of a specific dictionary `D` if
all of its <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="ref-for-map-entry④" data-link-type="dfn">entries</a> correspond to
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary members</a>, as long as those entries
have the correct types, and there are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="ref-for-map-entry⑤" data-link-type="dfn">entries</a> present for any
<a href="#required-dictionary-member"
id="ref-for-required-dictionary-member⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">required</a> or
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value④"
data-link-type="dfn">defaulted</a> dictionary members.

<div id="example-ba8998ea" class="example">

<a href="#example-ba8998ea" class="self-link"></a>

``` highlight
dictionary Descriptor {
  DOMString name;
  sequence<unsigned long> serviceIdentifiers;
};
```

A `Descriptor` dictionary could be created as in the following steps:

1.  Let `identifiers` be « 1, 3, 7 ».

2.  Return «\[ "name" → "test", "serviceIdentifiers" → `identifiers`
    \]».

</div>

Each
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a> (matching
[DictionaryMember](#prod-DictionaryMember)) is specified as a type
(matching [Type](#prod-Type)) followed by an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> (given by an
[identifier](#prod-identifier) token following the type). The identifier
is the key name of the key–value pair. If the [Type](#prod-Type) is an
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier③⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> followed by ?, then the identifier
must identify an <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef①①"
data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a>. If the dictionary member type is an
identifier not followed by ?, then the identifier must identify any one
of those definitions or a
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary</a>.

If the type of the
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a>, after resolving typedefs, is
a <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a>, its
<a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> must not be a
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a>.

``` highlight
dictionary identifier {
  type identifier;
};
```

If the identifier for an <a href="#dictionary-member-optional"
id="ref-for-dictionary-member-optional①"
data-link-type="dfn">optional</a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①①"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a> is followed by a U+003D (=)
and a value (matching [DefaultValue](#prod-DefaultValue)), then that
gives the dictionary member its
<span id="dfn-dictionary-member-default-value" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="dictionary member" dfn-type="dfn" export="">default
value</span>, which is the value used by default when author code or
specification text does not provide a value for that member.

``` highlight
dictionary identifier {
  type identifier = "value";
};
```

When a boolean literal token (true or false), the null token, an
[integer](#prod-integer) token, a [decimal](#prod-decimal) token, one of
the three special floating point literal values (Infinity, -Infinity or
NaN), a [string](#prod-string) token, the two token sequence \[\], or
the two token sequence {} is used as the
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a>, it is interpreted in the same
way as for an <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>’s
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">optional argument default value</a>.

If the type of the
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①②"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a> is an
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>, then its
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">default value</a> if specified must be one of the
<a href="#dfn-enumeration-value" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration-value①"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration’s values</a>.

If the type of the dictionary member is preceded by the required
keyword, the member is considered a
<a href="#required-dictionary-member"
id="ref-for-required-dictionary-member⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">required</a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①③"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a>.

``` highlight
dictionary identifier {
  required type identifier;
};
```

The type of a dictionary member must not include the dictionary it
appears on. A type includes a dictionary `D` if at least one of the
following is true:

- the type is `D`

- the type is a dictionary that
  <a href="#dfn-inherit-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit-dictionary①"
  data-link-type="dfn">inherits</a> from `D`

- the type is a
  <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①⓪"
  data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a> whose
  <a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> includes `D`

- the type is a <a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">sequence type</a> or
  <a href="#dfn-frozen-array-type" id="ref-for-dfn-frozen-array-type②"
  data-link-type="dfn">frozen array</a> whose element type includes `D`

- the type is a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>, one of whose
  <a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type②"
  data-link-type="dfn">member types</a> includes `D`

- the type is a dictionary, one of whose members or inherited members
  has a type that includes `D`

- the type is <a href="#idl-record" id="ref-for-idl-record①"
  data-link-type="dfn"><code class="idl">record</code></a>`<``K``, ``V``>`
  where `V` includes `D`

As with interfaces, the IDL for dictionaries can be split into multiple
parts by using <span id="dfn-partial-dictionary" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">partial dictionary</span> definitions (matching
partial [Dictionary](#prod-Dictionary)). The
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of a partial dictionary definition
must be the same as the identifier of a dictionary definition. All of
the members that appear on each of the partial dictionary definitions
are considered to be members of the dictionary itself.

``` highlight
dictionary SomeDictionary {
  /* dictionary_members... */
};

partial dictionary SomeDictionary {
  /* dictionary_members... */
};
```

<span class="marker">Note:</span> As with partial interface definitions,
partial dictionary definitions are intended for use as a specification
editorial aide, allowing the definition of an interface to be separated
over more than one section of the document, and sometimes multiple
documents.

The order of the
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①④"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary members</a> on a given dictionary is
such that inherited dictionary members are ordered before non-inherited
members, and the dictionary members on the one dictionary definition
(including any partial dictionary definitions) are ordered
lexicographically by the Unicode codepoints that comprise their
identifiers.

<div class="note" role="note">

For example, with the following definitions:

``` highlight
dictionary B : A {
  long b;
  long a;
};

dictionary A {
  long c;
  long g;
};

dictionary C : B {
  long e;
  long f;
};

partial dictionary A {
  long h;
  long d;
};
```

the order of the
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary members</a> of a dictionary value of
type `C` is c, d, g, h, a, b, e, f.

Dictionaries need to have their members ordered because in some language
bindings the behavior observed when passing a dictionary value to a
platform object depends on the order the dictionary members are fetched.
For example, consider the following additional interface:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Something {
  undefined f(A a);
};
```

and this JavaScript code:

``` highlight
var something = getSomething();  // Get an instance of Something.
var x = 0;

var dict = { };
Object.defineProperty(dict, "d", { get: function() { return ++x; } });
Object.defineProperty(dict, "c", { get: function() { return ++x; } });

something.f(dict);
```

The order that the dictionary members are fetched in determines what
values they will be taken to have. Since the order for `A` is defined to
be c then d, the value for c will be 1 and the value for d will be 2.

</div>

The identifier of a dictionary member must not be the same as that of
another dictionary member defined on the dictionary or on that
dictionary’s <a href="#dfn-inherited-dictionaries"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-dictionaries③" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
dictionaries</a>.

No
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②②"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> are applicable to
dictionaries.

<div>

``` grammar
Partial ::
    partial PartialDefinition
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
PartialDefinition ::
    interface PartialInterfaceOrPartialMixin
    PartialDictionary
    Namespace
```

</div>

``` grammar
Dictionary ::
    dictionary identifier Inheritance { DictionaryMembers } ;
```

``` grammar
DictionaryMembers ::
    DictionaryMember DictionaryMembers
    ε
```

``` grammar
DictionaryMember ::
    ExtendedAttributeList DictionaryMemberRest
```

``` grammar
DictionaryMemberRest ::
    required TypeWithExtendedAttributes identifier ;
    Type identifier Default ;
```

``` grammar
PartialDictionary ::
    dictionary identifier { DictionaryMembers } ;
```

``` grammar
Default ::
    = DefaultValue
    ε
```

<div>

``` grammar
DefaultValue ::
    ConstValue
    string
    [ ]
    { }
    null
    undefined
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
Inheritance ::
    : identifier
    ε
```

</div>

<div id="example-f7efabfd" class="example">

<a href="#example-f7efabfd" class="self-link"></a>

One use of dictionary types is to allow a number of
<span class="allow-rfc2119">optional</span> arguments to an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> without being constrained as to the
order they are specified at the call site. For example, consider the
following <a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a>:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Point {
  constructor();
  attribute double x;
  attribute double y;
};

dictionary PaintOptions {
  DOMString fillPattern = "black";
  DOMString strokePattern;
  Point position;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface GraphicsContext {
  undefined drawRectangle(double width, double height, optional PaintOptions options);
};
```

In a JavaScript implementation of the IDL, an Object can be passed in
for the <span class="allow-rfc2119">optional</span> `PaintOptions`
dictionary:

``` highlight
// Get an instance of GraphicsContext.
var ctx = getGraphicsContext();

// Draw a rectangle.
ctx.drawRectangle(300, 200, { fillPattern: "red", position: new Point(10, 10) });
```

The members of `PaintOptions` are <a href="#dictionary-member-optional"
id="ref-for-dictionary-member-optional②"
data-link-type="dfn">optional</a>. If `fillPattern` is omitted, the
definition of `drawRectangle` can assume that it has the given default
values and not include explicit wording to handle its omission.
`drawRectangle` needs to explicitly handle the case where
`strokePattern` and `position` are omitted.

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.8. </span><span class="content">Exceptions</span><a href="#idl-exceptions" class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="dfn-exception" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">exception</span> is a type of object that represents an error
and which can be thrown or treated as a first class value by
implementations. Web IDL has a number of pre-defined exceptions that
specifications can reference and throw in their definition of
operations, attributes, and so on. Custom exception types can also be
defined, as <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨④"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> that
<a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">inherit</a> from
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>.

A <span id="dfn-simple-exception" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">simple exception</span> is identified by one of the following
types:

- <span id="exceptiondef-evalerror" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code"
  dfn-type="exception" export="">`EvalError`</span>

- <span id="exceptiondef-rangeerror" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code"
  dfn-type="exception" export="">`RangeError`</span>

- <span id="exceptiondef-referenceerror"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="exception"
  export="">`ReferenceError`</span>

- <span id="exceptiondef-typeerror" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code"
  dfn-type="exception" export="">`TypeError`</span>

- <span id="exceptiondef-urierror" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code"
  dfn-type="exception" export="">`URIError`</span>

These correspond to all of the JavaScript
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-error-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-error-objects" data-link-type="dfn">error objects</a>
(apart from <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror"
id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a> and <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-error-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-error-objects①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Error</code></a>, which are deliberately omitted as they are
reserved for use by the JavaScript parser and by authors, respectively).
The meaning of each
<a href="#dfn-simple-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-simple-exception"
data-link-type="dfn">simple exception</a> matches its corresponding
error object in the JavaScript specification.

The second kind of exception is a
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>, which
provides further programmatically-introspectable detail on the error
that occurred by giving a
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name"
data-link-type="dfn">name</a>. Such
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name①"
data-link-type="dfn">names</a> are drawn from the
<a href="#dfn-error-names-table" id="ref-for-dfn-error-names-table"
data-link-type="dfn"><code>DOMException</code> names table</a> below.

As <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> is an
<a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a>, it can be used as a type in
IDL. This allows for example an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> to be declared to have a
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>
<a href="#dfn-return-type" id="ref-for-dfn-return-type③"
data-link-type="dfn">return type</a>. This is generally a bad pattern,
however, as exceptions are meant to be thrown and not returned.

The final kind of exception is a derived interface of
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>. These
are more complicated, and thus described in the dedicated section
[§ 2.8.2 DOMException derived
interfaces](#idl-DOMException-derived-interfaces).

<a href="#dfn-simple-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-simple-exception①"
data-link-type="dfn">Simple exceptions</a> can be
<span id="dfn-create-exception" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="exception" dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="create">created</span>
by providing their type name. A
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> can be
<a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception"
data-link-type="dfn">created</a> by providing its
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name②"
data-link-type="dfn">name</a> followed by
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>.
Exceptions can also be <span id="dfn-throw" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="exception" dfn-type="dfn" export="" lt="throw">thrown</span>,
by providing the same details required to
<a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception①"
data-link-type="dfn">create</a> one. In both cases, the caller may
provide additional information about what the exception indicates, which
is useful when constructing the exception’s message.

<div id="example-exception-creation-and-throwing" class="example">

<a href="#example-exception-creation-and-throwing"
class="self-link"></a>

Here is are some examples of wording to use to create and throw
exceptions. To throw a new
<a href="#dfn-simple-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-simple-exception②"
data-link-type="dfn">simple exception</a> whose type is
<a href="#exceptiondef-typeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-typeerror②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>:

> <a href="#dfn-throw" id="ref-for-dfn-throw"
> data-link-type="dfn">Throw</a> a
> <a href="#exceptiondef-typeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-typeerror③"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

To throw a new
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> with
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name③"
data-link-type="dfn">name</a>
"<a href="#notallowederror" id="ref-for-notallowederror"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">NotAllowedError</code></a>":

> <a href="#dfn-throw" id="ref-for-dfn-throw①"
> data-link-type="dfn">Throw</a> a
> "<a href="#notallowederror" id="ref-for-notallowederror①"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">NotAllowedError</code></a>"
> <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑧"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>.

To create a new
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> with
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name④"
data-link-type="dfn">name</a>
"<a href="#syntaxerror" id="ref-for-syntaxerror"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a>":

> Let `object` be a newly
> <a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception②"
> data-link-type="dfn">created</a>
> "<a href="#syntaxerror" id="ref-for-syntaxerror①"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a>"
> <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①⓪"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>.

To <a href="#reject" id="ref-for-reject" data-link-type="dfn">reject</a>
a promise with a new
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> with
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">name</a>
"<a href="#operationerror" id="ref-for-operationerror"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">OperationError</code></a>":

> <a href="#reject" id="ref-for-reject①" data-link-type="dfn">Reject</a>
> `p` with an "<a href="#operationerror" id="ref-for-operationerror①"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">OperationError</code></a>"
> <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①②"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>.

</div>

<div id="example-exception-throwing-message-hint" class="example">

<a href="#example-exception-throwing-message-hint"
class="self-link"></a>

An example of including additional information used to construct the
exception message would be:

> <a href="#dfn-throw" id="ref-for-dfn-throw②"
> data-link-type="dfn">Throw</a> a
> "<a href="#syntaxerror" id="ref-for-syntaxerror②"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a>"
> <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①③"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>
> indicating that the given value had disallowed trailing spaces.

Such additional context is most helpful to implementers when it is not
immediately obvious why the exception is being thrown, e.g., because
there are many different steps in the algorithm which throw a
"<a href="#syntaxerror" id="ref-for-syntaxerror③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a>"
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>. In
contrast, if your specification throws a
"<a href="#notallowederror" id="ref-for-notallowederror②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">NotAllowedError</code></a>"
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>
immediately after checking if the user has provided permission to use a
given feature, it’s fairly obvious what sort of message the
implementation ought to construct, and so specifying it is not
necessary.

</div>

The resulting behavior from creating and throwing an exception is
language binding specific.

See [§ 3.14.3 Creating and throwing
exceptions](#js-creating-throwing-exceptions) for details on what
creating and throwing an exception entails in the JavaScript language
binding.

#### <span class="secno">2.8.1. </span><span class="content">Base <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> error names</span><a href="#idl-DOMException-error-names" class="self-link"></a>

The <span id="dfn-error-names-table" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">`DOMException` names table</span> below lists
all the allowed
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">names</a> for instances of the base
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>
interface, along with a description of what such names mean, and legacy
numeric error code values.

Interfaces <a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">inheriting</a> from
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>, in the
manner described in [§ 2.8.2 DOMException derived
interfaces](#idl-DOMException-derived-interfaces), will have their own
names, not listed in this table.

When <a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception③"
data-link-type="dfn">creating</a> or
<a href="#dfn-throw" id="ref-for-dfn-throw③"
data-link-type="dfn">throwing</a> a
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException①⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>,
specifications must use one of these names. If a specification author
believes none of these names are a good fit for their case, they must
[file an
issue](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/new?title=DOMException%20name%20proposal)
to discuss adding a new name to the shared namespace, so that the
community can coordinate such efforts. Note that adding new
use-case-specific names is only important if you believe web developers
will discriminate multiple error conditions arising from a single API.

The <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException②⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> names
marked as deprecated are kept for legacy purposes, but their usage is
discouraged.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Don’t confuse the
"<a href="#syntaxerror" id="ref-for-syntaxerror④" class="idl-code"
data-link-type="exception"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a>"
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException②①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> defined
here with JavaScript’s <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror"
id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a>.
"<a href="#syntaxerror" id="ref-for-syntaxerror⑤" class="idl-code"
data-link-type="exception"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a>"
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException②②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> is used
to report parsing errors in web APIs, for example when parsing
selectors, while the JavaScript <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror"
id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a> is
reserved for the JavaScript parser. To help disambiguate this further,
always favor the
"<a href="#syntaxerror" id="ref-for-syntaxerror⑥" class="idl-code"
data-link-type="exception"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a>"
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException②③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> notation
over just using
<a href="#syntaxerror" id="ref-for-syntaxerror⑦" class="idl-code"
data-link-type="exception"><code class="idl">SyntaxError</code></a> to
refer to the <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException②④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>.
<a href="#biblio-dom" data-link-type="biblio"
title="DOM Standard">[DOM]</a>

| Name | Description | Legacy code name and value |
|----|----|----|

data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">RangeError</code></a> instead. | <span id="dom-domexception-index_size_err" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-for="DOMException" dfn-type="const" export="">`INDEX_SIZE_ERR`</span> (1) |

title="DOM Standard">[DOM]</a> | <span id="dom-domexception-invalid_node_type_err" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-for="DOMException" dfn-type="const" export="">`INVALID_NODE_TYPE_ERR`</span> (24) |

#### <span class="secno">2.8.2. </span><span class="content"><a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException②⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> derived interfaces</span><a href="#idl-DOMException-derived-interfaces" class="self-link"></a>

When an exception needs to carry additional
programmatically-introspectable information, beyond what can be provided
with a <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException②⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>’s
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">name</a>, specification authors can create an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> which
<a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">inherits</a> from
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>. Such
interfaces need to follow certain rules, in order to have a predictable
shape for developers. Specifically:

- The <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④①"
  data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of the
  <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> must end with `Error`, and must not
  be any of the names in the
  <a href="#dfn-error-names-table" id="ref-for-dfn-error-names-table①"
  data-link-type="dfn"><code>DOMException</code> names table</a>.

- The <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨⑦"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> must have a
  <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①④"
  data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> which sets the
  instance’s
  <a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">name</a> to the interface’s
  <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④②"
  data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>.

- Their <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> must take as its first
  parameter an
  <a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">optional</a>
  <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①④"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> named
  `message` defaulting to the empty string, and must set the instance’s
  <a href="#domexception-message" id="ref-for-domexception-message"
  data-link-type="dfn">message</a> to `message`.

- Their <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a> should take as its
  second parameter a
  <a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">dictionary</a> containing the additional
  information that needs to be exposed.

- They should have <a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only⑦"
  data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
  <a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>, whose names are the same as the
  members of the constructor dictionary, which return the values
  accepted by the constructor operation.

- They should be <a
  href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#serializable-objects"
  id="ref-for-serializable-objects" data-link-type="dfn">serializable
  objects</a>, whose <a
  href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#serialization-steps"
  id="ref-for-serialization-steps" data-link-type="dfn">serialization
  steps</a> and <a
  href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#deserialization-steps"
  id="ref-for-deserialization-steps" data-link-type="dfn">deserialization
  steps</a> preserve the additional information.

These requirements mean that the inherited
<a href="#dom-domexception-code" id="ref-for-dom-domexception-code"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">code</code></a> property of these
interfaces will always return 0.

To <a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception④"
data-link-type="dfn">create</a> or
<a href="#dfn-throw" id="ref-for-dfn-throw④"
data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> derived
interface, supply its
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④③"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> as well as the additional
information needed to construct it.

<div id="example-domexception-derived-throwing" class="example">

<a href="#example-domexception-derived-throwing" class="self-link"></a>

To throw an instance of
<a href="#quotaexceedederror" id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">QuotaExceededError</code></a>:

> <a href="#dfn-throw" id="ref-for-dfn-throw⑤"
> data-link-type="dfn">Throw</a> a
> <a href="#quotaexceedederror" id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror②"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">QuotaExceededError</code></a>
> whose <a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
> id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>
> is 42 and <a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
> id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested"
> data-link-type="dfn">requested</a> is 50.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.8.3. </span><span id="example-domexception-derived-interface" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Predefined <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> derived interfaces</span><a href="#idl-DOMException-derived-predefineds" class="self-link"></a>

This standard so far defines one predefined
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> derived
interface:

``` def
[Exposed=*, Serializable]
interface QuotaExceededError : DOMException {
  constructor(optional DOMString message = "", optional QuotaExceededErrorOptions options = {});

  readonly attribute double? quota;
  readonly attribute double? requested;
};

dictionary QuotaExceededErrorOptions {
  double quota;
  double requested;
};
```

The <a href="#quotaexceedederror" id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">QuotaExceededError</code></a>
exception can be thrown when a quota is exceeded. It has two properties
that are optionally present, to give more information to the web
developer about their request compared to the quota value.

Previous versions of this standard defined "`QuotaExceededError`" as one
of the [base `DOMException` error names](#idl-DOMException-error-names).
It has been upgraded to a full interface to support including such
information.

Every <a href="#quotaexceedederror" id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">QuotaExceededError</code></a>
instance has a <span id="quotaexceedederror-requested"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="QuotaExceededError" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">requested</span> and a <span id="quotaexceedederror-quota"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="QuotaExceededError" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">quota</span>, both numbers or null. They are both initially
null.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="QuotaExceededError(message, options)"
algorithm-for="QuotaExceededError">

The <span id="dom-quotaexceedederror-quotaexceedederror"
class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-for="QuotaExceededError"
dfn-type="constructor" export=""
lt="QuotaExceededError(message, options)|constructor(message, options)|QuotaExceededError(message)|constructor(message)|QuotaExceededError()|constructor()">`new QuotaExceededError(``message``, ``options``)`</span>
constructor steps are:

1.  Set
    <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①⓪" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
    <a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">name</a> to "`QuotaExceededError`".

2.  Set
    <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①①" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
    <a href="#domexception-message" id="ref-for-domexception-message①"
    data-link-type="dfn">message</a> to `message`.

3.  If `options`\["<a href="#dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-quota"
    id="ref-for-dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-quota"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">quota</code></a>"\] is
    present:

    1.  If `options`\["<a href="#dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-quota"
        id="ref-for-dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-quota①"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">quota</code></a>"\] is
        less than 0, then throw a
        <a href="#exceptiondef-rangeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-rangeerror①"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">RangeError</code></a>.

    2.  Set
        <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①②" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
        <a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
        id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota①" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>
        to `options`\["<a href="#dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-quota"
        id="ref-for-dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-quota②"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">quota</code></a>"\].

4.  If `options`\["<a href="#dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-requested"
    id="ref-for-dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-requested"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">requested</code></a>"\] is
    present:

    1.  If
        `options`\["<a href="#dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-requested"
        id="ref-for-dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-requested①"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">requested</code></a>"\]
        is less than 0, then throw a
        <a href="#exceptiondef-rangeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-rangeerror②"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">RangeError</code></a>.

    2.  Set
        <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①③" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
        <a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
        id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested①"
        data-link-type="dfn">requested</a> to
        `options`\["<a href="#dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-requested"
        id="ref-for-dom-quotaexceedederroroptions-requested②"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">requested</code></a>"\].

5.  If
    <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①④" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
    <a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
    id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota②" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>
    is not null,
    <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①⑤" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
    <a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
    id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested②"
    data-link-type="dfn">requested</a> is not null, and
    <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①⑥" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
    <a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
    id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested③"
    data-link-type="dfn">requested</a> is less than
    <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①⑦" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
    <a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
    id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota③" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>,
    then throw a
    <a href="#exceptiondef-rangeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-rangeerror③"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">RangeError</code></a>.

</div>

The <span id="dom-quotaexceedederror-quota"
class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-for="QuotaExceededError"
dfn-type="attribute" export="">`quota`</span> getter steps are to return
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①⑧" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
<a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota④" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>.

The <span id="dom-quotaexceedederror-requested"
class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-for="QuotaExceededError"
dfn-type="attribute" export="">`requested`</span> getter steps are to
return
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this①⑨" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
<a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested④"
data-link-type="dfn">requested</a>.

The <a href="#quotaexceedederror" id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">QuotaExceededError</code></a>
interface inherits the
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>
interface’s
<a href="#dom-domexception-code" id="ref-for-dom-domexception-code①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">code</code></a> getter, which
will always return 22. However, relying on this value is discouraged
(for both <a href="#quotaexceedederror" id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">QuotaExceededError</code></a> and
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>); it is
better to use the
<a href="#dom-domexception-name" id="ref-for-dom-domexception-name"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">name</code></a> getter.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a href="#quotaexceedederror" id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">QuotaExceededError</code></a>
objects are <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#serializable-objects"
id="ref-for-serializable-objects①" data-link-type="dfn">serializable
objects</a>.

<div class="algorithm"
algorithm="QuotaExceededError serialization steps">

Their <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#serialization-steps"
id="ref-for-serialization-steps①" data-link-type="dfn">serialization
steps</a>, given `value` and `serialized`, are:

1.  Run the <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③⑦"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#serialization-steps"
    id="ref-for-serialization-steps②" data-link-type="dfn">serialization
    steps</a> given `value` and `serialized`.

2.  Set `serialized`.\[\[Quota\]\] to `value`’s
    <a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
    id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota⑤" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>.

3.  Set `serialized`.\[\[Requested\]\] to `value`’s
    <a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
    id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">requested</a>.

</div>

<div class="algorithm"
algorithm="QuotaExceededError deserialization steps">

Their <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#deserialization-steps"
id="ref-for-deserialization-steps①" data-link-type="dfn">deserialization
steps</a>, given `serialized` and `value`, are:

1.  Run the <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③⑧"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#deserialization-steps"
    id="ref-for-deserialization-steps②" data-link-type="dfn">deserialization
    steps</a> given `serialized` and `value`.

2.  Set `value`’s <a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
    id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota⑥" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>
    to `serialized`.\[\[Quota\]\].

3.  Set `value`’s <a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
    id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">requested</a> to
    `serialized`.\[\[Requested\]\].

</div>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Specifications that
<a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">create</a> or
<a href="#dfn-throw" id="ref-for-dfn-throw⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a
<a href="#quotaexceedederror" id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">QuotaExceededError</code></a>
must not provide a <a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">requested</a> and
<a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota⑦" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>
that are both non-null and where <a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">requested</a> is less than
<a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota⑧" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>.

### <span class="secno">2.9. </span><span class="content">Enumerations</span><a href="#idl-enums" class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="dfn-enumeration" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">enumeration</span> is a definition (matching
[Enum](#prod-Enum)) used to declare a type whose valid values are a set
of predefined strings. Enumerations can be used to restrict the possible
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> values that
can be assigned to an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> or passed to an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>.

``` highlight
enum identifier { "enum", "values" /* , ... */ };
```

The <span id="dfn-enumeration-value" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export=""
lt="enumeration value|enumeration’s values">enumeration values</span>
are specified as a comma-separated list of [string](#prod-string)
literals. The list of
<a href="#dfn-enumeration-value" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration-value②"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration values</a> must not include duplicates.

It is strongly suggested that enumeration values be all lowercase, and
that multiple words be separated using dashes or not be separated at
all, unless there is a specific reason to use another value naming
scheme. For example, an enumeration value that indicates an object
should be created could be named "`createobject`" or "`create-object`".
Consider related uses of enumeration values when deciding whether to
dash-separate or not separate enumeration value words so that similar
APIs are consistent.

The behavior when a string value that is not a valid enumeration value
is used when assigning to an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a>, or passed as an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> argument, whose type is the
enumeration, is language binding specific.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> In the JavaScript binding, assignment
of an invalid string value to an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③①"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> is ignored, while passing such a
value in other contexts (for example as an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> argument) results in an exception
being thrown.

No
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②③"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> defined in this
specification are applicable to
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">enumerations</a>.

``` grammar
Enum ::
    enum identifier { EnumValueList } ;
```

``` grammar
EnumValueList ::
    string EnumValueListComma
```

``` grammar
EnumValueListComma ::
    , EnumValueListString
    ε
```

``` grammar
EnumValueListString ::
    string EnumValueListComma
    ε
```

<div id="example-43a649e6" class="example">

<a href="#example-43a649e6" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration①①"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a> that is used as the type of an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③②"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> and an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation③①"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> argument:

``` highlight
enum MealType { "rice", "noodles", "other" };

[Exposed=Window]
interface Meal {
  attribute MealType type;
  attribute double size;     // in grams

  undefined initialize(MealType type, double size);
};
```

A JavaScript implementation would restrict the strings that can be
assigned to the type property or passed to the initializeMeal function
to those identified in the
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration①②"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a>.

``` highlight
var meal = getMeal();                // Get an instance of Meal.

meal.initialize("rice", 200);        // Operation invoked as normal.

try {
  meal.initialize("sandwich", 100);  // Throws a TypeError.
} catch (e) {
}

meal.type = "noodles";               // Attribute assigned as normal.
meal.type = "dumplings";             // Attribute assignment ignored.
meal.type == "noodles";              // Evaluates to true.
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.10. </span><span class="content">Callback functions</span><a href="#idl-callback-functions" class="self-link"></a>

The “Custom DOM Elements” spec wants to use callback function types for
platform object provided functions. Should we rename “callback
functions” to just “functions” to make it clear that they can be used
for both purposes?

A <span id="dfn-callback-function" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">callback function</span> is a definition
(matching callback [CallbackRest](#prod-CallbackRest)) used to declare a
function type.

``` highlight
callback identifier = return_type (/* arguments... */);
```

<span class="marker">Note:</span> See also the similarly named
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②②"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interfaces</a>.

The <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④④"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> on the left of the equals sign gives
the name of the
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> and the return type and
argument list (matching [Type](#prod-Type) and
[ArgumentList](#prod-ArgumentList)) on the right side of the equals sign
gives the signature of the callback function type.

<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">Callback functions</a> must not be used as the type
of a <a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant③③"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a>.

The following extended attribute is applicable to callback functions:
\[<a href="#LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull"
id="ref-for-LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull</code></a>\].

<div>

``` grammar
CallbackOrInterfaceOrMixin ::
    callback CallbackRestOrInterface
    interface InterfaceOrMixin
```

</div>

<div>

</div>

``` grammar
CallbackRest ::
    identifier = Type ( ArgumentList ) ;
```

<div id="example-9e6fa35f" class="example">

<a href="#example-9e6fa35f" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines a
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> used for an API that invokes
a user-defined function when an operation is complete.

``` highlight
callback AsyncOperationCallback = undefined (DOMString status);

[Exposed=Window]
interface AsyncOperations {
  undefined performOperation(AsyncOperationCallback whenFinished);
};
```

In the JavaScript language binding, a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object②" data-link-type="dfn">function object</a>
is passed as the operation argument.

``` highlight
var ops = getAsyncOperations();  // Get an instance of AsyncOperations.

ops.performOperation(function(status) {
  window.alert("Operation finished, status is " + status + ".");
});
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.11. </span><span class="content">Typedefs</span><a href="#idl-typedefs" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-typedef" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">typedef</span> is a definition (matching
[Typedef](#prod-Typedef)) used to declare a new name for a type. This
new name is not exposed by language bindings; it is purely used as a
shorthand for referencing the type in the IDL.

``` highlight
typedef type identifier;
```

The <span id="type-being-given-a-new-name" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">type being given a new name</span> is
specified after the typedef keyword (matching
[TypeWithExtendedAttributes](#prod-Type)), and the
[identifier](#prod-identifier) token following the type gives the name.

The [Type](#prod-Type) must not be the identifier of the same or another
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef①②"
data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a>.

No
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②④"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> defined in this
specification are applicable to
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef①③"
data-link-type="dfn">typedefs</a>.

``` grammar
Typedef ::
    typedef TypeWithExtendedAttributes identifier ;
```

<div id="example-1aa575d3" class="example">

<a href="#example-1aa575d3" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> demonstrates the use of
<a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef①④"
data-link-type="dfn">typedefs</a> to allow the use of a short
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> instead of a long
<a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">sequence type</a>.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Point {
  attribute double x;
  attribute double y;
};

typedef sequence<Point> Points;

[Exposed=Window]
interface Widget {
  boolean pointWithinBounds(Point p);
  boolean allPointsWithinBounds(Points ps);
};
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.12. </span><span class="content">Objects implementing interfaces</span><a href="#idl-objects" class="self-link"></a>

In a given implementation of a set of
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a>, an object can be described as
being a <a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object③"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a>.

<span id="dfn-platform-object" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="" lt="platform object">Platform objects</span> are objects that
implement an <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface⑨⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>.

<span id="dfn-legacy-platform-object" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">Legacy platform objects</span> are
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object④"
data-link-type="dfn">platform objects</a> that implement an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> which does not have a
\[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>, and which
<a href="#dfn-support-indexed-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-indexed-properties⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">supports indexed properties</a>,
<a href="#dfn-support-named-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-named-properties②" data-link-type="dfn">named
properties</a>, or both.

In a browser, for example, the browser-implemented DOM objects
(implementing interfaces such as `Node` and `Document`) that provide
access to a web page’s contents to JavaScript running in the page would
be <a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">platform objects</a>. These objects might be exotic
objects, implemented in a language like C++, or they might be native
JavaScript objects. Regardless, an implementation of a given set of IDL
fragments needs to be able to recognize all
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">platform objects</a> that are created by the
implementation. This might be done by having some internal state that
records whether a given object is indeed a platform object for that
implementation, or perhaps by observing that the object is implemented
by a given internal C++ class. How exactly platform objects are
recognized by a given implementation of a set of IDL fragments is
implementation specific.

All other objects in the system would not be treated as platform
objects. For example, assume that a web page opened in a browser loads a
JavaScript library that implements DOM Core. This library would be
considered to be a different implementation from the browser provided
implementation. The objects created by the JavaScript library that
implement the `Node` interface will not be treated as platform objects
that implement `Node` by the browser implementation.

<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②③"
data-link-type="dfn">Callback interfaces</a>, on the other hand, can be
implemented by any JavaScript object. This allows Web APIs to invoke
author-defined operations. For example, the DOM Events implementation
allows authors to register callbacks by providing objects that implement
the <a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#callbackdef-eventlistener"
id="ref-for-callbackdef-eventlistener①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">EventListener</code></a> interface.

### <span class="secno">2.13. </span><span class="content">Types</span><a href="#idl-types" class="self-link"></a>

This section lists the types supported by Web IDL, the set of values or
<a href="#biblio-infra" data-link-type="biblio"
title="Infra Standard">Infra</a> type corresponding to each type, and
how <a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant③④"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> of that type are represented.

The following types are known as <span id="dfn-integer-type"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">integer types</span>:
<a href="#idl-byte" id="ref-for-idl-byte" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">byte</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-octet" id="ref-for-idl-octet" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">octet</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-short" id="ref-for-idl-short" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">short</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-unsigned-short" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-short"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned short</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">long</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-unsigned-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-long-long"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">long long</code></a> and
<a href="#idl-unsigned-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long-long"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long long</code></a>.

The following types are known as <span id="dfn-numeric-type"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">numeric types</span>:
