the <a href="#dfn-integer-type" id="ref-for-dfn-integer-type①"
data-link-type="dfn">integer types</a>,
<a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">float</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> and
<a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>.

The <span id="dfn-primitive-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">primitive types</span> are
<a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a> and the
<a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">numeric types</a>.

The <span id="dfn-string-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">string types</span> are
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>, all
<a href="#idl-enumeration" id="ref-for-idl-enumeration"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration types</a>,
<a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a> and
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a>.

The <span id="buffer-types" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">buffer types</span> are
<a href="#idl-ArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-ArrayBuffer"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBuffer</code></a> and
<a href="#idl-SharedArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-SharedArrayBuffer"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SharedArrayBuffer</code></a>.

The <span id="dfn-typed-array-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">typed array types</span> are
<a href="#idl-Int8Array" id="ref-for-idl-Int8Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Int8Array</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-Int16Array" id="ref-for-idl-Int16Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Int16Array</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-Int32Array" id="ref-for-idl-Int32Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Int32Array</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-Uint8Array" id="ref-for-idl-Uint8Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Uint8Array</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-Uint16Array" id="ref-for-idl-Uint16Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Uint16Array</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-Uint32Array" id="ref-for-idl-Uint32Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Uint32Array</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-Uint8ClampedArray" id="ref-for-idl-Uint8ClampedArray"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Uint8ClampedArray</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-BigInt64Array" id="ref-for-idl-BigInt64Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">BigInt64Array</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-BigUint64Array" id="ref-for-idl-BigUint64Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">BigUint64Array</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-Float16Array" id="ref-for-idl-Float16Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Float16Array</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-Float32Array" id="ref-for-idl-Float32Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Float32Array</code></a>, and
<a href="#idl-Float64Array" id="ref-for-idl-Float64Array"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Float64Array</code></a>.

The <span id="buffer-view-types" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">buffer view types</span> are
<a href="#idl-DataView" id="ref-for-idl-DataView"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DataView</code></a> and the
<a href="#dfn-typed-array-type" id="ref-for-dfn-typed-array-type"
data-link-type="dfn">typed array types</a>.

The <span id="dfn-buffer-source-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">buffer source types</span> are the
<a href="#buffer-types" id="ref-for-buffer-types"
data-link-type="dfn">buffer types</a> and the
<a href="#buffer-view-types" id="ref-for-buffer-view-types"
data-link-type="dfn">buffer view types</a>.

The <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> type, all
<a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface types</a>, and all
<a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface types</a> are known as
<span id="dfn-object-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">object types</span>.

When conversions are made from language binding specific types to IDL
types in order to invoke an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation③②"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> or assign a value to an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③③"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a>, all conversions necessary will be
performed before the specified functionality of the operation or
attribute assignment is carried out. If the conversion cannot be
performed, then the operation will not run or the attribute will not be
updated. In some language bindings, type conversions could result in an
exception being thrown. In such cases, these exceptions will be
propagated to the code that made the attempt to invoke the operation or
assign to the attribute.

``` grammar
Type ::
    SingleType
    UnionType Null
```

``` grammar
TypeWithExtendedAttributes ::
    ExtendedAttributeList Type
```

``` grammar
SingleType ::
    DistinguishableType
    any
    PromiseType
```

``` grammar
UnionType ::
    ( UnionMemberType or UnionMemberType UnionMemberTypes )
```

``` grammar
UnionMemberType ::
    ExtendedAttributeList DistinguishableType
    UnionType Null
```

``` grammar
UnionMemberTypes ::
    or UnionMemberType UnionMemberTypes
    ε
```

``` grammar
DistinguishableType ::
    PrimitiveType Null
    StringType Null
    identifier Null
    sequence < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null
    async_sequence < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null
    object Null
    symbol Null
    BufferRelatedType Null
    FrozenArray < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null
    ObservableArray < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null
    RecordType Null
    undefined Null
```

<div>

``` grammar
ConstType ::
    PrimitiveType
    identifier
```

</div>

``` grammar
PrimitiveType ::
    UnsignedIntegerType
    UnrestrictedFloatType
    boolean
    byte
    octet
    bigint
```

``` grammar
UnrestrictedFloatType ::
    unrestricted FloatType
    FloatType
```

``` grammar
FloatType ::
    float
    double
```

``` grammar
UnsignedIntegerType ::
    unsigned IntegerType
    IntegerType
```

``` grammar
IntegerType ::
    short
    long OptionalLong
```

``` grammar
OptionalLong ::
    long
    ε
```

``` grammar
StringType ::
    ByteString
    DOMString
    USVString
```

``` grammar
PromiseType ::
    Promise < Type >
```

``` grammar
RecordType ::
    record < StringType , TypeWithExtendedAttributes >
```

``` grammar
Null ::
    ?
    ε
```

#### <span class="secno">2.13.1. </span><span id="dom-any" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">any</span><a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any②①" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> type is the union of all other possible
non-<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">union</a> types.

The <a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> type is like a discriminated union type, in
that each of its values has a specific
non-<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> type associated with it. For example, one
value of the
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> type is the
<a href="#idl-unsigned-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long</code></a> 150,
while another is the
<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">long</code></a> 150. These are distinct values.

The particular type of an
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> value is known as its
<span id="dfn-specific-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">specific type</span>. (Values of
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">union types</a> also have
<a href="#dfn-specific-type" id="ref-for-dfn-specific-type"
data-link-type="dfn">specific types</a>.)

#### <span class="secno">2.13.2. </span><span id="idl-void" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">undefined</span><a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined②④"
class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a> type has a
unique value.

<a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a> constant
values in IDL are represented with the undefined token.

<a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a> must not be
used as the type of an argument in any circumstance (in an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation③③"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>,
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a>, etc), or as the type of
a <a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a>, whether directly or in a
union. Instead, use an
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">optional argument</a> or a
non-<a href="#required-dictionary-member"
id="ref-for-required-dictionary-member⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">required</a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> This value was previously spelled
`void`, and more limited in how it was allowed to be used.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.3. </span><span id="dom-boolean" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">boolean</span><a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean②③" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a> type
corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#boolean" id="ref-for-boolean"
data-link-type="dfn">booleans</a>.

<a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a> constant
values in IDL are represented with the true and false tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.4. </span><span id="dom-byte" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">byte</span><a href="#idl-byte" id="ref-for-idl-byte⑧" class="self-link"></a>

The
<a href="#idl-byte" id="ref-for-idl-byte①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">byte</code></a> type corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#8-bit-signed-integer"
id="ref-for-8-bit-signed-integer" data-link-type="dfn">8-bit signed
integers</a>.

<a href="#idl-byte" id="ref-for-idl-byte②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">byte</code></a> constant values in IDL are represented with
[integer](#prod-integer) tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.5. </span><span id="dom-octet" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">octet</span><a href="#idl-octet" id="ref-for-idl-octet①②" class="self-link"></a>

The
<a href="#idl-octet" id="ref-for-idl-octet①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">octet</code></a> type corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#8-bit-unsigned-integer"
id="ref-for-8-bit-unsigned-integer" data-link-type="dfn">8-bit unsigned
integers</a>.

<a href="#idl-octet" id="ref-for-idl-octet②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">octet</code></a> constant values in IDL are represented with
[integer](#prod-integer) tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.6. </span><span id="dom-short" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">short</span><a href="#idl-short" id="ref-for-idl-short⑦" class="self-link"></a>

The
<a href="#idl-short" id="ref-for-idl-short①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">short</code></a> type corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#16-bit-signed-integer"
id="ref-for-16-bit-signed-integer" data-link-type="dfn">16-bit signed
integers</a>.

<a href="#idl-short" id="ref-for-idl-short②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">short</code></a> constant values in IDL are represented with
[integer](#prod-integer) tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.7. </span><span id="dom-unsignedshort" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">unsigned short</span><a href="#idl-unsigned-short" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-short③③"
class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-unsigned-short" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-short①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned short</code></a> type
corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#16-bit-unsigned-integer"
id="ref-for-16-bit-unsigned-integer" data-link-type="dfn">16-bit
unsigned integers</a>.

<a href="#idl-unsigned-short" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-short②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned short</code></a>
constant values in IDL are represented with [integer](#prod-integer)
tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.8. </span><span id="dom-long" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">long</span><a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long①⑥" class="self-link"></a>

The
<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">long</code></a> type corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#32-bit-signed-integer"
id="ref-for-32-bit-signed-integer" data-link-type="dfn">32-bit signed
integers</a>.

<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long①⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">long</code></a> constant values in IDL are represented with
[integer](#prod-integer) tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.9. </span><span id="dom-unsignedlong" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">unsigned long</span><a href="#idl-unsigned-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long①②"
class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-unsigned-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long</code></a> type
corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#32-bit-unsigned-integer"
id="ref-for-32-bit-unsigned-integer" data-link-type="dfn">32-bit
unsigned integers</a>.

<a href="#idl-unsigned-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long</code></a> constant
values in IDL are represented with [integer](#prod-integer) tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.10. </span><span id="dom-longlong" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">long long</span><a href="#idl-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-long-long①⓪"
class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-long-long①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">long long</code></a> type
corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#64-bit-signed-integer"
id="ref-for-64-bit-signed-integer" data-link-type="dfn">64-bit signed
integers</a>.

<a href="#idl-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-long-long②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">long long</code></a> constant
values in IDL are represented with [integer](#prod-integer) tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.11. </span><span id="dom-unsignedlonglong" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">unsigned long long</span><a href="#idl-unsigned-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long-long⑨"
class="self-link"></a>

The
<a href="#idl-unsigned-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long-long①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long long</code></a>
type corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#64-bit-unsigned-integer"
id="ref-for-64-bit-unsigned-integer" data-link-type="dfn">64-bit
unsigned integers</a>.

<a href="#idl-unsigned-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long-long②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long long</code></a>
constant values in IDL are represented with [integer](#prod-integer)
tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.12. </span><span id="dom-float" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">float</span><a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float⑨" class="self-link"></a>

The
<a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">float</code></a> type is a floating point numeric type that
corresponds to the set of finite single-precision 32-bit IEEE 754
floating point numbers.
<a href="#biblio-ieee-754" data-link-type="biblio"
title="IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic">[IEEE-754]</a>

<a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">float</code></a> constant values in IDL are represented with
[decimal](#prod-decimal) tokens.

Unless there are specific reasons to use a 32-bit floating point type,
specifications should use
<a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> rather than
<a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">float</code></a>, since the set of values that a
<a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> can represent
more closely matches a JavaScript Number.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.13. </span><span id="dom-unrestrictedfloat" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">unrestricted float</span><a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float①②"
class="self-link"></a>

The
<a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>
type is a floating point numeric type that corresponds to the set of all
possible single-precision 32-bit IEEE 754 floating point numbers,
finite, non-finite, and special "not a number" values (NaNs).
<a href="#biblio-ieee-754" data-link-type="biblio"
title="IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic">[IEEE-754]</a>

<a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>
constant values in IDL are represented with [decimal](#prod-decimal)
tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.14. </span><span id="dom-double" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">double</span><a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①⑧" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> type is a
floating point numeric type that corresponds to the set of finite
double-precision 64-bit IEEE 754 floating point numbers.
<a href="#biblio-ieee-754" data-link-type="biblio"
title="IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic">[IEEE-754]</a>

<a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> constant values
in IDL are represented with [decimal](#prod-decimal) tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.15. </span><span id="dom-unrestricteddouble" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">unrestricted double</span><a href="#idl-unrestricted-double"
id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double①④" class="self-link"></a>

The
<a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>
type is a floating point numeric type that corresponds to the set of all
possible double-precision 64-bit IEEE 754 floating point numbers,
finite, non-finite, and special "not a number" values (NaNs).
<a href="#biblio-ieee-754" data-link-type="biblio"
title="IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic">[IEEE-754]</a>

<a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>
constant values in IDL are represented with [decimal](#prod-decimal)
tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.16. </span><span class="content">bigint</span><a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint②③" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> type is an
arbitrary integer type, unrestricted in range.

<a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> constant values
in IDL are represented with [integer](#prod-integer) tokens.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.17. </span><span id="dom-DOMString" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">DOMString</span><a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString④⑥"
class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> type
corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string" id="ref-for-string"
data-link-type="dfn">strings</a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> null is not a value of type
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString①⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>. To allow
null, a <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①①"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a>
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>, written as
`DOMString?` in IDL, needs to be used.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> A
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> value might
include unmatched <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#surrogate"
id="ref-for-surrogate" data-link-type="dfn">surrogate</a>
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point"
id="ref-for-code-point①" data-link-type="dfn">code points</a>. Use
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a> if this is
not desirable.

There is no way to represent a constant
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> value in
IDL, although <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">default values</a> and
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">operation optional argument</a>
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">default values</a> can be set to
<a href="#value-of-string-literal-tokens"
id="ref-for-value-of-string-literal-tokens" data-link-type="dfn">the
value</a> of a [string](#prod-string) literal.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.18. </span><span id="dom-ByteString" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">ByteString</span><a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString①③"
class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a> type
corresponds to <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#byte-sequence"
id="ref-for-byte-sequence" data-link-type="dfn">byte sequences</a>.

There is no way to represent a constant
<a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a> value in
IDL, although <a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">default values</a> and
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument②①"
data-link-type="dfn">operation optional argument</a>
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">default values</a> can be set to
<a href="#value-of-string-literal-tokens"
id="ref-for-value-of-string-literal-tokens①" data-link-type="dfn">the
value</a> of a [string](#prod-string) literal.

Specifications should only use
<a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a> for
interfacing with protocols that use bytes and strings interchangeably,
such as HTTP. In general, strings should be represented with
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> values, even
if it is expected that values of the string will always be in ASCII or
some 8-bit character encoding.
<a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">Sequences</a> or
<a href="#dfn-frozen-array-type" id="ref-for-dfn-frozen-array-type③"
data-link-type="dfn">frozen arrays</a> with
<a href="#idl-octet" id="ref-for-idl-octet③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">octet</code></a> or
<a href="#idl-byte" id="ref-for-idl-byte③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">byte</code></a> elements,
<a href="#idl-Uint8Array" id="ref-for-idl-Uint8Array①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Uint8Array</code></a>, or
<a href="#idl-Int8Array" id="ref-for-idl-Int8Array①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Int8Array</code></a> should be
used for holding 8-bit data rather than
<a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a>.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.19. </span><span id="dom-USVString" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">USVString</span><a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString①⑥"
class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a> type
corresponds to
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value-string"
id="ref-for-scalar-value-string" data-link-type="dfn">scalar value
strings</a>. Depending on the context, these can be treated as sequences
of <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit"
id="ref-for-code-unit" data-link-type="dfn">code units</a> or
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
id="ref-for-scalar-value⑦" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>.

There is no way to represent a constant
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a> value in
IDL, although <a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">default values</a> and
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument②②"
data-link-type="dfn">operation optional argument</a>
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">default values</a> can be set to
<a href="#value-of-string-literal-tokens"
id="ref-for-value-of-string-literal-tokens②" data-link-type="dfn">the
value</a> of a [string](#prod-string) literal.

Specifications should only use
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a> for APIs
that perform text processing and need a string of
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
id="ref-for-scalar-value⑧" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a> to
operate on. Most APIs that use strings should instead be using
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>, which does
not make any interpretations of the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit"
id="ref-for-code-unit①" data-link-type="dfn">code units</a> in the
string. When in doubt, use
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.20. </span><span id="dom-object" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">object</span><a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object②⑧" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> type
corresponds to the set of all possible non-null object references.

There is no way to represent a constant
<a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> value in IDL.

To denote a type that includes all possible object references plus the
null value, use the
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①②"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a> `object?`.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.21. </span><span class="content">symbol</span><a href="#idl-symbol" id="ref-for-idl-symbol" class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-symbol" id="ref-for-idl-symbol⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">symbol</code></a> type
corresponds to the set of all possible symbol values. Symbol values are
opaque, non-<a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> values which
nevertheless have identity (i.e., are only equal to themselves).

There is no way to represent a constant
<a href="#idl-symbol" id="ref-for-idl-symbol①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">symbol</code></a> value in IDL.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.22. </span><span class="content">Interface types</span><a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface②⑤"
class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> that identifies an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> is used to refer to a type that
corresponds to the set of all possible non-null references to objects
that implement that interface.

An IDL value of the interface type is represented just by an object
reference.

There is no way to represent a constant object reference value for a
particular interface type in IDL.

To denote a type that includes all possible references to objects
implementing the given interface plus the null value, use a
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①③"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a>.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.23. </span><span class="content">Callback interface types</span><a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface①②"
class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> that identifies a
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②④"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> is used to refer to a type
that corresponds to the set of all possible non-null references to
objects.

An IDL value of the interface type is represented by a tuple of an
object reference and a <span id="dfn-callback-context"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">callback
context</span>. The
<a href="#dfn-callback-context" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-context"
data-link-type="dfn">callback context</a> is a language binding specific
value, and is used to store information about the execution context at
the time the language binding specific object reference is converted to
an IDL value.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> For JavaScript objects, the
<a href="#dfn-callback-context" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-context①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback context</a> is used to hold a reference to
the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#incumbent-settings-object"
id="ref-for-incumbent-settings-object" data-link-type="dfn">incumbent
settings object</a> at the time the Object value is converted to an IDL
callback interface type value. See [§ 3.2.16 Callback interface
types](#js-callback-interface).

There is no way to represent a constant object reference value for a
particular
<a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface②"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface type</a> in IDL.

To denote a type that includes all possible references to objects plus
the null value, use a
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①④"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a>.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.24. </span><span class="content">Dictionary types</span><a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary②①"
class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> that identifies a
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary</a> is used to refer to a type that
corresponds to the set of all dictionaries that adhere to the dictionary
definition.

The literal syntax for
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="ref-for-ordered-map④" data-link-type="dfn">ordered maps</a> may also
be used to represent dictionaries, when it is implicitly understood from
context that the map is being treated as an instance of a specific
dictionary type. However, there is no way to represent a constant
dictionary value inside IDL fragments.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.25. </span><span class="content">Enumeration types</span><a href="#idl-enumeration" id="ref-for-idl-enumeration②"
class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier④⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> that identifies an
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration①③"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a> is used to refer to a type whose
values are the set of strings (sequences of
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit"
id="ref-for-code-unit②" data-link-type="dfn">code units</a>, as with
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>) that are
the <a href="#dfn-enumeration-value" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration-value③"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration’s values</a>.

Like <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>, there is no
way to represent a constant
<a href="#dfn-enumeration" id="ref-for-dfn-enumeration①④"
data-link-type="dfn">enumeration</a> value in IDL, although
enumeration-typed
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member②①"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary member</a>
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">default values</a> and
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument" id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument②③"
data-link-type="dfn">operation optional argument</a>
<a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value①①"
data-link-type="dfn">default values</a> can be set to
<a href="#value-of-string-literal-tokens"
id="ref-for-value-of-string-literal-tokens③" data-link-type="dfn">the
value</a> of a [string](#prod-string) literal.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.26. </span><span class="content">Callback function types</span><a href="#idl-callback-function" id="ref-for-idl-callback-function"
class="self-link"></a>

An <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> that identifies a
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> is used to refer to a type
whose values are references to objects that are functions with the given
signature.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> If the
\[<a href="#LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull"
id="ref-for-LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> is specified on the
<a href="#dfn-definition" id="ref-for-dfn-definition⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">definition</a> of the
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function②①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>, the values can be references
to objects that are not functions.

An IDL value of the callback function type is represented by a tuple of
an object reference and a
<a href="#dfn-callback-context" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-context②"
data-link-type="dfn">callback context</a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> As with
<a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface③"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface types</a>, the
<a href="#dfn-callback-context" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-context③"
data-link-type="dfn">callback context</a> is used to hold a reference to
the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#incumbent-settings-object"
id="ref-for-incumbent-settings-object①" data-link-type="dfn">incumbent
settings object</a> at the time a JavaScript Object value is converted
to an IDL callback function type value. See [§ 3.2.19 Callback function
types](#js-callback-function).

There is no way to represent a constant
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function②②"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> value in IDL.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.27. </span><span class="content">Nullable types — `T`?</span><a href="#idl-nullable-type" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-nullable-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">nullable type</span> is an IDL type constructed from an
existing type (called the <span id="dfn-inner-type"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="nullable types" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">inner type</span>), which just allows the additional value
null to be a member of its set of values.
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">Nullable types</a> are represented in IDL by
placing a U+003F (?) character after an existing type. The
<a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> must not be:

- <a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
  class="idl">any</code></a>,

- a <a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type④"
  data-link-type="dfn">promise type</a>,

- an <a href="#dfn-observable-array-type"
  id="ref-for-dfn-observable-array-type" data-link-type="dfn">observable
  array type</a>,

- another nullable type, or

- a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②①"
  data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> that itself
  <a href="#dfn-includes-a-nullable-type"
  id="ref-for-dfn-includes-a-nullable-type②" data-link-type="dfn">includes
  a nullable type</a> or has a dictionary type as one of its
  <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
  id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Although dictionary types can in
general be nullable, they cannot when used as the type of an operation
argument or a dictionary member.

Nullable type constant values in IDL are represented in the same way
that constant values of their
<a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> would be represented, or with the
null token.

<div id="example-93b2f0cf" class="example">

<a href="#example-93b2f0cf" class="self-link"></a>

For example, a type that allows the values true, false and null is
written as `boolean?`:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface NetworkFetcher {
  undefined get(optional boolean? areWeThereYet = false);
};
```

The following <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> has two
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③④"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>: one whose value can be a
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString②⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> or the null
value, and another whose value can be a reference to a `Node` object or
the null value:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Node {
  readonly attribute DOMString? namespaceURI;
  readonly attribute Node? parentNode;
  // ...
};
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.13.28. </span><span id="dom-sequence" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Sequence types — sequence\<`T`\></span><a href="#idl-sequence" id="ref-for-idl-sequence" class="self-link"></a>

The <span id="sequence-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="" lt="sequence type">sequence\<`T`\></span> type is a
parameterized type whose values are (possibly zero-length)
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">lists</a> of values of type `T`.

Sequences are always passed by value. In language bindings where a
sequence is represented by an object of some kind, passing a sequence to
a <a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> will not result in a reference
to the sequence being kept by that object. Similarly, any sequence
returned from a platform object will be a copy and modifications made to
it will not be visible to the platform object.

The literal syntax for
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">lists</a> may also be used to represent sequences,
when it is implicitly understood from context that the list is being
treated as a sequences. However, there is no way to represent a constant
sequence value inside IDL fragments.

Sequences must not be used as the type of an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> or
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant③⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> This restriction exists so that it is
clear to specification writers and API users that
<a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">sequences</a> are copied rather than having
references to them passed around. Instead of a writable
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> of a sequence type, it is suggested
that a pair of <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation③④"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> to get and set the sequence is used.

Any <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">list</a> can be implicitly treated as a
`sequence<``T``>`, as long as it contains only
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-item"
id="ref-for-list-item⑤" data-link-type="dfn">items</a> that are of type
`T`.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.29. </span><span class="content">Async sequence types — async_sequence\<`T`\></span><a href="#idl-async-iterable-type" id="ref-for-idl-async-iterable-type"
class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="async-sequence-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">async sequence type</span> is a parameterized type whose
values are references to objects that can produce an asynchronously
iterable, possibly infinite, sequence of values of type `T`.

Unlike <a href="#idl-sequence" id="ref-for-idl-sequence③"
data-link-type="dfn">sequences</a>, which are fixed-length lists where
all values are known in advance, the asynchronously iterable sequences
created by async sequences are lazy. Their values may be produced
asynchronously only during iteration, and thus the values or length
might not be known at the time the async sequence is created.

Async sequences are passed by reference in language bindings where they
are represented by an object. This means that passing an async sequence
to a <a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> will result in a reference to
the async sequence being kept by that object. Similarly, any async
sequence returned from a platform object will be a reference to the same
object and modifications made to it will be visible to the platform
object. This is in contrast to sequences, which are always passed by
value.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Async sequences cannot be constructed
from IDL. If returned from an operation, or used as the type of a
dictionary member, the async sequence will have originated from the host
environment and have been turned into an IDL type via a language
binding. Instead of returning an async sequence from an IDL operation,
the operation might want to return an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that has an
<a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration①④"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a>.

Async sequences must not be used as the type of an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> or
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant③⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a>.

There is no way to represent an async sequence value in IDL.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.30. </span><span class="content">Record types — record\<`K`, `V`\></span><a href="#idl-record" id="ref-for-idl-record①⓪" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="record-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">record type</span> is a parameterized type whose values are
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="ref-for-ordered-map⑤" data-link-type="dfn">ordered maps</a> with
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-getting-the-keys"
id="ref-for-map-getting-the-keys②" data-link-type="dfn">keys</a> that
are instances of `K` and
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-getting-the-values"
id="ref-for-map-getting-the-values②" data-link-type="dfn">values</a>
that are instances of `V`. `K` must be one of
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>,
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a>, or
<a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a>.

The literal syntax for
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="ref-for-ordered-map⑥" data-link-type="dfn">ordered maps</a> may also
be used to represent records, when it is implicitly understood from
context that the map is being treated as a record. However, there is no
way to represent a constant record value inside IDL fragments.

Records are always passed by value. In language bindings where a record
is represented by an object of some kind, passing a record to a
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> will not result in a reference
to the record being kept by that object. Similarly, any record returned
from a platform object will be a copy and modifications made to it will
not be visible to the platform object.

Records must not be used as the type of an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute③⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> or
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant③⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">constant</a>.

Any <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
id="ref-for-ordered-map⑦" data-link-type="dfn">ordered map</a> can be
implicitly treated as a `record<``K``, ``V``>`, as long as it contains
only <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-entry"
id="ref-for-map-entry⑥" data-link-type="dfn">entries</a> whose
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-getting-the-keys"
id="ref-for-map-getting-the-keys③" data-link-type="dfn">keys</a> are all
of of type `K` and whose
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-getting-the-values"
id="ref-for-map-getting-the-values③" data-link-type="dfn">values</a> are
all of type `V`.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.31. </span><span id="dom-promise" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Promise types — Promise\<`T`\></span><a href="#idl-promise" id="ref-for-idl-promise②①" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-promise-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">promise type</span> is a parameterized type whose values are
references to objects that “is used as a place holder for the eventual
results of a deferred (and possibly asynchronous) computation result of
an asynchronous operation”. See [section
25.4](https://tc39.github.io/ecma262/#sec-promise-objects) of the
JavaScript specification for details on the semantics of promise
objects.

Promise types are non-nullable, but `T` may be nullable.

There is no way to represent a promise value in IDL.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.32. </span><span class="content">Union types</span><a href="#idl-union" class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-union-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">union type</span> is a type whose set of values is the union
of those in two or more other types. Union types (matching
[UnionType](#prod-UnionType)) are written as a series of types separated
by the or keyword with a set of surrounding parentheses. The types which
comprise the union type are known as the union’s
<span id="dfn-union-member-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="union"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">member types</span>.

<div class="note" role="note">

For example, you might write `(Node or DOMString)` or
`(double or sequence<double>)`. When applying a ? suffix to a
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②②"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> as a whole, it is placed after the
closing parenthesis, as in `(Node or DOMString)?`.

Note that the
<a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type③"
data-link-type="dfn">member types</a> of a union type do not descend
into nested union types. So for
`(double or (sequence<long> or Event) or (Node or DOMString)?)` the
member types are `double`, `(sequence<long> or Event)` and
`(Node or DOMString)?`.

</div>

Like the
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> type, values of union types have a
<a href="#dfn-specific-type" id="ref-for-dfn-specific-type①"
data-link-type="dfn">specific type</a>, which is the particular
<a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type④"
data-link-type="dfn">member type</a> that matches the value.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="flattened member types"
algorithm-for="union">

The <span id="dfn-flattened-union-member-types" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="union" dfn-type="dfn" export="">flattened member types</span>
of a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②③"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>, possibly
<a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types②"
data-link-type="dfn">annotated</a>, is a set of types determined as
follows:

1.  Let `T` be the
    <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②④"
    data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>.

2.  Initialize `S` to ∅.

3.  For each
    <a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">member type</a> `U` of `T`:

    1.  If `U` is an
        <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types③"
        data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a>, then set `U` to be the
        <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
        id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type②" data-link-type="dfn">inner
        type</a> of `U`.

    2.  If `U` is a
        <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①⑥"
        data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a>, then set `U` to be the
        <a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type⑨"
        data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> of `U`.

    3.  If `U` is a
        <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②⑤"
        data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>, then add to `S` the
        <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
        id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types⑦"
        data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a> of `U`.

    4.  Otherwise, `U` is not a
        <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②⑥"
        data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>. Add `U` to `S`.

4.  Return `S`.

</div>

<span class="marker">Note:</span> For example, the
<a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a> of the
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>
`(Node or (sequence<long> or Event) or (XMLHttpRequest or DOMString)? or sequence<(sequence<double> or NodeList)>)`
are the six types `Node`, `sequence<long>`, `Event`, `XMLHttpRequest`,
`DOMString` and `sequence<(sequence<double> or NodeList)>`.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="number of nullable member types">

The <span id="dfn-number-of-nullable-member-types"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">number of nullable
member types</span> of a
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> is an integer determined as follows:

1.  Let `T` be the
    <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type②⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>.

2.  Initialize `n` to 0.

3.  For each
    <a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">member type</a> `U` of `T`:

    1.  If `U` is a
        <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①⑦"
        data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a>, then:

        1.  Set `n` to `n` + 1.

        2.  Set `U` to be the
            <a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type①⓪"
            data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a> of `U`.

    2.  If `U` is a
        <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type③⓪"
        data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>, then:

        1.  Let `m` be the
            <a href="#dfn-number-of-nullable-member-types"
            id="ref-for-dfn-number-of-nullable-member-types"
            data-link-type="dfn">number of nullable member types</a> of
            `U`.

        2.  Set `n` to `n` + `m`.

4.  Return `n`.

</div>

The <a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> type must not be used as a
<a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">union member type</a>.

The <a href="#dfn-number-of-nullable-member-types"
id="ref-for-dfn-number-of-nullable-member-types①"
data-link-type="dfn">number of nullable member types</a> of a
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type③①"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> must be 0 or 1, and if it is 1 then
the union type must also not have a
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary①①"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a> in its
<a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>.

A type <span id="dfn-includes-a-nullable-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">includes a nullable type</span> if:

- the type is a
  <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a>, or

- the type is an
  <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types④"
  data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a> and its
  <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
  id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type③" data-link-type="dfn">inner
  type</a> is a nullable type, or

- the type is a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type③②"
  data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> and its
  <a href="#dfn-number-of-nullable-member-types"
  id="ref-for-dfn-number-of-nullable-member-types②"
  data-link-type="dfn">number of nullable member types</a> is 1.

Each pair of <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a> in a
<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type③③"
data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>, `T` and `U`, must be
<a href="#dfn-distinguishable" id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishable③"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishable</a>.

It is possible to create a union of
<a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> and a
<a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">numeric type</a>. However, this is generally only
supposed to be used for interfaces such as
[NumberFormat](https://tc39.es/ecma402/#numberformat-objects), which
formats the values rather than using them in calculations. It would not
be appropriate to accept such a union, only to then convert values of
the <a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">numeric type</a> to a
<a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> for further
processing, as this runs the risk of introducing precision errors.
Please [file an
issue](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/new?title=Intent%20to%20use%20bigint/numeric%20union)
before using this feature.

A type <span id="dfn-includes-undefined" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">includes undefined</span> if:

- the type is <a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined④"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a>, or

- the type is a
  <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type①⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a> and its
  <a href="#dfn-inner-type" id="ref-for-dfn-inner-type①①"
  data-link-type="dfn">inner type</a>
  <a href="#dfn-includes-undefined" id="ref-for-dfn-includes-undefined"
  data-link-type="dfn">includes undefined</a>, or

- the type is an
  <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a> and its
  <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
  id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type④" data-link-type="dfn">inner
  type</a>
  <a href="#dfn-includes-undefined" id="ref-for-dfn-includes-undefined①"
  data-link-type="dfn">includes undefined</a>, or

- the type is a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type③④"
  data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> and one of its
  <a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">member types</a>
  <a href="#dfn-includes-undefined" id="ref-for-dfn-includes-undefined②"
  data-link-type="dfn">includes undefined</a>.

<a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type③⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">Union type</a> constant values in IDL are
represented in the same way that constant values of their
<a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">member types</a> would be represented.

<div>

``` grammar
UnionType ::
    ( UnionMemberType or UnionMemberType UnionMemberTypes )
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
UnionMemberType ::
    ExtendedAttributeList DistinguishableType
    UnionType Null
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
UnionMemberTypes ::
    or UnionMemberType UnionMemberTypes
    ε
```

</div>

<div>

``` grammar
DistinguishableType ::
    PrimitiveType Null
    StringType Null
    identifier Null
    sequence < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null
    async_sequence < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null
    object Null
    symbol Null
    BufferRelatedType Null
    FrozenArray < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null
    ObservableArray < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null
    RecordType Null
    undefined Null
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">2.13.33. </span><span class="content">Annotated types</span><a href="#idl-annotated-types" class="self-link"></a>

Additional types can be created from existing ones by specifying certain
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> on the existing types. Such
types are called <span id="annotated-types" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">annotated types</span>, and the types they
annotate are called <span id="annotated-types-inner-type"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="annotated types" dfn-type="dfn"
export="" lt="inner type">inner types</span>.

<div id="example-3082499a" class="example">

<a href="#example-3082499a" class="self-link"></a> `[Clamp] long`
defines a new <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a>, whose behavior is based on that
of the <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type⑤" data-link-type="dfn">inner
type</a>
<a href="#idl-long" id="ref-for-idl-long①①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">long</code></a>, but modified as specified by the
\[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\] extended attribute.

</div>

The following extended attributes are
<span id="extended-attributes-applicable-to-types"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attributes" dfn-type="dfn"
noexport="">applicable to types</span>:
\[<a href="#AllowResizable" id="ref-for-AllowResizable"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">AllowResizable</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#AllowShared" id="ref-for-AllowShared"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">AllowShared</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\],
\[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\], and
\[<a href="#LegacyNullToEmptyString" id="ref-for-LegacyNullToEmptyString"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNullToEmptyString</code></a>\].

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="extended attribute associated with"
algorithm-for="IDL type">

The <span id="idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="IDL type" dfn-type="dfn"
lt="extended attribute associated with|extended attributes associated with"
noexport="">extended attributes associated with</span> an IDL type
`type` are determined as follows:

1.  Let `extended attributes` be a new empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
    id="ref-for-ordered-set③" data-link-type="dfn">set</a>.

2.  If `type` appears as part of a
    [TypeWithExtendedAttributes](#prod-TypeWithExtendedAttributes)
    production, <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="ref-for-set-append③" data-link-type="dfn">append</a> each of the
    <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> present in the
    production’s [ExtendedAttributeList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeList) to
    `extended attributes`.

    <div id="example-92fcfefb" class="example">

    <a href="#example-92fcfefb" class="self-link"></a>
    ``` def
    [Exposed=Window]
    interface I {
        attribute [XAttr] long attrib;
        undefined f1(sequence<[XAttr] long> arg);
        undefined f2(optional [XAttr] long arg);

        maplike<[XAttr2] DOMString, [XAttr3] long>;
    };

    dictionary D {
        required [XAttr] long member;
    };
    ```

    </div>

3.  If `type` is a
    <a href="#dfn-union-member-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-member-type①⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">member type</a> of a
    <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type③⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> `U`,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="ref-for-set-append④" data-link-type="dfn">append</a> each of the
    <a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
    id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes associated with</a> `U` to
    `extended attributes`.

    <div id="example-2017de6a" class="example">

    <a href="#example-2017de6a" class="self-link"></a>
    ``` def
    [Exposed=Window]
    interface I {
        attribute [XAttr] (long or Node) attrib;
    };
    ```

    </div>

4.  If `type` appears as part of a [Type](#prod-Type) production
    directly within an [Argument](#prod-Argument) production,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="ref-for-set-append⑤" data-link-type="dfn">append</a> to
    `extended attributes` all of the
    <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute②⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> present in the
    production’s [ExtendedAttributeList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeList)
    that are <a href="#extended-attributes-applicable-to-types"
    id="ref-for-extended-attributes-applicable-to-types"
    data-link-type="dfn">applicable to types</a>.

    <div id="example-3f984a52" class="example">

    <a href="#example-3f984a52" class="self-link"></a>
    ``` def
    [Exposed=Window]
    interface I {
        undefined f([XAttr] long attrib);
    };
    ```

    Note that this is an example of this step only if \[`XAttr`\] is
    <a href="#extended-attributes-applicable-to-types"
    id="ref-for-extended-attributes-applicable-to-types①"
    data-link-type="dfn">applicable to types</a>; otherwise \[`XAttr`\]
    applies to the argument, and not the argument’s type.

    </div>

5.  If `type` appears as part of a [Type](#prod-Type) production
    directly within a [DictionaryMember](#prod-DictionaryMember)
    production, <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="ref-for-set-append⑥" data-link-type="dfn">append</a> to
    `extended attributes` all of the
    <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute③⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> present in the
    production’s [ExtendedAttributeList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeList)
    that are <a href="#extended-attributes-applicable-to-types"
    id="ref-for-extended-attributes-applicable-to-types②"
    data-link-type="dfn">applicable to types</a>.

    <div id="example-916df766" class="example">

    <a href="#example-916df766" class="self-link"></a>
    ``` def
    dictionary D {
        [XAttr] long member;
    };
    ```

    Note that this is an example of this step only if \[`XAttr`\] is
    <a href="#extended-attributes-applicable-to-types"
    id="ref-for-extended-attributes-applicable-to-types③"
    data-link-type="dfn">applicable to types</a>; otherwise \[`XAttr`\]
    applies to the dictionary member, and not the member’s type.

    </div>

6.  If `type` is a <a href="#dfn-typedef" id="ref-for-dfn-typedef①⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">typedef</a>,
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-append"
    id="ref-for-set-append⑦" data-link-type="dfn">append</a> the
    <a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
    id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with①"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes associated with</a> the
    <a href="#type-being-given-a-new-name"
    id="ref-for-type-being-given-a-new-name①" data-link-type="dfn">type
    being given a new name</a> to `extended attributes`.

    <div id="example-ee0b958b" class="example">

    <a href="#example-ee0b958b" class="self-link"></a>
    ``` def
    typedef [XAttr] long xlong;
    ```

    </div>

7.  Return `extended attributes`.

</div>

For any type, the <a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with②"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes associated with</a> it must
only contain
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute③①"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> that are
<a href="#extended-attributes-applicable-to-types"
id="ref-for-extended-attributes-applicable-to-types④"
data-link-type="dfn">applicable to types</a>.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.34. </span><span class="content">Buffer source types</span><a href="#idl-buffer-source-types" class="self-link"></a>

There are a number of types that correspond to sets of all possible
non-null references to objects that represent a buffer of data or a view
on to a buffer of data. The table below lists these types and the kind
of buffer or view they represent.

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Type | Kind of buffer |
| <span id="idl-ArrayBuffer" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`ArrayBuffer`</span> | An object that holds a pointer (which can be null) to a buffer of a fixed number of bytes |
| <span id="idl-SharedArrayBuffer" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`SharedArrayBuffer`</span> | An object that holds a pointer (which cannot be null) to a shared buffer of a fixed number of bytes |
| <span id="idl-DataView" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`DataView`</span> | A view on to a <a href="#buffer-types" id="ref-for-buffer-types①"
data-link-type="dfn">buffer type</a> instance that allows typed access to integers and floating point values stored at arbitrary offsets into the buffer |
| <span id="idl-Int8Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Int8Array`</span> | A view on to a <a href="#buffer-types" id="ref-for-buffer-types②"
data-link-type="dfn">buffer type</a> instance that exposes it as an array of two’s complement signed integers of the given size in bits |
| <span id="idl-Int16Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Int16Array`</span> |  |
| <span id="idl-Int32Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Int32Array`</span> |  |
| <span id="idl-BigInt64Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`BigInt64Array`</span> |  |
| <span id="idl-Uint8Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Uint8Array`</span> | A view on to a <a href="#buffer-types" id="ref-for-buffer-types③"
data-link-type="dfn">buffer type</a> instance that exposes it as an array of unsigned integers of the given size in bits |
| <span id="idl-Uint16Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Uint16Array`</span> |  |
| <span id="idl-Uint32Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Uint32Array`</span> |  |
| <span id="idl-BigUint64Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`BigUint64Array`</span> |  |
| <span id="idl-Uint8ClampedArray" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Uint8ClampedArray`</span> | A view on to a <a href="#buffer-types" id="ref-for-buffer-types④"
data-link-type="dfn">buffer type</a> instance that exposes it as an array of <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#8-bit-unsigned-integer"
id="ref-for-8-bit-unsigned-integer①" data-link-type="dfn">8-bit unsigned
integers</a> with clamped conversions |
| <span id="idl-Float16Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Float16Array`</span> | A view on to a <a href="#buffer-types" id="ref-for-buffer-types⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">buffer type</a> instance that exposes it as an array of IEEE 754 floating point numbers of the given size in bits; Float16Array corresponds to the ECMAScript proposal <a href="#biblio-proposal-float16array" data-link-type="biblio"
title="Proposal to add float16 TypedArrays to JavaScript">[PROPOSAL-FLOAT16ARRAY]</a>. |
| <span id="idl-Float32Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Float32Array`</span> |  |
| <span id="idl-Float64Array" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-type="interface" export="">`Float64Array`</span> |  |

<span class="marker">Note:</span> These types all correspond to classes
defined in JavaScript.

There is no way to represent a constant value of any of these types in
IDL.

At the specification prose level, IDL
<a href="#dfn-buffer-source-type" id="ref-for-dfn-buffer-source-type①"
data-link-type="dfn">buffer source types</a> are simply references to
objects. To inspect or manipulate the bytes inside the buffer,
specification prose needs to use the algorithms in [§ 3.2.26 Buffer
source types](#js-buffer-source-types).

``` grammar
BufferRelatedType ::
    ArrayBuffer
    SharedArrayBuffer
    DataView
    Int8Array
    Int16Array
    Int32Array
    Uint8Array
    Uint16Array
    Uint32Array
    Uint8ClampedArray
    BigInt64Array
    BigUint64Array
    Float16Array
    Float32Array
    Float64Array
```

#### <span class="secno">2.13.35. </span><span id="dom-FrozenArray" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Frozen array types — FrozenArray\<`T`\></span><a href="#idl-frozen-array" id="ref-for-idl-frozen-array"
class="self-link"></a>

A <span id="dfn-frozen-array-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">frozen array type</span> is a parameterized
type whose values are references to objects that hold a fixed length
array of unmodifiable values. The values in the array are of type `T`.

Frozen array types must only be used as the type of
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attributes</a> or
<a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">static attributes</a> defined on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>.

<div id="example-frozen-array" class="example">

<a href="#example-frozen-array" class="self-link"></a> The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with two frozen array attributes, one
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a> and one not.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface PersonalPreferences {
    readonly attribute FrozenArray<DOMString> favoriteColors;
    attribute FrozenArray<DOMString> favoriteFoods;

    undefined randomizeFavoriteColors();
};
```

The behavior of these attributes could be defined like so:

> Each `PersonalPreferences` has associated **favorite colors**, a
> <a href="#idl-frozen-array" id="ref-for-idl-frozen-array⑦"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">FrozenArray</code></a>\<<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③①"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>\>,
> initially equal to the result of
> <a href="#dfn-create-frozen-array" id="ref-for-dfn-create-frozen-array"
> data-link-type="dfn">creating a frozen array</a> from « "`purple`",
> "`aquamarine`" ».
>
> Each `PersonalPreferences` has an associated **favorite foods**, a
> <a href="#idl-frozen-array" id="ref-for-idl-frozen-array①"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">FrozenArray</code></a>\<<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③②"
> data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>\>,
> initially equal to the result of
> <a href="#dfn-create-frozen-array" id="ref-for-dfn-create-frozen-array①"
> data-link-type="dfn">creating a frozen array</a> from the empty list.
>
> The `favoriteColors`
> <a href="#getter-steps" id="ref-for-getter-steps③"
> data-link-type="dfn">getter steps</a> are to return
> <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this②⓪" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
> favorite colors.
>
> The `favoriteFoods` <a href="#getter-steps" id="ref-for-getter-steps④"
> data-link-type="dfn">getter steps</a> are to return
> <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this②①" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
> favorite foods.
>
> The `favoriteFoods` <a href="#setter-steps" id="ref-for-setter-steps③"
> data-link-type="dfn">setter steps</a> are to set
> <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this②②" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
> favorite foods to
> <a href="#the-given-value" id="ref-for-the-given-value①"
> data-link-type="dfn">the given value</a>.
>
> The `randomizeFavoriteColors()`
> <a href="#method-steps" id="ref-for-method-steps⑥"
> data-link-type="dfn">method steps</a> are:
>
> 1.  Let `newFavoriteColors` be a list of two strings representing
>     colors, chosen randomly.
>
> 2.  Set
>     <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this②③" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
>     favorite colors to the result of
>     <a href="#dfn-create-frozen-array" id="ref-for-dfn-create-frozen-array②"
>     data-link-type="dfn">creating a frozen array</a> from
>     `newFavoriteColors`.

</div>

Since <a href="#idl-frozen-array" id="ref-for-idl-frozen-array②"
class="idl-code"
data-link-type="interface">FrozenArray&lt;<var>T</var>&gt;</a> values
are references, they are unlike
<a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">sequence types</a>, which are lists of values that
are passed by value.

There is no way to represent a constant frozen array value in IDL.

#### <span class="secno">2.13.36. </span><span class="content">Observable array types — ObservableArray\<`T`\></span><a href="#idl-observable-array" id="ref-for-idl-observable-array"
class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="dfn-observable-array-type" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">observable array type</span> is a parameterized
type whose values are references to a combination of a mutable list of
objects of type `T`, as well as behavior to perform when author code
modifies the contents of the list.

The parameterized type `T` must not be a
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary①②"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a>,
<a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type①①"
data-link-type="dfn">sequence type</a>,
<a href="#record-type" id="ref-for-record-type②"
data-link-type="dfn">record type</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-observable-array-type"
id="ref-for-dfn-observable-array-type①" data-link-type="dfn">observable
array type</a>. However, `T` may be nullable.

Similar to <a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type①②"
data-link-type="dfn">sequence types</a> and
<a href="#dfn-frozen-array-type" id="ref-for-dfn-frozen-array-type④"
data-link-type="dfn">frozen array types</a>, observable array types wrap
around JavaScript array types, imposing additional semantics on their
usage.

Observable array types must only be used as the type of
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attributes</a> defined on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>.

For an attribute whose type is an observable array type, specification
authors can specify a series of algorithms:

- <span id="observable-array-attribute-set-an-indexed-value"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="observable array attribute"
  dfn-type="dfn" export="">set an indexed value</span>, which accepts an
  IDL value that is about to be set in the observable array, and the
  index at which it is being set;

- <span id="observable-array-attribute-delete-an-indexed-value"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="observable array attribute"
  dfn-type="dfn" export="">delete an indexed value</span>, which accepts
  an IDL value that is about to be removed from the observable array,
  and the index from which it is being removed.

Both of these algorithms are optional, and if not provided, the default
behavior will be to do nothing. Either algorithm may throw an exception,
e.g., to reject invalid values.

Note that when JavaScript code sets an existing index to a new value,
this will first call the
<a href="#observable-array-attribute-delete-an-indexed-value"
id="ref-for-observable-array-attribute-delete-an-indexed-value"
data-link-type="dfn">delete an indexed value</a> algorithm to remove the
existing value, and then the
<a href="#observable-array-attribute-set-an-indexed-value"
id="ref-for-observable-array-attribute-set-an-indexed-value"
data-link-type="dfn">set an indexed value</a> algorithm with the new
value.

Every
