<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a> whose type is an
<a href="#dfn-observable-array-type"
id="ref-for-dfn-observable-array-type②" data-link-type="dfn">observable
array type</a> has a <span id="observable-array-attribute-backing-list"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="observable array attribute"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">backing list</span>, which is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">list</a>, initially empty. Specification authors
can modify the contents of the backing list, which will automatically be
reflected in the contents of the observable array as observed by
JavaScript code. Similarly, any modifications by JavaScript code to the
contents of the observable array will be reflected back into the backing
list, after passing through the
<a href="#observable-array-attribute-set-an-indexed-value"
id="ref-for-observable-array-attribute-set-an-indexed-value①"
data-link-type="dfn">set an indexed value</a> and
<a href="#observable-array-attribute-delete-an-indexed-value"
id="ref-for-observable-array-attribute-delete-an-indexed-value①"
data-link-type="dfn">delete an indexed value</a> algorithms.

There is no way to represent a constant observable array value in IDL.

<div id="example-observable-array" class="example">

<a href="#example-observable-array" class="self-link"></a>
<span id="example-af5d265e"></span> The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③①"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with an observable array attribute:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Building {
  attribute ObservableArray<Employee> employees;
};
```

The behavior of the attribute could be defined like so:

> The <a href="#observable-array-attribute-set-an-indexed-value"
> id="ref-for-observable-array-attribute-set-an-indexed-value②"
> data-link-type="dfn">set an indexed value</a> algorithm for
> `Building`’s `employees` attribute, given `employee` and `index`, is:
>
> 1.  If `employee` is not allowed to enter the building today, then
>     throw a "<a href="#notallowederror" id="ref-for-notallowederror④"
>     data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">NotAllowedError</code></a>"
>     <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException③⑨"
>     data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>.
>
> 2.  If `index` is greater than or equal to 200, then throw a
>     <a href="#quotaexceedederror" id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror⑨"
>     data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">QuotaExceededError</code></a>
>     whose <a href="#quotaexceedederror-quota"
>     id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-quota⑨" data-link-type="dfn">quota</a>
>     is 200 and <a href="#quotaexceedederror-requested"
>     id="ref-for-quotaexceedederror-requested⑨"
>     data-link-type="dfn">requested</a> is `index`.
>
> 3.  Put `employee` to work!
>
> The <a href="#observable-array-attribute-delete-an-indexed-value"
> id="ref-for-observable-array-attribute-delete-an-indexed-value②"
> data-link-type="dfn">delete an indexed value</a> algorithm for
> `Building`’s `employees` attribute, given `employee` and `index`, is:
>
> 1.  Alert security that `employee` has left the building.

Then, JavaScript code could manipulate the `employees` property in
various ways:

``` highlight
// Get an instance of Building.
const building = getBuilding();

building.employees.push(new Employee("A"));
building.employees.push(new Employee("B"));
building.employees.push(new Employee("C"));

building.employees.splice(2, 1);
const employeeB = building.employees.pop();

building.employees = [new Employee("D"), employeeB, new Employee("C")];

building.employees.length = 0;

// Will throw:
building.employees.push("not an Employee; a string instead");
```

All of these manipulations would pass through the above-defined
<a href="#observable-array-attribute-set-an-indexed-value"
id="ref-for-observable-array-attribute-set-an-indexed-value③"
data-link-type="dfn">set an indexed value</a> algorithm, potentially
throwing if the conditions described there were met. They would also
perform the appropriate side effects listed there and in the
<a href="#observable-array-attribute-delete-an-indexed-value"
id="ref-for-observable-array-attribute-delete-an-indexed-value③"
data-link-type="dfn">delete an indexed value</a> algorithm.

Another thing to note about the above code example is how all of the
JavaScript array methods from <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/indexed-collections.html#sec-properties-of-the-array-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-sec-properties-of-the-array-prototype-object"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">%Array.prototype%</code></a> work
on the observable array. Indeed, it fully behaves like an `Array`
instance:

``` highlight
const normalArray = [];

// If building.employees were defined as an indexed property getter interface: normalArray
// would contains a single item, building.employees.
//
// For observable arrays (and frozen arrays): normalArray contains all of the items inside
// of building.employees.
normalArray.concat(building.employees);

// names is a JavaScript Array.
const names = building.employees.map(employee => employee.name);

// Passes various brand checks:
console.assert(building.employees instanceof Array);
console.assert(Array.isArray(building.employees));
console.assert(building.employees.constructor === Array);

// Even is treated as an array by JSON.stringify! (Note the outer []s.)
console.assert(JSON.stringify(building.employees) === `[{}]`);
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">2.14. </span><span class="content">Extended attributes</span><a href="#idl-extended-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

An <span id="dfn-extended-attribute" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">extended attribute</span> is an annotation that
can appear on <a href="#dfn-definition" id="ref-for-dfn-definition⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">definitions</a>, types as
<a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">annotated types</a>,
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface members</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin members</a>,
<a href="#callback-interface-member"
id="ref-for-callback-interface-member③" data-link-type="dfn">callback
interface members</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member④"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace members</a>,
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member②②"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary members</a>, and
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation③⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> arguments, and is used to control how
language bindings will handle those constructs. Extended attributes are
specified with an [ExtendedAttributeList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeList),
which is a square bracket enclosed, comma separated list of
[ExtendedAttribute](#prod-ExtendedAttribute)s.

The [ExtendedAttribute](#prod-ExtendedAttribute) grammar symbol matches
nearly any sequence of tokens, however the
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute③②"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> defined in this document
only accept a more restricted syntax. Any extended attribute encountered
in an <a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③②"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> is matched against the following
grammar symbols to determine which form (or forms) it is in:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
| Grammar symbol | Form | Example |
| [ExtendedAttributeNoArgs](#prod-ExtendedAttributeNoArgs) | <span id="dfn-xattr-no-arguments" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes no arguments</span> | `[Replaceable]` |
| [ExtendedAttributeArgList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeArgList) | <span id="dfn-xattr-argument-list" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes an argument list</span> | Not currently used; previously used by `[Constructor(double x, double y)]` |
| [ExtendedAttributeNamedArgList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeNamedArgList) | <span id="dfn-xattr-named-argument-list" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes a named argument list</span> | `[LegacyFactoryFunction=Image(DOMString src)]` |
| [ExtendedAttributeIdent](#prod-ExtendedAttributeIdent) | <span id="dfn-xattr-identifier" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes an identifier</span> | `[PutForwards=name]` |
| [ExtendedAttributeString](#prod-ExtendedAttributeString) | <span id="dfn-xattr-string" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes a string</span> | `[Reflect="popover"]` |
| [ExtendedAttributeInteger](#prod-ExtendedAttributeInteger) | <span id="dfn-xattr-integer" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes an integer</span> | `[ReflectDefault=2]` |
| [ExtendedAttributeDecimal](#prod-ExtendedAttributeDecimal) | <span id="dfn-xattr-decimal" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes a decimal</span> | `[ReflectDefault=2.0]` |
| [ExtendedAttributeIntegerList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeIntegerList) | <span id="dfn-xattr-integer-list" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes an integer list</span> | `[ReflectRange=(2, 600)]` |
| [ExtendedAttributeIdentList](#prod-ExtendedAttributeIdentList) | <span id="dfn-xattr-identifier-list" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes an identifier list</span> | `[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]` |
| [ExtendedAttributeWildcard](#prod-ExtendedAttributeWildcard) | <span id="dfn-xattr-wildcard" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="extended attribute" dfn-type="dfn" export="">takes a wildcard</span> | `[Exposed=*]` |

This specification defines a number of extended attributes that are
applicable to the JavaScript language binding, which are described in
[§ 3.3 Extended attributes](#js-extended-attributes). Each extended
attribute definition will state which of the above five forms are
allowed.

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeList ::
    [ ExtendedAttribute ExtendedAttributes ]
    ε
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributes ::
    , ExtendedAttribute ExtendedAttributes
    ε
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttribute ::
    ( ExtendedAttributeInner ) ExtendedAttributeRest
    [ ExtendedAttributeInner ] ExtendedAttributeRest
    { ExtendedAttributeInner } ExtendedAttributeRest
    Other ExtendedAttributeRest
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeRest ::
    ExtendedAttribute
    ε
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeInner ::
    ( ExtendedAttributeInner ) ExtendedAttributeInner
    [ ExtendedAttributeInner ] ExtendedAttributeInner
    { ExtendedAttributeInner } ExtendedAttributeInner
    OtherOrComma ExtendedAttributeInner
    ε
```

``` grammar
Other ::
    integer
    decimal
    identifier
    string
    other
    -
    -Infinity
    .
    ...
    :
    ;
    <
    =
    >
    ?
    *
    ByteString
    DOMString
    FrozenArray
    Infinity
    NaN
    ObservableArray
    Promise
    USVString
    any
    bigint
    boolean
    byte
    double
    false
    float
    long
    null
    object
    octet
    or
    optional
    record
    sequence
    short
    symbol
    true
    unsigned
    undefined
    ArgumentNameKeyword
    BufferRelatedType
```

``` grammar
OtherOrComma ::
    Other
    ,
```

``` grammar
IdentifierList ::
    identifier Identifiers
```

``` grammar
Identifiers ::
    , identifier Identifiers
    ε
```

``` grammar
IntegerList ::
    integer Integers
```

``` grammar
Integers ::
    , integer Integers
    ε
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeNoArgs ::
    identifier
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeArgList ::
    identifier ( ArgumentList )
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeIdent ::
    identifier = identifier
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeString ::
    identifier = string
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeInteger ::
    identifier = integer
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeDecimal ::
    identifier = decimal
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeWildcard ::
    identifier = *
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeIdentList ::
    identifier = ( IdentifierList )
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeIntegerList ::
    identifier = ( IntegerList )
```

``` grammar
ExtendedAttributeNamedArgList ::
    identifier = identifier ( ArgumentList )
```

## <span class="secno">3. </span><span id="ecmascript-binding" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">JavaScript binding</span><a href="#javascript-binding" class="self-link"></a>

This section describes how definitions written with the IDL defined in
[§ 2 Interface definition language](#idl) correspond to particular
constructs in JavaScript, as defined by the ECMAScript Language
Specification <a href="#biblio-ecma-262" data-link-type="biblio"
title="ECMAScript Language Specification">[ECMA-262]</a>.

Unless otherwise specified, objects defined in this section are ordinary
objects as described in [ECMAScript § 10.1 Ordinary Object Internal
Methods and Internal
Slots](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ordinary-and-exotic-objects-behaviours.html#sec-ordinary-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots),
and if the object is a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object③" data-link-type="dfn">function object</a>,
[ECMAScript § 10.3 Built-in Function
Objects](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ordinary-and-exotic-objects-behaviours.html#sec-built-in-function-objects).

This section may redefine certain internal methods and internal slots of
objects. Other specifications may also override the definitions of any
internal method or internal slots of a
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> that is an instance of an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>. These objects with changed semantics
shall be treated in accordance with the rules for exotic objects.

As overriding internal JavaScript object methods is a low level
operation and can result in objects that behave differently from
ordinary objects, this facility should not be used unless necessary for
security or compatibility. <span class="non-normative">This is currently
used to define the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#htmlallcollection"
id="ref-for-htmlallcollection" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">HTMLAllCollection</code></a> and <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#location"
id="ref-for-location" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Location</code></a> interfaces.
<a href="#biblio-html" data-link-type="biblio"
title="HTML Standard">[HTML]</a></span>

Unless otherwise specified, exotic objects defined in this section and
other specifications have the same <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinary-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots"
id="ref-for-sec-ordinary-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots"
data-link-type="dfn">internal slots</a> as ordinary objects, and all of
the internal methods for which alternative definitions are not given are
the same as <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinary-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots"
id="ref-for-sec-ordinary-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots①"
data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="4be80daa">those</a> of ordinary
objects.

Unless otherwise specified, the \[\[Extensible\]\] internal slot of
objects defined in this section has the value true.

Unless otherwise specified, the \[\[Prototype\]\] internal slot of
objects defined in this section is <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">%Object.prototype%</code></a>.

Some objects described in this section are defined to have a
<span id="dfn-class-string" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">class string</span>, which is the string to include in the
string returned from `Object.prototype.toString`.

If an object has a
<a href="#dfn-class-string" id="ref-for-dfn-class-string"
data-link-type="dfn">class string</a> `classString`, then the object
must, at the time it is created, have a property whose name is the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.toStringTag%</code></a> symbol with
PropertyDescriptor{\[\[Writable\]\]: false, \[\[Enumerable\]\]: false,
\[\[Configurable\]\]: true, \[\[Value\]\]: `classString`}.

Algorithms in this section use the conventions described in [ECMAScript
§ 5.2 Algorithm
Conventions](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/notational-conventions.html#sec-algorithm-conventions),
such as the use of steps and substeps, the use of mathematical
operations, and so on. This section may also reference abstract
operations and notations defined in other parts of ECMA-262.

When an algorithm says to <span id="javascript-throw"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="JavaScript" dfn-type="dfn"
local-lt="throw" lt="JavaScript throw|ECMAScript throw"
noexport=""><span id="ecmascript-throw"
class="bs-old-id"></span>throw</span> a `Something``Error` then this
means to construct a new JavaScript `Something``Error` object in the
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm"
id="ref-for-current-realm" data-link-type="dfn">current realm</a> and to
throw it, just as the algorithms in ECMA-262 do.

Note that algorithm steps can call in to other algorithms and abstract
operations and not explicitly handle exceptions that are thrown from
them. When an exception is thrown by an algorithm or abstract operation
and it is not explicitly handled by the caller, then it is taken to end
the algorithm and propagate out to its caller, and so on.

<div id="example-18239b52" class="example">

<a href="#example-18239b52" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="example algorithm">

Consider the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be the JavaScript value passed in to this algorithm.

2.  Let `y` be the result of calling
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tostring"
    id="ref-for-sec-tostring" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToString</a>(`x`).

3.  Return `y`.

</div>

Since <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tostring"
id="ref-for-sec-tostring①" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToString</a> can
throw an exception (for example if passed the object
`({ toString: function() { throw 1 } })`), and the exception is not
handled in the above algorithm, if one is thrown then it causes this
algorithm to end and for the exception to propagate out to its caller,
if there is one.

</div>

### <span class="secno">3.1. </span><span id="es-environment" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">JavaScript environment</span><a href="#js-environment" class="self-link"></a>

In a JavaScript implementation of a given set of
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③③"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a>, there will exist a number of
JavaScript objects that correspond to definitions in those
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③④"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a>. These objects are termed the
<span id="dfn-initial-object" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">initial objects</span>, and comprise the following:

- <a href="#dfn-interface-object" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-object②"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface objects</a>

- <a href="#dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object"
  id="ref-for-dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object"
  data-link-type="dfn">legacy callback interface objects</a>

- <a href="#dfn-legacy-factory-function"
  id="ref-for-dfn-legacy-factory-function①" data-link-type="dfn">legacy
  factory functions</a>

- <a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
  id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype objects</a>

- <a href="#dfn-named-properties-object"
  id="ref-for-dfn-named-properties-object" data-link-type="dfn">named
  properties objects</a>

- <a href="#dfn-iterator-prototype-object"
  id="ref-for-dfn-iterator-prototype-object" data-link-type="dfn">iterator
  prototype objects</a>

- <a href="#dfn-attribute-getter" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute-getter"
  data-link-type="dfn">attribute getters</a>

- <a href="#dfn-attribute-setter" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute-setter"
  data-link-type="dfn">attribute setters</a>

- [the function objects that correspond to operations](#js-operations)

- [the function objects that correspond to
  stringifiers](#js-stringifier)

Each <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm①" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a> must have its own
unique set of each of the
<a href="#dfn-initial-object" id="ref-for-dfn-initial-object"
data-link-type="dfn">initial objects</a>, created before control enters
any JavaScript execution context associated with the realm, but after
the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-global"
id="ref-for-concept-realm-global①" data-link-type="dfn">global
object</a> for that realm is created. The \[\[Prototype\]\]s of all
initial objects in a given <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm②" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a> must come from that
same <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm③" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a>.

<div id="example-9af59e92" class="example">

<a href="#example-9af59e92" class="self-link"></a>

In an HTML user agent, multiple <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm④" data-link-type="dfn">realms</a> can exist when
multiple frames or windows are created. Each frame or window will have
its own set of
<a href="#dfn-initial-object" id="ref-for-dfn-initial-object①"
data-link-type="dfn">initial objects</a>, which the following HTML
document demonstrates:

``` highlight
<!DOCTYPE html>
<title>Different Realms</title>
<iframe id=a></iframe>
<script>
var iframe = document.getElementById("a");
var w = iframe.contentWindow;              // The global object in the frame

Object == w.Object;                        // Evaluates to false, per ECMA-262
Node == w.Node;                            // Evaluates to false
iframe instanceof w.Node;                  // Evaluates to false
iframe instanceof w.Object;                // Evaluates to false
iframe.appendChild instanceof Function;    // Evaluates to true
iframe.appendChild instanceof w.Function;  // Evaluates to false
</script>
```

</div>

<span class="marker">Note:</span> All
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⓪⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> define which <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤" data-link-type="dfn">realms</a> they are
<a href="#dfn-exposed" id="ref-for-dfn-exposed①"
data-link-type="dfn">exposed</a> in. This allows, for example, <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑥" data-link-type="dfn">realms</a> for Web Workers to
<a href="#dfn-exposed" id="ref-for-dfn-exposed②"
data-link-type="dfn">expose</a> different sets of supported interfaces
from those exposed in realms for Web pages.

Although at the time of this writing the JavaScript specification does
not reflect this, every JavaScript object must have an
<span id="dfn-associated-realm" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">associated <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑦" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a></span>. The
mechanisms for associating objects with realms are, for now,
underspecified. However, we note that in the case of
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object①①"
data-link-type="dfn">platform objects</a>, the associated realm is equal
to the object’s <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-relevant-realm"
id="ref-for-concept-relevant-realm" data-link-type="dfn">relevant
realm</a>, and for non-exotic <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object④" data-link-type="dfn">function objects</a>
(i.e. not <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-iscallable"
id="ref-for-sec-iscallable①" data-link-type="dfn">callable</a> proxies,
and not bound functions) the associated realm is equal to the value of
the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object⑤" data-link-type="dfn">function object</a>’s
\[\[Realm\]\] internal slot.

### <span class="secno">3.2. </span><span id="es-type-mapping" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">JavaScript type mapping</span><a href="#js-type-mapping" class="self-link"></a>

This section describes how types in the IDL map to types in JavaScript.

Each sub-section below describes how values of a given IDL type are
represented in JavaScript. For each IDL type, it is described how
JavaScript values are <span id="dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export=""
lt="converted to an IDL value|converted to IDL values">converted to an
IDL value</span> when passed to a
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object①②"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> expecting that type, and how
IDL values of that type are
<span id="dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export=""
lt="converted to a JavaScript value|converted to JavaScript values|converted to an ECMAScript value|converted to ECMAScript values"><span id="dfn-convert-idl-to-ecmascript-value"
class="bs-old-id"></span>converted to JavaScript values</span> when
returned from a platform object.

Note that the sub-sections and algorithms below also apply to
<a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">annotated types</a> created by applying extended
attributes to the types named in their headers.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.1. </span><span id="es-any" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">any</span><a href="#js-any" class="self-link"></a>

Since the IDL
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> type is the union of all other IDL types, it
can correspond to any JavaScript value type.

<div id="js-to-any" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to any">

<span id="es-to-any"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any①⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> value by running the following algorithm:

1.  If `V` is undefined, then return the unique
    <a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined⑤"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a> IDL
    value.

2.  If `V` is null, then return the null
    <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object⑤"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object?</code></a> reference.

3.  If `V` <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-boolean-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-boolean-type"
    data-link-type="dfn">is a Boolean</a>, then return the
    <a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean⑦"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a> value that
    represents the same truth value.

4.  If `V` <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type"
    data-link-type="dfn">is a Number</a>, then return the result of
    [converting](#js-to-unrestricted-double) `V` to an
    <a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double⑦"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>.

5.  If `V` <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-bigint-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-bigint-type"
    data-link-type="dfn">is a BigInt</a>, then return the result of
    [converting](#js-to-bigint) `V` to a
    <a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint⑥"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a>.

6.  If `V` <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-string-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-string-type"
    data-link-type="dfn">is a String</a>, then return the result of
    [converting](#js-to-DOMString) `V` to a
    <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③③"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>.

7.  If `V` <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-symbol-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-symbol-type"
    data-link-type="dfn">is a Symbol</a>, then return the result of
    [converting](#js-symbol) `V` to a
    <a href="#idl-symbol" id="ref-for-idl-symbol②"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">symbol</code></a>.

8.  If `V` <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-object-type" data-link-type="dfn">is an Object</a>,
    then return an IDL <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object⑥"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> value that
    references `V`.

</div>

<span id="any-to-es"></span> An IDL
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any①①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> value is
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
data-link-type="dfn">converted to a JavaScript value</a> according to
the rules for converting the
<a href="#dfn-specific-type" id="ref-for-dfn-specific-type②"
data-link-type="dfn">specific type</a> of the IDL
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any①②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> value as described in the remainder of this
section.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.2. </span><span id="void-to-es" class="bs-old-id"></span><span id="es-to-void" class="bs-old-id"></span><span id="es-void" class="bs-old-id"></span><span id="es-undefined" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">undefined</span><a href="#js-undefined" class="self-link"></a>

<span id="es-to-undefined"></span> A JavaScript value `V` is
<a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a> value by
returning the unique
<a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a> value,
ignoring `V`.

<span id="undefined-to-es"></span> The unique IDL
<a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a> value is
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to the JavaScript undefined value.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.3. </span><span id="es-boolean" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">boolean</span><a href="#js-boolean" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-boolean" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to boolean">

<span id="es-to-boolean"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value②"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a> value by
running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be the result of computing <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-toboolean"
    id="ref-for-sec-toboolean" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToBoolean</a>(`V`).

2.  Return the IDL <a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean⑨"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a> value that
    is the one that represents the same truth value as the JavaScript
    Boolean value `x`.

</div>

<span id="boolean-to-es"></span> The IDL
<a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a> value `true`
is <a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value②"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to the JavaScript true value and the
IDL <a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a> value `false`
is converted to the JavaScript false value.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.4. </span><span id="es-integer-types" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Integer types</span><a href="#js-integer-types" class="self-link"></a>

Mathematical operations used in this section, including those defined in
[ECMAScript § 5.2 Algorithm
Conventions](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/notational-conventions.html#sec-algorithm-conventions),
are to be understood as computing exact mathematical results on
mathematical real numbers.

In effect, where `x` is a Number value, “operating on `x`” is shorthand
for “operating on the mathematical real number that represents the same
numeric value as `x`”.

##### <span class="secno">3.2.4.1. </span><span id="es-byte" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">byte</span><a href="#js-byte" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-byte" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to byte">

<span id="es-to-byte"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value③"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-byte" id="ref-for-idl-byte④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">byte</code></a> value by running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a href="#abstract-opdef-converttoint"
    id="ref-for-abstract-opdef-converttoint"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">ConvertToInt</a>(`V`, 8, "`signed`").

2.  Return the IDL

range \[−2<sup>53</sup> + 1, 2<sup>53</sup> − 1\], then the Number will
be able to represent exactly the same value as the
<a href="#idl-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-long-long⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">long long</code></a>.

    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long long</code></a>
    value that represents the same numeric value as `x`.

</div>

##### <span class="secno">3.2.4.9. </span><span id="es-integer-types-abstract-ops" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Abstract operations</span><a href="#js-integer-types-abstract-ops" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="IntegerPart">

<span id="abstract-opdef-integerpart" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="abstract-op" export=""
lt="IntegerPart">IntegerPart(`n`)</span>:

1.  Let `r` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#eqn-floor" id="ref-for-eqn-floor"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">floor</a>(<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#eqn-abs" id="ref-for-eqn-abs"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">abs</a>(`n`)).

2.  If `n` \< 0, then return -1 × `r`.

3.  Otherwise, return `r`.

</div>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="ConvertToInt">

<span id="abstract-opdef-converttoint" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="abstract-op" export="" lt="ConvertToInt">ConvertToInt(`V`,
`bitLength`, `signedness`)</span>:

1.  If `bitLength` is 64, then:

    1.  Let `upperBound` be 2<sup>53</sup> − 1.

    2.  If `signedness` is "`unsigned`", then let `lowerBound` be 0.

    3.  Otherwise let `lowerBound` be −2<sup>53</sup> + 1.

        <span class="marker">Note:</span> this ensures
        <a href="#idl-long-long" id="ref-for-idl-long-long⑨"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">long long</code></a>
        types <a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
        id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with③"
        data-link-type="dfn">associated with</a>
        \[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange①"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
        or
        \[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp②" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\]
        <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute③③"
        data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> are representable
        in JavaScript’s <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type"
        id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type③"
        data-link-type="dfn">Number type</a> as unambiguous integers.

2.  Otherwise, if `signedness` is "`unsigned`", then:

    1.  Let `lowerBound` be 0.

    2.  Let `upperBound` be 2<sup>`bitLength`</sup> − 1.

3.  Otherwise:

    1.  Let `lowerBound` be -2<sup>`bitLength` − 1</sup>.

    2.  Let `upperBound` be 2<sup>`bitLength` − 1</sup> − 1.

4.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands⑨" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tonumber"
    id="ref-for-sec-tonumber" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToNumber</a>(`V`).

5.  If `x` is −0, then set `x` to +0.

6.  If the conversion is to an IDL type
    <a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
    id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with④"
    data-link-type="dfn">associated with</a> the
    \[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange②"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
    <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute③④"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>, then:

    1.  If `x` is NaN, +∞, or −∞, then
        <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw"
        data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

    2.  Set `x` to <a href="#abstract-opdef-integerpart"
        id="ref-for-abstract-opdef-integerpart"
        data-link-type="abstract-op">IntegerPart</a>(`x`).

    3.  If `x` \< `lowerBound` or `x` \> `upperBound`, then
        <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw①"
        data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror①"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

    4.  Return `x`.

7.  If `x` is not NaN and the conversion is to an IDL type
    <a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
    id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">associated with</a> the
    \[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp③" data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\] extended attribute, then:

    1.  Set `x` to
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#eqn-min" id="ref-for-eqn-min"
        data-link-type="abstract-op">min</a>(<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#eqn-max" id="ref-for-eqn-max①"
        data-link-type="abstract-op">max</a>(`x`, `lowerBound`),
        `upperBound`).

    2.  Round `x` to the nearest integer, choosing the even integer if
        it lies halfway between two, and choosing +0 rather than −0.

    3.  Return `x`.

8.  If `x` is NaN, +0, +∞, or −∞, then return +0.

9.  Set `x` to <a href="#abstract-opdef-integerpart"
    id="ref-for-abstract-opdef-integerpart①"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">IntegerPart</a>(`x`).

10. Set `x` to `x`
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#eqn-modulo" id="ref-for-eqn-modulo"
    data-link-type="dfn">modulo</a> 2<sup>`bitLength`</sup>.

11. If `signedness` is "`signed`" and `x` ≥ 2<sup>`bitLength` − 1</sup>,
    then return `x` − 2<sup>`bitLength`</sup>.

12. Otherwise, return `x`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.2.5. </span><span id="es-float" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">float</span><a href="#js-float" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-float" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to float">

<span id="es-to-float"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①①"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">float</code></a> value by running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⓪" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tonumber"
    id="ref-for-sec-tonumber①" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToNumber</a>(`V`).

2.  If `x` is NaN, +∞, or −∞, then
    <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw②"
    data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror②"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

3.  Let `S` be the set of finite IEEE 754 single-precision floating
    point values except −0, but with two special values added:
    2<sup>128</sup> and −2<sup>128</sup>.

4.  Let `y` be the number in `S` that is closest to `x`, selecting the
    number with an *even significand* if there are two <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type④"
    data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="f912dff2">equally close
    values</a>. (The two special values 2<sup>128</sup> and
    −2<sup>128</sup> are considered to have even significands for this
    purpose.)

5.  If `y` is 2<sup>128</sup> or −2<sup>128</sup>, then
    <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw③"
    data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror③"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

6.  If `y` is +0 and `x` is negative, return −0.

7.  Return `y`.

</div>

<span id="float-to-es"></span> The result of
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①①"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">float</code></a> value to a JavaScript value is the Number
value that represents the same numeric value as the IDL
<a href="#idl-float" id="ref-for-idl-float⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">float</code></a> value.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.6. </span><span id="es-unrestricted-float" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">unrestricted float</span><a href="#js-unrestricted-float" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-unrestricted-float" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to unrestricted float">

<span id="es-to-unrestricted-float"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①②"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>
value by running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①①" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tonumber"
    id="ref-for-sec-tonumber②" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToNumber</a>(`V`).

2.  If `x` is NaN, then return the IDL
    <a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float⑧"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>
    value that represents the IEEE 754 NaN value with the bit pattern
    0x7fc00000 <a href="#biblio-ieee-754" data-link-type="biblio"
    title="IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic">[IEEE-754]</a>.

3.  Let `S` be the set of finite IEEE 754 single-precision floating
    point values except −0, but with two special values added:
    2<sup>128</sup> and −2<sup>128</sup>.

4.  Let `y` be the number in `S` that is closest to `x`, selecting the
    number with an *even significand* if there are two <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="f912dff2">equally close
    values</a>. (The two special values 2<sup>128</sup> and
    −2<sup>128</sup> are considered to have even significands for this
    purpose.)

5.  If `y` is 2<sup>128</sup>, return +∞.

6.  If `y` is −2<sup>128</sup>, return −∞.

7.  If `y` is +0 and `x` is negative, return −0.

8.  Return `y`.

</div>

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Since there is only a single
JavaScript NaN value, it must be canonicalized to a particular single
precision IEEE 754 NaN value. The NaN value mentioned above is chosen
simply because it is the quiet NaN with the lowest value when its bit
pattern is interpreted as an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#32-bit-unsigned-integer"
id="ref-for-32-bit-unsigned-integer①" data-link-type="dfn">32-bit
unsigned integer</a>.

<div id="unrestricted-float-to-js" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert an unrestricted float to a JavaScript value">

<span id="unrestricted-float-to-es"></span>

The result of <a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①②"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>
value to a JavaScript value is a Number:

1.  If the IDL
    <a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float①⓪"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>
    value is a NaN, then the Number value is NaN.

2.  Otherwise, the Number value is the one that represents the same
    numeric value as the IDL
    <a href="#idl-unrestricted-float" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-float①①"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted float</code></a>
    value.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.2.7. </span><span id="es-double" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">double</span><a href="#js-double" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-double" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to double">

<span id="es-to-double"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①③"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> value by
running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①②" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tonumber"
    id="ref-for-sec-tonumber③" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToNumber</a>(`V`).

2.  If `x` is NaN, +∞, or −∞, then
    <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw④"
    data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror④"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

3.  Return the IDL <a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①⑤"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> value that
    represents the same numeric value as `x`.

</div>

<span id="double-to-es"></span> The result of
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①③"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> value to a
JavaScript value is the Number value that represents the same numeric
value as the IDL <a href="#idl-double" id="ref-for-idl-double①⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">double</code></a> value.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.8. </span><span id="es-unrestricted-double" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">unrestricted double</span><a href="#js-unrestricted-double" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-unrestricted-double" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to unrestricted double">

<span id="es-to-unrestricted-double"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①④"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>
value by running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①③" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tonumber"
    id="ref-for-sec-tonumber④" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToNumber</a>(`V`).

2.  If `x` is NaN, then return the IDL
    <a href="#idl-unrestricted-double" id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double⑨"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a>
    value that represents the IEEE 754 NaN value with the bit pattern
    0x7ff8000000000000
    <a href="#biblio-ieee-754" data-link-type="biblio"
    title="IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic">[IEEE-754]</a>.

3.  Return the IDL <a href="#idl-unrestricted-double"
    id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double①⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a> value that represents the
    same numeric value as `x`.

</div>

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Since there is only a single
JavaScript NaN value, it must be canonicalized to a particular double
precision IEEE 754 NaN value. The NaN value mentioned above is chosen
simply because it is the quiet NaN with the lowest value when its bit
pattern is interpreted as an
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#64-bit-unsigned-integer"
id="ref-for-64-bit-unsigned-integer①" data-link-type="dfn">64-bit
unsigned integer</a>.

<div id="unrestricted-double-to-js" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert an unrestricted double to a JavaScript value">

<span id="unrestricted-double-to-es"></span>

The result of <a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①④"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-unrestricted-double"
id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double①①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a> value to a JavaScript value
is a Number:

1.  If the IDL <a href="#idl-unrestricted-double"
    id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double①②" data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a> value is a NaN, then the
    Number value is NaN.

2.  Otherwise, the Number value is the one that represents the same
    numeric value as the IDL <a href="#idl-unrestricted-double"
    id="ref-for-idl-unrestricted-double①③" data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">unrestricted double</code></a> value.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.2.9. </span><span id="es-bigint" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">bigint</span><a href="#js-bigint" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-bigint" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to a bigint">

<span id="es-to-bigint"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> value by
running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①④" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tobigint"
    id="ref-for-sec-tobigint" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToBigInt</a>(`V`).

2.  Return the IDL <a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint⑧"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> value that
    represents the same numeric value as `x`.

</div>

<div id="bigint-to-js" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a bigint to a JavaScript value">

<span id="bigint-to-es"></span>

The result of <a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> value to a
JavaScript value is a BigInt:

1.  Return the <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/numbers-and-dates.html#sec-bigint-objects"
    id="ref-for-sec-bigint-objects" data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">BigInt</code></a> value that represents the same numeric
    value as the IDL <a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint①⓪"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> value.

</div>

<div id="js-to-bigint-or-numeric" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to a numeric type or a bigint">

<span id="es-to-bigint-or-numeric"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is
<span id="converted-to-a-numeric-type-or-bigint" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" lt="converted to a numeric type or bigint"
noexport="">converted</span> to an IDL
<a href="#dfn-numeric-type" id="ref-for-dfn-numeric-type⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">numeric type</a> `T` or
<a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> value by
running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tonumeric"
    id="ref-for-sec-tonumeric" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToNumeric</a>(`V`).

2.  If `x` <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-bigint-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-bigint-type①"
    data-link-type="dfn">is a BigInt</a>, then

    1.  Return the IDL <a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint①②"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a> value
        that represents the same numeric value as `x`.

3.  Assert: `x` <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">is a Number</a>.

4.  Return the result of <a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
    id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `x` to `T`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.2.10. </span><span id="es-DOMString" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">DOMString</span><a href="#js-DOMString" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-DOMString" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to DOMString">

<span id="es-to-DOMString"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> value by
running the following algorithm:

1.  If `V` is null and the conversion is to an IDL type
    <a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
    id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">associated with</a> the
    \[<a href="#LegacyNullToEmptyString" id="ref-for-LegacyNullToEmptyString①"
    data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">LegacyNullToEmptyString</code></a>\] extended attribute,
    then return the
    <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③⑤"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> value
    that represents the empty string.

2.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑥" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tostring"
    id="ref-for-sec-tostring②" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToString</a>(`V`).

3.  Return the IDL <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③⑥"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> value
    that represents the same sequence of code units as the one the
    JavaScript String value `x` represents.

</div>

<span id="DOMString-to-es"></span> The result of
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> value to a
JavaScript value is the String value that represents the same sequence
of <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-unit"
id="ref-for-code-unit③" data-link-type="dfn">code units</a> that the IDL
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> represents.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.11. </span><span id="es-ByteString" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">ByteString</span><a href="#js-ByteString" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-ByteString" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to ByteString">

<span id="es-to-ByteString"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a> value by
running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑦" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tostring"
    id="ref-for-sec-tostring③" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToString</a>(`V`).

2.  If the value of any <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-string-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-string-type①"
    data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="fe0437f8">element</a> of `x`
    is greater than 255, then
    <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror⑤"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

3.  Return an IDL <a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString⑨"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a> value
    whose length is the length of `x`, and where the value of each
    element is the value of the corresponding element of `x`.

</div>

<span id="ByteString-to-es"></span> The result of
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a> value to a
JavaScript value is a String value whose length is the length of the
<a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a>, and the
value of each <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-string-type"
id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-string-type②"
data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="fe0437f8">element</a> of which is
the value of the corresponding element of the
<a href="#idl-ByteString" id="ref-for-idl-ByteString①②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ByteString</code></a>.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.12. </span><span id="es-USVString" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">USVString</span><a href="#js-USVString" class="self-link"></a>

<div id="js-to-USVString" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to USVString">

<span id="es-to-USVString"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a> value by
running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `string` be the result of
    <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
    id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value①⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `V` to a
    <a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString③⑨"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a>.

2.  Return an IDL <a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString①①"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a> value
    that is the result of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-string-convert"
    id="ref-for-javascript-string-convert"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `string` to a sequence of
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
    id="ref-for-scalar-value⑨" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>.

</div>

<div id="USVString-to-js" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert an USVString to a JavaScript value">

<span id="USVString-to-es"></span>

The result of <a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString①②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a> value `S` to
a JavaScript value is `S`.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.2.13. </span><span id="es-object" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">object</span><a href="#js-object" class="self-link"></a>

IDL <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> values are
represented by JavaScript Object values.

<div id="js-to-object" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to object">

<span id="es-to-object"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> value by
running the following algorithm:

1.  If `V` <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-object-type①" data-link-type="dfn"
    data-refhint-key="df9c128d">is not an Object</a>, then
    <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror⑥"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

2.  Return the IDL <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object⑨"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> value that
    is a reference to the same object as `V`.

</div>

<span id="object-to-es"></span> The result of
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> value to a
JavaScript value is the Object value that represents a reference to the
same object that the IDL <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> represents.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.14. </span><span id="es-symbol" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">symbol</span><a href="#js-symbol" class="self-link"></a>

IDL <a href="#idl-symbol" id="ref-for-idl-symbol③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">symbol</code></a> values are
represented by JavaScript Symbol values.

<div id="js-to-symbol" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to a symbol">

<span id="es-to-symbol"></span> A JavaScript value `V` is
<a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value②①"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-symbol" id="ref-for-idl-symbol④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">symbol</code></a> value by
running the following algorithm:

1.  If `V` <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-symbol-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-ecmascript-language-types-symbol-type①"
    data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="845a9e60">is not a Symbol</a>,
    then <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror⑦"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

2.  Return the IDL <a href="#idl-symbol" id="ref-for-idl-symbol⑤"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">symbol</code></a> value that
    is a reference to the same symbol as `V`.

</div>

<span id="symbol-to-es"></span> The result of
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value②①"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-symbol" id="ref-for-idl-symbol⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">symbol</code></a> value to a
JavaScript value is the Symbol value that represents a reference to the
same symbol that the IDL <a href="#idl-symbol" id="ref-for-idl-symbol⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">symbol</code></a> represents.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.15. </span><span id="es-interface" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Interface types</span><a href="#js-interface" class="self-link"></a>

IDL <a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> values are represented by
JavaScript Object values (including <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object⑥" data-link-type="dfn">function objects</a>).

<div id="js-to-interface" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to interface">

<span id="es-to-interface"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value②②"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> value by running the following
algorithm (where `I` is the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>):

1.  If `V` <a href="#implements" id="ref-for-implements③"
    data-link-type="dfn">implements</a> `I`, then return the IDL
    <a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> value that represents a
    reference to that platform object.

2.  <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">Throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror⑧"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

</div>

<span id="interface-to-es"></span> The result of
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value②②"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> value to a JavaScript value is
the Object value that represents a reference to the same object that the
IDL <a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> value represents.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.16. </span><span id="es-callback-interface" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Callback interface types</span><a href="#js-callback-interface" class="self-link"></a>

IDL
<a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface④"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface type</a> values are represented
by JavaScript Object values (including <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object⑦" data-link-type="dfn">function objects</a>).

<div id="js-to-callback-interface" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to callback interface">

<span id="es-to-callback-interface"></span>

A JavaScript value `V` is <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value②③"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface type</a> value by running the
following algorithm:

1.  If `V` <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-object-type②" data-link-type="dfn"
    data-refhint-key="df9c128d">is not an Object</a>, then
    <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror⑨"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

2.  Return the IDL
    <a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">callback interface type</a> value that
    represents a reference to `V`, with the <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#incumbent-settings-object"
    id="ref-for-incumbent-settings-object②" data-link-type="dfn">incumbent
    settings object</a> as the
    <a href="#dfn-callback-context" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-context④"
    data-link-type="dfn">callback context</a>.

</div>

<span id="callback-interface-to-es"></span> The result of
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value②③"
data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> an IDL
<a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface type</a> value to a JavaScript
value is the Object value that represents a reference to the same object
that the IDL
<a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface type</a> value represents.

#### <span class="secno">3.2.17. </span><span id="es-dictionary" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Dictionary types</span><a href="#js-dictionary" class="self-link"></a>

IDL <a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary①③"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a> values are represented by
JavaScript Object values. Properties on the object (or its prototype
chain) correspond to
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member②③"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary members</a>.

<div id="js-to-dictionary" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a JavaScript value to dictionary">

<span id="es-to-dictionary"></span>

A JavaScript value `jsDict` is
<a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value②④"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to an IDL
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary①④"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a> value by running the following
algorithm (where `D` is the
<a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a>):

1.  If `jsDict` <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-object-type③" data-link-type="dfn"
    data-refhint-key="df9c128d">is not an Object</a> and `jsDict` is
    neither undefined nor null, then
    <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw①⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror①⓪"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

2.  Let `idlDict` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-map"
    id="ref-for-ordered-map⑧" data-link-type="dfn">ordered map</a>,
    representing a dictionary of type `D`.

3.  Let `dictionaries` be a list consisting of `D` and all of `D`’s
    <a href="#dfn-inherited-dictionaries"
    id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-dictionaries④" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
    dictionaries</a>, in order from least to most derived.

4.  For each dictionary `dictionary` in `dictionaries`, in order:

    1.  For each dictionary member `member` declared on `dictionary`, in
        lexicographical order:

        1.  Let `key` be the
            <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤①"
            data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of `member`.

        2.  If `jsDict` is either undefined or null, then:

            1.  Let `jsMemberValue` be undefined.

        3.  Otherwise,

            1.  Let `jsMemberValue` be
                <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
                id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑧" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
                <a
                href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-get-o-p"
                id="ref-for-sec-get-o-p" data-link-type="abstract-op">Get</a>(`jsDict`,
                `key`).

        4.  If `jsMemberValue` is not undefined, then:

            1.  Let `idlMemberValue` be the result of
                <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
                id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value②⑤"
                data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `jsMemberValue` to
                an IDL value whose type is the type `member` is declared
                to be of.

            2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set" id="ref-for-map-set"
                data-link-type="dfn">Set</a> `idlDict`\[`key`\] to
                `idlMemberValue`.

        5.  Otherwise, if `jsMemberValue` is undefined but `member` has
            a <a href="#dfn-dictionary-member-default-value"
            id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member-default-value①①"
            data-link-type="dfn">default value</a>, then:

            1.  Let `idlMemberValue` be `member`’s default value.

            2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-set" id="ref-for-map-set①"
                data-link-type="dfn">Set</a> `idlDict`\[`key`\] to
                `idlMemberValue`.

        6.  Otherwise, if `jsMemberValue` is undefined and `member` is
            <a href="#required-dictionary-member"
            id="ref-for-required-dictionary-member⑧"
            data-link-type="dfn">required</a>, then throw a
            <a href="#exceptiondef-typeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-typeerror⑥"
            data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

5.  Return `idlDict`.

</div>

<span class="marker">Note:</span> The order that
<a href="#dfn-dictionary-member" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary-member②④"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary members</a> are looked up on the
JavaScript object are not necessarily the same as the object’s property
enumeration order.

<div id="dictionary-to-js" class="algorithm"
algorithm="convert a dictionary to a JavaScript value">

<span id="dictionary-to-es"></span>

An IDL dictionary value `V` is
<a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value②④"
data-link-type="dfn">converted</a> to a JavaScript Object value by
running the following algorithm (where `D` is the
<a href="#dfn-dictionary" id="ref-for-dfn-dictionary①①"
data-link-type="dfn">dictionary</a>):

1.  Let `O` be <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ordinary-and-exotic-objects-behaviours.html#sec-ordinaryobjectcreate"
    id="ref-for-sec-ordinaryobjectcreate"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">OrdinaryObjectCreate</a>(<a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object"
    id="ref-for-sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object②"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">%Object.prototype%</code></a>).

2.  Let `dictionaries` be a list consisting of `D` and all of `D`’s
    <a href="#dfn-inherited-dictionaries"
    id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-dictionaries⑤" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
    dictionaries</a>, in order from least to most derived.

3.  For each dictionary `dictionary` in `dictionaries`, in order:

    1.  For each dictionary member `member` declared on `dictionary`, in
        lexicographical order:

        1.  Let `key` be the
            <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤②"
            data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of `member`.

        2.  If `V`\[`key`\]
            <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#map-exists"
            id="ref-for-map-exists①" data-link-type="dfn">exists</a>,
            then:

            1.  Let `idlValue` be `V`\[`key`\].

            2.  Let `value` be the result of
                <a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
                id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value②⑤"
                data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `idlValue` to a
                JavaScript value.

            3.  Perform
