- A call to `writeIntoSharedResizable` will accept any
  <a href="#buffer-view-types" id="ref-for-buffer-view-types①⓪"
  data-link-type="dfn">buffer view type</a> backed by a
  <a href="#idl-ArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-ArrayBuffer②①"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBuffer</code></a> instance
  or a
  <a href="#idl-SharedArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-SharedArrayBuffer①⑤"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SharedArrayBuffer</code></a>
  instance.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.3. </span><span class="content">\[Clamp\]</span><a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp①②" class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑤⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on one of the
<a href="#dfn-integer-type" id="ref-for-dfn-integer-type②"
data-link-type="dfn">integer types</a>, it creates a new IDL type such
that that when a JavaScript Number is converted to the IDL type,
out-of-range values will be clamped to the range of valid values, rather
than using the operators that use a modulo operation (<a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-toint32"
id="ref-for-sec-toint32" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToInt32</a>, <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-touint32"
id="ref-for-sec-touint32" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToUint32</a>,
etc.).

The \[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\] extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments②"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

A type annotated with the
\[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\] extended attribute must not appear in a
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a> attribute. A type must not be
<a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with②①"
data-link-type="dfn">associated with</a> both the
\[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\] and
\[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
extended attributes. A type that is not an
<a href="#dfn-integer-type" id="ref-for-dfn-integer-type③"
data-link-type="dfn">integer type</a> must not be
<a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with②②"
data-link-type="dfn">associated with</a> the
\[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\] extended attribute.

See the rules for converting JavaScript values to the various IDL
integer types in [§ 3.2.4 Integer types](#js-integer-types) for the
specific requirements that the use of
\[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\] entails.

<div id="example-401309f5" class="example">

<a href="#example-401309f5" class="self-link"></a>

In the following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a>, two
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation④②"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> are declared that take three
<a href="#idl-octet" id="ref-for-idl-octet⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">octet</code></a> arguments; one uses the
\[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp①⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑤⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> on all three arguments,
while the other does not:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface GraphicsContext {
  undefined setColor(octet red, octet green, octet blue);
  undefined setColorClamped([Clamp] octet red, [Clamp] octet green, [Clamp] octet blue);
};
```

A call to `setColorClamped` with Number values that are out of range for
an
<a href="#idl-octet" id="ref-for-idl-octet⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">octet</code></a> are clamped to the range \[0, 255\].

``` highlight
// Get an instance of GraphicsContext.
var context = getGraphicsContext();

// Calling the non-[Clamp] version uses ToUint8 to coerce the Numbers to octets.
// This is equivalent to calling setColor(255, 255, 1).
context.setColor(-1, 255, 257);

// Call setColorClamped with some out of range values.
// This is equivalent to calling setColorClamped(0, 255, 255).
context.setColorClamped(-1, 255, 257);
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.4. </span><span class="content">\[CrossOriginIsolated\]</span><a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated②⓪"
class="self-link"></a>

If the
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑤⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①①③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>,
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface mixin</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①①"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace②"
data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a>,
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>, it indicates that the
construct is <a href="#dfn-exposed" id="ref-for-dfn-exposed③"
data-link-type="dfn">exposed</a> only within an environment whose <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
id="ref-for-concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
data-link-type="dfn">cross-origin isolated capability</a> is true. The
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\]
extended attribute must not be used on any other construct.

The \[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\]
extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments③"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

If \[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\]
appears on an <a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded①①"
data-link-type="dfn">overloaded</a>
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation④③"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>, then it must appear on all
overloads.

The \[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> must not be specified both
on

- an <a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a> and its
  <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①①④"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> or
  <a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①⓪"
  data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>;

- an
  <a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①⓪"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a> and its
  <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③③"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> or
  <a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin⑦"
  data-link-type="dfn">partial interface mixin</a>;

- a <a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a> and its
  <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①②"
  data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> or
  <a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace③"
  data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> This is because adding the
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥①"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> on a
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> when its containing definition is also
annotated with the
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥②"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> does not further restrict
the exposure of the <a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①①"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a>.

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> without the
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥③"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> must not
<a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">inherit</a> from another interface that does
specify
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\].

<div id="example-3d6a455d" class="example">

<a href="#example-3d6a455d" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface with one
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation④④"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> that is executable from all contexts,
and two which are executable only from cross-origin isolated contexts.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface ExampleFeature {
  // This call will succeed in all contexts.
  Promise <Result> calculateNotSoSecretResult();

  // This operation will not be exposed to a non-isolated context. In such a context,
  // there will be no "calculateSecretResult" property on ExampleFeature.prototype.
  [CrossOriginIsolated] Promise<Result> calculateSecretResult();

  // The same applies here: the attribute will not be exposed to a non-isolated context,
  // and in such a context there will be no "secretBoolean" property on
  // ExampleFeature.prototype.
  [CrossOriginIsolated] readonly attribute boolean secretBoolean;
};

// HighResolutionTimer will not be exposed in a non-isolated context, nor will its members.
// In such a context, there will be no "HighResolutionTimer" property on Window.
[Exposed=Window, CrossOriginIsolated]
interface HighResolutionTimer {
  DOMHighResTimeStamp getHighResolutionTime();
};

// The interface mixin members defined below will never be exposed in a non-isolated
// context, regardless of whether the interface that includes them is. That is, in
// non-isolated context, there will be no "snap" property on ExampleFeature.prototype.
[CrossOriginIsolated]
interface mixin Snapshotable {
  Promise<boolean> snap();
};
ExampleFeature includes Snapshotable;

// On the other hand, the following interface mixin members will be exposed to a
// non-isolated context when included by a host interface that doesn't have the
// [CrossOriginIsolated] extended attribute. That is, in a non-isolated context, there will
// be a "log" property on ExampleFeature.prototype.
interface mixin Loggable {
  Promise<boolean> log();
};
ExampleFeature includes Loggable;
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.5. </span><span class="content">\[Default\]</span><a href="#Default" id="ref-for-Default①⓪" class="self-link"></a>

If the
\[<a href="#Default" id="ref-for-Default②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Default</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥④"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a>, then it indicates that the
appropriate
<a href="#default-method-steps" id="ref-for-default-method-steps"
data-link-type="dfn">default method steps</a> must be carried out when
the operation is invoked.

The
\[<a href="#Default" id="ref-for-Default③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Default</code></a>\] extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments④"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

The
\[<a href="#Default" id="ref-for-Default④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Default</code></a>\] extended attribute must not be used on
anything other than a
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a> that
<a href="#has-default-method-steps"
id="ref-for-has-default-method-steps" data-link-type="dfn">has default
method steps</a> defined.

<div id="example-tojson-default" class="example">

<a href="#example-tojson-default" class="self-link"></a>

As an example, the
\[<a href="#Default" id="ref-for-Default⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Default</code></a>\] extended attribute is suitable for use
on `toJSON`
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operations</a>:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Animal {
  attribute DOMString name;
  attribute unsigned short age;
  [Default] object toJSON();
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Human : Animal {
  attribute Dog? pet;
  [Default] object toJSON();
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Dog : Animal {
  attribute DOMString? breed;
};
```

In the JavaScript language binding, there would exist a `toJSON()`
method on `Animal`, `Human`, and (via inheritance) `Dog` objects:

``` highlight
// Get an instance of Human.
var alice = getHuman();

// Evaluates to an object like this (notice how "pet" still holds
// an instance of Dog at this point):
//
// {
//   name: "Alice",
//   age: 59,
//   pet: Dog
// }
alice.toJSON();

// Evaluates to an object like this (notice how "breed" is absent,
// as the Dog interface doesn't use the default toJSON steps):
//
// {
//   name: "Tramp",
//   age: 6
// }
alice.pet.toJSON();

// Evaluates to a string like this:
// '{"name":"Alice","age":59,"pet":{"name":"Tramp","age":6}}'
JSON.stringify(alice);
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.6. </span><span class="content">\[EnforceRange\]</span><a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange①①"
class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on one of the
<a href="#dfn-integer-type" id="ref-for-dfn-integer-type④"
data-link-type="dfn">integer types</a>, it creates a new IDL type such
that that when a JavaScript Number is converted to the IDL type,
out-of-range values will cause an exception to be thrown, rather than
being converted to a valid value using using the operators that use a
modulo operation (<a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-toint32"
id="ref-for-sec-toint32①" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToInt32</a>, <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-touint32"
id="ref-for-sec-touint32①" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToUint32</a>,
etc.). The Number will be rounded toward zero before being checked
against its range.

The \[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

A type annotated with the
\[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
extended attribute must not appear in a
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a> attribute. A type must not be
<a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with②③"
data-link-type="dfn">associated with</a> both the
\[<a href="#Clamp" id="ref-for-Clamp①①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Clamp</code></a>\] and
\[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
extended attributes. A type that is not an
<a href="#dfn-integer-type" id="ref-for-dfn-integer-type⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">integer type</a> must not be
<a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with②④"
data-link-type="dfn">associated with</a> the
\[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
extended attribute.

See the rules for converting JavaScript values to the various IDL
integer types in [§ 3.2 JavaScript type mapping](#js-type-mapping) for
the specific requirements that the use of
\[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
entails.

<div id="example-1a34c82a" class="example">

<a href="#example-1a34c82a" class="self-link"></a>

In the following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a>, two
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation④⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> are declared that take three
<a href="#idl-octet" id="ref-for-idl-octet①⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">octet</code></a> arguments; one uses the
\[<a href="#EnforceRange" id="ref-for-EnforceRange①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">EnforceRange</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> on all three arguments,
while the other does not:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface GraphicsContext {
  undefined setColor(octet red, octet green, octet blue);
  undefined setColorEnforcedRange([EnforceRange] octet red, [EnforceRange] octet green, [EnforceRange] octet blue);
};
```

In a JavaScript implementation of the IDL, a call to
setColorEnforcedRange with Number values that are out of range for an
<a href="#idl-octet" id="ref-for-idl-octet①①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">octet</code></a> will result in an exception being thrown.

``` highlight
// Get an instance of GraphicsContext.
var context = getGraphicsContext();

// Calling the non-[EnforceRange] version uses ToUint8 to coerce the Numbers to octets.
// This is equivalent to calling setColor(255, 255, 1).
context.setColor(-1, 255, 257);

// When setColorEnforcedRange is called, Numbers are rounded towards zero.
// This is equivalent to calling setColor(0, 255, 255).
context.setColorEnforcedRange(-0.9, 255, 255.2);

// The following will cause a TypeError to be thrown, since even after
// rounding the first and third argument values are out of range.
context.setColorEnforcedRange(-1, 255, 256);
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.7. </span><span class="content">\[Exposed\]</span><a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed③④" class="self-link"></a>

When the
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①①"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>,
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface mixin</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①③"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace④"
data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a>, or an individual
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>, it indicates that the
construct is exposed on that particular set of global interfaces.

The
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> must either
<a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier"
data-link-type="dfn">take an identifier</a>,
<a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier-list"
id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier-list" data-link-type="dfn">take an
identifier list</a> or
<a href="#dfn-xattr-wildcard" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-wildcard"
data-link-type="dfn">take a wildcard</a>. Each of the identifiers
mentioned must be a
<a href="#dfn-global-name" id="ref-for-dfn-global-name"
data-link-type="dfn">global name</a> of some
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> and be unique.

The <span id="own-exposure-set" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
noexport="">own exposure set</span> is either a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="ref-for-ordered-set④" data-link-type="dfn">set</a> of identifiers or
the special value `*`, defined as follows:

If the \[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑥⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> <a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier①"
data-link-type="dfn">takes an identifier</a> `I`  
The <a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set"
data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a> is the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="ref-for-ordered-set⑤" data-link-type="dfn">set</a> « `I` ».

If the \[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> <a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier-list"
id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier-list①" data-link-type="dfn">takes an
identifier list</a> `I`  
The <a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set①"
data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a> is the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ordered-set"
id="ref-for-ordered-set⑥" data-link-type="dfn">set</a> `I`.

If the \[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦①"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> <a href="#dfn-xattr-wildcard" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-wildcard①"
data-link-type="dfn">takes a wildcard</a>  
The <a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set②"
data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a> is `*`.

`[Exposed=*]` is to be used with care. It is only appropriate when an
API does not expose significant new capabilities. If the API might be
restricted or disabled in some environments, it is preferred to list the
globals explicitly.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="exposure set intersection">

The <span id="exposure-set-intersection" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">exposure set intersection</span> of a
construct `C` and interface-or-null `H` is defined as follows:

1.  Assert: `C` is an
    <a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①①"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
    <a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①②"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①②"
    data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
    <a href="#partial-interface-mixin" id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">partial interface mixin</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a>, or
    <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>.

2.  Assert: `H` is an
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①①⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> or null.

3.  If `H` is null, return `C`’s
    <a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set③"
    data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a>.

4.  If `C`’s <a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set④"
    data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a> is `*`, return `H`’s
    <a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set"
    data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a>.

5.  If `H`’s <a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set①"
    data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a> is `*`, return `C`’s
    <a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a>.

6.  Return the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-intersection"
    id="ref-for-set-intersection" data-link-type="dfn">intersection</a>
    of `C`’s <a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a> and `H`’s
    <a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set②"
    data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a>.

</div>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="exposure set">

To get the <span id="dfn-exposure-set" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">exposure set</span> of a construct `C`, run the
following steps:

1.  Assert: `C` is an
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①①⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①④"
    data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①②"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
    <a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①③"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or
    <a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>.

2.  Let `H` be `C`’s
    <a href="#host-interfaces" id="ref-for-host-interfaces①"
    data-link-type="dfn">host interface</a> if `C` is an
    <a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①④"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or null otherwise.

3.  If `C` is an
    <a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①③"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
    <a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or
    <a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member①⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>, then:

    1.  If the
        \[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
        <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦②"
        data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> is specified on `C`,
        return the <a href="#exposure-set-intersection"
        id="ref-for-exposure-set-intersection" data-link-type="dfn">exposure set
        intersection</a> of `C` and `H`.

    2.  Set `C` to the
        <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②⓪"
        data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
        <a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①③"
        data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
        <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③⑥"
        data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>,
        <a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
        id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①⓪" data-link-type="dfn">partial
        interface mixin</a>,
        <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①⑤"
        data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>, or
        <a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace⑥"
        data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a> `C` is declared on.

4.  If `C` is a
    <a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①④"
    data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
    <a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
    id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①①" data-link-type="dfn">partial
    interface mixin</a>, or
    <a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a>, then:

    1.  If the
        \[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed①⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
        <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦③"
        data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> is specified on `C`,
        return the <a href="#exposure-set-intersection"
        id="ref-for-exposure-set-intersection①" data-link-type="dfn">exposure
        set intersection</a> of `C` and `H`.

    2.  Set `C` to the original
        <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②①"
        data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
        <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③⑦"
        data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>, or
        <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①⑥"
        data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> definition of `C`.

5.  If `C` is an
    <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>, then:

    1.  Assert: `H` is not null.

    2.  If the
        \[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
        <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦④"
        data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> is specified on `C`,
        return the <a href="#exposure-set-intersection"
        id="ref-for-exposure-set-intersection②" data-link-type="dfn">exposure
        set intersection</a> of `C` and `H`.

    3.  Set `C` to `H`.

6.  Assert: `C` is an
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②②"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface②⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> or
    <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

7.  Assert: The
    \[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②①" data-link-type="idl"><code
    class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
    <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> is specified on `C`.

8.  Return `C`’s
    <a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a>.

</div>

If
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] appears on an
<a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded①②"
data-link-type="dfn">overloaded</a>
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation④⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>, then it must appear identically on
all overloads.

The
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] extended attribute must not be
specified both on an
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member①①"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>, and on the
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①②" data-link-type="dfn">partial
interface mixin</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a> definition the
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①②"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> is declared on.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> This is because adding an
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> on a
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①③" data-link-type="dfn">partial
interface mixin</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a> is shorthand for annotating
each of its <a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①③"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a>.

If
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] appears on a
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a>, then the partial’s
<a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a> must be a subset of the
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set③"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a> of the partial’s original
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

If
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member①②"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>, then the
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①④"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a>’s
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set④"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a> must be a subset of the
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a> of the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> or
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> it is a member of.

If
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] appears both on a
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①④" data-link-type="dfn">partial
interface mixin</a> and its original
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin③⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>, then the
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①⑤" data-link-type="dfn">partial
interface mixin</a>’s
<a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a> must be a subset of the
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>’s
<a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a>.

If
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] appears both on an
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a> and the
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> it is a member of, then the
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin members</a>’s
<a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set①①"
data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a> must be a subset of the
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>’s
<a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set①②"
data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a>.

If an interface `X` <a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">inherits</a> from another interface `Y` then the
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a> of `X` must be a subset of the
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a> of `Y`.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> As an
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> can be
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">included</a> by different
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a>, the
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a> of its
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> is a function of the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that
<a href="#include" id="ref-for-include①①"
data-link-type="dfn">includes</a> them. If the
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>,
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①⑥" data-link-type="dfn">partial
interface mixin</a>, or
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> is annotated with an
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed②⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>, then the
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member②①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>’s
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a> is the
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#set-intersection"
id="ref-for-set-intersection①" data-link-type="dfn">intersection</a> of
the relevant construct’s
<a href="#own-exposure-set" id="ref-for-own-exposure-set①③"
data-link-type="dfn">own exposure set</a> with the
<a href="#host-interfaces" id="ref-for-host-interfaces②"
data-link-type="dfn">host interface</a>’s
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a>. Otherwise, it is the
<a href="#host-interfaces" id="ref-for-host-interfaces③"
data-link-type="dfn">host interface</a>’s
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set①①"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a>.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="exposed">

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> `construct` is <span id="dfn-exposed"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">exposed</span> in a
given <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm①⑦" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a> `realm` if the
following steps return true:

1.  If `construct`’s
    <a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set①②"
    data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a> is not `*`, and
    `realm`.\[\[GlobalObject\]\] does not implement an
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that is in `construct`’s
    <a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set①③"
    data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a>, then return false.

2.  If `realm`’s <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-settings-object"
    id="ref-for-concept-realm-settings-object" data-link-type="dfn">settings
    object</a> is not a <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#secure-context"
    id="ref-for-secure-context" data-link-type="dfn">secure context</a>,
    and `construct` is <a href="#dfn-conditionally-exposed"
    id="ref-for-dfn-conditionally-exposed"
    data-link-type="dfn">conditionally exposed</a> on
    \[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext⑨"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\],
    then return false.

3.  If `realm`’s <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-settings-object"
    id="ref-for-concept-realm-settings-object①"
    data-link-type="dfn">settings object</a>’s <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
    id="ref-for-concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability①"
    data-link-type="dfn">cross-origin isolated capability</a> is false,
    and `construct` is <a href="#dfn-conditionally-exposed"
    id="ref-for-dfn-conditionally-exposed①"
    data-link-type="dfn">conditionally exposed</a> on
    \[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①⑧"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\],
    then return false.

4.  Return true.

</div>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="conditionally exposed">

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface③①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②①"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> `construct` is
<span id="dfn-conditionally-exposed" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">conditionally exposed</span> on a given
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> `exposure condition` if the
following steps return true:

1.  Assert: `construct` is an
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface③②"
    data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②②"
    data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
    <a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member②②"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or
    <a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member①③"
    data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>.

2.  Let `H` be `construct`’s
    <a href="#host-interfaces" id="ref-for-host-interfaces④"
    data-link-type="dfn">host interface</a> if `construct` is an
    <a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member②③"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or null otherwise.

3.  If `construct` is an
    <a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
    <a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member②④"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or
    <a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member①④"
    data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>, then:

    1.  If the `exposure condition`
        <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑦⑨"
        data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> is specified on
        `construct`, then return true.

    2.  Otherwise, set `construct` to be the
        <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③①"
        data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
        <a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①⑧"
        data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
        <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④⑤"
        data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>,
        <a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
        id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①⑦" data-link-type="dfn">partial
        interface mixin</a>,
        <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②③"
        data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>, or
        <a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace①①"
        data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a> `construct` is
        declared on.

4.  If `construct` is a
    <a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface①⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
    <a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
    id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①⑧" data-link-type="dfn">partial
    interface mixin</a>, or
    <a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace①②"
    data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a>, then:

    1.  If the `exposure condition`
        <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧⓪"
        data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> is specified on
        `construct`, then return true.

    2.  Otherwise, set `construct` to be the original
        <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③②"
        data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
        <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④⑥"
        data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>, or
        <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②④"
        data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> definition of `construct`.

5.  If `construct` is an
    <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>, then:

    1.  If the `exposure condition`
        <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧①"
        data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> is specified on
        `construct`, then return true.

    2.  Otherwise, set `construct` to `H`.

6.  Assert: `construct` is an
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③③"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
    <a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface③③"
    data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> or
    <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

7.  If the `exposure condition`
    <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧②"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> is specified on
    `construct`, then return true.

8.  Otherwise, return false.

</div>

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Since it is not possible for the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#relevant-settings-object"
id="ref-for-relevant-settings-object" data-link-type="dfn">relevant
settings object</a> for a JavaScript global object to change whether it
is a <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#secure-context"
id="ref-for-secure-context①" data-link-type="dfn">secure context</a> or
<a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
id="ref-for-concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability②"
data-link-type="dfn">cross-origin isolated capability</a> over time, an
implementation’s decision to create properties for an interface or
interface member can be made once, at the time the
<a href="#dfn-initial-object" id="ref-for-dfn-initial-object②"
data-link-type="dfn">initial objects</a> are created.

See [§ 3.7 Interfaces](#js-interfaces), [§ 3.7.5
Constants](#js-constants), [§ 3.7.6 Attributes](#js-attributes),
[§ 3.7.7 Operations](#js-operations), and for the specific requirements
that the use of
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed③⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] entails.

<div id="example-d5c14f84" class="example">

<a href="#example-d5c14f84" class="self-link"></a>

\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed③①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] is intended to be used to control
whether <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③④"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface③④"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interfaces</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">namespaces</a>, or individual
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">mixin</a> or
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace members</a> are available for use in
workers,
<a href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/worklets.html#worklet"
id="ref-for-worklet" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Worklet</code></a>, <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window"
id="ref-for-window①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Window</code></a>, or any combination of the above.

The following IDL fragment shows how that might be achieved:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window, Global=Window]
interface Window {
  // ...
};

// By using the same identifier Worker for both SharedWorkerGlobalScope
// and DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope, both can be addressed in an [Exposed]
// extended attribute at once.
[Exposed=Worker, Global=Worker]
interface SharedWorkerGlobalScope : WorkerGlobalScope {
  // ...
};

[Exposed=Worker, Global=Worker]
interface DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope : WorkerGlobalScope {
  // ...
};

// Dimensions is available for use in workers and on the main thread.
[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
interface Dimensions {
  constructor(double width, double height);
  readonly attribute double width;
  readonly attribute double height;
};

// WorkerNavigator is only available in workers.  Evaluating WorkerNavigator
// in the global scope of a worker would give you its interface object, while
// doing so on the main thread will give you a ReferenceError.
[Exposed=Worker]
interface WorkerNavigator {
  // ...
};

// Node is only available on the main thread.  Evaluating Node
// in the global scope of a worker would give you a ReferenceError.
[Exposed=Window]
interface Node {
  // ...
};

// MathUtils is available for use in workers and on the main thread.
[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
namespace MathUtils {
  double someComplicatedFunction(double x, double y);
};

// WorkerUtils is only available in workers.  Evaluating WorkerUtils
// in the global scope of a worker would give you its namespace object, while
// doing so on the main thread will give you a ReferenceError.
[Exposed=Worker]
namespace WorkerUtils {
  undefined setPriority(double x);
};

// NodeUtils is only available in the main thread.  Evaluating NodeUtils
// in the global scope of a worker would give you a ReferenceError.
[Exposed=Window]
namespace NodeUtils {
  DOMString getAllText(Node node);
};
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.8. </span><span id="PrimaryGlobal" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">\[Global\]</span><a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global②⑧" class="self-link"></a>

If the
\[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧③"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, it indicates that objects
implementing this interface will be used as the global object in a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm①⑧" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a>.

The \[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧④"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> also defines the
<span id="dfn-global-name" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
export="">global names</span> for the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>:

If the \[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\] <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> <a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier②"
data-link-type="dfn">takes an identifier</a>  
« the given <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤③"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> »

If the \[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\] <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> <a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier-list"
id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier-list②" data-link-type="dfn">takes an
identifier list</a>  
the identifier list

The \[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\] extended attribute must be one of the
forms given above.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> The
<a href="#dfn-global-name" id="ref-for-dfn-global-name①"
data-link-type="dfn">global names</a> for the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> are the
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤④"
data-link-type="dfn">identifiers</a> that can be used to reference it in
the
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed③②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>. A single name can be shared
across multiple different global interfaces, allowing an interface to
more easily use
\[<a href="#Exposed" id="ref-for-Exposed③③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Exposed</code></a>\] to expose itself to all of them at
once. For example, "`Worker`" is used to refer to several distinct types
of threading-related global interfaces.

For these global <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a>, the structure of the prototype
chain and how properties corresponding to
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface members</a> will be reflected on the
prototype objects will be different from other interfaces. Specifically:

1.  Any
    <a href="#idl-named-properties" id="ref-for-idl-named-properties④"
    data-link-type="dfn">named properties</a> will be exposed on an
    object in the prototype chain – the
    <a href="#dfn-named-properties-object"
    id="ref-for-dfn-named-properties-object①" data-link-type="dfn">named
    properties object</a> – rather than on the object itself.

2.  <a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member②⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">Interface members</a> from the
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①③⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> will correspond to properties on
    the object itself rather than on
    <a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
    id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype objects</a>.

All <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm①⑨" data-link-type="dfn">realms</a> have an
<span id="realm-is-global-prototype-chain-mutable"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="realm" dfn-type="dfn" export="">is
global prototype chain mutable</span> boolean, which can be set when the
<a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm②⓪" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a> is created. Its
value can not change during the lifetime of the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm②①" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a>. By default it is
set to false.

This allows the `ShadowRealm` global to have a mutable prototype.

<div class="note" role="note">

Placing named properties on an object in the prototype chain is done so
that variable declarations and bareword assignments will shadow the
named property with a property on the global object itself.

Placing properties corresponding to interface members on the object
itself will mean that common feature detection methods like the
following will work:

``` highlight
var indexedDB = window.indexedDB || window.webkitIndexedDB ||
                window.mozIndexedDB || window.msIndexedDB;

var requestAnimationFrame = window.requestAnimationFrame ||
                            window.mozRequestAnimationFrame || ...;
```

Because of the way variable declarations are handled in JavaScript, the
code above would result in the `window.indexedDB` and
`window.requestAnimationFrame` evaluating to undefined, as the shadowing
variable property would already have been created before the assignment
is evaluated.

</div>

If the
\[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> is used on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, then:

- The interface must not define a <a href="#dfn-named-property-setter"
  id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-setter②" data-link-type="dfn">named
  property setter</a>.

- The interface must not define <a href="#dfn-indexed-property-getter"
  id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-getter⑥" data-link-type="dfn">indexed
  property getters</a> or <a href="#dfn-indexed-property-setter"
  id="ref-for-dfn-indexed-property-setter②"
  data-link-type="dfn">setters</a>.

- The interface must not define a
  <a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a>.

- The interface must not also be declared with the
  \[<a href="#LegacyOverrideBuiltIns" id="ref-for-LegacyOverrideBuiltIns②"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyOverrideBuiltIns</code></a>\]
  extended attribute.

- The interface must not
  <a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit①①"
  data-link-type="dfn">inherit</a> from another interface with the
  \[<a href="#LegacyOverrideBuiltIns" id="ref-for-LegacyOverrideBuiltIns③"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyOverrideBuiltIns</code></a>\]
  extended attribute.

- Any other interface must not
  <a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit①②"
  data-link-type="dfn">inherit</a> from it.

If \[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\] is specified on a
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a> definition, then that partial
interface definition must be the part of the interface definition that
defines the <a href="#dfn-named-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-getter④" data-link-type="dfn">named
property getter</a>.

The \[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑧⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> must not be used on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that can have more than one object
implementing it in the same <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm②②" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> This is because the
<a href="#dfn-named-properties-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-properties-object②" data-link-type="dfn">named
properties object</a>, which exposes the named properties, is in the
prototype chain, and it would not make sense for more than one object’s
named properties to be exposed on an object that all of those objects
inherit from.

If an interface is declared with the
\[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global①⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>, then there must not be more
than one <a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> across the interface with the same
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>. There also must not be more than
one <a href="#dfn-stringifier" id="ref-for-dfn-stringifier③"
data-link-type="dfn">stringifier</a> or more than one
<a href="#dfn-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-iterable-declaration①①" data-link-type="dfn">iterable
declaration</a>, <a href="#dfn-async-iterable-declaration"
id="ref-for-dfn-async-iterable-declaration①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">asynchronously iterable declaration</a>,
<a href="#dfn-maplike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-maplike-declaration⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">maplike declaration</a> or
<a href="#dfn-setlike-declaration" id="ref-for-dfn-setlike-declaration⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">setlike declaration</a> across those interfaces.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> This is because all of the
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">members</a> of the interface get flattened down on
to the object that <a href="#implements" id="ref-for-implements⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">implements</a> the interface.

See [§ 3.7.4 Named properties object](#named-properties-object) for the
specific requirements that the use of
\[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global①①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\] entails for
<a href="#idl-named-properties" id="ref-for-idl-named-properties①"
data-link-type="dfn">named properties</a>, and [§ 3.7.5
Constants](#js-constants), [§ 3.7.6 Attributes](#js-attributes) and
[§ 3.7.7 Operations](#js-operations) for the requirements relating to
the location of properties corresponding to
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member②①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface members</a>.

<div id="example-2e291568" class="example">

<a href="#example-2e291568" class="self-link"></a>

The `Window` interface exposes frames as properties on the `Window`
object. Since the `Window` object also serves as the JavaScript global
object, variable declarations or assignments to the named properties
will result in them being replaced by the new value. Variable
declarations for attributes will not create a property that replaces the
existing one.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window, Global=Window]
interface Window {
  getter any (DOMString name);
  attribute DOMString name;
  // ...
};
```

The following HTML document illustrates how the named properties on the
`Window` object can be shadowed, and how the property for an attribute
will not be replaced when declaring a variable of the same name:

``` highlight
<!DOCTYPE html>
<title>Variable declarations and assignments on Window</title>
<iframe name=abc></iframe>
<!-- Shadowing named properties -->
<script>
  window.abc;    // Evaluates to the iframe's Window object.
  abc = 1;       // Shadows the named property.
  window.abc;    // Evaluates to 1.
</script>

<!-- Preserving properties for IDL attributes -->
<script>
  Window.prototype.def = 2;         // Places a property on the prototype.
  window.hasOwnProperty("length");  // Evaluates to true.
  length;                           // Evaluates to 1.
  def;                              // Evaluates to 2.
</script>
<script>
  var length;                       // Variable declaration leaves existing property.
  length;                           // Evaluates to 1.
  var def;                          // Variable declaration creates shadowing property.
  def;                              // Evaluates to undefined.
</script>
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.9. </span><span class="content">\[NewObject\]</span><a href="#NewObject" id="ref-for-NewObject④" class="self-link"></a>

If the
\[<a href="#NewObject" id="ref-for-NewObject①" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">NewObject</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨①"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">regular</a> or
<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">static</a>
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation④⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>, then it indicates that when calling
the operation, a reference to a newly created object must always be
returned.

The
\[<a href="#NewObject" id="ref-for-NewObject②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">NewObject</code></a>\] extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

The
\[<a href="#NewObject" id="ref-for-NewObject③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">NewObject</code></a>\] extended attribute must not be used
on anything other than a
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation③①"
data-link-type="dfn">regular</a> or
<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">static</a>
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation④⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> whose
<a href="#dfn-return-type" id="ref-for-dfn-return-type④"
data-link-type="dfn">return type</a> is an
<a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface①①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> or a
<a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">promise type</a>.

<div id="example-5b56e2ba" class="example">

<a href="#example-5b56e2ba" class="self-link"></a>

As an example, this extended attribute is suitable for use on the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelement"
id="ref-for-dom-document-createelement" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">createElement()</code></a> operation on the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document" id="ref-for-document"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Document</code></a> interface,
since a new object is always returned when it is called.
<a href="#biblio-dom" data-link-type="biblio"
title="DOM Standard">[DOM]</a>

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Document : Node {
  [NewObject] Element createElement(DOMString localName);
  // ...
};
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.10. </span><span class="content">\[PutForwards\]</span><a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards①⑧" class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨②"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①①"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute①③"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a> declaration whose type is an
<a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface①②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a>, it indicates that assigning to
the attribute will have specific behavior. Namely, the assignment is
“forwarded” to the attribute (specified by the extended attribute
argument) on the object that is currently referenced by the attribute
being assigned to.

The \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\] extended
attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier③"
data-link-type="dfn">take an identifier</a>. Assuming that:

- `A` is the <a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute④③"
  data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> on which the
  \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards④"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\]
  extended attribute appears,

- `I` is the <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④②"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> on which `A` is declared,

- `J` is the <a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface①③"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> that `A` is declared to be of,
  and

- `N` is the <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> argument of the extended
  attribute,

then there must be another
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute④④"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> `B` declared on `J` whose
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> is `N`. Assignment of a value to the
attribute `A` on an object implementing `I` will result in that value
being assigned to attribute `B` of the object that `A` references,
instead.

Note that \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\]-annotated
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute④⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a> can be chained. That is, an
attribute with the \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨③"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> can refer to an attribute
that itself has that extended attribute. There must not exist a cycle in
a chain of forwarded assignments. A cycle exists if, when following the
chain of forwarded assignments, a particular attribute on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> is encountered more than once.

An attribute with the \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not also be declared with the
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\]
or \[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\] extended
attributes.

The \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not be used on an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute④⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> that is not
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①②"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>.

The \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not be used on a
<a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">static attribute</a>.

The \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not be used on an attribute declared on a
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

See the [Attributes](#js-attributes) section for how
\[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\] is to be
implemented.

<div id="example-dc4da779" class="example">

<a href="#example-dc4da779" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment③⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines interfaces for names and
people. The \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards①②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\] extended
attribute is used on the `name` attribute of the `Person` interface to
indicate that assignments to that attribute result in assignments to the
`full` attribute of the `Person` object:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Name {
  attribute DOMString full;
  attribute DOMString family;
  attribute DOMString given;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface Person {
  [PutForwards=full] readonly attribute Name name;
  attribute unsigned short age;
};
```

In the JavaScript binding, this would allow assignments to the `name`
property:

``` highlight
var p = getPerson();           // Obtain an instance of Person.

p.name = 'John Citizen';       // This statement...
p.name.full = 'John Citizen';  // ...has the same behavior as this one.
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.11. </span><span class="content">\[Replaceable\]</span><a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable①③" class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨④"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①③"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute①④"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a>, it indicates that setting
the corresponding property on the
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> will result in an own property
with the same name being created on the object which has the value being
assigned. This property will shadow the accessor property corresponding
to the attribute, which exists on the
<a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype object</a>.

The \[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\] extended
attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

An attribute with the \[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not also be declared with the
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\]
or \[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards①③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\] extended
attributes.

The \[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not be used on an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute④⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> that is not
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①④"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>.

The \[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not be used on a
<a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">static attribute</a>.

The \[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not be used on an attribute declared on a
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

See [§ 3.7.6 Attributes](#js-attributes) for the specific requirements
that the use of \[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\] entails.

<div id="example-fe2bdbf4" class="example">

<a href="#example-fe2bdbf4" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment④⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation④⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> that increments a counter, and an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute④⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> that exposes the counter’s value,
which is initially 0:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Counter {
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute unsigned long value;
  undefined increment();
};
```

Assigning to the `value` property on a
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> implementing `Counter` will
shadow the property that corresponds to the
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute④⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a>:

``` highlight
var counter = getCounter();                              // Obtain an instance of Counter.
counter.value;                                           // Evaluates to 0.

counter.hasOwnProperty("value");                         // Evaluates to false.
Object.getPrototypeOf(counter).hasOwnProperty("value");  // Evaluates to true.

counter.increment();
counter.increment();
counter.value;                                           // Evaluates to 2.

counter.value = 'a';                                     // Shadows the property with one that is unrelated
                                                         // to Counter::value.

counter.hasOwnProperty("value");                         // Evaluates to true.

counter.increment();
counter.value;                                           // Evaluates to 'a'.

delete counter.value;                                    // Reveals the original property.
counter.value;                                           // Evaluates to 3.
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.12. </span><span class="content">\[SameObject\]</span><a href="#SameObject" id="ref-for-SameObject⑤" class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#SameObject" id="ref-for-SameObject②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SameObject</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑤⓪"
