data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a>, then it indicates that when getting
the value of the attribute on a given object, the same value must always
be returned.

The \[<a href="#SameObject" id="ref-for-SameObject③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SameObject</code></a>\] extended
attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

The \[<a href="#SameObject" id="ref-for-SameObject④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SameObject</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not be used on anything other than a
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑤①"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> whose type is an
<a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface①④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> or
<a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object①⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a>.

<div id="example-4032028d" class="example">

<a href="#example-4032028d" class="self-link"></a>

As an example, this extended attribute is suitable for use on the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-implementation"
id="ref-for-dom-document-implementation" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">implementation</code></a> attribute on the
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document" id="ref-for-document①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Document</code></a> interface
since the same object is always returned for a given
<a href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document" id="ref-for-document②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Document</code></a> object.
<a href="#biblio-dom" data-link-type="biblio"
title="DOM Standard">[DOM]</a>

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Document : Node {
  [SameObject] readonly attribute DOMImplementation implementation;
  // ...
};
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.13. </span><span class="content">\[SecureContext\]</span><a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext②⓪"
class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface②①"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a>,
<a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin①⑨" data-link-type="dfn">partial
interface mixin</a>,
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface③⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>,
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>,
<a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace①③"
data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a>,
<a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member②②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a>,
<a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a>, or
<a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a>, it indicates that the
construct is <a href="#dfn-exposed" id="ref-for-dfn-exposed④"
data-link-type="dfn">exposed</a> only within a <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#secure-context"
id="ref-for-secure-context②" data-link-type="dfn">secure context</a>.
The \[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
extended attribute must not be used on any other construct.

The \[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

If \[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
appears on an <a href="#dfn-overloaded" id="ref-for-dfn-overloaded①③"
data-link-type="dfn">overloaded</a>
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>, then it must appear on all
overloads.

The \[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> must not be specified both
on

- an <a href="#dfn-interface-member" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-member②③"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface member</a> and its
  <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> or
  <a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface②②"
  data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a>;

- an
  <a href="#interface-mixin-member" id="ref-for-interface-mixin-member②⑦"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin member</a> and its
  <a href="#interface-mixin" id="ref-for-interface-mixin④⑨"
  data-link-type="dfn">interface mixin</a> or
  <a href="#partial-interface-mixin"
  id="ref-for-partial-interface-mixin②⓪" data-link-type="dfn">partial
  interface mixin</a>;

- a <a href="#dfn-namespace-member" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-member①⑦"
  data-link-type="dfn">namespace member</a> and its
  <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace③⓪"
  data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> or
  <a href="#dfn-partial-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-namespace①④"
  data-link-type="dfn">partial namespace</a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> This is because adding the
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> on a
<a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a> when its containing definition is also
annotated with the
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute⑨⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> does not further restrict
the exposure of the <a href="#dfn-member" id="ref-for-dfn-member②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">member</a>.

An <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> without the
\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> must not
<a href="#dfn-inherit" id="ref-for-dfn-inherit①③"
data-link-type="dfn">inherit</a> from another interface that does
specify \[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\].

\[<a href="#SecureContext" id="ref-for-SecureContext①⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SecureContext</code></a>\] must
not be specified on a construct is that is
<a href="#dfn-conditionally-exposed"
id="ref-for-dfn-conditionally-exposed②"
data-link-type="dfn">conditionally exposed</a> on
\[<a href="#CrossOriginIsolated" id="ref-for-CrossOriginIsolated①⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">CrossOriginIsolated</code></a>\].
(Doing so would be redundant, since every environment which is <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability"
id="ref-for-concept-settings-object-cross-origin-isolated-capability③"
data-link-type="dfn">cross-origin isolated</a> is also a <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#secure-context"
id="ref-for-secure-context③" data-link-type="dfn">secure context</a>.)

<div id="example-9e6148d4" class="example">

<a href="#example-9e6148d4" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment④①"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface with one
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤①"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> that is executable from all contexts,
and two which are executable only from secure contexts.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface ExampleFeature {
  // This call will succeed in all contexts.
  Promise <Result> calculateNotSoSecretResult();

  // This operation will not be exposed to a non-secure context. In such a context,
  // there will be no "calculateSecretResult" property on ExampleFeature.prototype.
  [SecureContext] Promise<Result> calculateSecretResult();

  // The same applies here: the attribute will not be exposed to a non-secure context,
  // and in a non-secure context there will be no "secretBoolean" property on
  // ExampleFeature.prototype.
  [SecureContext] readonly attribute boolean secretBoolean;
};

// HeartbeatSensor will not be exposed in a non-secure context, nor will its members.
// In such a context, there will be no "HeartbeatSensor" property on Window.
[Exposed=Window, SecureContext]
interface HeartbeatSensor {
  Promise<float> getHeartbeatsPerMinute();
};

// The interface mixin members defined below will never be exposed in a non-secure context,
// regardless of whether the interface that includes them is. That is, in a non-secure
// context, there will be no "snap" property on ExampleFeature.prototype.
[SecureContext]
interface mixin Snapshotable {
  Promise<boolean> snap();
};
ExampleFeature includes Snapshotable;

// On the other hand, the following interface mixin members will be exposed to a non-secure
// context when included by a host interface that doesn't have the [SecureContext] extended
// attribute. That is, in a non-secure context, there will be a "log" property on
// ExampleFeature.prototype.
interface mixin Loggable {
  Promise<boolean> log();
};
ExampleFeature includes Loggable;
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.3.14. </span><span class="content">\[Unscopable\]</span><a href="#Unscopable" id="ref-for-Unscopable" class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#Unscopable" id="ref-for-Unscopable⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Unscopable</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪①"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a> or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation③②"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a>, it indicates that an object
that <a href="#implements" id="ref-for-implements⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">implements</a> an interface with the given
interface member will not include its property name in any object
environment record with it as its base object. The result of this is
that bare identifiers matching the property name will not resolve to the
property in a `with` statement. This is achieved by including the
property name on the <a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype object</a>’s <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-well-known-symbols"
id="ref-for-sec-well-known-symbols①⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">%Symbol.unscopables%</code></a> property’s value.

The \[<a href="#Unscopable" id="ref-for-Unscopable①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Unscopable</code></a>\] extended
attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

The \[<a href="#Unscopable" id="ref-for-Unscopable②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Unscopable</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not appear on anything other than a
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a> or
<a href="#dfn-regular-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-operation③③"
data-link-type="dfn">regular operation</a>.

The \[<a href="#Unscopable" id="ref-for-Unscopable③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Unscopable</code></a>\] extended
attribute must not be used on an attribute declared on a
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace③①"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

See [§ 3.7.3 Interface prototype object](#interface-prototype-object)
for the specific requirements that the use of
\[<a href="#Unscopable" id="ref-for-Unscopable④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Unscopable</code></a>\] entails.

<div class="note" role="note">

For example, with the following IDL:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Thing {
  undefined f();
  [Unscopable] g();
};
```

the `f` property can be referenced with a bare identifier in a `with`
statement but the `g` property cannot:

``` highlight
var thing = getThing();  // An instance of Thing
with (thing) {
  f;                     // Evaluates to a Function object.
  g;                     // Throws a ReferenceError.
}
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">3.4. </span><span id="es-legacy-extended-attributes" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Legacy extended attributes</span><a href="#js-legacy-extended-attributes" class="self-link"></a>

This section defines a number of
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪②"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> whose presence affects the
JavaScript binding. Unlike those in [§ 3.3 Extended
attributes](#js-extended-attributes), these exist only so that legacy
Web platform features can be specified. They should not be used in
specifications, unless required to specify the behavior of legacy APIs.

Editors who believe they have a good reason for using these extended
attributes are strongly advised to discuss this by [filing an
issue](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/new?title=Intent%20to%20use%20a%20legacy%20extended%20attribute)
before proceeding.

#### <span class="secno">3.4.1. </span><span id="NamedConstructor" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">\[LegacyFactoryFunction\]</span><a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction②②"
class="self-link"></a>

Instead of using this feature, give your interface a
<a href="#idl-constructors" id="ref-for-idl-constructors①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">constructor operation</a>.

If the
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪③"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, it indicates that the JavaScript
global object will have a property with the specified name whose value
is a function that can create objects that implement the interface.
Multiple
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
extended attributes may appear on a given interface.

The
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
extended attribute must <a href="#dfn-xattr-named-argument-list"
id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-named-argument-list②" data-link-type="dfn">take a
named argument list</a>. The [identifier](#prod-identifier) that occurs
directly after the “=” is the
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]'s
<span id="legacyfactoryfunction-identifier" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" lt="LegacyFactoryFunction identifier"
noexport="">identifier</span>. For each
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
extended attribute on the interface, there will be a way to construct an
object that <a href="#implements" id="ref-for-implements⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">implements</a> the interface by passing the
specified arguments to the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#constructor"
id="ref-for-constructor②" data-link-type="dfn">constructor</a> that is
the value of the aforementioned property.

The <a href="#legacyfactoryfunction-identifier"
id="ref-for-legacyfactoryfunction-identifier"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> used for the legacy factory function
must not be the same as that used by a
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
extended attribute on another interface, must not be the same as an
<a href="#legacywindowalias-identifier"
id="ref-for-legacywindowalias-identifier"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> used by a
\[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
extended attribute on this interface or another interface, must not be
the same as an <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of an interface that has an
<a href="#dfn-interface-object" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-object③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface object</a>, and must not be one of the
<a href="#dfn-reserved-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-reserved-identifier①"
data-link-type="dfn">reserved identifiers</a>.

The
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction①②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
and \[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global①②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪④"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> must not be specified on
the same <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①④⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>.

See [§ 3.7.2 Legacy factory functions](#legacy-factory-functions) for
details on how legacy factory functions are to be implemented.

<div id="example-c9fe335f" class="example">

<a href="#example-c9fe335f" class="self-link"></a>

The following IDL defines an interface that uses the
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction①③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
extended attribute.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyFactoryFunction=Audio(DOMString src)]
interface HTMLAudioElement : HTMLMediaElement {
  // ...
};
```

A JavaScript implementation that supports this interface will allow the
construction of `HTMLAudioElement` objects using the `Audio` function.

``` highlight
typeof Audio;                   // Evaluates to 'function'.

var a2 = new Audio('a.flac');   // Creates an HTMLAudioElement using the
                                // one-argument constructor.
```

As an additional legacy quirk, these factory functions will have a
`prototype` property equal to the `prototype` of the original interface:

``` highlight
console.assert(Audio.prototype === HTMLAudioElement.prototype);
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.4.2. </span><span id="LenientSetter" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">\[LegacyLenientSetter\]</span><a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter①③"
class="self-link"></a>

If the
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a>, it indicates that a no-op
setter will be generated for the attribute’s accessor property. This
results in erroneous assignments to the property in strict mode to be
ignored rather than causing an exception to be thrown.

Pages have been observed where authors have attempted to polyfill an IDL
attribute by assigning to the property, but have accidentally done so
even if the property exists. In strict mode, this would cause an
exception to be thrown, potentially breaking page. Without
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\],
this could prevent a browser from shipping the feature.

The \[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\]
extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments①①"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>. It must not be used on
anything other than a
<a href="#dfn-read-only" id="ref-for-dfn-read-only①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">read only</a>
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a>.

An attribute with the
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\]
extended attribute must not also be declared with the
\[<a href="#PutForwards" id="ref-for-PutForwards①④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">PutForwards</code></a>\] or
\[<a href="#Replaceable" id="ref-for-Replaceable①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">Replaceable</code></a>\] extended
attributes.

The \[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\]
extended attribute must not be used on an attribute declared on a
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace③②"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

See the [Attributes](#js-attributes) section for how
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\]
is to be implemented.

<div id="example-15547457" class="example">

<a href="#example-15547457" class="self-link"></a>

The following IDL fragment defines an interface that uses the
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientSetter" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientSetter①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientSetter</code></a>\]
extended attribute.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Example {
  [LegacyLenientSetter] readonly attribute DOMString x;
  readonly attribute DOMString y;
};
```

A JavaScript implementation that supports this interface will have a
setter on the accessor property that correspond to x, which allows any
assignment to be ignored in strict mode.

``` highlight
"use strict";

var example = getExample();  // Get an instance of Example.

// Fine; while we are in strict mode, there is a setter that is a no-op.
example.x = 1;

// Throws a TypeError, since we are in strict mode and there is no setter.
example.y = 1;
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.4.3. </span><span id="LenientThis" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">\[LegacyLenientThis\]</span><a href="#LegacyLenientThis" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientThis①⓪"
class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#LegacyLenientThis" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientThis①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientThis</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a>, it indicates that
invocations of the attribute’s getter or setter with a this value that
is not an object that <a href="#implements" id="ref-for-implements⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">implements</a> the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> on which the attribute appears will
be ignored.

The \[<a href="#LegacyLenientThis" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientThis②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientThis</code></a>\]
extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments①②"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>. It must not be used on a
<a href="#dfn-static-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-static-attribute⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">static attribute</a>.

The \[<a href="#LegacyLenientThis" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientThis③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientThis</code></a>\]
extended attribute must not be used on an attribute declared on a
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace③③"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

See the [Attributes](#js-attributes) section for how
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientThis" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientThis④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientThis</code></a>\] is
to be implemented.

<div id="example-b5f368f2" class="example">

<a href="#example-b5f368f2" class="self-link"></a>

The following IDL fragment defines an interface that uses the
\[<a href="#LegacyLenientThis" id="ref-for-LegacyLenientThis⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyLenientThis</code></a>\]
extended attribute.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Example {
  [LegacyLenientThis] attribute DOMString x;
  attribute DOMString y;
};
```

A JavaScript implementation that supports this interface will allow the
getter and setter of the accessor property that corresponds to x to be
invoked with something other than an `Example` object.

``` highlight
var example = getExample();  // Get an instance of Example.
var obj = { };

// Fine.
example.x;

// Ignored, since the this value is not an Example object and [LegacyLenientThis] is used.
Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(Example.prototype, "x").get.call(obj);

// Also ignored, since Example.prototype is not an Example object and [LegacyLenientThis] is used.
Example.prototype.x;

// Throws a TypeError, since Example.prototype is not an Example object.
Example.prototype.y;
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.4.4. </span><span class="content">\[LegacyNamespace\]</span><a href="#LegacyNamespace" id="ref-for-LegacyNamespace①⓪"
class="self-link"></a>

Instead of using this feature, interface names can be formed with a
naming convention of starting with a particular prefix for a set of
interfaces, as part of the identifier, without the intervening dot.

If the \[<a href="#LegacyNamespace" id="ref-for-LegacyNamespace②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyNamespace</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, it indicates that the
<a href="#dfn-interface-object" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-object④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface object</a> for this interface will not be
created as a property of the global object, but rather as a property of
the <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace③④"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> identified by the argument to the
extended attribute.

The \[<a href="#LegacyNamespace" id="ref-for-LegacyNamespace③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyNamespace</code></a>\]
extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier④"
data-link-type="dfn">take an identifier</a>. This identifier must be the
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑤⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of a
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace③⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> definition.

The \[<a href="#LegacyNamespace" id="ref-for-LegacyNamespace④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyNamespace</code></a>\] and
\[<a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject" id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject①"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNoInterfaceObject</code></a>\] extended attributes
must not be specified on the same interface.

See [§ 3.13.1 Namespace object](#namespace-object) for details on how an
interface is exposed on a namespace.

<div id="example-194971b0" class="example">

<a href="#example-194971b0" class="self-link"></a> The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment④②"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines a
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace③⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> and an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤②"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> which uses
\[<a href="#LegacyNamespace" id="ref-for-LegacyNamespace⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyNamespace</code></a>\] to
be defined inside of it.

``` highlight
namespace Foo { };

[LegacyNamespace=Foo]
interface Bar {
  constructor();
};
```

In a JavaScript implementation of the above namespace and interface, the
constructor Bar can be accessed as follows:

``` highlight
var instance = new Foo.Bar();
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.4.5. </span><span id="NoInterfaceObject" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">\[LegacyNoInterfaceObject\]</span><a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject"
id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject①④" class="self-link"></a>

If the
\[<a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject" id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject②"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNoInterfaceObject</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, it indicates that an
<a href="#dfn-interface-object" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-object⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface object</a> will not exist for the
interface in the JavaScript binding.

The
\[<a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject" id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject③"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNoInterfaceObject</code></a>\] extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments①③"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

The
\[<a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject" id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject④"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNoInterfaceObject</code></a>\] extended attribute must
not be specified on an interface that has any <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#constructor"
id="ref-for-constructor③" data-link-type="dfn">constructors</a> or
<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">static operations</a> defined on it.

An interface that does not have the
\[<a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject" id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNoInterfaceObject</code></a>\] extended attribute
specified must not inherit from an interface that has the
\[<a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject" id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNoInterfaceObject</code></a>\] extended attribute
specified.

See [§ 3.7 Interfaces](#js-interfaces) for the specific requirements
that the use of
\[<a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject" id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNoInterfaceObject</code></a>\] entails.

<div id="example-ecf33c5c" class="example">

<a href="#example-ecf33c5c" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment④③"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines two interfaces, one whose
interface object is exposed on the JavaScript global object, and one
whose isn’t:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Storage {
  undefined addEntry(unsigned long key, any value);
};

[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyNoInterfaceObject]
interface Query {
  any lookupEntry(unsigned long key);
};
```

A JavaScript implementation of the above IDL would allow manipulation of
`Storage`’s prototype, but not `Query`’s.

``` highlight
typeof Storage;                        // evaluates to "object"

// Add some tracing alert() call to Storage.addEntry.
var fn = Storage.prototype.addEntry;
Storage.prototype.addEntry = function(key, value) {
  alert('Calling addEntry()');
  return fn.call(this, key, value);
};

typeof Query;                          // evaluates to "undefined"
var fn = Query.prototype.lookupEntry;  // exception, Query isn't defined
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.4.6. </span><span id="TreatNullAs" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">\[LegacyNullToEmptyString\]</span><a href="#LegacyNullToEmptyString" id="ref-for-LegacyNullToEmptyString⑥"
class="self-link"></a>

If the
\[<a href="#LegacyNullToEmptyString" id="ref-for-LegacyNullToEmptyString②"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNullToEmptyString</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⓪⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on the
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString④⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> or
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString①④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a> type, it
creates a new IDL type such that that when a JavaScript null is
converted to the IDL type, it will be handled differently from its
default handling. Instead of being stringified to "`null`", which is the
default, it will be converted to the empty string.

The
\[<a href="#LegacyNullToEmptyString" id="ref-for-LegacyNullToEmptyString③"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNullToEmptyString</code></a>\] extended attribute must
not be <a href="#idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with"
id="ref-for-idl-type-extended-attribute-associated-with②⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">associated with</a> a type that is not
<a href="#idl-DOMString" id="ref-for-idl-DOMString④①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMString</code></a> or
<a href="#idl-USVString" id="ref-for-idl-USVString①⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">USVString</code></a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span> This means that even `DOMString?` must
not use
\[<a href="#LegacyNullToEmptyString" id="ref-for-LegacyNullToEmptyString④"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNullToEmptyString</code></a>\], since null is a valid
value of that type.

See [§ 3.2.10 DOMString](#js-DOMString) for the specific requirements
that the use of
\[<a href="#LegacyNullToEmptyString" id="ref-for-LegacyNullToEmptyString⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNullToEmptyString</code></a>\] entails.

<div id="example-485c9e14" class="example">

<a href="#example-485c9e14" class="self-link"></a> The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment④④"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface that has one
attribute whose type has the extended attribute, and one operation whose
argument’s type has the extended attribute:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Dog {
  attribute DOMString name;
  attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString owner;

  boolean isMemberOfBreed([LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString breedName);
};
```

A JavaScript implementation implementing the `Dog` interface would
convert a null value assigned to the `owner` property or passed as the
argument to the `isMemberOfBreed` function to the empty string rather
than "`null`":

``` highlight
var d = getDog();         // Assume d is a platform object implementing the Dog
                          // interface.

d.name = null;            // This assigns the string "null" to the .name
                          // property.

d.owner = null;           // This assigns the string "" to the .owner property.

d.isMemberOfBreed(null);  // This passes the string "" to the isMemberOfBreed
                          // function.
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.4.7. </span><span id="OverrideBuiltins" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">\[LegacyOverrideBuiltIns\]</span><a href="#LegacyOverrideBuiltIns" id="ref-for-LegacyOverrideBuiltIns①③"
class="self-link"></a>

If the
\[<a href="#LegacyOverrideBuiltIns" id="ref-for-LegacyOverrideBuiltIns④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyOverrideBuiltIns</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, it indicates that for a
<a href="#dfn-legacy-platform-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-legacy-platform-object①" data-link-type="dfn">legacy
platform object</a> implementing the interface, properties corresponding
to all of the object’s <a href="#dfn-supported-property-names"
id="ref-for-dfn-supported-property-names②"
data-link-type="dfn">supported property names</a> will appear to be on
the object, regardless of what other properties exist on the object or
its prototype chain. This means that named properties will always shadow
any properties that would otherwise appear on the object. This is in
contrast to the usual behavior, which is for named properties to be
exposed only if there is no property with the same name on the object
itself or somewhere on its prototype chain.

The
\[<a href="#LegacyOverrideBuiltIns" id="ref-for-LegacyOverrideBuiltIns⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyOverrideBuiltIns</code></a>\]
extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments①④"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a> and must not appear on an
interface that does not define a <a href="#dfn-named-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-getter⑤" data-link-type="dfn">named
property getter</a> or that also is declared with the
\[<a href="#Global" id="ref-for-Global①③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Global</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①①"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>. If the extended attribute
is specified on a
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface②③"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a> definition, then that partial
interface definition must be the part of the interface definition that
defines the <a href="#dfn-named-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-getter⑥" data-link-type="dfn">named
property getter</a>.

If the
\[<a href="#LegacyOverrideBuiltIns" id="ref-for-LegacyOverrideBuiltIns⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyOverrideBuiltIns</code></a>\]
extended attribute is specified on a
<a href="#dfn-partial-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-partial-interface②④"
data-link-type="dfn">partial interface</a> definition, it is considered
to appear on the <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> itself.

See [§ 3.9 Legacy platform objects](#js-legacy-platform-objects) and
[§ 3.9.3
\[\[DefineOwnProperty\]\]](#legacy-platform-object-defineownproperty)
for the specific requirements that the use of
\[<a href="#LegacyOverrideBuiltIns" id="ref-for-LegacyOverrideBuiltIns⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyOverrideBuiltIns</code></a>\]
entails.

<div id="example-b703da70" class="example">

<a href="#example-b703da70" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment④⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines two
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a>, one that has a
<a href="#dfn-named-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-getter⑦" data-link-type="dfn">named
property getter</a> and one that does not.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface StringMap {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter DOMString lookup(DOMString key);
};

[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyOverrideBuiltIns]
interface StringMap2 {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter DOMString lookup(DOMString key);
};
```

In a JavaScript implementation of these two interfaces, getting certain
properties on objects implementing the interfaces will result in
different values:

``` highlight
// Obtain an instance of StringMap.  Assume that it has "abc", "length" and
// "toString" as supported property names.
var map1 = getStringMap();

// This invokes the named property getter.
map1.abc;

// This fetches the "length" property on the object that corresponds to the
// length attribute.
map1.length;

// This fetches the "toString" property from the object's prototype chain.
map1.toString;

// Obtain an instance of StringMap2.  Assume that it also has "abc", "length"
// and "toString" as supported property names.
var map2 = getStringMap2();

// This invokes the named property getter.
map2.abc;

// This also invokes the named property getter, despite the fact that the "length"
// property on the object corresponds to the length attribute.
map2.length;

// This too invokes the named property getter, despite the fact that "toString" is
// a property in map2's prototype chain.
map2.toString;
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.4.8. </span><span id="TreatNonObjectAsNull" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">\[LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull\]</span><a href="#LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull"
id="ref-for-LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull①⓪" class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull"
id="ref-for-LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①②"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function②⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a>, then it indicates that any
value assigned to an
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑤②"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> whose type is a
<a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a>
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function②⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> will be converted more
loosely: if the value is not an object, it will be converted to null,
and if the value is not
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-iscallable"
id="ref-for-sec-iscallable④" data-link-type="dfn">callable</a>, it will
be converted to a
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function②⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> value that does nothing when
called.

See [§ 3.2.20 Nullable types — T?](#js-nullable-type), [§ 3.2.19
Callback function types](#js-callback-function) and [§ 3.12 Invoking
callback functions](#js-invoking-callback-functions) for the specific
requirements that the use of \[<a href="#LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull"
id="ref-for-LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull</code></a>\] entails.

<div id="example-abade5af" class="example">

<a href="#example-abade5af" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment④⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface that has one
attribute whose type is a \[<a href="#LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull"
id="ref-for-LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull⑧" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull</code></a>\]-annotated
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function②⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> and another whose type is a
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function③⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> without the
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①③"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>:

``` highlight
callback OccurrenceHandler = undefined (DOMString details);

[LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull]
callback ErrorHandler = undefined (DOMString details);

[Exposed=Window]
interface Manager {
  attribute OccurrenceHandler? handler1;
  attribute ErrorHandler? handler2;
};
```

In a JavaScript implementation, assigning a value that is not an object
(such as a Number value), or that is not
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-iscallable"
id="ref-for-sec-iscallable⑤" data-link-type="dfn">callable</a> to
handler1 will have different behavior from that when assigning to
handler2:

``` highlight
var manager = getManager();  // Get an instance of Manager.

manager.handler1 = function() { };
manager.handler1;            // Evaluates to the function.

try {
  manager.handler1 = 123;    // Throws a TypeError.
} catch (e) {
}

try {
  manager.handler1 = {};     // Throws a TypeError.
} catch (e) {
}

manager.handler2 = function() { };
manager.handler2;            // Evaluates to the function.

manager.handler2 = 123;
manager.handler2;            // Evaluates to null.

manager.handler2 = {};
manager.handler2;            // Evaluates to the object.
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.4.9. </span><span class="content">\[LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties\]</span><a href="#LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties"
id="ref-for-LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties" class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties"
id="ref-for-LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①④"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on a
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> that
<a href="#dfn-support-named-properties"
id="ref-for-dfn-support-named-properties③" data-link-type="dfn">supports
named properties</a>, it indicates that all the interface’s named
properties are unenumerable.

The \[<a href="#LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties"
id="ref-for-LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties①"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties</code></a>\] extended
attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a> and must not appear on an
interface that does not define a <a href="#dfn-named-property-getter"
id="ref-for-dfn-named-property-getter⑧" data-link-type="dfn">named
property getter</a>.

If the \[<a href="#LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties"
id="ref-for-LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties②"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties</code></a>\] extended
attribute is specified on an interface, then it applies to all its
derived interfaces and must not be specified on any of them.

See <a href="#legacy-platform-object-getownproperty"
id="ref-for-legacy-platform-object-getownproperty">§ 3.9.1
[[GetOwnProperty]]</a> for the specific requirements that the use of
\[<a href="#LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties"
id="ref-for-LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties③"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties</code></a>\] entails.

#### <span class="secno">3.4.10. </span><span id="Unforgeable" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">\[LegacyUnforgeable\]</span><a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable⑨"
class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyUnforgeable</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attributes</a> or
non-<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation①①"
data-link-type="dfn">static</a>
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤②"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a>, it indicates that the attribute or
operation will be reflected as a JavaScript property in a way that means
its behavior cannot be modified and that performing a property lookup on
the object will always result in the attribute’s property value being
returned. In particular, the property will be non-configurable and will
exist as an own property on the object itself rather than on its
prototype.

An attribute or operation is said to be
<span id="dfn-unforgeable-on-an-interface" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">unforgeable</span> on a given interface `A` if
the attribute or operation is declared on `A`, and is annotated with the
\[<a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyUnforgeable</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a>.

The \[<a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyUnforgeable</code></a>\]
extended attribute must
<a href="#dfn-xattr-no-arguments" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-no-arguments①⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">take no arguments</a>.

The \[<a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyUnforgeable</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> must not appear on anything
other than a
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute②①"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a> or a
non-<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation①②"
data-link-type="dfn">static</a>
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤③"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>. If it does appear on an
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤④"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a>, then it must appear on all
operations with the same
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑥⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> on that interface.

The \[<a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyUnforgeable</code></a>\]
extended attribute must not be used on an attribute declared on a
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace③⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>.

If an attribute or operation `X` is
<a href="#dfn-unforgeable-on-an-interface"
id="ref-for-dfn-unforgeable-on-an-interface"
data-link-type="dfn">unforgeable</a> on an interface `A`, and `A` is one
of the <a href="#dfn-inherited-interfaces"
id="ref-for-dfn-inherited-interfaces①⑦" data-link-type="dfn">inherited
interfaces</a> of another interface `B`, then `B` must not have a
<a href="#dfn-regular-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-regular-attribute②②"
data-link-type="dfn">regular attribute</a> or
non-<a href="#dfn-static-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-static-operation①③"
data-link-type="dfn">static</a>
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> with the same
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑥①"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> as `X`.

<div class="note" role="note">

For example, the following is disallowed:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface A1 {
  [LegacyUnforgeable] readonly attribute DOMString x;
};
[Exposed=Window]
interface B1 : A1 {
  undefined x();  // Invalid; would be shadowed by A1's x.
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface B2 : A1 { };
B2 includes M1;
interface mixin M1 {
  undefined x();  // Invalid; B2's copy of x would be shadowed by A1's x.
};
```

</div>

See [§ 3.7.6 Attributes](#js-attributes), [§ 3.7.7
Operations](#js-operations), [§ 3.8 Platform objects implementing
interfaces](#js-platform-objects), [§ 3.9 Legacy platform
objects](#js-legacy-platform-objects) and [§ 3.9.3
\[\[DefineOwnProperty\]\]](#legacy-platform-object-defineownproperty)
for the specific requirements that the use of
\[<a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyUnforgeable</code></a>\]
entails.

<div id="example-526d5162" class="example">

<a href="#example-526d5162" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment④⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines an interface that has two
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑤③"
data-link-type="dfn">attributes</a>, one of which is designated as
\[<a href="#LegacyUnforgeable" id="ref-for-LegacyUnforgeable⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyUnforgeable</code></a>\]:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface System {
  [LegacyUnforgeable] readonly attribute DOMString username;
  readonly attribute long long loginTime;
};
```

In a JavaScript implementation of the interface, the username attribute
will be exposed as a non-configurable property on the object itself:

``` highlight
var system = getSystem();                      // Get an instance of System.

system.hasOwnProperty("username");             // Evaluates to true.
system.hasOwnProperty("loginTime");            // Evaluates to false.
System.prototype.hasOwnProperty("username");   // Evaluates to false.
System.prototype.hasOwnProperty("loginTime");  // Evaluates to true.

try {
  // This call would fail, since the property is non-configurable.
  Object.defineProperty(system, "username", { value: "administrator" });
} catch (e) { }

// This defineProperty call would succeed, because System.prototype.loginTime
// is configurable.
var forgedLoginTime = 5;
Object.defineProperty(System.prototype, "loginTime", { value: forgedLoginTime });

system.loginTime;  // So this now evaluates to forgedLoginTime.
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.4.11. </span><span class="content">\[LegacyWindowAlias\]</span><a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias①⑥"
class="self-link"></a>

If the \[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> appears on an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>, it indicates that the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window"
id="ref-for-window②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Window</code></a>
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑤⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> will have a property for each
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑥②"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> mentioned in the extended attribute,
whose value is the
<a href="#dfn-interface-object" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-object⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">interface object</a> for the interface.

The \[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
extended attribute must either
<a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">take an identifier</a> or
<a href="#dfn-xattr-identifier-list"
id="ref-for-dfn-xattr-identifier-list③" data-link-type="dfn">take an
identifier list</a>. The [identifier](#prod-identifier)s that occur
after the “=” are the
\[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]'s
<span id="legacywindowalias-identifier" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" lt="LegacyWindowAlias identifier"
noexport="">identifiers</span>.

Each of the <a href="#legacywindowalias-identifier"
id="ref-for-legacywindowalias-identifier①"
data-link-type="dfn">identifiers</a> of
\[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
must not be the same as one used by a
\[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
extended attribute on this interface or another interface, must not be
the same as the <a href="#legacyfactoryfunction-identifier"
id="ref-for-legacyfactoryfunction-identifier①"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> used by a
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction①④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
extended attribute on this interface or another interface, must not be
the same as an <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑥③"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of an interface that has an
<a href="#dfn-interface-object" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-object⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface object</a>, and must not be one of the
<a href="#dfn-reserved-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-reserved-identifier②"
data-link-type="dfn">reserved identifiers</a>.

The \[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
and
\[<a href="#LegacyNoInterfaceObject" id="ref-for-LegacyNoInterfaceObject⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">LegacyNoInterfaceObject</code></a>\] extended attributes
must not be specified on the same interface.

The \[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
and \[<a href="#LegacyNamespace" id="ref-for-LegacyNamespace⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyNamespace</code></a>\]
extended attributes must not be specified on the same interface.

The \[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
extended attribute must not be specified on an interface that does not
include the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window"
id="ref-for-window③" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Window</code></a>
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface①⑥⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> in its
<a href="#dfn-exposure-set" id="ref-for-dfn-exposure-set①④"
data-link-type="dfn">exposure set</a>.

An interface must not have more than one
\[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias①⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
extended attributes specified.

See [§ 3.7 Interfaces](#js-interfaces) for details on how legacy window
aliases are to be implemented.

<div id="example-758340c7" class="example">

<a href="#example-758340c7" class="self-link"></a>

The following IDL defines an interface that uses the
\[<a href="#LegacyWindowAlias" id="ref-for-LegacyWindowAlias①①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyWindowAlias</code></a>\]
extended attribute.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyWindowAlias=WebKitCSSMatrix]
interface DOMMatrix : DOMMatrixReadOnly {
  // ...
};
```

A JavaScript implementation that supports this interface will expose two
properties on the <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window"
id="ref-for-window④" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Window</code></a> object with the same value and the same
characteristics; one for exposing the
<a href="#dfn-interface-object" id="ref-for-dfn-interface-object⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">interface object</a> normally, and one for exposing
it with a legacy name.

``` highlight
WebKitCSSMatrix === DOMMatrix;     // Evaluates to true.

var m = new WebKitCSSMatrix();     // Creates a new object that
                                   // implements DOMMatrix.

m.constructor === DOMMatrix;       // Evaluates to true.
m.constructor === WebKitCSSMatrix; // Evaluates to true.
{}.toString.call(m);               // Evaluates to '[object DOMMatrix]'.
```

</div>

### <span class="secno">3.5. </span><span id="es-security" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Security</span><a href="#js-security" class="self-link"></a>

Certain algorithms in the sections below are defined to
<span id="dfn-perform-a-security-check" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">perform a security check</span> on a given
object. This check is used to determine whether a given
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> invocation or
<a href="#dfn-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-attribute⑤④"
data-link-type="dfn">attribute</a> access should be allowed. The
security check takes the following three inputs:

1.  the
    <a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object①⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> on which the operation
    invocation or attribute access is being done,

2.  the <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑥④"
    data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of the operation or attribute,
    and

3.  the type of the <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
    id="ref-for-function-object⑨" data-link-type="dfn">function object</a>
    – "`method`" (when it corresponds to an IDL operation), or
    "`getter`" or "`setter`" (when it corresponds to the getter or
    setter function of an IDL attribute).

<span class="marker">Note:</span> The HTML Standard defines how a
security check is performed.
<a href="#biblio-html" data-link-type="biblio"
title="HTML Standard">[HTML]</a>

### <span class="secno">3.6. </span><span id="es-overloads" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Overload resolution algorithm</span><a href="#js-overloads" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="overload resolution algorithm">

In order to define how function invocations are resolved, the
<span id="dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">overload resolution algorithm</span> is
defined. Its input is an <a href="#dfn-effective-overload-set"
id="ref-for-dfn-effective-overload-set①②" data-link-type="dfn">effective
overload set</a>, `S`, and a list of JavaScript values, `args`. Its
output is a pair consisting of the
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> or
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> of one of `S`’s entries and
a list of IDL values or the special value “missing”. The algorithm
behaves as follows:

1.  Let `maxarg` be the length of the longest type list of the entries
    in `S`.

2.  Let `n` be the <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
    id="ref-for-list-size④" data-link-type="dfn">size</a> of `args`.

3.  Initialize `argcount` to be min(`maxarg`, `n`).

4.  Remove from `S` all entries whose type list is not of length
    `argcount`.

5.  If `S` is empty, then
    <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw③④"
    data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror③④"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

6.  Initialize `d` to −1.

7.  Initialize `method` to undefined.

8.  If there is more than one entry in `S`, then set `d` to be the
    <a href="#dfn-distinguishing-argument-index"
    id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishing-argument-index⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">distinguishing argument index</a> for the
    entries of `S`.

9.  Initialize `values` to be an empty list, where each entry will be
    either an IDL value or the special value “missing”.

10. Initialize `i` to 0.

11. While `i` \< `d`:

    1.  Let `V` be `args`\[`i`\].

    2.  Let `type` be the type at index `i` in the type list of any
        entry in `S`.

        <span class="marker">Note:</span> All entries in `S` at this
        point have the same type and
        <a href="#dfn-optionality-value" id="ref-for-dfn-optionality-value①"
        data-link-type="dfn">optionality value</a> at index `i`.

    3.  Let `optionality` be the value at index `i` in the list of
        <a href="#dfn-optionality-value" id="ref-for-dfn-optionality-value②"
        data-link-type="dfn">optionality values</a> of any entry in `S`.

    4.  If `optionality` is “optional” and `V` is undefined, then:

        1.  If the argument at index `i` is declared with a
            <a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
            id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value①②"
            data-link-type="dfn">default value</a>, then append to
            `values` that default value.

        2.  Otherwise, append to `values` the special value “missing”.

    5.  Otherwise, append to `values` the result of
        <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
        id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value⑦⓪"
        data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `V` to IDL type `type`.

    6.  Set `i` to `i` + 1.

12. If `i` = `d`, then:

    1.  Let `V` be `args`\[`i`\].

        <span class="marker">Note:</span> This is the argument that will
        be used to resolve which overload is selected.

    2.  If `V` is undefined, and there is an entry in `S` whose list of
        <a href="#dfn-optionality-value" id="ref-for-dfn-optionality-value③"
        data-link-type="dfn">optionality values</a> has “optional” at
        index `i`, then remove from `S` all other entries.

    3.  Otherwise: if `V` is null or undefined, and there is an entry in
        `S` that has one of the following types at position `i` of its
        type list,

        - a
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type③⓪"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable type</a>

        - a <a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary①⑧"
          data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a>

        - an <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types⑨"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a> whose
          <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
          id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type⑥" data-link-type="dfn">inner
          type</a> is one of the above types

        - a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type④②"
          data-link-type="dfn">union type</a> or
          <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types①⓪"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated</a> union type that
          <a href="#dfn-includes-a-nullable-type"
          id="ref-for-dfn-includes-a-nullable-type④" data-link-type="dfn">includes
          a nullable type</a> or that has a
          <a href="#idl-dictionary" id="ref-for-idl-dictionary①⑨"
          data-link-type="dfn">dictionary type</a> in its
          <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
          id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types①②"
          data-link-type="dfn">flattened members</a>

        then remove from `S` all other entries.

    4.  Otherwise: if `V`
        <a href="#is-a-platform-object" id="ref-for-is-a-platform-object①"
        data-link-type="dfn">is a platform object</a>, and there is an
        entry in `S` that has one of the following types at position `i`
        of its type list,

        - an <a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface①⑤"
          data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> that `V`
          <a href="#implements" id="ref-for-implements①⓪"
          data-link-type="dfn">implements</a>

        - <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object②⓪"
          data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a>

        - a
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type③①"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a> version of any of the above
          types

        - an <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types①①"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a> whose
          <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
          id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type⑦" data-link-type="dfn">inner
          type</a> is one of the above types

        - a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type④③"
          data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>,
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type③②"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a> union type, or
          <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types①②"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated</a> union type that has one of
          the above types in its
          <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
          id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types①③"
          data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>

        then remove from `S` all other entries.

    5.  Otherwise: if `V`
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-type"
        id="ref-for-sec-object-type①⑨" data-link-type="dfn">is an Object</a>,
        `V` has an \[\[ArrayBufferData\]\] <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots"
        id="ref-for-sec-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots①①"
        data-link-type="dfn">internal slot</a>, and there is an entry in
        `S` that has one of the following types at position `i` of its
        type list,

        - <a href="#idl-ArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-ArrayBuffer②②"
          data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBuffer</code></a>

        - <a href="#idl-SharedArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-SharedArrayBuffer①⑥"
          data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SharedArrayBuffer</code></a>

        - <a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object②①"
          data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a>

        - a
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type③③"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a> version of either of the
          above types

        - an <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types①③"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a> whose
          <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
          id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type⑧" data-link-type="dfn">inner
          type</a> is one of the above types

        - a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type④④"
          data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>,
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type③④"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a> union type, or
          <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types①④"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated</a> union type that has one of
          the above types in its
          <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
          id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types①④"
          data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>

        then remove from `S` all other entries.

    6.  Otherwise: if `V`
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-type"
        id="ref-for-sec-object-type②⓪" data-link-type="dfn">is an Object</a>,
        `V` has a \[\[DataView\]\] <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots"
        id="ref-for-sec-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots①②"
        data-link-type="dfn">internal slot</a>, and there is an entry in
        `S` that has one of the following types at position `i` of its
        type list,

        - <a href="#idl-DataView" id="ref-for-idl-DataView⑦"

          id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type②⓪" data-link-type="dfn">inner
          type</a> is one of the above types

        - a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type⑤⑥"
          data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>,
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑤⑧"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a> union type, or
          <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types③⑧"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated</a> union type that has one of
          the above types in its
          <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
          id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types②⑥"
          data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>

        then remove from `S` all other entries.

    17. Otherwise: if there is an entry in `S` that has one of the
        following types at position `i` of its type list,

        - <a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean①⑧"
          data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a>

        - a
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑤⑨"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a>
          <a href="#idl-boolean" id="ref-for-idl-boolean①⑨"
          data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">boolean</code></a>

        - an <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types③⑨"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a> whose
          <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
          id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type②①" data-link-type="dfn">inner
          type</a> is one of the above types

        - a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type⑤⑦"
          data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>,
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑥⓪"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a> union type, or
          <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types④⓪"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated</a> union type that has one of
          the above types in its
          <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
          id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types②⑦"
          data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>

        then remove from `S` all other entries.

    18. Otherwise: if there is an entry in `S` that has one of the
        following types at position `i` of its type list,

        - <a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint②①"
          data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a>

        - a
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑥①"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a>
          <a href="#idl-bigint" id="ref-for-idl-bigint②②"
          data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">bigint</code></a>

        - an <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types④①"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated type</a> whose
          <a href="#annotated-types-inner-type"
          id="ref-for-annotated-types-inner-type②②" data-link-type="dfn">inner
          type</a> is one of the above types

        - a <a href="#dfn-union-type" id="ref-for-dfn-union-type⑤⑧"
          data-link-type="dfn">union type</a>,
          <a href="#dfn-nullable-type" id="ref-for-dfn-nullable-type⑥②"
          data-link-type="dfn">nullable</a> union type, or
          <a href="#annotated-types" id="ref-for-annotated-types④②"
          data-link-type="dfn">annotated</a> union type that has one of
          the above types in its
          <a href="#dfn-flattened-union-member-types"
          id="ref-for-dfn-flattened-union-member-types②⑧"
          data-link-type="dfn">flattened member types</a>

        then remove from `S` all other entries.

    19. Otherwise: if there is an entry in `S` that has
        <a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any①⑤" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">any</code></a> at position `i` of its type list,
        then remove from `S` all other entries.

    20. Otherwise:
        <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw③⑤"
        data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> a <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror③⑤"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

13. Let `callable` be the
    <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑤⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> or
    <a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①②⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> of the single entry in
    `S`.

14. If `i` = `d` and `method` is not undefined, then

    1.  Let `V` be `args`\[`i`\].

    2.  Let `T` be the type at index `i` in the type list of the
        remaining entry in `S`.

    3.  Assert: `T` is a
        <a href="#sequence-type" id="ref-for-sequence-type②③"
        data-link-type="dfn">sequence type</a>.

    4.  Append to `values` the result of
        <a href="#create-sequence-from-iterable"
        id="ref-for-create-sequence-from-iterable③"
        data-link-type="dfn">creating a sequence</a> of type `T` from
        `V` and `method`.

    5.  Set `i` to `i` + 1.

15. While `i` \< `argcount`:

    1.  Let `V` be `args`\[`i`\].

    2.  Let `type` be the type at index `i` in the type list of the
        remaining entry in `S`.

    3.  Let `optionality` be the value at index `i` in the list of
        <a href="#dfn-optionality-value" id="ref-for-dfn-optionality-value④"
        data-link-type="dfn">optionality values</a> of the remaining
        entry in `S`.

    4.  If `optionality` is “optional” and `V` is undefined, then:

        1.  If the argument at index `i` is declared with a
            <a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
            id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value①③"
            data-link-type="dfn">default value</a>, then append to
            `values` that default value.

        2.  Otherwise, append to `values` the special value “missing”.

    5.  Otherwise, append to `values` the result of
        <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
        id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value⑦①"
        data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `V` to IDL type `type`.

    6.  Set `i` to `i` + 1.

16. While `i` is less than the number of arguments `callable` is
    declared to take:

    1.  If `callable`’s argument at index `i` is declared with a
        <a href="#dfn-optional-argument-default-value"
        id="ref-for-dfn-optional-argument-default-value①④"
        data-link-type="dfn">default value</a>, then append to `values`
        that default value.

    2.  Otherwise, if `callable`’s argument at index `i` is not
        variadic, then append to `values` the special value “missing”.

    3.  Set `i` to `i` + 1.

17. Return the pair \<`callable`, `values`\>.

</div>

<div class="note" role="note">

The overload resolution algorithm performs both the identification of
which overloaded operation, constructor, etc. is being called, and the
conversion of the JavaScript argument values to their corresponding IDL
values. Informally, it operates as follows.

First, the selection of valid overloads is done by considering the
number of JavaScript arguments that were passed in to the function:

- If there are more arguments passed in than the longest overload
  argument list, then they are ignored.

- After ignoring these trailing arguments, only overloads that can take
  this exact number of arguments are considered. If there are none, then
  a
  <a href="#exceptiondef-typeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-typeerror①②"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a> is thrown.

Once we have a set of possible overloads with the right number of
arguments, the JavaScript values are converted from left to right. The
nature of the restrictions on overloading means that if we have multiple
possible overloads at this point, then there will be one position in the
argument list that will be used to distinguish which overload we will
finally select; this is the <a href="#dfn-distinguishing-argument-index"
id="ref-for-dfn-distinguishing-argument-index⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">distinguishing argument index</a>.

We first convert the arguments to the left of the distinguishing
argument. (There is a requirement that an argument to the left of the
distinguishing argument index has the same type as in the other
overloads, at the same index.) Then we inspect the type of the
JavaScript value that is passed in at the distinguishing argument index
to determine which IDL type it can correspond to. This allows us to
select the final overload that will be invoked. If the value passed in
is undefined and there is an overload with an
