#### <span class="secno">3.10.4. </span><span id="es-observable-array-getOwnPropertyDescriptor" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`</span><a href="#js-observable-array-getOwnPropertyDescriptor"
class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm"
algorithm="observable array exotic object getOwnPropertyDescriptor trap">

The steps for the `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` proxy trap for
<a href="#observable-array-exotic-object"
id="ref-for-observable-array-exotic-object④"
data-link-type="dfn">observable array exotic objects</a>, given `O` and
`P`, are as follows:

1.  Let `handler` be the this value.

2.  Let `length` be `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\]'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
    id="ref-for-list-size①⑤" data-link-type="dfn">size</a>.

3.  If `P` is "length", then return
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①④⑧" data-link-type="dfn"
    data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-frompropertydescriptor"
    id="ref-for-sec-frompropertydescriptor"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">FromPropertyDescriptor</a>(PropertyDescriptor{\[\[Configurable\]\]:
    false, \[\[Enumerable\]\]: false, \[\[Writable\]\]: true,
    \[\[Value\]\]: `length` }).

4.  If `P` <a href="#is-an-array-index" id="ref-for-is-an-array-index⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">is an array index</a>, then

    1.  Let `index` be
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
        id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①④⑨" data-link-type="dfn"
        data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-touint32"
        id="ref-for-sec-touint32⑦" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToUint32</a>(`P`).

    2.  If `index` ≥ `length`, then return undefined.

    3.  Let `jsValue` be the result of
        <a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
        id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value⑦⑨"
        data-link-type="dfn">converting</a>
        `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\]\[`index`\] to a JavaScript value.

    4.  Assert: the above step never throws an exception.

    5.  Return <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-frompropertydescriptor"
        id="ref-for-sec-frompropertydescriptor①"
        data-link-type="abstract-op">FromPropertyDescriptor</a>(PropertyDescriptor{\[\[Configurable\]\]:
        true, \[\[Enumerable\]\]: true, \[\[Writable\]\]: true,
        \[\[Value\]\]: `jsValue` }).

5.  Return <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-frompropertydescriptor"
    id="ref-for-sec-frompropertydescriptor②"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">FromPropertyDescriptor</a>(<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤⓪" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    `O`.\[\[GetOwnProperty\]\](`P`)).

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.10.5. </span><span id="es-observable-array-has" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">`has`</span><a href="#js-observable-array-has" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm"
algorithm="observable array exotic object has trap">

The steps for the `has` proxy trap for
<a href="#observable-array-exotic-object"
id="ref-for-observable-array-exotic-object⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">observable array exotic objects</a>, given `O` and
`P`, are as follows:

1.  Let `handler` be the this value.

2.  If `P` is "length", then return true.

3.  If `P` <a href="#is-an-array-index" id="ref-for-is-an-array-index⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">is an array index</a>, then:

    1.  Let `index` be
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
        id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤①" data-link-type="dfn"
        data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-touint32"
        id="ref-for-sec-touint32⑧" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToUint32</a>(`P`).

    2.  If `index` \< `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\]'s
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
        id="ref-for-list-size①⑥" data-link-type="dfn">size</a>, then
        return true.

    3.  Return false.

4.  Return
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤②" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    `O`.\[\[HasProperty\]\](`P`).

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.10.6. </span><span id="es-observable-array-ownKeys" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">`ownKeys`</span><a href="#js-observable-array-ownKeys" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm"
algorithm="observable array exotic object ownKeys trap">

The steps for the `ownKeys` proxy trap for
<a href="#observable-array-exotic-object"
id="ref-for-observable-array-exotic-object⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">observable array exotic objects</a>, given `O`, are
as follows:

1.  Let `handler` be the this value.

2.  Let `length` be `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\]'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
    id="ref-for-list-size①⑦" data-link-type="dfn">size</a>.

3.  Let `keys` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list③③"
    data-link-type="dfn">list</a>.

4.  Let `i` be 0.

5.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-while"
    id="ref-for-iteration-while②" data-link-type="dfn">While</a> `i` \<
    `length`:

    1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="ref-for-list-append①④" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
        id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤③" data-link-type="dfn"
        data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tostring"
        id="ref-for-sec-tostring⑧" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToString</a>(`i`)
        to `keys`.

    2.  Set `i` to `i` + 1.

6.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-extend"
    id="ref-for-list-extend" data-link-type="dfn">Extend</a> `keys` with
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤④" data-link-type="dfn"
    data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> `O`.\[\[OwnPropertyKeys\]\]().

7.  Return <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-createarrayfromlist"
    id="ref-for-sec-createarrayfromlist②"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">CreateArrayFromList</a>(`keys`).

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.10.7. </span><span id="es-observable-array-preventExtensions" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">`preventExtensions`</span><a href="#js-observable-array-preventExtensions" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm"
algorithm="observable array exotic object preventExtensions trap">

The steps for the `preventExtensions` proxy trap for
<a href="#observable-array-exotic-object"
id="ref-for-observable-array-exotic-object⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">observable array exotic objects</a> are as follows:

1.  Return false.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.10.8. </span><span id="es-observable-array-set" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">`set`</span><a href="#js-observable-array-set" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm"
algorithm="observable array exotic object set trap">

The steps for the `set` proxy trap for
<a href="#observable-array-exotic-object"
id="ref-for-observable-array-exotic-object⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">observable array exotic objects</a>, given `O`,
`P`, `V`, and `Receiver`, are as follows:

1.  Let `handler` be the this value.

2.  If `P` is "length", then return the result of
    <a href="#observable-array-exotic-object-set-the-length"
    id="ref-for-observable-array-exotic-object-set-the-length②"
    data-link-type="dfn">setting the length</a> given `handler` and `V`.

3.  If `P` <a href="#is-an-array-index" id="ref-for-is-an-array-index⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">is an array index</a>, then return the result
    of <a href="#observable-array-exotic-object-set-the-indexed-value"
    id="ref-for-observable-array-exotic-object-set-the-indexed-value①"
    data-link-type="dfn">setting the indexed value</a> given `handler`,
    `P`, and `V`.

4.  Return
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤⑤" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    `O`.\[\[Set\]\](`P`, `V`, `Receiver`).

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.10.9. </span><span id="es-observable-array-abstract-operations" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Abstract operations</span><a href="#js-observable-array-abstract-operations"
class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="set the length"
algorithm-for="observable array exotic object">

To <span id="observable-array-exotic-object-set-the-length"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="observable array exotic object"
dfn-type="dfn" lt="set the length|setting the length" noexport="">set
the length</span> of an observable array exotic object given `handler`
and `newLen`:

1.  Let `uint32Len` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤⑥" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-touint32"
    id="ref-for-sec-touint32⑨" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToUint32</a>(`newLen`).

2.  Let `numberLen` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤⑦" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
    <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-tonumber"
    id="ref-for-sec-tonumber⑤" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToNumber</a>(`newLen`).

3.  If `uint32Len` ≠ `numberLen`, then throw a
    <a href="#exceptiondef-rangeerror" id="ref-for-exceptiondef-rangeerror⑤"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">RangeError</code></a>
    exception.

4.  Let `oldLen` be `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\]'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
    id="ref-for-list-size①⑧" data-link-type="dfn">size</a>.

5.  If `uint32Len` \> `oldLen`, then return false.

6.  Let `indexToDelete` be `oldLen` − 1.

7.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-while"
    id="ref-for-iteration-while③" data-link-type="dfn">While</a>
    `indexToDelete` ≥ `uint32Len`:

    1.  Perform the algorithm steps given by
        `handler`.\[\[DeleteAlgorithm\]\], given
        `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\]\[`indexToDelete`\] and
        `indexToDelete`.

    2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-remove"
        id="ref-for-list-remove④" data-link-type="dfn">Remove</a> the
        last item from `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\].

    3.  Set `indexToDelete` to `indexToDelete` − 1.

8.  Return true.

</div>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="set the indexed value"
algorithm-for="observable array exotic object">

To <span id="observable-array-exotic-object-set-the-indexed-value"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-for="observable array exotic object"
dfn-type="dfn" lt="set the indexed value|setting the indexed value"
noexport="">set the indexed value</span> of an observable array exotic
object given `handler`, `P`, and `V`:

1.  Let `oldLen` be `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\]'s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
    id="ref-for-list-size①⑨" data-link-type="dfn">size</a>.

2.  Let `index` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤⑧" data-link-type="dfn"
    data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-touint32"
    id="ref-for-sec-touint32①⓪" data-link-type="abstract-op">ToUint32</a>(`P`).

3.  If `index` \> `oldLen`, return false.

4.  Let `idlValue` be the result of
    <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
    id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value⑧⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `V` to the type given by
    `handler`.\[\[Type\]\].

5.  If `index` \< `oldLen`, then:

    1.  Perform the algorithm steps given by
        `handler`.\[\[DeleteAlgorithm\]\], given
        `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\]\[`index`\] and `index`.

6.  Perform the algorithm steps given by `handler`.\[\[SetAlgorithm\]\],
    given `idlValue` and `index`.

7.  If `index` = `oldLen`, then
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
    id="ref-for-list-append①⑤" data-link-type="dfn">append</a>
    `idlValue` to `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\].

8.  Otherwise, set `handler`.\[\[BackingList\]\]\[`index`\] to
    `idlValue`.

9.  Return true.

</div>

### <span class="secno">3.11. </span><span id="es-user-objects" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Callback interfaces</span><a href="#js-user-objects" class="self-link"></a>

As described in [§ 2.12 Objects implementing interfaces](#idl-objects),
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface③⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interfaces</a> can be implemented in
script by any JavaScript object. The following cases explain how a
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface③⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>’s
<a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑥③"
data-link-type="dfn">operation</a> is invoked on a given object:

- If the object is <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-iscallable"
  id="ref-for-sec-iscallable①⓪" data-link-type="dfn">callable</a>, then
  the implementation of the operation is the callable object itself.

- Otherwise, the implementation of the operation is calling the result
  of invoking the internal \[\[Get\]\] method on the object with a
  property name that is the
  <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑨⑧"
  data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of the operation.

Note that JavaScript objects need not have properties corresponding to
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant④②"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> on them to be considered as
implementing
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface④⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interfaces</a> that happen to have
constants declared on them.

A <span id="web-idl-arguments-list" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">Web IDL arguments list</span> is a
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list③④"
data-link-type="dfn">list</a> of values each of which is either an IDL
value or the special value “missing”, which represents a missing
optional argument.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="converting"
algorithm-for="Web IDL arguments list">

To <span id="web-idl-arguments-list-converting" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="Web IDL arguments list" dfn-type="dfn" lt="converting"
noexport="">convert a Web IDL arguments list to a JavaScript arguments
list</span>, given a
<a href="#web-idl-arguments-list" id="ref-for-web-idl-arguments-list"
data-link-type="dfn">Web IDL arguments list</a> `args`, perform the
following steps:

1.  Let `jsArgs` be an empty
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list" id="ref-for-list③⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">list</a>.

2.  Let `i` be 0.

3.  Let `count` be 0.

4.  While `i` \< `args`’s
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-size"
    id="ref-for-list-size②⓪" data-link-type="dfn">size</a>:

    1.  If `args`\[`i`\] is the special value “missing”, then
        <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
        id="ref-for-list-append①⑥" data-link-type="dfn">append</a>
        undefined to `jsArgs`.

    2.  Otherwise, `args`\[`i`\] is an IDL value:

        1.  Let `convertResult` be the result of
            <a href="#dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value"
            id="ref-for-dfn-convert-idl-to-javascript-value⑧⓪"
            data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `args`\[`i`\] to a
            JavaScript value. Rethrow any exceptions.

        2.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append"
            id="ref-for-list-append①⑦" data-link-type="dfn">Append</a>
            `convertResult` to `jsArgs`.

        3.  Set `count` to `i` + 1.

    3.  Set `i` to `i` + 1.

5.  Truncate `jsArgs` to contain `count` items.

6.  Return `jsArgs`.

</div>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="to call a user object's operation">

To <span id="call-a-user-objects-operation" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">call a user object’s operation</span>, given a
<a href="#idl-callback-interface" id="ref-for-idl-callback-interface①①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface type</a> value `value`,
operation name `opName`,
<a href="#web-idl-arguments-list" id="ref-for-web-idl-arguments-list①"
data-link-type="dfn">Web IDL arguments list</a> `args`, and optional
<span id="dfn-callback-this-value" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">callback this value</span> `thisArg`, perform
the following steps. These steps will either return an IDL value or
throw an exception.

1.  Let `completion` be an uninitialized variable.

2.  If `thisArg` was not given, let `thisArg` be undefined.

3.  Let `O` be the JavaScript object corresponding to `value`.

4.  Let `realm` be `O`’s
    <a href="#dfn-associated-realm" id="ref-for-dfn-associated-realm②"
    data-link-type="dfn">associated realm</a>.

5.  Let `relevant settings` be `realm`’s <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-settings-object"
    id="ref-for-concept-realm-settings-object②"
    data-link-type="dfn">settings object</a>.

6.  Let `stored settings` be `value`’s
    <a href="#dfn-callback-context" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-context⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">callback context</a>.

7.  <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#prepare-to-run-script"
    id="ref-for-prepare-to-run-script" data-link-type="dfn">Prepare to run
    script</a> with `relevant settings`.

8.  <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#prepare-to-run-a-callback"
    id="ref-for-prepare-to-run-a-callback" data-link-type="dfn">Prepare to
    run a callback</a> with `stored settings`.

9.  Let `X` be `O`.

10. If <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-iscallable"
    id="ref-for-sec-iscallable①①"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">IsCallable</a>(`O`) is false, then:

    1.  Let `getResult` be <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
        id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type⑤"
        data-link-type="abstract-op" data-refhint-key="8231699a">Completion</a>(<a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-get-o-p"
        id="ref-for-sec-get-o-p④" data-link-type="abstract-op">Get</a>(`O`,
        `opName`)).

    2.  If `getResult` is an <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
        id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type⑥"
        data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a>, set `completion` to
        `getResult` and jump to the step labeled
        [*return*](#call-user-object-operation-return).

    3.  Set `X` to `getResult`.\[\[Value\]\].

    4.  If <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-iscallable"
        id="ref-for-sec-iscallable①②"
        data-link-type="abstract-op">IsCallable</a>(`X`) is false, then
        set `completion` to <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
        id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type⑦"
        data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="c8a04a12">Completion Record</a>
        { \[\[Type\]\]: throw, \[\[Value\]\]: a newly created <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror⑤⑦"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>
        object, \[\[Target\]\]: empty }, and jump to the step labeled
        [*return*](#call-user-object-operation-return).

    5.  Set `thisArg` to `O` (overriding the provided value).

11. Let `jsArgs` be the result of
    <a href="#web-idl-arguments-list-converting"
    id="ref-for-web-idl-arguments-list-converting"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `args` to a JavaScript arguments
    list. If this throws an exception, set `completion` to the
    completion value representing the thrown exception and jump to the
    step labeled [*return*](#call-user-object-operation-return).

12. Let `callResult` be <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type⑧"
    data-link-type="abstract-op" data-refhint-key="8231699a">Completion</a>(<a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-call"
    id="ref-for-sec-call①⑥" data-link-type="abstract-op">Call</a>(`X`,
    `thisArg`, `jsArgs`)).

13. If `callResult` is an <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a>, set `completion` to
    `callResult` and jump to the step labeled
    [*return*](#call-user-object-operation-return).

14. Set `completion` to the result of
    <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
    id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value⑧⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `callResult`.\[\[Value\]\] to an
    IDL value of the same type as the operation’s return type. If this
    throws an exception, set `completion` to the completion value
    representing the thrown exception.

15. *Return:* at this point `completion` will be set to an IDL value or
    an <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a>.

    1.  <a
        href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#clean-up-after-running-a-callback"
        id="ref-for-clean-up-after-running-a-callback"
        data-link-type="dfn">Clean up after running a callback</a> with
        `stored settings`.

    2.  <a
        href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#clean-up-after-running-script"
        id="ref-for-clean-up-after-running-script" data-link-type="dfn">Clean up
        after running script</a> with `relevant settings`.

    3.  If `completion` is an IDL value, return `completion`.

    4.  If `completion` is an <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
        id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①①"
        data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a> and the operation has
        a <a href="#dfn-return-type" id="ref-for-dfn-return-type⑧"
        data-link-type="dfn">return type</a> that is *not* a
        <a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type①②"
        data-link-type="dfn">promise type</a>, throw
        `completion`.\[\[Value\]\].

    5.  Let `rejectedPromise` be
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
        id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑤⑨" data-link-type="dfn"
        data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-call"
        id="ref-for-sec-call①⑦" data-link-type="abstract-op">Call</a>(<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-promise.reject"
        id="ref-for-sec-promise.reject②" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">%Promise.reject%</code></a>, <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/control-abstraction-objects.html#sec-promise-constructor"
        id="ref-for-sec-promise-constructor①③" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">%Promise%</code></a>, «`completion`.\[\[Value\]\]»).

    6.  Return the result of
        <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
        id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value⑧⑧"
        data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `rejectedPromise` to the
        operation’s return type.

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.11.1. </span><span class="content">Legacy callback interface object</span><a href="#legacy-callback-interface-object" class="self-link"></a>

For every
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface④①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> that is
<a href="#dfn-exposed" id="ref-for-dfn-exposed①⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">exposed</a> in a given <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤①" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a> and on which
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant④③"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> are defined, a corresponding property
exists on the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤②" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a>’s <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-global"
id="ref-for-concept-realm-global⑧" data-link-type="dfn">global
object</a>. The name of the property is the
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier⑨⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of the
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface④②"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a>, and its value is an object
called the <span id="dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">legacy callback
interface object</span>.

The <a href="#dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object②"
data-link-type="dfn">legacy callback interface object</a> for a given
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface④③"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> is a
<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-built-in-function-objects③②"
data-link-type="dfn">built-in function object</a>. It has properties
that correspond to the
<a href="#dfn-constant" id="ref-for-dfn-constant④④"
data-link-type="dfn">constants</a> defined on that interface, as
described in sections [§ 3.7.5 Constants](#js-constants).

<span class="marker">Note:</span> Since a
<a href="#dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object③"
data-link-type="dfn">legacy callback interface object</a> is a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object⑤②" data-link-type="dfn">function object</a>
the `typeof` operator will return "function" when applied to a
<a href="#dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object④"
data-link-type="dfn">legacy callback interface object</a>.

<div class="algorithm"
algorithm="create a legacy callback interface object">

The <a href="#dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-legacy-callback-interface-object⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">legacy callback interface object</a> for a given
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface④④"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> `interface` with
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⓪⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> `id` and in <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤③" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a> `realm` is
<span id="create-a-legacy-callback-interface-object"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn"
lt="create a legacy callback interface object"
noexport="">created</span> as follows:

1.  Let `steps` be the following steps:

    1.  <a href="#javascript-throw" id="ref-for-javascript-throw⑤⑥"
        data-link-type="dfn">Throw</a> a <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
        id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror⑤⑧"
        data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>.

2.  Let `F` be <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ordinary-and-exotic-objects-behaviours.html#sec-createbuiltinfunction"
    id="ref-for-sec-createbuiltinfunction②⑨"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">CreateBuiltinFunction</a>(`steps`, 0,
    `id`, « », `realm`).

3.  <a href="#define-the-constants" id="ref-for-define-the-constants②"
    data-link-type="dfn">Define the constants</a> of `interface` on `F`
    given `realm`.

4.  Return `F`.

</div>

### <span class="secno">3.12. </span><span id="es-invoking-callback-functions" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Invoking callback functions</span><a href="#js-invoking-callback-functions" class="self-link"></a>

A JavaScript <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-iscallable"
id="ref-for-sec-iscallable①③" data-link-type="dfn">callable</a> object
that is being used as a
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function③②"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> value is called in a manner
similar to how <a href="#dfn-operation" id="ref-for-dfn-operation⑥④"
data-link-type="dfn">operations</a> on
<a href="#dfn-callback-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-interface④⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">callback interface</a> values are called (as
described in the previous section).

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="invoke">

To <span id="invoke-a-callback-function" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">invoke</span> a
<a href="#idl-callback-function" id="ref-for-idl-callback-function⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function type</a> value `callable` with a
<a href="#web-idl-arguments-list" id="ref-for-web-idl-arguments-list②"
data-link-type="dfn">Web IDL arguments list</a> `args`, exception
behavior `exceptionBehavior` (either "`report`" or "`rethrow`"), and an
optional
<a href="#dfn-callback-this-value" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-this-value①"
data-link-type="dfn">callback this value</a> `thisArg`, perform the
following steps. These steps will either return an IDL value or throw an
exception.

The `exceptionBehavior` argument must be supplied if, and only if,
`callable`’s <a href="#dfn-return-type" id="ref-for-dfn-return-type⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">return type</a> is not a
<a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type①③"
data-link-type="dfn">promise type</a>. If `callable`’s return type is
neither <a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined②⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a> nor
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any①⑥" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a>, it must be "`rethrow`".

<div class="XXX">

Until call sites are updated to respect this, specifications which fail
to provide a value here when it would be mandatory should be understood
as supplying "`rethrow`".

</div>

1.  Let `completion` be an uninitialized variable.

2.  If `thisArg` was not given, let `thisArg` be undefined.

3.  Let `F` be the JavaScript object corresponding to `callable`.

4.  If <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-iscallable"
    id="ref-for-sec-iscallable①④"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">IsCallable</a>(`F`) is false:

    1.  <span class="marker">Note:</span> This is only possible when the
        <a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function③③"
        data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> came from an
        attribute marked with \[<a href="#LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull"
        id="ref-for-LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull⑨" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull</code></a>\].

    2.  Return the result of
        <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
        id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value⑧⑨"
        data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> undefined to the callback
        function’s return type.

5.  Let `realm` be `F`’s
    <a href="#dfn-associated-realm" id="ref-for-dfn-associated-realm③"
    data-link-type="dfn">associated realm</a>.

6.  Let `relevant settings` be `realm`’s <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-settings-object"
    id="ref-for-concept-realm-settings-object③"
    data-link-type="dfn">settings object</a>.

7.  Let `stored settings` be `callable`’s
    <a href="#dfn-callback-context" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-context⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">callback context</a>.

8.  <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#prepare-to-run-script"
    id="ref-for-prepare-to-run-script①" data-link-type="dfn">Prepare to run
    script</a> with `relevant settings`.

9.  <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#prepare-to-run-a-callback"
    id="ref-for-prepare-to-run-a-callback①" data-link-type="dfn">Prepare to
    run a callback</a> with `stored settings`.

10. Let `jsArgs` be the result of
    <a href="#web-idl-arguments-list-converting"
    id="ref-for-web-idl-arguments-list-converting①"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `args` to a JavaScript arguments
    list. If this throws an exception, set `completion` to the
    completion value representing the thrown exception and jump to the
    step labeled [*return*](#invoke-return).

11. Let `callResult` be <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①②"
    data-link-type="abstract-op" data-refhint-key="8231699a">Completion</a>(<a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-call"
    id="ref-for-sec-call①⑧" data-link-type="abstract-op">Call</a>(`F`,
    `thisArg`, `jsArgs`)).

12. If `callResult` is an <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①③"
    data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a>, set `completion` to
    `callResult` and jump to the step labeled
    [*return*](#invoke-return).

13. Set `completion` to the result of
    <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
    id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value⑨⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `callResult`.\[\[Value\]\] to an
    IDL value of the same type as `callable`’s return type. If this
    throws an exception, set `completion` to the completion value
    representing the thrown exception.

14. *Return:* at this point `completion` will be set to an IDL value or
    an <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①④"
    data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a>.

    1.  <a
        href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#clean-up-after-running-a-callback"
        id="ref-for-clean-up-after-running-a-callback①"
        data-link-type="dfn">Clean up after running a callback</a> with
        `stored settings`.

    2.  <a
        href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#clean-up-after-running-script"
        id="ref-for-clean-up-after-running-script①" data-link-type="dfn">Clean
        up after running script</a> with `relevant settings`.

    3.  If `completion` is an IDL value, return `completion`.

    4.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert" id="ref-for-assert"
        data-link-type="dfn">Assert</a>: `completion` is an <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
        id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①⑤"
        data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a>.

    5.  If `exceptionBehavior` is "`rethrow`", throw
        `completion`.\[\[Value\]\].

    6.  Otherwise, if `exceptionBehavior` is "`report`":

        1.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert" id="ref-for-assert①"
            data-link-type="dfn">Assert</a>: `callable`’s
            <a href="#dfn-return-type" id="ref-for-dfn-return-type①⓪"
            data-link-type="dfn">return type</a> is
            <a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined②①"
            data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a>
            or
            <a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any①⑦" data-link-type="idl"><code
            class="idl">any</code></a>.

        2.  <a
            href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#report-an-exception"
            id="ref-for-report-an-exception" data-link-type="dfn">Report an
            exception</a> `completion`.\[\[Value\]\] for `realm`’s <a
            href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-global"
            id="ref-for-concept-realm-global⑨" data-link-type="dfn">global
            object</a>.

        3.  Return the unique
            <a href="#idl-undefined" id="ref-for-idl-undefined②②"
            data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">undefined</code></a>
            IDL value.

    7.  <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert" id="ref-for-assert②"
        data-link-type="dfn">Assert</a>: `callable`’s
        <a href="#dfn-return-type" id="ref-for-dfn-return-type①①"
        data-link-type="dfn">return type</a> is a
        <a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type①④"
        data-link-type="dfn">promise type</a>.

    8.  Let `rejectedPromise` be
        <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
        id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑥⓪" data-link-type="dfn"
        data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-call"
        id="ref-for-sec-call①⑨" data-link-type="abstract-op">Call</a>(<a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-promise.reject"
        id="ref-for-sec-promise.reject③" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">%Promise.reject%</code></a>, <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/control-abstraction-objects.html#sec-promise-constructor"
        id="ref-for-sec-promise-constructor①④" data-link-type="idl"><code
        class="idl">%Promise%</code></a>, «`completion`.\[\[Value\]\]»).

    9.  Return the result of
        <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
        id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value⑨①"
        data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `rejectedPromise` to the
        callback function’s return type.

</div>

Some callback functions are instead used as <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#constructor"
id="ref-for-constructor⑥" data-link-type="dfn">constructors</a>. Such
callback functions must not have a return type that is a
<a href="#dfn-promise-type" id="ref-for-dfn-promise-type①⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">promise type</a>.

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="construct">

To <span id="construct-a-callback-function" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" export="">construct</span> a
<a href="#idl-callback-function" id="ref-for-idl-callback-function⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function type</a> value `callable` with a
<a href="#web-idl-arguments-list" id="ref-for-web-idl-arguments-list③"
data-link-type="dfn">Web IDL arguments list</a> `args`, perform the
following steps. These steps will either return an IDL value or throw an
exception.

1.  Let `completion` be an uninitialized variable.

2.  Let `F` be the JavaScript object corresponding to `callable`.

3.  If <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-isconstructor"
    id="ref-for-sec-isconstructor"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">IsConstructor</a>(`F`) is false, throw
    a <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror"
    id="ref-for-sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror⑤⑨"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">TypeError</code></a>
    exception.

4.  Let `realm` be `F`’s
    <a href="#dfn-associated-realm" id="ref-for-dfn-associated-realm④"
    data-link-type="dfn">associated realm</a>.

5.  Let `relevant settings` be `realm`’s <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-settings-object"
    id="ref-for-concept-realm-settings-object④"
    data-link-type="dfn">settings object</a>.

6.  Let `stored settings` be `callable`’s
    <a href="#dfn-callback-context" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-context⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">callback context</a>.

7.  <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#prepare-to-run-script"
    id="ref-for-prepare-to-run-script②" data-link-type="dfn">Prepare to run
    script</a> with `relevant settings`.

8.  <a
    href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#prepare-to-run-a-callback"
    id="ref-for-prepare-to-run-a-callback②" data-link-type="dfn">Prepare to
    run a callback</a> with `stored settings`.

9.  Let `jsArgs` be the result of
    <a href="#web-idl-arguments-list-converting"
    id="ref-for-web-idl-arguments-list-converting②"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `args` to a JavaScript arguments
    list. If this throws an exception, set `completion` to the
    completion value representing the thrown exception and jump to the
    step labeled [*return*](#construct-return).

10. Let `callResult` be <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①⑥"
    data-link-type="abstract-op" data-refhint-key="8231699a">Completion</a>(<a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-construct"
    id="ref-for-sec-construct①" data-link-type="abstract-op">Construct</a>(`F`,
    `jsArgs`)).

11. If `callResult` is an <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a>, set `completion` to
    `callResult` and jump to the step labeled
    [*return*](#construct-return).

12. Set `completion` to the result of
    <a href="#dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value"
    id="ref-for-dfn-convert-ecmascript-to-idl-value⑨②"
    data-link-type="dfn">converting</a> `callResult`.\[\[Value\]\] to an
    IDL value of the same type as `callable`’s return type. If this
    throws an exception, set `completion` to the completion value
    representing the thrown exception.

13. *Return:* at this point `completion` will be set to an IDL value or
    an <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
    id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①⑧"
    data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a>.

    1.  <a
        href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#clean-up-after-running-a-callback"
        id="ref-for-clean-up-after-running-a-callback②"
        data-link-type="dfn">Clean up after running a callback</a> with
        `stored settings`.

    2.  <a
        href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#clean-up-after-running-script"
        id="ref-for-clean-up-after-running-script②" data-link-type="dfn">Clean
        up after running script</a> with `relevant settings`.

    3.  If `completion` is an <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
        id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type①⑨"
        data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completion</a>, throw
        `completion`.\[\[Value\]\].

    4.  Return `completion`.

</div>

### <span class="secno">3.13. </span><span id="es-namespaces" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Namespaces</span><a href="#js-namespaces" class="self-link"></a>

For every <a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace⑤②"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> that is
<a href="#dfn-exposed" id="ref-for-dfn-exposed②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">exposed</a> in a given <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤④" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a>, a corresponding
property exists on the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤⑤" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a>’s <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-realm-global"
id="ref-for-concept-realm-global①⓪" data-link-type="dfn">global
object</a>. The name of the property is the
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⓪①"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> of the namespace, and its value is
an object called the <span id="dfn-namespace-object"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">namespace
object</span>.

The characteristics of a namespace object are described in [§ 3.13.1
Namespace object](#namespace-object).

#### <span class="secno">3.13.1. </span><span class="content">Namespace object</span><a href="#namespace-object" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="create a namespace object">

The namespace object for a given
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace⑤③"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a> `namespace` and <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤⑥" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a> `realm` is
<span id="create-a-namespace-object" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-type="dfn" lt="create a namespace object" noexport="">created</span>
as follows:

1.  Let `namespaceObject` be <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ordinary-and-exotic-objects-behaviours.html#sec-ordinaryobjectcreate"
    id="ref-for-sec-ordinaryobjectcreate⑧"
    data-link-type="abstract-op">OrdinaryObjectCreate</a>(`realm`.\[\[Intrinsics\]\].\[\[<a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object"
    id="ref-for-sec-properties-of-the-object-prototype-object⑦"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">%Object.prototype%</code></a>\]\]).

2.  <a href="#define-the-regular-attributes"
    id="ref-for-define-the-regular-attributes②" data-link-type="dfn">Define
    the regular attributes</a> of `namespace` on `namespaceObject` given
    `realm`.

3.  <a href="#define-the-regular-operations"
    id="ref-for-define-the-regular-operations②" data-link-type="dfn">Define
    the regular operations</a> of `namespace` on `namespaceObject` given
    `realm`.

4.  <a href="#define-the-constants" id="ref-for-define-the-constants③"
    data-link-type="dfn">Define the constants</a> of `namespace` on
    `namespaceObject` given `realm`.

5.  For each <a href="#dfn-exposed" id="ref-for-dfn-exposed②①"
    data-link-type="dfn">exposed</a>
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑤⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> `interface` which has the
    \[<a href="#LegacyNamespace" id="ref-for-LegacyNamespace⑨"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyNamespace</code></a>\]
    extended attribute with the identifier of `namespace` as its
    argument,

    1.  Let `id` be `interface`’s
        <a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⓪②"
        data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>.

    2.  Let `interfaceObject` be the result of
        <a href="#create-an-interface-object"
        id="ref-for-create-an-interface-object①" data-link-type="dfn">creating
        an interface object</a> for `interface` with `id` in `realm`.

    3.  Perform <a
        href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ordinary-and-exotic-objects-behaviours.html#sec-definemethodproperty"
        id="ref-for-sec-definemethodproperty⑨"
        data-link-type="abstract-op">DefineMethodProperty</a>(`namespaceObject`,
        `id`, `interfaceObject`, false).

6.  Return `namespaceObject`.

</div>

The <a href="#dfn-class-string" id="ref-for-dfn-class-string⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">class string</a> of a
<a href="#dfn-namespace-object" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace-object"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace object</a> is the
<a href="#dfn-namespace" id="ref-for-dfn-namespace⑤④"
data-link-type="dfn">namespace</a>’s
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⓪③"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a>.

### <span class="secno">3.14. </span><span id="es-exceptions" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Exceptions</span><a href="#js-exceptions" class="self-link"></a>

#### <span class="secno">3.14.1. </span><span id="es-DOMException-prototype-object" class="bs-old-id"></span><span id="es-DOMException-constructor-object" class="bs-old-id"></span><span id="es-DOMException-specialness" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content"><a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException④⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> custom bindings</span><a href="#js-DOMException-specialness" class="self-link"></a>

In the JavaScript binding, the <a href="#dfn-interface-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-dfn-interface-prototype-object④⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">interface prototype object</a> for
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException④⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> has its
\[\[Prototype\]\] <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots"
id="ref-for-sec-object-internal-methods-and-internal-slots②②"
data-link-type="dfn">internal slot</a> set to the intrinsic object <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-properties-of-the-error-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-sec-properties-of-the-error-prototype-object①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">%Error.prototype%</code></a>, as
defined in the <a href="#create-an-interface-prototype-object"
id="ref-for-create-an-interface-prototype-object①"
data-link-type="dfn">create an interface prototype object</a> abstract
operation. It also has an \[\[ErrorData\]\] slot, like all built-in
exceptions.

Additionally, if an implementation gives native <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/fundamental-objects.html#sec-error-objects"
id="ref-for-sec-error-objects②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Error</code></a> objects special powers or nonstandard
properties (such as a `stack` property), it should also expose those on
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException④⑧"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> objects.

#### <span class="secno">3.14.2. </span><span id="es-exception-objects" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Exception objects</span><a href="#js-exception-objects" id="ref-for-js-exception-objects①"
class="self-link"></a>

<a href="#dfn-simple-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-simple-exception③"
data-link-type="dfn">Simple exceptions</a> are represented by native
JavaScript objects of the corresponding type.

A <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException④⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> is
represented by a
<a href="#dfn-platform-object" id="ref-for-dfn-platform-object③④"
data-link-type="dfn">platform object</a> that implements the
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑤⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>
interface.

#### <span class="secno">3.14.3. </span><span id="es-creating-throwing-exceptions" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Creating and throwing exceptions</span><a href="#js-creating-throwing-exceptions" class="self-link"></a>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="to create a simple exception">

To <a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception⑥"
data-link-type="dfn">create</a> a
<a href="#dfn-simple-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-simple-exception④"
data-link-type="dfn">simple exception</a> of type `T`:

1.  Let `message` be an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="ref-for-implementation-defined"
    data-link-type="dfn">implementation-defined</a> message appropriate
    for the exceptional situation. The calling specification may contain
    information to to help implementations construct this message.

    Implementations need to be cautious not to leak sensitive or secured
    information when constructing this message, e.g., by including the
    URL of a cross-origin frame, or information which could identify the
    user.

2.  Let `args` be « `message` ».

3.  Let `constructor` be
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm"
    id="ref-for-current-realm②" data-link-type="dfn">current realm</a>.\[\[Intrinsics\]\].\[\[%`T`%\]\].

4.  Return
    <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
    id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑥①" data-link-type="dfn"
    data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> <a
    href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/abstract-operations.html#sec-construct"
    id="ref-for-sec-construct②" data-link-type="abstract-op">Construct</a>(`constructor`,
    `args`).

</div>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="to create a DOMException">

To <a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">create</a> a
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑤①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> given a
string `name`:

1.  Assert: `name` appears in the
    <a href="#dfn-error-names-table" id="ref-for-dfn-error-names-table②"
    data-link-type="dfn"><code>DOMException</code> names table</a>.

2.  Let `ex` be a
    <a href="#new" id="ref-for-new①" data-link-type="dfn">new</a>
    <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑤②"
    data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a>
    created in the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm"
    id="ref-for-current-realm③" data-link-type="dfn">current realm</a>.

3.  Set `ex`’s
    <a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name①⓪"
    data-link-type="dfn">name</a> to `name`.

4.  Set `ex`’s
    <a href="#domexception-message" id="ref-for-domexception-message②"
    data-link-type="dfn">message</a> to an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="ref-for-implementation-defined①"
    data-link-type="dfn">implementation-defined</a> message appropriate
    for the exceptional situation. The calling specification may contain
    information to to help implementations construct this message.

    Implementations need to be cautious not to leak sensitive or secured
    information when constructing this message, e.g., by including the
    URL of a cross-origin frame, or information which could identify the
    user.

5.  Return `ex`.

</div>

<div class="algorithm"
algorithm="to create a DOMException derived interface">

To <a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">create</a> a
<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑤③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> derived
interface given the
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑤①"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a>
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⓪④"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> `type` and additional initialization
instructions:

1.  Let `ex` be a
    <a href="#new" id="ref-for-new②" data-link-type="dfn">new</a>
    instance of the
    <a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑤②"
    data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> identified by `type`, created in
    the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm"
    id="ref-for-current-realm④" data-link-type="dfn">current realm</a>.

2.  Set `ex`’s
    <a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name①①"
    data-link-type="dfn">name</a> to `type`.

3.  Set `ex`’s
    <a href="#domexception-message" id="ref-for-domexception-message③"
    data-link-type="dfn">message</a> to an
    <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined"
    id="ref-for-implementation-defined②"
    data-link-type="dfn">implementation-defined</a> message appropriate
    for the exceptional situation. The calling specification may contain
    information to to help implementations construct this message.

    Implementations need to be cautious not to leak sensitive or secured
    information when constructing this message, e.g., by including the
    URL of a cross-origin frame, or information which could identify the
    user.

4.  Perform any additional initialization on `ex` as described by the
    caller.

5.  Return `ex`.

</div>

<div class="algorithm" algorithm="throw an exception">

To <a href="#dfn-throw" id="ref-for-dfn-throw⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">throw</a> an
<a href="#dfn-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-exception"
data-link-type="dfn">exception</a>:

1.  Let `O` be the result of
    <a href="#dfn-create-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-create-exception⑨"
    data-link-type="dfn">creating an exception</a> with the same
    arguments.

2.  Throw `O`.

</div>

<div class="note" role="note">

The above algorithms restrict
<a href="#js-exception-objects" id="ref-for-js-exception-objects②"
data-link-type="dfn">objects representing exceptions</a> propagating out
of a <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object⑤③" data-link-type="dfn">function object</a>
to be ones that are associated with the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤⑦" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a> of that <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#function-object"
id="ref-for-function-object⑤④" data-link-type="dfn">function object</a>
(i.e., the <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm"
id="ref-for-current-realm⑤" data-link-type="dfn">current realm</a> at
the time the function executes). For example, consider the IDL:

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface MathUtils {
  // If x is negative, throws a "NotSupportedError" DOMException.
  double computeSquareRoot(double x);
};
```

If we apply `computeSquareRoot` to a `MathUtils` object from a different
<a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤⑧" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a>, then the exception
thrown will be from the <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#realm"
id="ref-for-realm⑤⑨" data-link-type="dfn">realm</a> of the method, not
the object it is applied to:

``` highlight
const myMU = window.getMathUtils();          // A MathUtils object from this realm
const otherMU = otherWindow.getMathUtils();  // A MathUtils object from a different realm

myMU instanceof Object;                      // Evaluates to true.
otherMU instanceof Object;                   // Evaluates to false.
otherMU instanceof otherWindow.Object;       // Evaluates to true.

try {
  otherMU.doComputation.call(myMU, -1);
} catch (e) {
  console.assert(!(e instanceof DOMException));
  console.assert(e instanceof otherWindow.DOMException);
}
```

</div>

#### <span class="secno">3.14.4. </span><span id="es-handling-exceptions" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Handling exceptions</span><a href="#js-handling-exceptions" class="self-link"></a>

Unless specified otherwise, whenever JavaScript runtime semantics are
invoked due to requirements in this document and end due to an exception
being thrown, that exception must propagate to the caller, and if not
caught there, to its caller, and so on.

Per [Document conventions](#conventions), an algorithm specified in this
document may intercept thrown exceptions, either by specifying the exact
steps to take if <span id="an-exception-was-thrown"
class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">an exception was
thrown</span>, or by explicitly handling <a
href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type②⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">abrupt completions</a>.

<div id="example-17059fd2" class="example">

<a href="#example-17059fd2" class="self-link"></a>

The following
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑤⓪"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a> defines two
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑤③"
data-link-type="dfn">interfaces</a> and an
<a href="#dfn-exception" id="ref-for-dfn-exception①"
data-link-type="dfn">exception</a>. The `valueOf` attribute on
`ExceptionThrower` is defined to throw an exception whenever an attempt
is made to get its value.

``` highlight
[Exposed=Window]
interface Dahut {
  attribute DOMString type;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface ExceptionThrower {
  // This attribute always throws a NotSupportedError and never returns a value.
  attribute long valueOf;
};
```

Assuming a JavaScript implementation supporting this interface, the
following code demonstrates how exceptions are handled:

``` highlight
var d = getDahut();              // Obtain an instance of Dahut.
var et = getExceptionThrower();  // Obtain an instance of ExceptionThrower.

try {
  d.type = { toString: function() { throw "abc"; } };
} catch (e) {
  // The string "abc" is caught here, since as part of the conversion
  // from the native object to a string, the anonymous function
  // was invoked, and none of the [[DefaultValue]], ToPrimitive or
  // ToString algorithms are defined to catch the exception.
}

try {
  d.type = { toString: { } };
} catch (e) {
  // An exception is caught here, since an attempt is made to invoke
  // [[Call]] on the native object that is the value of toString
  // property.
}

try {
  d.type = Symbol();
} catch (e) {
  // An exception is caught here, since an attempt is made to invoke
  // the JavaScript ToString abstract operation on a Symbol value.
}

d.type = et;
// An uncaught "NotSupportedError" DOMException is thrown here, since the
// [[DefaultValue]] algorithm attempts to get the value of the
// "valueOf" property on the ExceptionThrower object.  The exception
// propagates out of this block of code.
```

</div>

## <span class="secno">4. </span><span class="content">Common definitions</span><a href="#common" class="self-link"></a>

This section specifies some common definitions that all
<a href="#dfn-conforming-implementation"
id="ref-for-dfn-conforming-implementation"
data-link-type="dfn">conforming implementations</a> must support.

### <span class="secno">4.1. </span><span id="common-ArrayBufferView" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">ArrayBufferView</span><a href="#ArrayBufferView" id="ref-for-ArrayBufferView⑧"
class="self-link"></a>

``` def
typedef (Int8Array or Int16Array or Int32Array or
         Uint8Array or Uint16Array or Uint32Array or Uint8ClampedArray or
         BigInt64Array or BigUint64Array or
         Float16Array or Float32Array or Float64Array or DataView) ArrayBufferView;
```

The <a href="#ArrayBufferView" id="ref-for-ArrayBufferView⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBufferView</code></a>
typedef is used to represent objects that provide a view on to an
<a href="#idl-ArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-ArrayBuffer②③"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBuffer</code></a> or
<a href="#idl-SharedArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-SharedArrayBuffer①⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SharedArrayBuffer</code></a>
(when \[<a href="#AllowShared" id="ref-for-AllowShared①⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">AllowShared</code></a>\] is
used).

### <span class="secno">4.2. </span><span id="common-BufferSource" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">BufferSource</span><a href="#BufferSource" id="ref-for-BufferSource" class="self-link"></a>

``` def
typedef (ArrayBufferView or ArrayBuffer) BufferSource;
```

The <a href="#BufferSource" id="ref-for-BufferSource①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">BufferSource</code></a> typedef
is used to represent objects that are either themselves an
<a href="#idl-ArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-ArrayBuffer②⑤"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBuffer</code></a> or which
provide a view on to an
<a href="#idl-ArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-ArrayBuffer②⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBuffer</code></a>.

<span class="marker">Note:</span>
\[<a href="#AllowShared" id="ref-for-AllowShared①⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">AllowShared</code></a>\] cannot
be used with <a href="#BufferSource" id="ref-for-BufferSource②"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">BufferSource</code></a> as
<a href="#idl-ArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-ArrayBuffer②⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBuffer</code></a> does not
support it. Use
<a href="#AllowSharedBufferSource" id="ref-for-AllowSharedBufferSource"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">AllowSharedBufferSource</code></a> instead.

### <span class="secno">4.3. </span><span class="content">AllowSharedBufferSource</span><a href="#AllowSharedBufferSource" id="ref-for-AllowSharedBufferSource③"
class="self-link"></a>

``` def
typedef (ArrayBuffer or SharedArrayBuffer or [AllowShared] ArrayBufferView) AllowSharedBufferSource;
```

The
<a href="#AllowSharedBufferSource" id="ref-for-AllowSharedBufferSource②"
data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">AllowSharedBufferSource</code></a> typedef is used to
represent objects that are either themselves an
<a href="#idl-ArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-ArrayBuffer②⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBuffer</code></a> or
<a href="#idl-SharedArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-SharedArrayBuffer①⑨"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SharedArrayBuffer</code></a> or
which provide a view on to an
<a href="#idl-ArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-ArrayBuffer③⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">ArrayBuffer</code></a> or
<a href="#idl-SharedArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-SharedArrayBuffer②⓪"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SharedArrayBuffer</code></a>.

### <span class="secno">4.4. </span><span id="dfn-DOMException" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">DOMException</span><a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑤⑧"
class="self-link"></a>

The <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑤④"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> type is
an <a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface②③"
data-link-type="dfn">interface type</a> defined by the following IDL
fragment:

``` def
[Exposed=*,
 Serializable]
interface DOMException { // but see below note about JavaScript binding
  constructor(optional DOMString message = "", optional DOMString name = "Error");
  readonly attribute DOMString name;
  readonly attribute DOMString message;
  readonly attribute unsigned short code;

  const unsigned short INDEX_SIZE_ERR = 1;
  const unsigned short DOMSTRING_SIZE_ERR = 2;
  const unsigned short HIERARCHY_REQUEST_ERR = 3;
  const unsigned short WRONG_DOCUMENT_ERR = 4;
  const unsigned short INVALID_CHARACTER_ERR = 5;
  const unsigned short NO_DATA_ALLOWED_ERR = 6;
  const unsigned short NO_MODIFICATION_ALLOWED_ERR = 7;
  const unsigned short NOT_FOUND_ERR = 8;
  const unsigned short NOT_SUPPORTED_ERR = 9;
  const unsigned short INUSE_ATTRIBUTE_ERR = 10;
  const unsigned short INVALID_STATE_ERR = 11;
  const unsigned short SYNTAX_ERR = 12;
  const unsigned short INVALID_MODIFICATION_ERR = 13;
  const unsigned short NAMESPACE_ERR = 14;
  const unsigned short INVALID_ACCESS_ERR = 15;
  const unsigned short VALIDATION_ERR = 16;
  const unsigned short TYPE_MISMATCH_ERR = 17;
  const unsigned short SECURITY_ERR = 18;
  const unsigned short NETWORK_ERR = 19;
  const unsigned short ABORT_ERR = 20;
  const unsigned short URL_MISMATCH_ERR = 21;
  const unsigned short QUOTA_EXCEEDED_ERR = 22;
  const unsigned short TIMEOUT_ERR = 23;
  const unsigned short INVALID_NODE_TYPE_ERR = 24;
  const unsigned short DATA_CLONE_ERR = 25;
};
```

<span class="marker">Note:</span> as discussed in [§ 3.14.1 DOMException
custom bindings](#js-DOMException-specialness), the JavaScript binding
imposes additional requirements beyond the normal ones for
<a href="#idl-interface" id="ref-for-idl-interface②④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface types</a>.

Each <a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑤⑥"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> object
has an associated <span id="domexception-name" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="DOMException" dfn-type="dfn" export="">name</span> and
<span id="domexception-message" class="dfn dfn-paneled"
dfn-for="DOMException" dfn-type="dfn" export="">message</span>, both
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string" id="ref-for-string①"
data-link-type="dfn">strings</a>.

The <span id="dom-domexception-domexception"
class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code" dfn-for="DOMException"
dfn-type="constructor" export=""
lt="DOMException(message, name)|constructor(message, name)|DOMException(message)|constructor(message)|DOMException()|constructor()">`new DOMException(``message``, ``name``)`</span>
constructor steps are:

1.  Set
    <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this④④" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
    <a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name①②"
    data-link-type="dfn">name</a> to `name`.

2.  Set
    <a href="#this" id="ref-for-this④⑤" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
    <a href="#domexception-message" id="ref-for-domexception-message④"
    data-link-type="dfn">message</a> to `message`.

The <span id="dom-domexception-name" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code"
dfn-for="DOMException" dfn-type="attribute" export="">`name`</span>
getter steps are to return
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this④⑥" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name①③"
data-link-type="dfn">name</a>.

The <span id="dom-domexception-message" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code"
dfn-for="DOMException" dfn-type="attribute" export="">`message`</span>
getter steps are to return
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this④⑦" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
<a href="#domexception-message" id="ref-for-domexception-message⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">message</a>.

The <span id="dom-domexception-code" class="dfn dfn-paneled idl-code"
dfn-for="DOMException" dfn-type="attribute" export="">`code`</span>
getter steps are to return the legacy code indicated in the
<a href="#dfn-error-names-table" id="ref-for-dfn-error-names-table③"
data-link-type="dfn"><code>DOMException</code> names table</a> for
<a href="#this" id="ref-for-this④⑧" data-link-type="dfn">this</a>’s
<a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name①④"
data-link-type="dfn">name</a>, or 0 if no such entry exists in the
table.

<a href="#idl-DOMException" id="ref-for-idl-DOMException⑤⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">DOMException</code></a> objects
are <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#serializable-objects"
id="ref-for-serializable-objects②" data-link-type="dfn">serializable
objects</a>.

Their <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#serialization-steps"
id="ref-for-serialization-steps③" data-link-type="dfn">serialization
steps</a>, given `value` and `serialized`, are:

1.  Set `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\] to `value`’s
    <a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name①⑤"
    data-link-type="dfn">name</a>.
2.  Set `serialized`.\[\[Message\]\] to `value`’s
    <a href="#domexception-message" id="ref-for-domexception-message⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">message</a>.
3.  User agents should attach a serialized representation of any
    interesting accompanying data which are not yet specified, notably
    the `stack` property, to `serialized`.

Their <a
href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/structured-data.html#deserialization-steps"
id="ref-for-deserialization-steps③" data-link-type="dfn">deserialization
steps</a>, given `value` and `serialized`, are:

1.  Set `value`’s
    <a href="#domexception-name" id="ref-for-domexception-name①⑥"
    data-link-type="dfn">name</a> to `serialized`.\[\[Name\]\].
2.  Set `value`’s
    <a href="#domexception-message" id="ref-for-domexception-message⑦"
    data-link-type="dfn">message</a> to `serialized`.\[\[Message\]\].
3.  If any other data is attached to `serialized`, then deserialize and
    attach it to `value`.

### <span class="secno">4.5. </span><span id="common-Function" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Function</span><a href="#Function" id="ref-for-Function③" class="self-link"></a>

``` def
callback Function = any (any... arguments);
```

The
<a href="#Function" id="ref-for-Function②" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">Function</code></a>
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function③④"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> type is used for representing
function values with no restriction on what arguments are passed to it
or what kind of value is returned from it.

### <span class="secno">4.6. </span><span class="content">VoidFunction</span><a href="#VoidFunction" id="ref-for-VoidFunction" class="self-link"></a>

``` def
callback VoidFunction = undefined ();
```

The <a href="#VoidFunction" id="ref-for-VoidFunction①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">VoidFunction</code></a>
<a href="#dfn-callback-function" id="ref-for-dfn-callback-function③⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">callback function</a> type is used for representing
function values that take no arguments and do not return any value.

## <span class="secno">5. </span><span class="content">Extensibility</span><a href="#extensibility" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is informative.*

Extensions to language binding requirements can be specified using
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⑤⑦"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> that do not conflict with
those defined in this document. Extensions for private, project-specific
use ought not be included in
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑤①"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a> appearing in other
specifications. It is recommended that extensions that are required for
use in other specifications be coordinated with the group responsible
for work on Web IDL, which at the time of writing is the [W3C Web
Platform Working Group](http://www.w3.org/WebPlatform/WG/), for possible
inclusion in a future version of this document.

Extensions to any other aspect of the IDL language are strongly
discouraged.

## <span class="secno">6. </span><span class="content">Legacy constructs</span><a href="#legacy-constructs" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is informative.*

Legacy Web IDL constructs exist only so that legacy Web platform
features can be specified. They are generally prefixed with the
"`Legacy`" string. It is strongly discouraged to use legacy Web IDL
constructs in specifications unless required to specify the behavior of
legacy Web platform features, or for consistency with such features.
Editors who wish to use legacy Web IDL constructs are strongly advised
to discuss this by [filing an
issue](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/new?title=Intent%20to%20use%20a%20legacy%20Web%20IDL%20construct)
before proceeding.

Marking a construct as legacy does not, in itself, imply that it is
about to be removed from this specification. It does suggest however,
that it is a good candidate for future removal from this specification,
whenever various heuristics indicate that the Web platform features it
helps specify can be removed altogether or can be modified to rely on
non-legacy Web IDL constructs instead.

## <span class="secno">7. </span><span class="content">Referencing this specification</span><a href="#referencing" class="self-link"></a>

*This section is informative.*

It is expected that other specifications that define Web platform
interfaces using one or more
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑤②"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a> will reference this
specification. It is suggested that those specifications include a
sentence such as the following, to indicate that the IDL is to be
interpreted as described in this specification:

> The IDL fragment in Appendix A of this specification must, in
> conjunction with the IDL fragments defined in this specification’s
> normative references, be interpreted as required for *conforming sets
> of IDL fragments*, as described in the “Web IDL” specification.
> \[WEBIDL\]

In addition, it is suggested that the conformance class for user agents
in referencing specifications be linked to the
<a href="#dfn-conforming-implementation"
id="ref-for-dfn-conforming-implementation①"
data-link-type="dfn">conforming implementation</a> class from this
specification:

> A conforming FooML user agent must also be a *conforming
> implementation* of the IDL fragment in Appendix A of this
> specification, as described in the “Web IDL” specification. \[WEBIDL\]

## <span class="secno">8. </span><span class="content">Privacy and Security Considerations</span><a href="#priv-sec" class="self-link"></a>

This specification defines a conversion layer between JavaScript and IDL
values. An incorrect implementation of this layer can lead to security
issues.

This specification also provides the ability to use JavaScript values
directly, through the
<a href="#idl-any" id="ref-for-idl-any②⓪" data-link-type="idl"><code
class="idl">any</code></a> and
<a href="#idl-object" id="ref-for-idl-object②⑦"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">object</code></a> IDL types.
These values need to be handled carefully to avoid security issues. In
particular, user script can run in response to nearly any manipulation
of these values, and invalidate the expectations of specifications or
implementations using them.

This specification makes it possible to interact with
<a href="#idl-SharedArrayBuffer" id="ref-for-idl-SharedArrayBuffer②①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">SharedArrayBuffer</code></a>
objects, which can be used to build timing attacks. Specifications that
use these objects need to consider such attacks.
