## <span class="content">IDL grammar</span><a href="#idl-grammar" class="self-link"></a>

This section defines an LL(1) grammar whose start symbol,
[Definitions](#prod-Definitions), matches an entire
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑤③"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a>.

Each production in the grammar has on its right hand side either a
non-zero sequence of terminal and non-terminal symbols, or an epsilon
(ε) which indicates no symbols. Symbols that begin with an uppercase
letter are non-terminal symbols. Symbols in monospaced fonts are
terminal symbols. Symbols in sans-serif font that begin with a lowercase
letter are terminal symbols that are matched by the regular expressions
(using Perl 5 regular expression syntax
<a href="#biblio-perlre" data-link-type="biblio"
title="Perl regular expressions (Perl 5.8.8)">[PERLRE]</a>) as follows:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
| integer | `=` | <span class="mute">`/`</span>`-?([1-9][0-9]*|0[Xx][0-9A-Fa-f]+|0[0-7]*)`<span class="mute">`/`</span> |
| decimal | `=` | <span class="mute">`/`</span>`-?(([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|[0-9]*\.[0-9]+)([Ee][+-]?[0-9]+)?|[0-9]+[Ee][+-]?[0-9]+)`<span class="mute">`/`</span> |
| identifier | `=` | <span class="mute">`/`</span>`[_-]?[A-Za-z][0-9A-Z_a-z-]*`<span class="mute">`/`</span> |
| string | `=` | <span class="mute">`/`</span>`"[^"]*"`<span class="mute">`/`</span> |
| whitespace | `=` | <span class="mute">`/`</span>`[\t\n\r ]+`<span class="mute">`/`</span> |
| comment | `=` | <span class="mute">`/`</span><span class="mute">`\`</span>`/`<span class="mute">`\`</span>`/.*|`<span class="mute">`\`</span>`/\*(.|\n)*?\*`<span class="mute">`\`</span>`/`<span class="mute">`/`</span> |
| other | `=` | <span class="mute">`/`</span>`[^\t\n\r 0-9A-Za-z]`<span class="mute">`/`</span> |

The tokenizer operates on a sequence of
<a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#scalar-value"
id="ref-for-scalar-value①⓪" data-link-type="dfn">scalar values</a>. When
tokenizing, the longest possible match must be used. For example, if the
input text is “<span class="input">a1</span>”, it is tokenized as a
single [identifier](#prod-identifier), and not as a separate
[identifier](#prod-identifier) and [integer](#prod-integer). If the
longest possible match could match one of the above named terminal
symbols or one of the other terminal symbols from the grammar, it must
be tokenized as the latter. Thus, the input text
“<span class="input">long</span>” is tokenized as the terminal symbol
long rather than an [identifier](#prod-identifier) called "`long`", and
“<span class="input">.</span>” is tokenized as the terminal symbol .
rather than an [other](#prod-other).

The IDL syntax is case sensitive, both for the monospaced terminal
symbols used in the grammar and the values used for
[identifier](#prod-identifier) terminals. Thus, for example, the input
text “<span class="input">Const</span>” is tokenized as an
[identifier](#prod-identifier) rather than the terminal symbol const, an
<a href="#dfn-interface" id="ref-for-dfn-interface②⑤④"
data-link-type="dfn">interface</a> with
<a href="#dfn-identifier" id="ref-for-dfn-identifier①⓪⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">identifier</a> "`A`" is distinct from one named
"`a`", and an
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⑤⑧"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attribute</a> \[`legacyfactoryfunction`\]
will not be recognized as the
\[<a href="#LegacyFactoryFunction" id="ref-for-LegacyFactoryFunction②①"
data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">LegacyFactoryFunction</code></a>\]
extended attribute.

Implicitly, any number of [whitespace](#prod-whitespace) and
[comment](#prod-comment) terminals are allowed between every other
terminal in the input text being parsed. Such
[whitespace](#prod-whitespace) and [comment](#prod-comment) terminals
are ignored while parsing.

The following LL(1) grammar, starting with
[Definitions](#prod-Definitions), matches an
<a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑤④"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragment</a>:

<div>

``` grammar
Definitions ::
    ExtendedAttributeList Definition Definitions
    ε

Definition ::
    CallbackOrInterfaceOrMixin
    Namespace
    Partial
    Dictionary
    Enum
    Typedef
    IncludesStatement

ArgumentNameKeyword ::
    attribute
    callback
    const
    constructor
    deleter
    dictionary
    enum
    getter
    includes
    inherit
    interface
    iterable
    maplike
    mixin
    namespace
    partial
    readonly
    required
    setlike
    setter
    static
    stringifier
    typedef
    unrestricted

CallbackOrInterfaceOrMixin ::
    callback CallbackRestOrInterface
    interface InterfaceOrMixin

InterfaceOrMixin ::
    InterfaceRest
    MixinRest

InterfaceRest ::
    identifier Inheritance { InterfaceMembers } ;

Partial ::
    partial PartialDefinition

PartialDefinition ::
    interface PartialInterfaceOrPartialMixin
    PartialDictionary
    Namespace

PartialInterfaceOrPartialMixin ::
    PartialInterfaceRest
    MixinRest

PartialInterfaceRest ::
    identifier { PartialInterfaceMembers } ;

InterfaceMembers ::
    ExtendedAttributeList InterfaceMember InterfaceMembers
    ε

InterfaceMember ::
    PartialInterfaceMember
    Constructor

PartialInterfaceMembers ::
    ExtendedAttributeList PartialInterfaceMember PartialInterfaceMembers
    ε

PartialInterfaceMember ::
    Const
    Operation
    Stringifier
    StaticMember
    Iterable
    AsyncIterable
    ReadOnlyMember
    ReadWriteAttribute
    ReadWriteMaplike
    ReadWriteSetlike
    InheritAttribute

Inheritance ::
    : identifier
    ε

MixinRest ::
    mixin identifier { MixinMembers } ;

MixinMembers ::
    ExtendedAttributeList MixinMember MixinMembers
    ε

MixinMember ::
    Const
    RegularOperation
    Stringifier
    OptionalReadOnly AttributeRest

IncludesStatement ::
    identifier includes identifier ;

CallbackRestOrInterface ::
    CallbackRest
    interface identifier { CallbackInterfaceMembers } ;

CallbackInterfaceMembers ::
    ExtendedAttributeList CallbackInterfaceMember CallbackInterfaceMembers
    ε

CallbackInterfaceMember ::
    Const
    RegularOperation

Const ::
    const ConstType identifier = ConstValue ;

ConstValue ::
    BooleanLiteral
    FloatLiteral
    integer

BooleanLiteral ::
    true
    false

FloatLiteral ::
    decimal
    -Infinity
    Infinity
    NaN

ConstType ::
    PrimitiveType
    identifier

ReadOnlyMember ::
    readonly ReadOnlyMemberRest

ReadOnlyMemberRest ::
    AttributeRest
    MaplikeRest
    SetlikeRest

ReadWriteAttribute ::
    AttributeRest

InheritAttribute ::
    inherit AttributeRest

AttributeRest ::
    attribute TypeWithExtendedAttributes AttributeName ;

AttributeName ::
    AttributeNameKeyword
    identifier

AttributeNameKeyword ::
    required

OptionalReadOnly ::
    readonly
    ε

DefaultValue ::
    ConstValue
    string
    [ ]
    { }
    null
    undefined

Operation ::
    RegularOperation
    SpecialOperation

RegularOperation ::
    Type OperationRest

SpecialOperation ::
    Special RegularOperation

Special ::
    getter
    setter
    deleter

OperationRest ::
    OptionalOperationName ( ArgumentList ) ;

OptionalOperationName ::
    OperationName
    ε

OperationName ::
    OperationNameKeyword
    identifier

OperationNameKeyword ::
    includes

ArgumentList ::
    Argument Arguments
    ε

Arguments ::
    , Argument Arguments
    ε

Argument ::
    ExtendedAttributeList ArgumentRest

ArgumentRest ::
    optional TypeWithExtendedAttributes ArgumentName Default
    Type Ellipsis ArgumentName

ArgumentName ::
    ArgumentNameKeyword
    identifier

Ellipsis ::
    ...
    ε

Constructor ::
    constructor ( ArgumentList ) ;

Stringifier ::
    stringifier StringifierRest

StringifierRest ::
    OptionalReadOnly AttributeRest
    ;

StaticMember ::
    static StaticMemberRest

StaticMemberRest ::
    OptionalReadOnly AttributeRest
    RegularOperation

Iterable ::
    iterable < TypeWithExtendedAttributes OptionalType > ;

OptionalType ::
    , TypeWithExtendedAttributes
    ε

AsyncIterable ::
    async_iterable < TypeWithExtendedAttributes OptionalType > OptionalArgumentList ;

OptionalArgumentList ::
    ( ArgumentList )
    ε

ReadWriteMaplike ::
    MaplikeRest

MaplikeRest ::
    maplike < TypeWithExtendedAttributes , TypeWithExtendedAttributes > ;

ReadWriteSetlike ::
    SetlikeRest

SetlikeRest ::
    setlike < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > ;

Namespace ::
    namespace identifier { NamespaceMembers } ;

NamespaceMembers ::
    ExtendedAttributeList NamespaceMember NamespaceMembers
    ε

NamespaceMember ::
    RegularOperation
    readonly AttributeRest
    Const

Dictionary ::
    dictionary identifier Inheritance { DictionaryMembers } ;

DictionaryMembers ::
    DictionaryMember DictionaryMembers
    ε

DictionaryMember ::
    ExtendedAttributeList DictionaryMemberRest

DictionaryMemberRest ::
    required TypeWithExtendedAttributes identifier ;
    Type identifier Default ;

PartialDictionary ::
    dictionary identifier { DictionaryMembers } ;

Default ::
    = DefaultValue
    ε

Enum ::
    enum identifier { EnumValueList } ;

EnumValueList ::
    string EnumValueListComma

EnumValueListComma ::
    , EnumValueListString
    ε

EnumValueListString ::
    string EnumValueListComma
    ε

CallbackRest ::
    identifier = Type ( ArgumentList ) ;

Typedef ::
    typedef TypeWithExtendedAttributes identifier ;

Type ::
    SingleType
    UnionType Null

TypeWithExtendedAttributes ::
    ExtendedAttributeList Type

SingleType ::
    DistinguishableType
    any
    PromiseType

UnionType ::
    ( UnionMemberType or UnionMemberType UnionMemberTypes )

UnionMemberType ::
    ExtendedAttributeList DistinguishableType
    UnionType Null

UnionMemberTypes ::
    or UnionMemberType UnionMemberTypes
    ε

DistinguishableType ::
    PrimitiveType Null

    sequence < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null

    object Null

    BufferRelatedType Null
    FrozenArray < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null
    ObservableArray < TypeWithExtendedAttributes > Null

PrimitiveType ::

ExtendedAttributeList ::

    ε

ExtendedAttributes ::
    , ExtendedAttribute ExtendedAttributes
    ε

ExtendedAttribute ::
    ( ExtendedAttributeInner ) ExtendedAttributeRest
    [ ExtendedAttributeInner ] ExtendedAttributeRest
    { ExtendedAttributeInner } ExtendedAttributeRest
    Other ExtendedAttributeRest

ExtendedAttributeRest ::
    ExtendedAttribute
    ε

ExtendedAttributeInner ::
    ( ExtendedAttributeInner ) ExtendedAttributeInner
    [ ExtendedAttributeInner ] ExtendedAttributeInner
    { ExtendedAttributeInner } ExtendedAttributeInner
    OtherOrComma ExtendedAttributeInner
    ε

Other ::
    integer
    decimal

ExtendedAttributeNoArgs ::

ExtendedAttributeIdent ::

```

</div>

<span class="marker">Note:</span> The [Other](#prod-Other) non-terminal
matches any single terminal symbol except for (, ), \[, \], {, } and ,.

While the [ExtendedAttribute](#prod-ExtendedAttribute) non-terminal
matches any non-empty sequence of terminal symbols (as long as any
parentheses, square brackets or braces are balanced, and the , token
appears only within those balanced brackets), only a subset of those
possible sequences are used by the
<a href="#dfn-extended-attribute" id="ref-for-dfn-extended-attribute①⑤⑨"
data-link-type="dfn">extended attributes</a> defined in this
specification — see [§ 2.14 Extended
attributes](#idl-extended-attributes) for the syntaxes that are used by
these extended attributes.

## <span class="content">Document conventions</span><a href="#conventions" class="self-link"></a>

The following typographic conventions are used in this document:

- Defining instances of terms: <span id="dfn-example-term"
  class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" noexport="">example term</span>

- Links to terms defined in this document or elsewhere:
  <a href="#dfn-example-term" id="ref-for-dfn-example-term"
  data-link-type="dfn">example term</a>

- Grammar terminals: sometoken

- Grammar non-terminals: ExampleGrammarNonTerminal

- Grammar symbols: identifier

- IDL types:
  <a href="#idl-unsigned-long" id="ref-for-idl-unsigned-long①①"
  data-link-type="idl"><code class="idl">unsigned long</code></a>

- JavaScript classes: <a
  href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/keyed-collections.html#sec-map-objects"
  id="ref-for-sec-map-objects①" data-link-type="idl"><code
  class="idl">Map</code></a>

- JavaScript language types: Object

- Code snippets: `a = b + obj.f()`

- Scalar values: U+0030 (0)

- Extended attributes: \[`ExampleExtendedAttribute`\]

- Variable names in prose and algorithms: `exampleVariableName`.

- IDL informal syntax examples:

  ``` highlight
  [extended_attributes]
  interface identifier {
    /* interface_members... */
  };
  ```

  (Specific parts of the syntax discussed in surrounding prose are
  <span class="mark">highlighted</span>.)

- IDL grammar snippets:

  ``` grammar
  ExampleGrammarNonTerminal ::
      OtherNonTerminal sometoken
      other AnotherNonTerminal
      ε  // nothing
  ```

- Non-normative notes:

  <span class="marker">Note:</span> This is a note.

- Non-normative examples:

  <div id="example-263fb1aa" class="example">

  <a href="#example-263fb1aa" class="self-link"></a> This is an example.

  </div>

- Normative warnings:

  This is a warning.

- Code blocks:

  ``` highlight
  // This is an IDL code block.
  [Exposed=Window]
  interface Example {
    attribute long something;
  };
  ```

  ``` highlight
  // This is a JavaScript code block.
  window.onload = function() { window.alert("loaded"); };
  ```

The following conventions are used in the algorithms in this document:

- Algorithms use the
  <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-algorithm-conventions"
  id="ref-for-sec-algorithm-conventions"
  data-link-type="dfn">conventions</a> of the JavaScript specification,
  including the
  <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
  id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑥②" data-link-type="dfn"
  data-refhint-key="548dbb6b">!</a> and
  <a href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands"
  id="ref-for-sec-returnifabrupt-shorthands①⑥③" data-link-type="dfn">?</a>
  notation for unwrapping <a
  href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
  id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type②①"
  data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="c8a04a12">Completion Records</a>.

- Algorithms sometimes treat returning/throwing values and returning <a
  href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
  id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type②②"
  data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="c8a04a12">Completion Records</a>
  interchangeably. That is, an algorithm that uses return/throw
  terminology may be treated as returning a <a
  href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
  id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type②③"
  data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="c8a04a12">Completion Record</a>,
  while one that returns a <a
  href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
  id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type②④"
  data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="c8a04a12">Completion Record</a>
  may be treated as returning a value or throwing an exception.
  Similarly, to catch exceptions, defining the behavior to adopt when
  <a href="#an-exception-was-thrown" id="ref-for-an-exception-was-thrown②"
  data-link-type="dfn">an exception was thrown</a> and checking if the
  <a
  href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
  id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type②⑤"
  data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="c8a04a12">Completion Record</a>’s
  \[\[Type\]\] field is “throw” are equivalent.

- <a
  href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type"
  id="ref-for-sec-completion-record-specification-type②⑥"
  data-link-type="dfn" data-refhint-key="c8a04a12">Completion Records</a>
  are extended by allowing them to contain values that are not
  JavaScript values, such as Web IDL values.

## <span id="conformant-algorithms" class="bs-old-id"></span><span class="content">Conformance</span><a href="#conformance" class="self-link"></a>

Everything in this specification is normative except for diagrams,
examples, notes and sections marked as being informative.

This specification depends on the Infra Standard.
<a href="#biblio-infra" data-link-type="biblio"
title="Infra Standard">[INFRA]</a>

The following conformance classes are defined by this specification:

<span id="dfn-conforming-set-of-idl-fragments" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">conforming set of IDL fragments</span>  
A set of <a href="#dfn-idl-fragment" id="ref-for-dfn-idl-fragment⑤⑤"
data-link-type="dfn">IDL fragments</a> is considered to be a
<a href="#dfn-conforming-set-of-idl-fragments"
id="ref-for-dfn-conforming-set-of-idl-fragments"
data-link-type="dfn">conforming set of IDL fragments</a> if, taken
together, they satisfy all of the must-, required- and shall-level
criteria in this specification that apply to IDL fragments.

<span id="dfn-conforming-implementation" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export="">conforming implementation</span>  
A user agent is considered to be a
<a href="#dfn-conforming-implementation"
id="ref-for-dfn-conforming-implementation②"
data-link-type="dfn">conforming implementation</a> relative to a
<a href="#dfn-conforming-set-of-idl-fragments"
id="ref-for-dfn-conforming-set-of-idl-fragments①"
data-link-type="dfn">conforming set of IDL fragments</a> if it satisfies
all of the must-, required- and shall-level criteria in this
specification that apply to implementations for all language bindings
that the user agent supports.

<span id="dfn-conforming-javascript-implementation" class="dfn dfn-paneled" dfn-type="dfn" export=""><span id="dfn-conforming-ecmascript-implementation" class="bs-old-id"></span>conforming JavaScript implementation</span>  
A user agent is considered to be a
<a href="#dfn-conforming-javascript-implementation"
id="ref-for-dfn-conforming-javascript-implementation"
data-link-type="dfn">conforming JavaScript implementation</a> relative
to a <a href="#dfn-conforming-set-of-idl-fragments"
id="ref-for-dfn-conforming-set-of-idl-fragments②"
data-link-type="dfn">conforming set of IDL fragments</a> if it satisfies
all of the must-, required- and shall-level criteria in this
specification that apply to implementations for the JavaScript language
binding.
